notes: M21's 벗다 + 기 — and read the invitation carefully: this one is from the M37 party, not the M36 one. The 기 that made 끊기다 done-to (M36) makes 벗기다 make-do, alongside M37's 맡기다, 남기다, 숨기다 and M19's 웃기다: membership, not rule. The M37 md left the bedtime routine — '눕히다 (lay someone down), 씻기다 (wash someone), 신기다 (put shoes on someone)' — as table-only guests; 벗기다 is the missing step: 아이 옷을 벗기다 (M4's 아이, M7's 옷) = undress the child. Also the kitchen: 사과 껍질을 벗기다 (M3's 사과, M40's 껍질) = peel an apple — the 껍질 comes off because someone took it off.

Hey! — Module 19's vocative section taught that vowel-ending names take 야 (민수야!); this is that call unhooked from any name and aimed at whoever is in range. Friends, juniors, kids — and NEVER upward: a 야 at a boss or a stranger is a fight, not a greeting. Alone, 야! is also the yelp of surprise — the sound of a dropped phone. Radar: the night-야 of M16's 야근하다 and the field-야 of M17's 야구 are hanja; this one is breath.

The casual yes. M33's 예 note said it — '반말 drops it to 어 or 응' — and the slang appendix's ㅇㅇ is '응 (casual yes) stripped to its consonant, twice.' The answer to 밥 먹었어? between friends; doubled, 응응 is the listening-nod that keeps a story going. Same floor as M19's 반말: to an elder, a customer, or a stranger the word is still 네.

응 with a longer breath — NIKL files it separately, and the breath changes the job: falling, it is reluctant agreement (으응… 알았어 = fine, okay); rising, 으응? asks you to repeat. Also the toddler's whine, hanging on a parent's sleeve. Same floor as 응 — friends and juniors only.

en: how about it? / how is it? (casual)
notes: M24's 어떻다 note gave you '어때요? — how is it?'; take the 요 off by the subtraction rule of M19's 반말 and 어때 is what friends actually say: 이거 어때? = how about this one?; 어때, 괜찮아? = well? okay? Past tense asks how it went — 어땠어? Polite listeners get 어때요 back; the 요 is the whole difference.

M29's 그렇다 wearing the bare -지 tag that the M51 markdown filed ('반말 keeps just -지 (알지?)'): falling, 그렇지! = exactly, that's it; rising, 그렇지? = right? Its polite face is 그렇죠 (the -죠 ending from M51), and M34's 당연하다 note promised that 'the full casual form 당연하지! arrives with Ring 2's -지 ending' — same tag, delivered today. Radar: one syllable from M29's 그렇지만 — 'right?' vs 'however.'

Module 19's markdown called 아니에요 → 아니야 'the one genuinely new form', and NIKL files the result as an interjection in its own right: the flat casual no, and the denial of M19's 아니다, in one shape. M37's 장난 note ran 장난 아니야 = seriously intense; the dialect appendix's 아이가 is its 경상도 shape. Radar vs M29's 아니: 아니 opens a protest (아니, 왜?), 아니야 closes a question. Friends and juniors; upward it is 아니에요.

M1's 아니요 squeezed to its 준말 (the shortened form) — the polite no as it actually leaves the mouth: 아뇨, 괜찮아요. Same register as 아니요 (any listener, any age), one syllable cheaper; print writes 아니요, speech says 아뇨. With 아니야 above you now hold the whole no-ladder: 아니 (M29) among friends, 아뇨 upward, 아닙니다 in uniform.

Pure noise with a job: 자, 시작합시다 (the -(으)ㅂ시다 let's-form from M9, on M8's 시작하다) = right then, let's begin — the sound teachers, hosts, and tour guides make to gather a room; 자, 자 hurries it along. Register: aimed at a group you are leading, or at equals — you don't 자 a boss to his feet. Radar: not the stem of M1's 자다, not the person-者 of M43's 소비자, not a ruler; this one means nothing and moves everyone.

The thinking noise — 음… 글쎄 — buying a second before an opinion, and the pleasure noise, 음, 맛있다 (M1's 맛있다), before a second bite. Any register: it commits to nothing, so it offends no one. Radar: the 음 inside M1's 음식 and M2's 음악 is hanja (飮, 音); this one is breath.

M24's 글쎄요 note filed the receipt — 'Drop the 요 among friends; M19 rules apply' — and here it is, dropped: 글쎄… = well, dunno; 글쎄, 모르겠어 — M4's 모르다, shrugging — = beats me. It also disagrees softly: 글쎄, 그럴까? = hmm, would it, though? The gap deck holds its best trick, 글쎄 말이야, where the hedge flips into total agreement. Friends and juniors; upward the 요 goes back on.

The surprise noise, feminine-coded — men default to 어 or M29's 아이고 — and the first half of the pair this module completes: 어머, 어떡해 = oh no, what now. Longer form 어머나; doubled 어머 어머 for gossip-grade shock. Any register — it is aimed at the event, not the listener. Radar: not a clipped call to M4's 어머니; the shapes rhyme, the words don't.

Laughter spelled out — NIKL files it as an adverb, so it rides with 웃다 (M7): 하하 웃다 = laugh out loud. The slang appendix's ㅎㅎ note called itself 'the h of 하하' — this is the full breath. The vowel is the demographic: 호호 for women, 허허 for grandfathers, 히히 for kids, 하하 for everyone. Any register; laughter has no 요.

en: anyway, in any case (a shade formal)
notes: 何如- 'however it is' + the -튼 that M33's 어쨌든 note built from 어찌+했+든 ('however it went'). That note said 'the -든 piece is a Ring 2 pattern still in the mail' — it still is; hear the shrug, don't build with it yet. 하여튼 is the shade-formal anyway: 하여튼 고마워요 = anyway, thank you. Any register; it changes the topic, not the listener.

M29's 아무 — 'the any-pointer' — plus the same -튼: any-way, literally. The mouth's favorite of the three: 어쨌든 (M33) is neutral, 하여튼 a shade formal, 아무튼 what people actually say — 아무튼, 밥 먹자 (the -자 let's-ending from M19). Any register; the trio differs in starch, not in politeness.

分明 divided-bright: M34's 분명하다 minus its 하다, the bare adverb, placed before a judgment: 분명 무슨 일이 있어요 = there is DEFINITELY something going on. Radar vs M62's 분명히 — 'the eyewitness word', sworn to what the eyes saw — 분명 infers: the detective says 분명, the witness says 분명히. Register-neutral; it states certainty, not respect.

M24's 아마 + M2's 도: probably, plus a hedge — the 도 softens the guess one notch. 아마도 그럴 거예요 (the guessing future -(으)ㄹ 거예요 from M8) = probably so, I'd say; 아마도… alone answers a question without answering it. Any register; certainty is still not the Korean way.

The blink, and the slip: M14's 눈 blinks — 눈을 깜빡이다; M13's 불 flickers — 불이 깜빡이다; and M15's 잊다 slips — 깜빡 잊었어요 = it slipped my mind; 깜빡했어요 (깜빡하다, riding free) = I forgot, the everyday confession. A mimetic, the same sound-as-shape mold as M54's 튼튼하다 and M60's 딱딱하다. Radar vs M62's 깜짝: 깜빡 blinks and forgets, 깜짝 jumps.

M38's 자꾸 — 'Repetition, minus the control' — plus M30's 만 (only/just), fused into one adverb: the repetition with the exasperation added. M67's 생각나다 on loop — 자꾸만 생각나 = I just keep thinking of it, the ballad line; 왜 자꾸만 그래? = why do you KEEP doing that. Any register; the 만 supplies the sigh.

en: to tell, say (humbly, to an elder)
notes: M27's 말씀 note wrote the IOU — 'Humble twist: it also lowers YOUR words to an elder (말씀 드릴게요 — Ring 2 machinery, previewed)' — paid: 말씀 + M9's 드리다 ('giving UPWARD'), welded into one verb. 말씀드릴 게 있어요 = there is something I need to tell you; 다시 말씀드리면 = to put it again, the presenter's phrase. Radar, same 말씀, opposite direction: 말씀하세요 (the honorific -(으)시- from M4 — YOU, honored, speak) vs 말씀드려요 (I, lowered, speak). Upward only — to a friend it is just 말할게.

en: to see, meet (humble); to be visible (contracted 보이다)
notes: Two dictionary entries, one spelling, and NIKL lists both. The first is M36's 보이다 squeezed, alive in set phrases — the gap deck's 눈에 뵈는 게 없다, nothing visible to the eye = blind with rage. The second is the humble see-meet, the twin behind M47's 뵙다: that note said 'Before vowels it writes 뵈-' and ran 내일 봬요 and 뵈러 가요 as its examples; the fuller truth is two verbs sharing one job — 뵈다 before vowel endings (봬요, 뵈러, 뵀어요), 뵙다 before consonant endings (뵙겠습니다, the formula M15's 처음 note filed; 뵙고 싶어요). Upward only, always: you 뵈다 elders and seniors; they 보다 (M1) you.

M15's 답 — 'The noun inside M10's 대답하다' — plus 하다: the short, written twin. 질문에 답하다 — M10's 질문 — = answer the question, on forms, exams, and in news prose; 대답하다 lives in mouths. Register by medium: 답하세요 on the test paper, 대답해 주세요 across the table.

M24's 대화 — 'face-to-face speech… 대화가 필요해요' — plus 하다. Radar vs M10's 이야기하다 (chat, tell): 대화 is two-way by definition, the counselor's and the couple's verb — 부모님과 대화하다 — with M4's 부모님 — is what teenagers refuse and therapists prescribe. Any register; the honorific rides in as 대화하시다.

en: to take pains, put in effort
notes: The verb inside the M16 gap deck's 수고하셨습니다 ('honors the effort') — here is the engine. Three settings, the honorific -(으)시- from M4 riding every one: 수고하셨습니다 to someone finishing, 수고하세요 leaving them to it (the sign-off to shop staff and colleagues), 수고 많으셨어요 — M7's 많다 — the warm version. The register rule worth the whole note: never aim 수고하세요 UP at a boss — it rates effort, which is a superior's privilege; equals and downward only. Leaving a senior, bow and say 내일 뵙겠습니다 instead.

M5's 하나 note showed the contraction 'Before a counter it contracts: 한 — 커피 한 잔'; close the space and the count becomes an occasion: 한잔 = a drink, meaning alcohol, meaning company. 한잔 할까요? (the -(으)ㄹ까요 shall-we from M9); 한잔하자 among friends. Radar: 커피 한 잔 (spaced, counted, M5's 잔) vs 한잔 (fused, poured) — the spacing is the entire difference. Register: the invitation goes sideways and down; upward, you wait to be invited.

한잔 + 하다: to have a drink, or several. M16's 퇴근하다 — 'the day's sweetest verb' — leads straight into it: 퇴근하고 한잔해요 is the sentence that starts M16's 회식 ('officially optional and practically not'). 한잔했어요? = been drinking? — asked gently at the door. Any register once the invitation exists; declining is 오늘은 좀… with the sentence left unfinished, which in Korean is a complete refusal.

en: to do how; what to do (the panic verb)
notes: 어떻게 하다 — M10's 어떻게 + 하다 — contracted into one irregular verb (NIKL: 어떠하게 하다), living almost entirely in one panic: 어떡해(요)? = what do I do? / oh no. M29's 아이고 note already ran 아이고, 어떡해; 어머, 어떡해 is this module's pair. Talking to yourself it takes the bare -지 tag from M51: 어떡하지? = what now?; asking others politely, 어떡할까요? Spelling trap: 어떡해, never 어떻해 — 어떻게 (M10) is M24's 어떻다 in adverb form, and 어떡- is a different squeeze. Any register; the 요 decides.

An animal's young — the primary sense, and the only one you will use: 새끼 고양이 (M22's 고양이) = kitten, 새끼 새 (M22's 새) = a chick, 새끼를 낳다 (M47's 낳다) = have a litter. Parents say 내 새끼 of their own children, rough and fond — the same double agent M47's 자식 note showed with 이 자식. Third sense, and the reason this note is long: aimed at a person, 새끼 is the language's heaviest common curse. Say it about kittens. Never say it AT anyone, in any register, at any volume.

科學者 science-person: 과학 (M15) + the person-者 that M27's 환자 note introduced ('기자, 학자 — reporter, scholar'), M43's 소비자 formalized ('기자 M16 records, 환자 suffers, 소비자 spends'), and M48's 저자/독자 extended — the payroll's biggest hire yet. M46's 장래 note already used the word: 'every Korean adult once wrote 과학자 or 가수 in it' — receipt, paid. 학자 (scholar — riding frozen) is the suffix bare; 과학자 is the one with a lab coat.

硏究者: 연구 (M32) + the same person-者 — the researcher as a CATEGORY, the paper's 'the researchers' (연구자들은 …). Radar vs 연구원, which M44's 연구하다 note listed ('연구원 = researcher'): 연구원 is a job title on a badge at a 연구소 (next entry); 연구자 is what anyone is the moment they research something. The news says 연구자들에 따르면; the payroll says 연구원.

硏究所 research-place: 연구 + the place-所 that M52's 숙소 note decoded ('장소's place-所 (M27)') — the institute. M32's 연구 note filed the room: '연구실 is the lab/office every Korean grad student calls home'; the 소 zooms out — 연구실 is the room, 연구소 is the building with a sign on it. The same 所 sits inside 장소 (M27) itself, and inside this shelf's 산소, four entries down.

機械 machine-gear: the machine-機 that M33's 기회 note named ('The 기 is 비행기's machine-기 (M12)') and M54's 선풍기 pinned onto 세탁기 (M13), + 械 (frozen — contraption). The iron itself: 기계를 돌리다 — M37's 돌리다, whose note already runs the washer. Radar vs M44's 기술 ('skill and technology, undivided'): 기술 is the know-how, 기계 is the iron that runs on it. Rank 910 — the pool's highest-ranked noun, because everything from the 세탁기 to the 공장 (M43) is one.

Loan, through the converter: energy → 에너지, the E landing as 에 and the r-vowel as 어. Radar vs M14's 힘 ('힘이 없어요 — no energy: the universal symptom'): both live — 힘 is the energy you feel, 에너지 is the energy science measures and the bill charges: 에너지 절약 (절약 — saving, riding frozen) on every office light switch, 태양 에너지 (M49's 태양) on the roof. Your body runs out of 힘; the country worries about 에너지.

電子 electric-child: the electric-電 that M36's 전기 note finally isolated ('the FIRST 전 finally alone') + the child-子 that M47's 자식 note found hiding inside 남자/여자 (M4). The electron — and the adjective 'electronic': 전자 제품 (M43's 제품), 전자레인지 (the microwave — riding frozen: an 'electronic range'), and 삼성전자 printed on the back of half the world's phones. Radar: M50's 운전자 also spells 전자, by accident — that split is 운전 + person-者, no electrons involved.

酸素 acid-element: acid-酸 (frozen) + element-素, the 素 that M38's 평소 note glossed ('平素 flat-ordinary') — the plain stuff things are made of; 수소 (hydrogen) and 질소 (nitrogen) share the -소, riding frozen. RADAR, and it is a good one: a second 산소 (山所) is a GRAVE — M11's 산 + the place-所 of 장소 (M27), the ancestral mound on a hillside, M69's 조상 territory. 병원 (M6) 산소 keeps you breathing; 추석 (M25) 산소 is where the family bows.

石油 stone-oil: stone-石 (frozen — M22's 돌 is the native stone, the one that shares its syllable with a baby's first birthday) + the oil-油 of M59's 식용유. Radar vs M40's 기름 ('All oil, one word' — that note also filed 기름값 = fuel prices): 기름 is the oil in the pan and in the tank; 석유 is the commodity on the news — 석유 가격 (M21's 가격), 석유 회사 (M2's 회사). You put 기름 in the car; the anchor reports 석유.

自動 self-moving: M50's 자동차 minus the cart — that note decoded 自動車 'self-moving-cart', and the 動 is the move-動 M57's 활동 note traced to 운동하다 (M8). Bare, it stamps machines: 자동문 (M6's 문, opening for you), 자동 판매기 → clipped to 자판기 (the vending machine, riding frozen); with M6's 으로 it adverbs — 자동으로 = automatically, the word your phone's settings screen repeats. 자동차 is one self-moving thing; 자동 is the idea.

Loan, three jobs: the runway (패션 모델 — 패션 riding frozen), the product (신모델 / 새 모델 — M13's 새; the version your phone is not), and the scientist's model — 경제 모델 (M32's 경제), the simplified machine a 연구자 builds to think with. English quietly split the word three ways; Korean kept one loan for all of them, and the 모델 on the billboard and the 모델 in the paper share a spelling and nothing else.

道具 way-gear: the way-道 that M38's 도로 note decoded (道路 way-road — the province-道 of M31 'doing street work') — NOT M32's 정도, whose 도 is degree-度 — + the gear-具 of M54's 가구 ('家具 house-gear'). Tools, as a category: 요리 도구 (the 요리 inside M3's 요리하다), 도구를 사용하다 (M10). Furniture is house-gear; a tool is way-gear, the gear for getting somewhere. Where 기계 runs on power, 도구 runs on your hand.

事物 matter-thing: the 事 of M36's 사고/사건 + the thing-物 that M48's 인물 note lifted from 물건 (M9). The abstract 'things': 사물을 보는 눈 (M14's 눈 — an eye for objects, the critic's compliment), 사물함 = the locker (a things-box, riding frozen). RADAR: the 사물놀이 in M51's 북 note is 四物 — FOUR things, the four instruments — a different 사 in the same spelling; the gap deck has it. 물건 is the stuff you buy; 사물 is the stuff philosophers count.

實際 real-between: the real-實 of M34's 확실하다 ('確實 firm-real') + the between-際 of M31's 국제 — reality, as it actually plays out between things. 실제 크기 (M57's 크기) = actual size; 실제로 = actually, in reality — the adverb rides free on M6's 으로, and NIKL lists it as its own entry. Radar, three ways: M24's 사실 is a FACT (and 사실은… confesses), M11's 진짜 is really (a feeling), 실제 is measured reality — what the ruler says after the brochure has finished talking.

開發 open-launch: open-開 (frozen — its first appearance) + the launch-發 of M8's 출발하다 that M35's 발전하다 and M56's 발견하다 both decoded — to develop is to open ground and launch something on it. 신제품을 개발하다 (M43's 제품 note already ran 신제품), 앱을 개발하다 (M20's 앱); 개발자 = the developer, person-者 doing its usual job (riding frozen). And 재개발 was already in the building: M49's 지구 note zoned '재개발 지구', M50's 골목길 note warned of 'the 재개발 (redevelopment) crews' — receipt.

發達: the bare noun of M56's 발달하다, dismounting the way M57's 결정 did from 결정하다 — launch-arrive, standing alone. 기술의 발달 (M44), 과학의 발달 (M15), 언어 발달 (M26): capability, grown. Radar vs M57's 발전 (whose note warned 'Progress and electricity share a spelling') — M56 drew the line once and it holds: 'Skills 발달; skylines 발전.' A child's 언어 발달 is this word; a city's 경제 발전 is the other.

分析 divide-split: the divide-分 of M32's 부분 and M34's 분명하다 ('分明 divided-bright') + split-析 (frozen — an axe at a tree: 木 + 斤). To analyze is to divide until it's bright: 결과를 분석하다 (M32's 결과), 자료를 분석하다 (M44's 자료). The noun 분석 rides free — 데이터 분석 (데이터 riding frozen) on every job posting — and NIKL grades it C while the verb ranks B, which tells you where the frequency lives: in the doing.

觀察 view-inspect: the see-觀 of 관광 (M23) that M35's 습관 note pointed at ('관광's see-觀') + inspect-察 — the second syllable of M16's 경찰, never decoded until now: the police are the inspectors, and 察 rides frozen. To observe is to look with a notebook: 동물을 관찰하다 (M22's 동물), 아이의 행동을 관찰하다 (M57's 행동). The noun 관찰 rides free — 관찰 일기 (M48's 일기) is the bean-sprout diary every Korean schoolchild keeps. 보다 sees; 관찰하다 sees on purpose.

M32's 의미 ('the formal register of M10's 뜻') + 하다: to mean, to signify — the written verb. 무슨 의미예요? and 무슨 뜻이에요? both ask; only 의미하다 answers in print, in the bare -ㄴ다 form the quote machine (M32) already showed you inside -다고: 이 결과는 …을 의미한다. Speech says 뜻이에요; paper says 의미한다.

en: to be related; ~와 관련해서 = in relation to
notes: M56's 관련 + 하다, and like M56's 의하다 it barely conjugates: it lives as 관련해서 / 관련하여 = in relation to — M56's 관련 note already gave '[noun]와 관련해서 = in connection with'. Radar, all three in one line: 관련 is the noun (관련 기사), 관련하다 makes the frame (이 문제와 관련해서), and M61's 관련되다 is the passive twin that wears the badge ('~와 관련된'). Says 괄련 — the ㄴ bows to the ㄹ, a merge the bare noun has carried since M56 without saying so.

利用 benefit-use: the bare noun of M56's 이용하다 — and the SIGN word: 이용 안내 (안내 — guidance, riding frozen), 이용 시간 (M1's 시간), 이용료 (the fee-料 of M20's 무료). The M56 radar patrol holds: '사용 uses a thing, 이용 uses a service' — so M10's 사용하다 note put 사용 on the bathroom door (사용 중) and 이용 goes on the library door (이용 시간). Two nouns, two doors.

The 되다-row (M36) — the swap-the-하다 move — run on 이용: to be used, the way a service is. 많이 이용되다 / 널리 이용되다 (널리 — widely, riding frozen) is the phrase every statistic ends on: 이 앱은 학생들에게 많이 이용되고 있습니다 (M20's 앱). M61 graduated 사용되다 in the same row; the two are twins with the M56 line between them — 사용되다 for the thing, 이용되다 for the service. Formal furniture: read it everywhere, say it from a podium.

en: to make use of, utilize fully
notes: 活用 live-use: the live-活 of M57's 활동 and M29's 생활 + the use-用 of M10's 사용하다 — M63's 소용없다 note filed it as 'the use-用 inside M10's 사용하다'. The third use, and the ambitious one: 사용 uses, 이용 uses a service, 활용 makes the MOST of — 시간을 활용하다 (M1's 시간), 자료를 활용하다 (M44's 자료), 배운 것을 활용하다 = put what you learned to work. A thing 활용된 has been squeezed for everything it had; this app hopes to be.

M32's 변화 ('M26's 변하다 grown into a noun by -화') + 하다: the formal twin of M26's 변하다 — 변하다 speaks, 변화하다 prints, the register pair M56 modeled with 나다 and 발생하다. 세상이 변했어요 (M22's 세상) is what you say; 사회가 크게 변화했다 (M32's 사회) is what the textbook says about the same decades. Same change, one more syllable of paperwork.

擴大 widen-big: widen-擴 (frozen) + the big-大 of M48's 대중 ('대학교's (M15) big-大'). Two fingers on a screen: 사진을 확대하다 (M17's 사진) = zoom in; a boardroom: 사업을 확대하다 (M43's 사업) = expand the business. Radar vs M37's 늘리다 (make-grow — the volume knob: 시간을 늘려요): 늘리다 turns a quantity up; 확대하다 is the formal, two-dimensional one — it widens the whole frame. Its shrink-twin 축소하다 rides frozen for now.

en: to be enlarged, expand (on its own)
notes: The 되다-row again, and the news form: 범위가 확대되다 (범위 — scope, riding frozen) = the scope widens; 사업이 확대됐어요 = the business has expanded, nobody named as the widener. You 확대하다 a photo; a 문제 (M7) 확대되다-s on its own — which is why the pair is taught side by side: the same hanja, the agent removed.

連結 link-tie: link-連 (frozen — a chain of carts) + the tie-結 of M32's 결과 ('結果 tie-fruit'), the knot M56's 해결하다 note flagged as NOT its own 결. To connect is to link and tie: 인터넷에 연결하다 (M20's 인터넷), 선을 연결하다 (선 — a cord or line, riding frozen), 두 문제를 연결해서 생각하다. The tie-結 now runs three jobs: M25's 결혼하다 ties people, 결과 ties off effort, 연결 ties things to each other.

The everyday one, and the one your phone says first: 와이파이가 연결됐어요 (M20's 와이파이) = the wifi's connected; 연결이 안 돼요 = it won't connect — the modern 문이 안 열려요 (M36's 열리다 filed that panic). 되다-row (M36) by construction, but this member lives in speech as much as print, because the thing that connects itself is a machine, and machines get passive verbs even at dinner.

解決: the bare noun of M56's 해결하다 ('untie it AND rule on it'), standing alone the way this shelf's other nouns do. 문제 해결 (M7's 문제) = problem-solving, on every résumé; 해결 방법 (M32's 방법) = the fix; 해결이 안 돼요 = it isn't getting solved (M10's 되다 declining, 집중이 안 돼요-style). The knot metaphor holds: 해결 is the knot, untied and filed.

發見: the bare noun of M56's 발견하다 — launch-see, now a thing you can hold: 새로운 발견 (M35's 새롭다) = a new discovery; 대발견 (big-大 again) when the lab celebrates. M61's 발견되다 is the taught passive; today the noun completes the set — 발견하다 / 발견되다 / 발견. The wink: 발견 for what was already there (a 맛집 (M18), a planet), 발명 (invention — riding frozen) for what wasn't.

發生: the bare noun of M56's 발생하다 ('사고가 발생했습니다'). In print it stacks bare: 사고 발생 (M36's 사고) on the traffic board, 발생 원인 (원인 — cause, riding frozen) in the report, 화재 발생 시 (화재 — fire, riding frozen) on every stairwell placard. What M28's 나다 lets happen in conversation, 발생 files as a noun with a timestamp.

M63's 정확하다 on the -히 rack — and the pair rule, taught once, here: the -게 adverb (M33) is the live adverbializer any adjective can wear, -히 is the fossilized Sino one, and 하다-adjectives keep BOTH — 정확하게/정확히, 간단하게/간단히 — same meaning, -히 a shade more written. That note already ran '정확하게 = precisely (the -게 adverb, M33)'; today the shorter twin: 정확히 세 시에 = at three exactly (M5's 셋, clipped before its counter). The rack's lineage: 천천히/열심히 (M10), then M32's 특히, which M33's 조용히 note called 'the adverb factory from M32's 특히, now clearly a factory' — and today it runs at full capacity.

M63's 간단하다 ('Simple as in SHORT') on the rack: 간단히 말하면 = to put it briefly — the exact line that note ran as 간단하게 말하면, one syllable shorter and a shade more written, the pair rule in action. 간단히 설명해 주세요 (M24's 설명하다) = give me the short version; 간단히 먹었어요 (M1's 먹다) = grabbed a quick bite. Short, not shallow — the next entry measures the other axis.

M63's 단순하다 ('단순하다 measures complexity') on the rack, and the adverb tilts toward MERELY: 단순히 돈 문제가 아니에요 (돈 M9, 문제 M7) = it isn't simply a money problem — there is more than one moving part. 간단히 shortens the telling; 단순히 flattens the thing itself. Beside M62's 단지 (which deflates a whole clause), 단순히 argues: 'not just X' is its natural home.

M57's 특별 note already ran the word: 'And the adverb comes free: 특별히 = especially, particularly — the -히 of 천천히/열심히 (M10) on 특별, the aimed version of M32's 특히.' Receipt paid — and the radar drawn: 특히 spotlights a PART (that note's '특히 이 부분'), 특별히 does a THING specially — 특별히 준비했어요 (M8's 준비하다) = I made it just for you. One points, the other performs.

M24's 대단하다 ('대단해요! — impressive!') on the rack, and the adverb went formal: 대단히 감사합니다 (M1's 감사합니다) is the thank-you of speeches, ceremonies, and customer-service scripts — 'greatly' where speech says 정말. The adjective wows out loud; the adverb bows in print. Hear it at award podiums and airport announcements, and say it when the bow needs to be deep.

宏壯 vast-grand — both characters new today (굉장하다, the adjective, tremendous, rides frozen and glossed). The SPOKEN strong very: 굉장히 좋아요, 굉장히 커요 (M1's 크다). Calibrate: M11's 아주 is the neutral very, 너무 tips into excess, and M62's strong pair goes to print — '무척 feels; 몹시 suffers', that note said, and called both 'print-flavored' — while 굉장히 is the strong one Koreans actually say aloud, at the table, about the food.

仔細 (both characters new — 자세하다, detailed, rides frozen and glossed): in detail. 자세히 설명해 주세요 (M24's 설명하다) = walk me through it — the follow-up to 간단히's short version; 자세히 보세요 (M1's 보다) = look closely. Radar, one line: 자세 (posture — 姿勢, untaught) is a different word wearing the same two syllables; looking 자세히 improves nobody's 자세.

適當 suitable-fitting: the fit-適 that M64's 적용하다 decoded ('適 (fit)') + the fitting-當 of M34's 당연하다 ('當然 fitting-so'). Suited to the case, and not too much of it: 적당한 가격 (M21's 가격) = a reasonable price, 적당한 운동 (the 운동 of M8's 운동하다) = moderate exercise. Not a match on the nose — that was M63's 알맞다 — but the right size: where 알맞다 fits, 적당하다 suffices. Its adverb is next door.

적당하다 through the rack: in moderation, to taste — 적당히 넣으세요 (M28's 넣다) is the recipe's shrug: add what seems right. And the national idiom: 적당히 해 = take it easy / don't overdo it — said to the workaholic, and with a colder face to the slacker (that's enough of that). Sometimes 적당히 is the whole philosophy: enough, not more.

Native, no hanja to decode (꾸준하다, steady, rides frozen): without letting up. 꾸준히 공부하다 (M1's 공부하다) — the study adverb beside M10's 열심히, which is literally 'with a burning heart': 열심히 burns, 꾸준히 lasts. Coaches, doctors, and language apps all prescribe it — 꾸준히 하세요 — because M62's 조금씩 only works if this word shows up every day.

偶然 by-chance: a chance-偶 (new) + the so-然 of M34's 당연하다 ('當然 fitting-so') — the same 然 inside M22's 자연, which shipped without a decode: 自然 = self-so, nature as what is so by itself (M44's 자료 note had already filed 'the self-自 of 자신/자연/자유'). 우연히 만났어요 (M2's 만나다) = ran into each other. Radar vs M62's 마침 ('Lucky timing'): 우연히 is chance, 마침 is chance that helped. The noun rides free — 우연이에요 = it's a coincidence.

M12's 편하다 ('편해요. 편의점 (M6) is literally the 편-store') on the rack: 편히 쉬세요 (M8's 쉬다) = rest easy, 편히 앉으세요 (M9's 앉다) = make yourself comfortable. And the goodnight up the ladder: 편히 주무세요 — M47's 주무시다, whose note pairs it with 안녕히 주무세요. 편히 wishes comfort where 안녕히 wishes peace; both go to the elder in the room.

M7's 깨끗하다 + -이, NOT -히: the spelling rule. After a ㅅ-final 하다-stem the adverb is written -이 (깨끗이; 따뜻이 from M7's 따뜻하다), because that is what the mouth says — 깨끄시. M62 named the native line 'The -이 press'; 깨끗이 is the 하다-adjective adverb that defected to it. 깨끗이 치우세요 (M54's 치우다) = clear it away properly; 깨끗이 잊었어요 (M15's 잊다) = forgot it clean, wiped.

굳다 (to harden — untaught, riding frozen) + -이: hardened-ly = insistently, 'if you must.' 굳이 왜? (M10's 왜) = why bother?; 굳이 안 가도 돼요 (-아/어도 from M39, on the -(으)면 돼요 lineage from M23) = you don't HAVE to go. Said 구지 — ㄷ+이 → 지, the same rule M9's 같이 note filed: 'Pronounced 가치 — a sound-change bonus (ㅌ+이 → 치)'. The one-word retort 굳이? is in the gap deck.

The rung M9's 더 ('더 주세요 — more, please. Later it builds comparisons') never had: LESS. 덜 맵게 해 주세요 (M3's 맵다, the -게 adverb from M33, the do-for-me machine from M9) = make it less spicy — THE restaurant sentence; 덜 익었어요 (M40's 익다: '고기가 다 익었어요 = the meat's ready') = undercooked. Radar: the 덜덜 in M41's 떨다 note ('추워서 덜덜 떨었어요') is a shiver sound, not this word.

The spoken really: 되게 맛있어 (M1's 맛있다) — M10's 되다 wearing the -게 shape from M33, frozen into an intensifier. Register is the whole lesson: 반말-flavored, friends-only — 되게 좋아, 되게 커; M11's 아주 is the neutral very, M29's 매우 'The textbook's very'. Hear it in every café conversation; write it in none of your essays.

Quite — with raised eyebrows: 제법 잘하네요 (M17's 잘하다, -네요 from M26 noticing live) = not bad at all! Calibrate against M62's 꽤 ('The understatement professional'): 꽤 measures a notch, 제법 is surprised by it — praise that admits it expected less. Aimed at a junior's work it is a compliment; aimed at the weather (제법 춥네요, M11's 춥다) it is early winter.

Negative-polarity, like its siblings: 그다지 안 좋아요, 그다지 재미있지 않았어요 (M7's 재미있다). M62's 그리 note drew the line — '별로 shrugs, 그리 measures' — and M17's 별로 is 'The politest possible shrug'; 그다지 is 그리's fuller, more spoken form. Three not-thats: 별로 shrugs, 그리 measures, 그다지 says the measurement out loud.

比較 compare-compare — M56's 비교하다 said it: 'both characters mean it'. The noun stands alone today: 비교가 안 돼요 = no comparison (M10's 되다, declining); 가격 비교 (M21's 가격) = price comparison, the tab every shopper opens. 다른 사람과 비교 — the habit that note advised against — is a noun now, which does not make it healthier.

Pays M56's wink: its 비교하다 note ended 'Wink: 비교적 = comparatively' and called the badge 'one badge early'. Today it lands, off the -적 factory (M45): 비교적 싸요 (M7's 싸다) = relatively cheap, 비교적 쉬운 문제 (M7's 쉽다 and 문제) = a relatively easy problem. NIKL files it as an adverb — the one -적 word that stopped badging nouns and started modifying whatever follows.

The click of something fitting: 딱 맞아요 (M15's 맞다) = fits perfectly, 딱 하나 (M5's 하나) = just one, 딱 좋아요 = just right. NIKL files the OTHER two: a spread sense — 어깨가 딱 벌어지다 (M14's 어깨, M61's 벌어지다, whose note filed 'Second sense, gaps' and 'seams, teeth, and friendships all widen with it') = broad-shouldered — and a halt sense, 딱 멈추다 (M50's 멈추다) = stop dead. Radar: M60's 딱딱하다 ('Hard-and-stiff') is the mimetic knuckle-rap; single 딱 is the snap of a lid closing on the right box. The gap deck has 딱이에요.

Fully decodable: M10's 곧 ('곧 도착해요') + M28's 바로 ('바로 옆에', '바로 지금') fused — straight away, no detour: 곧바로 집에 갔어요 (M1's 집) = went straight home. Two immediacy words welded into one emphatic one; the ladder it sits on is in the next entry.

卽時 that-very-hour: the 즉 of S2's restater (its note: 'a verbal colon') + the o'clock 시 of M5 ('The word 시간 you know is this 시 + 간'). The SIGN and rulebook register — 즉시 연락하세요 (M19's 연락하다) is what the notice says; a friend would say 바로. The ladder: 바로 (M28, spoken) / 곧바로 (spoken, emphatic) / 즉시 (printed). NIKL files it as a noun — 즉시 배송 (immediate delivery; 배송 riding frozen) — which is how it stacks onto other nouns on the sign.

en: all at once, in one go
notes: 한 (M5's 하나 — 'Before a counter it contracts: 한') + 꺼번 (a fossil meaning one-go, surviving only here) + 에: in-one-go. 한꺼번에 하지 마세요 (-지 마세요 from M14) = don't do it all at once; 한꺼번에 다 먹었어요 (M9's 다) = ate it all in one sitting. Radar vs M28's 한번 ('one-time'; '한번 해 보세요'): one TIME vs one GO — 한번 counts the attempt, 한꺼번에 counts the batch.

The adverb that fronts M30's 만 ('하나만 — just one; 너만 — only you') and M55's 뿐 ('너뿐이야 = it's only you'): 오직 너만, 오직 하나뿐 — the particle says only, 오직 says it first and louder. The ballad's only, and the sign's: 오직 회원만 (M58's 회원) = members only. Where 만 picks the item, 오직 clears the rest of the table before picking.

乃至 (both characters new): the range word on forms — 3 내지 5명 (M5's 명) = three to five; also 'or' in legalese (A 내지 B). Written only — out loud, say 에서 … 까지. Radar, a homograph trap: the 내지 in M34's 짜증 note ('짜증 내지 마세요') is M28's 내다 + -지 마세요 — a verb mid-negation, not this word.

各自 each-self: M55's 각 ('the written-notice determiner') + the self-自 of M32's 자기 ('自己 self'). 각자 계산해요 (M9's 계산하다) = everyone pays their own — the Dutch-pay line, beside M62's 따로 (whose note ran 따로따로 계산해 주세요). NIKL files it as noun and adverb, both free: 각자의 방 (M8's 방) = each one's room; 각자 준비하세요 = each of you, get ready. The gap deck runs it into a four-character survival idiom.

en: all of it, the whole; entirely
notes: 全部 all-part: the all-全 of M31's 전국 (which M39's 전혀 note also credits to M31) + the part-部 of M32's 부분 ('部分 section-portion') — every part = the whole. 전부 얼마예요? = how much for all of it — M29's 모두 note asked '모두 얼마예요?'; the trio in one line: 다 (M9, native, 'Sits right before the verb') / 모두 (M29, 'counts the crowd') / 전부 (totals the bill). 전부 다, doubled, is normal speech; NIKL files it as noun and adverb, both yours.

Pays M38's 매년 note word for word: '매년 = 해마다, same promise, different register'. M11's 해 (its note: year, as in 새해) + M31's 마다 — the native every-year, where 매년 is the Sino one. The rail is open: 날마다 (which the 마다 note already ran), 달마다 (M16's 달), 주말마다 (M2's 주말). 해마다 여름이 더 길어져요 (M11's 여름, M7's 길다) = every year the summer runs longer — -아/어지다 from M35 on an annual timer.

The stretch, felt from inside — it follows its span: 여름 내내 (M11's 여름) = all summer long, 하루 내내 = all day, 회의 내내 (M10's 회의) = the entire meeting. Beside M38's 종일 ('usually as 하루 종일'): 종일 is the unit, 내내 is the duration you sat through — 내내 기다렸어요 (M8's 기다리다) = waited the whole time. Doubled syllable, undoubled patience.

Fully decodable: M29's 또 + M10's 다시, fused — and M29's 또 note already sorted the halves: 'M10's 다시 is redo-again; 또 is once-more-again.' Together they are the narrator's yet-again: 또다시 실패했어요 (M44's 실패) — the third act's opening line. In speech 또 alone does the work; 또다시 is for stories and sighs.

M10's 오래 ('오래 기다렸어요? — did you wait long?') + -도록, an ending meaning 'until / so that' (untaught glue, riding frozen here — read it as 'to the point of'): for a long, long time. 오래도록 기억할게요 (M19's 기억하다) = I'll remember this for a long time — a toast and a farewell in one. The 오래 family assembles: 오래 (M10) / 오랜만 (M19) / 오랫동안 (M46) / 오래도록 / and the determiner next door.

The determiner: 오랜 친구 (M1's 친구) = an old friend — NOT 늙은 (M35's 늙다 is aging; 오랜 is duration), 오랜 시간 = a long time. M19's 오랜만 note said 'M10's 오래 grew a suffix and became a greeting' — the suffix was this: 오랜 + 만, a long-gap all along; M46's 오랫동안 is the sibling that 'measures the stretch itself'. Shelved with M46's 옛 and M13's 새 — the words that only live in front of a noun.

M28's 생기다 — 'Things sprout: 문제가 생겼어요' — in its -어 coat + M28's 나다, the eruption door M67 sent the feelings through, welded: come-into-being-and-OUT. The first weld on the shelf and the rule for all of them: two owned verbs, the first wearing -아/어, fused into one dictionary word that conjugates on its tail (생겨나요, 생겨났어요). Radar: 생기다 is the casual arising — a problem, a girlfriend; 생겨나다 is the chronicled emergence — 새로운 문제가 생겨났어요 (M35's 새롭다, badged) is how the news and the history book say it, never the group chat.

en: to grow up, sprout up (a generation, a seedling)
notes: M35's 자라다 — 'Children 자라요; so do plants, cities, and rumors' — plus the same 나다-door: grow-up-and-OUT, the sprout pushing into view. Wearing the -는 badge (M24) it is the newspaper's favorite phrase: 자라나는 아이들 (M4's 아이, pluralized) = the growing generation. Radar: 자라다 for one biography (서울에서 자랐어요); 자라나다 when a whole cohort, or a seedling, is being watched come up.

en: to become known, get around (a rumor)
notes: M24's 소문 — 'Things-heard' that 'travels faster than 뉴스' — + 나다: the rumor erupts and the thing becomes known. The first noun + verb weld today: 소문이 나다 spaced is the event; fused, 소문나다 is a verb you can badge — 소문난 맛집, on the sign of every restaurant that ever had a line, is M18's 맛집 ('the place worth the pilgrimage and the line') with its reputation pre-attached. 소문났어요 = word got out; 동네에서 소문난 집 — M22's 동네 — = the house the whole neighborhood talks about.

en: to find out, dig up, track down
notes: M6's 찾다 — its note admitted 'One verb covers both the searching and the finding' — in its -아 coat + M28's 내다, the put-it-out verb ('시간을 내다 — MAKE time'): search, then FORCE the find out into the open. 찾아내다 is the finding half alone, with the effort showing: 답을 찾아냈어요 (M15's 답) = I dug up the answer; 방법을 찾아내다 (M32's 방법) = to work out a way. The 내다-rail carries a sibling too: 알아내다 (find out — riding frozen) is M4's 알다 + 내다, knowledge forced out the same door.

M28's 잠 ('잠이 들다 — you fall IN') + M28's 들다 ('sleep is entered (잠이 들어요)'), welded shut: the moment of crossing. The M41 sentence 눈을 감자마자 잠이 들었어요 spaced the two; today the dictionary fuses them — 아기가 잠들었어요 (M25's 아기) = the baby's asleep, the sentence every parent whispers. The sleep shelf assembles here: M1's 자다 is the state, 잠 the noun, 잠들다 the crossing, and 졸다 (below) the crossing attempted and lost. ㄹ-verb: 잠듭니다, 잠드는 badge.

M35's 흐르다 — 'Water, time, tears, music — Korean lets them all 흐르다' — in its 르-family coat (흘러, per the table M7 hung) + M1's 가다, on the [action] + 가다 rail M28 laid down for 들어가다 and 걸어가다: flow-AWAY. 시간이 흘러가요 = time flows on past you; 물이 흘러가요 (M1's 물) = the water runs off downstream. Radar, three flows: 흐르다 flows in place, 흘러가다 flows past and is gone, and M66's 흘리다 ('The run-out spill verb') is the flow with a clumsy hand behind it. Conjugates on the 가다 end: 흘러가요, 흘러갔어요.

M36's 넘다 ('To go over: 산을 넘다') + a -치다 that is NOT M17's 치다 ('The strike-play verb'): here 치다 is a tail meaning with force, and over-with-force = overflow. 물이 넘쳐요 = the water's spilling over the rim; 자신감이 넘쳐요 (M39's 자신감) = brimming with confidence — one verb reviews the cup and the person. 합치다, next, wears the same tail. Says 넘쳐요, 넘쳤어요 — the ㅊ runs straight into the vowel.

合 — the fit-合 of M44's 합격, the one M57's 종합 note re-used — + the same with-force 치다: fit-together-hard = to combine, merge. 두 반을 합쳤어요 (M15's 반, the homeroom) = they merged two classes; 힘을 합치다 (M14's 힘) = to join forces, the sports-day phrase. Radar, three ways of putting together: 더하다 (next) adds, arithmetic-style; 합치다 merges, two become one; M17's 모으다 collects, many into a pile.

en: to add; to be worse, more so
notes: M9's 더 ('더 주세요 — more, please') + M1's 하다, welded: do-more = to add. 2 더하기 3 = two plus three — 더하기, riding free, is what the plus sign says out loud — and 소금을 더하다 (M3's 소금) adds salt. Then the second life, pure adverb logic: 더하다 = to be even more so, usually worse — 겨울에는 더해요 (M11's 겨울) = in winter it's worse still; 밤에는 더해요 (M8's 밤) = at night, worse again. An adverb + 하다 weld readable both ways is the shelf's whole lesson in one word.

M10's 잘 + M4's 살다, fused — and the space is the meaning. 잘 살아요 spaced = lives well, a life going fine; 잘살아요 fused = is rich: 잘사는 나라 (M23's 나라, wearing the -는 badge from M24) = a wealthy country, 잘사는 집 = a family with money. The same trick M63's 잘못 note filed ('Spacing radar: 잘 못 해요 pleads inability; 잘못했어요 admits guilt') and M41's 잘생기다 ran on faces ('잘 (M10) + 생기다 = came-out-well'). The 잘-welds are a family — 잘살다, 잘생기다, 잘못: close the gap and a new word appears. Opposites: 못살다 (poor — riding free) and M43's 가난하다.

M8's 밤 + M8's 늦다, welded into one adjective that lives ninety percent of its life as an adverb: 밤늦게 (the -게 adverbializer from M33) = late at night — 밤늦게까지 공부했어요 (까지 from M6, M1's 공부하다) = I studied until late at night. The badge form 밤늦은 시간 (M1's 시간) = a late hour is the other ten percent. Radar vs M38's 밤새다: 밤늦다 is late IN the night; 밤새다 is all the way through it to dawn.

M1's 없다 + 애: the odd sixth causative. The causative party (M37) taught 이/히/리/기 and the recruit 우; 애 is a one-off that makes 없다 transitive — make-not-exist = get rid of: 냄새를 없애다 (M41's 냄새), 스트레스를 없애다 (M14's 스트레스), and 없애 버렸어요 with -아/어 버리다 from M52 = gone for good. Radar vs M61's 없어지다 ('just stops being where you left it'): 없어지다 happens on its own, 없애다 is done by someone — the happen-form and the do-form, the split M35's 이루어지다 note named. Says 업쌔다; the ㅅ jumps forward onto the 애.

The stop-by verb, 르-family per the table M7 hung: 들러요, 들렀어요, 들를게요. 편의점에 들렀어요 (M6's 편의점) = I stopped by the convenience store; 잠깐 들를게요 (M28's 잠깐) = I'll drop in for a minute — the whole verb is detours. Two radars, both real: M28's 들다 (enter, hold, cost) is the stem it looks like but isn't, and M36's 들리다 ('to be heard') conjugates to 들려요 — one vowel from 들러요. Say them side by side: 들려요 (I can hear it) / 들러요 (I'm stopping by).

To nod off where you sit — the head dropping, the jerk back up, the losing fight: 수업 시간에 졸았어요 (M10's 수업) = I dozed in class. ㄹ-verb: 졸아요, 좁니다, 조는 badge. Its adjective 졸리다 (sleepy — riding frozen) is the sentence everyone actually says: 졸려요 = I'm sleepy. Radar on the sleep shelf: 잠들다 crosses over; 졸다 fights and loses — the gap deck (M70) already poured the drowsiness on you as 잠이 쏟아지다.

M54's 빨래 note left an IOU — 'frozen inside rides 빨다, the wash-clothes verb, untaught and waiting in the pool' — paid today: 옷을 빨다 (M7's 옷) = to wash clothes, 손으로 빨았어요 (M8's 손) = washed by hand. ㄹ-verb: 빨아요, 빱니다, 빤 badge. Register: M8's 빨래하다 is the chore as a whole; 빨다 is the verb your hands do to the actual garment. NIKL files a second, C-grade 빨다 in the same spelling: 젖을 빨다 = to suck (젖, milk — frozen), the 빨 inside 빨대, the straw, literally the suck-stick — a wink, not a lesson.

便利 convenient-benefit: the 편 of M12's 편하다 ('편의점 (M6) is literally the 편-store') + the benefit-利 of M56's 이용하다 ('利用 benefit-use'). For sixty modules 편하다 has held two jobs — the sofa is comfortable AND the app is convenient; M42's 편안하다 split off at-ease ('편하다 says the sofa is comfortable; 편안하다 says YOU are at peace'), and today the other side splits: 편리하다 is convenient ONLY, and only of things and services — 교통이 편리해요 (M12's 교통), 편리한 앱 (M20's 앱) — never of a person's feelings. Says 펼리하다: ㄴ + ㄹ slides to ㄹㄹ, the way M25's 설날 says 설랄.

不便: the 불- ledger M42's 불만 note told you to keep ('불가능, 불편, 불안, 불만 — file the prefix, it keeps paying') and M67's 불행하다 note re-ran — 불편 finally lands as its own word. Three jobs: uncomfortable (신발이 불편해요 — M9's 신발), inconvenient (교통이 불편해요), and socially awkward — 불편한 자리 (M12's 자리) = a gathering you'd rather leave, 마음이 불편해요 (M19's 마음) = it doesn't sit right with me. The sign register 몸이 불편하신 분 — M14's 몸, and 분, the honorific person, riding frozen — is the public euphemism for persons with disabilities. The three-way split in one line: 편리하다 for things, 편안하다 for people, 불편하다 negates both.

華麗 flowery-beautiful: 華, splendor, on its first appearance + 麗, the beautiful-麗 of 高麗 Goryeo, which M61's 고려하다 note filed as the dynasty that gave Korea its name — so the country is called high-and-beautiful, and this adjective is half of it. 화려한 무대 (M51's 무대, 'the raised floor performance happens on') is what every K-pop review says; 화려한 옷 (M7's 옷) is what your aunt says with an eyebrow. The dig is real: 화려한 싱글 (싱글 — Konglish single, frozen) = the flashy bachelor life, said half in envy.

Cute — small, charming, and asking to be picked up. ㅂ-irregular per the table M7 hung (ㅂ → 워): 귀여워요, 귀여운 badge. Radar vs M1's 예쁘다: 예쁘다 is pretty, a verdict on beauty; 귀엽다 is small-and-charming — M22's 강아지 (its note: 'Also a term of endearment for children'), M25's 아기, and boyfriends being silly all get 귀여워. The aegyo adjective: 귀여운 척 (척 — pretending, frozen) is the performance, and the gap deck (M28) already measured the maximum with 눈에 넣어도 안 아프다.

en: to be full (to the brim), filled with
notes: M62's 가득 ('Brimful — a container meeting its limit') + 하다: the STATE adjective, where 가득 차다 — the 'full (가득 차다)' M66's 차다 note listed among its four — is the event of filling. 사랑이 가득한 집 (사랑, the noun inside M7's 사랑하다; M1's 집) = a house full of love; 눈물이 가득했어요 (M14's 눈물) = eyes brimming. An adjective, so it badges as 가득한; the bare adverb 가득 stays in front of verbs — 가득 채웠어요 (M37's 채우다) is you doing the filling.

Spirited, plucky — the kindergarten virtue: 씩씩한 아이 (M4's 아이) marches in and says hello loudly; 씩씩하게 대답하다 (M10's 대답하다 with the -게 adverbializer from M33) = to answer up boldly. A mimetic in the mold M71's 깜빡 note named — 'the same sound-as-shape mold as M54's 튼튼하다 and M60's 딱딱하다' — and you can hear the shoulders squared in 씩씩. Radar vs 용감하다 (brave — riding frozen): 용감하다 is courage under real danger; 씩씩하다 is pep and bearing, the bright step. It stands beside 튼튼하다 in every kindergarten song: sturdy body, bright spirit.

The root M21's 멋있다 note pre-split — '멋 (style/flair) + 있다: style-exists' — landing alone: flair, the quality itself. 멋을 부리다 (부리다 — to put on, act out; frozen) = to dress up, put on style; 멋을 내다 (M28's 내다, the put-it-out verb) = to make yourself look sharp — style, put forth. Its adjective twin 멋지다 (splendid — riding frozen) does what 멋있다 does with more voltage: 멋져요! Radar: M18's 맛 is what food has; 멋 is what people have — one vowel apart, and Korean keeps both on the sign.

M19's 거짓말 note pre-split this one too — '거짓 (false) + 말 (speech): false-speech' — and now the root stands: falsehood itself, no speech required. 거짓 정보 (M33's 정보) = false information, the fact-check word; 거짓이에요 = it's false; 거짓으로 = falsely. Print uses the root; the mouth says 거짓말. Radar: M24's 사실 is a fact, 거짓 is its shadow; the formal pair is 진실 (truth — riding frozen) / 거짓. Says 거짇, the ㅅ neutralizing at the end.

The -짜 family, named once: 진짜 (M11) / 가짜 / 공짜 — real, fake, free. 짜 is a native tail meaning roughly the-thing-itself; the heads are 眞 true and 假 false, both hanja on their first appearance — M11's 진짜 note never X-rayed its 진. 가짜 뉴스 (M24's 뉴스) = fake news, the phrase that needed no translation; 가짜 명품 (명품 — luxury goods, which the gap deck (M21) filed) = a knockoff. Radar: 거짓 (above) is falsehood as a claim; 가짜 is the fake as an object — 가짜 뉴스 is a thing, 거짓 정보 is a statement.

空 empty — the sky-空 that M43's 공장 note filed inside 공항 (M12) and M50's 공간 read as 'empty-between' — + the -짜 tail: the empty-thing, nothing paid. 공짜로 받았어요 (M9's 받다) = I got it for free; 공짜 밥 (M1's 밥) = a free meal. Radar vs M20's 무료 ('Fee-less. Opposite: 유료, with-fee'): 무료 is the sign on the door, 공짜 is the grin on your face — the same fact in the shop's register and yours. The gap deck files the proverb Koreans tell each other about loving it too much.

Everyone who isn't 우리 (M4): others, strangers, other people's. 남의 일 (the work-일 inside M2's 일하다) = someone else's business; 남 앞에서 (M6's 앞) = in front of others; 남 이야기 (M24's 이야기) = gossip, other-people talk; 남남 = two people who are nothing to each other. Radar, because NIKL stacks three 남s on this spelling: not the 男 of M4's 남자, not the 南 of M27's 남쪽 (the compass south M31's 남산 sits on) — this 남 is native, and it means not-us. The gap deck files the rice cake in the other person's hand; its sibling 그림의 떡 has hung there since M30.

en: an errand, business to see to
notes: M1's 보다 wearing the future badge -(으)ㄹ (M24) + the work-일 inside M2's 일하다: a thing-to-see-to. 볼일이 있어요 = I've got something to take care of — the polite exit line that ends any conversation without giving a reason; 볼일 다 봤어요 = all done, errands run. Said 볼릴: the ㄴ that wedges into M67's 큰일 (said 큰닐) wedges in here too, then slides to ㄹ behind the ㄹ, exactly as M25's 설날 says 설랄. Mandatory wink, filed in the gap deck: 볼일(을) 보다 also means to use the restroom.

M1's 밥 + M18's 맛 ('The noun hiding inside 맛있다'): the taste of rice = your appetite. 밥맛이 없어요 = no appetite, the sick-day sentence — with 입맛, the near-twin S2's 당기다 note pulled on (입맛이 당기다), riding frozen beside it. Then the register landmine, handled the way M71's 새끼 was: 밥맛이야 / 밥맛 없어 in 반말, aimed at a person, = you're gross, you turn my stomach — an insult, never a food review. Say 밤맏 (rom bammat), the ㅂ nasalizing before ㅁ; say it about lunch, and never AT anyone across a table.

M57's 행동 ('going-and-moving = how you act') + 하다: to act, to behave. That note already ran 행동으로 보여 주세요; today the noun mounts its verb — 행동하기 전에 생각하세요 = think before you act, the classroom proverb, built from M10's 생각하다 with the -기 nominalizer (M13) and 전에 from M13; 빨리 행동하다 = act fast. The hinge's first rule, live: 행동 is an ACTION noun, so 하다 mounts it — M24's 관심 is a STATE, so it stays on 있다 (관심이 있어요, never 관심하다).

en: to live one's daily life, to get by
notes: M29's 생활 ('life as it's actually lived. 한국 생활이 어때요?') + 하다: to run a life day to day — 혼자 (M10) 생활해요, M23's 외국 + 에서 생활하다. Radar vs M4's 살다: 살다 dwells (that note: '한국에 살아요'), 생활하다 runs a life — rent, meals, routines. 살다 answers where; 생활하다 answers how. The 활 is the live-活 that M72's 활용하다 note traced ('the live-活 of M57's 활동 and M29's 생활').

M53's 치료 ('治療 govern-heal') + 하다 — and that note already assigned the verb: 'The verb 치료하다 belongs to the one in the white coat.' M4's 의사 + M27's 환자 + 을: 의사가 환자를 치료하다 — the doctor does it; the patient 치료를 받다, because the same note ruled treatment 'is received' (M9's 받다 — the one M53's 수술 note put 'in scrubs'). One noun, two seats: 치료하다 for the coat, 치료를 받다 for the gown. Wounds too: M36's 상처 + 를 치료하다.

en: to be hospitalized, to be admitted
notes: M53's 입원 ('入院 enter-the-institution') + 하다 — receipt: that note already ran '입원하다 = to be admitted, and Korea admits lightly'. Its bookend rides on the same page — '퇴원하다 = to be discharged' (M53's 퇴원). The building takes 에, not 을: M6's 병원 + 에 입원하다 — you enter INTO it, like 입학하다 next door; M25's 지난주 + 에 입원했어요 stamps the date. The in-hospital STATE is 입원 중이에요 — S2's 중, the busy-sign that M52's 외출 note hung on 'a thousand doors' as 외출 중.

en: to enter a school, to be admitted
notes: M44's 입학 ('入學 enter-study') + 하다: M15's 대학교 + 에 입학했어요 — and the particle is 에, not 을: you enter INTO the school, through the enter-入 of M12's 입구. M44 said 'Its bookend is the next entry' (졸업), and the verb bookend has been yours since M15's 졸업하다 ('Said 조러파다'). Rom radar, and the house rule: the app files 졸업하다 as joreopada, the merge written out, but 입학하다 keeps its letters — iphakhada — coda + ㅎ on the page, merged only in the mouth: say 이파카다. 입학식 — M44 named the March ceremony — is what the verb walks into.

M44's 복습 ('復習 again-practice') + 하다: to review — that note already wrote the teacher's line, '복습하세요 is every teacher's closing line', and this verb is what the app's review queue makes you do: 배운 것을 복습하다 = go over what you learned, M5's 매일 복습해요. M44 promised 'Its mirror is 예습' — so 예습하다 (豫習 — the beforehand-豫 that M52's 예약 note filed as '예상's beforehand-豫 (M34)') rides frozen: preview tomorrow, review today. The radar holds from M44: again-復, not M25's luck-福.

M26's 발음 ('Every rom in this app encodes it') + 하다: to pronounce. 발음하기 어려워요 — M7's 어렵다 on the -기 nominalizer (M13) — is the sentence every ㄹ and every 의 earns; 정확하게 발음하다 = pronounce precisely, M63's 정확하다 wearing the -게 adverb that note already filed ('정확하게 = precisely'). 發音 launch-sound: the launch-發 that M44's 발표 note ran ('발음 M26 launches sound') + the sound-音 inside M2's 음악. The noun takes the compliment (발음이 좋네요!); the verb takes the work.

M8's 계획 ('주말 계획 — weekend plans') + 하다: to plan — M11's 여행 + 을 계획하다, and, in print, M32's 정부 + 가 …을 계획하고 있다. 計劃 count-scheme: the count-計 of M43's 계산기 ('計算器 count-machine') + 劃 (frozen — a stroke drawn out). But speech keeps the noun bare and reaches for a Ring 1 verb: 계획을 세우다 — M12's 세우다, taught as the taxi's '세워 주세요 — please pull over', doing its literal make-STAND job on a plan. Both live: 계획하다 in the report, 계획을 세우다 at the table — and M38's 미리 belongs in front of either.

M43's 수입 taught 'TWO words in one spelling' — '輸入 ship-IN' and '收入 gather-in: income' — and the verb belongs to ship-in ONLY: M1's 커피 + 를 수입하다, 수입 맥주 (that note's well-traveled M3's 맥주). Income never conjugates: it is 수입을 얻다 (M35's 얻다) or 수입이 늘다 (M35's 늘다), never 수입하다 — say 수입했어요 and you have imported something, not earned it. NIKL keeps the two as separate rows; the hinge sorts them for you — only an ACTION noun mounts, and gathering-in income is a state of your account.

M43's 수출 ('輸出 ship-out') + 하다 — receipt: that note already ran the verb, '수출하다 sends the semiconductors, cars, and dramas abroad'. M50's 자동차 + 를 수출하다; 반도체 (semiconductor — riding frozen) + 를 수출하다 is the sentence the news repeats monthly. With 수입하다 above you hold M43's 무역 as two verbs: 수입 buys the world in, 수출 sends Korea out. Radar filed ahead: goods 수출, companies 진출 — three entries from the end.

en: to win the championship, take the title
notes: M51's 우승 ('優勝 excel-win') + 하다 — receipt: that note already said '우승하다 = to take the title' and drew the line against M17's 이기다 ('우리 팀이 이겼어요!'): 'you 이기다 six times and 우승 once'. The particle keeps them apart too: M51's 대회 + 에서 우승하다 — the win happens IN the tournament — while 이기다 takes 을/를 for the opponent. 우승한 팀 (M16's 팀 under the badge from M24) lifts the 우승컵 M51 engraved.

en: to go out (from home, the ward, the office)
notes: M52's 외출 ('外出 outside-go') + 하다 — receipt: that note closed with '외출하다 to verb it.' 외출할 때 (-(으)ㄹ 때 from M25) 불을 끄세요 — M13's 불, M13's 끄다 — is the note by every door; 외출 준비 keeps the noun. The out-出 is the one M43's 수출 note decoded ('出 is the out-door of 출구') and this shelf's 진출 reuses. Radar vs M8's 나가다: 나가다 is any exit, 밖에 나가요; 외출하다 is leaving the house or the ward properly, shoes on, for a while.

M47's 이혼 ('離婚 part-marriage') + 하다 — receipt: '이혼하다 = to divorce', and that note set the register: 'a legal noun, not a melodrama'. Pair it with M25's 결혼하다: 결혼했어요 and 이혼했어요 are said in the same plain voice, and both take 하고 or M30's 와 for the other person. 이혼한 부모님 — the badge from M24 on M4's 부모님 — is the form on which the word most often appears, quietly, on a school form.

取消 take-and-erase: the bare noun of M52's 취소하다, whose note decoded it and named the button pair — 'Every Korean screen runs on the button pair 확인/취소'. Dismounted, it stacks: 예약 취소 with M52's 예약, 취소 문자 with M20's 문자 = the cancellation text, 취소 버튼 (버튼 — riding frozen). The move is the one M72 made: it dismounted 이용, 해결, and 발견 from the M56 verbs, and its 발달 note named the precedent — 'dismounting the way M57's 결정 did from 결정하다'. This shelf dismounts three; 취소 is the one on your phone.

歸國 return-country: the bare noun of M52's 귀국하다 ('歸國 return-country'). 귀국 후에 (후에 from M13) = after coming home; 귀국 날짜 (M25's 날짜) = the return date on the ticket; 귀국 준비 stacks the way 외출 준비 does. The 국 is the country-國 that note routed through M32's 국민. M52's 유학생 lives between two dates: 출국 (departure — riding frozen, the out-出 + 國) and 귀국.

複寫 double-write: the bare noun of M16's 복사하다, whose note ran '복사기 — the copy machine'. 複 (double) is frozen; 寫 is write — and it is the 사 inside M17's 사진 (寫眞, write-the-real: a photo is reality written down), a decode that note never gave, paid here as a first. 복사 한 장 (M30's 장 — '종이 한 장') = one copy; 복사해 주세요 at any counter. On the screen it pairs: 복사/붙여넣기 = copy/paste — M37's 붙이다 + M28's 넣다 fused into a menu item (riding frozen). Radar: this 복 is double-複, not the again-復 of M44's 복습 nor M25's luck-福 — the third 복.

en: to ignore; to look down on
notes: 無視 no-see: the nothing-無 of M20's 무료 ('무 (without)') and M39's 무조건 ('it doesn't negate, it EMPTIES') + the see-視 that M31's 시청 note surfaced as a homograph ('시청 (視聽) is also TV-watching') and M48's 시청자 decoded as 'watch-視'. To ignore — and to belittle: 무시하지 마세요 (-지 마세요 from M14) means both don't-ignore-me and don't-look-down-on-me, and Korean does not separate them — being unseen IS being disrespected. M38's 신호 + 를 무시하다 runs the red light. 무시 rides free.

批判 strike-judge: 批 (frozen — a hand delivering the verdict) + the judge-判 of M34's 판단 ('判斷 judge-cut'). To criticize with arguments: M32's 정부 + 를 비판하다; and its receiving side is M9's 받다 — 비판을 받다, criticism received the way M53's 치료 is. Radar, three 비s: M56's 비교하다 is 比 ('比較 compare-compare'), M11's 비 is rain, this 批 strikes. And 비판 (argued) is not 욕 (abuse — riding frozen, glossed). 비판 rides free; 비판적 사고 = critical thinking — the -적 badge (M45) on the think-사고 (思考) that M36's 사고 note set aside for 'philosophy books'.

en: to keep, store, hold for safekeeping
notes: 保管 keep-manage: the keep-保 of M43's 보험 ('保 is keeping-safe') + the manage-管 of M57's 관리 ('pipe-管 (control, as plumbing)'). To store, to hold in keeping: 냉장 보관 — M13's 냉장고 minus its warehouse-고 — is printed on every yogurt and on M2's 우유; M13's 짐 + 을 보관하다 at the hotel desk; 보관함 = the locker (함 — a box, riding frozen; M72's 사물 note ran 사물함 for the same box). Radar vs M40's 두다 ('두다 keeps custody'): 두다 is your own cupboard, 보관하다 is a service or a label. 보관 rides free.

訪問 visit-ask: 訪 (frozen — to seek someone out) + the ask-問 inside M10's 질문 (質問, quality-ask — that note gave no decode; here is its first). To visit, formally, and it takes 을/를: M2's 회사 + 를 방문하다, M58's 고객 + 을 방문하다, and M32's 대통령 + 이 M12's 부산 + 을 방문했습니다 — the news verb for a trip with a purpose. Casual visiting is M19's 놀다 on the errand-form -(으)러 from M12: 친구 집에 놀러 가다. Where M16's 다니다 takes 에, 방문하다 takes the object; the noun is next.

訪問: the noun of the verb above — 방문 전에 (전에 from M13), 방문 시간 with M1's 시간 on the clinic door, M46's 첫 + 방문 for the first one. NIKL's sense collapse is MANDATORY here, and it is a good one: 방문 also spells 房門, the room-door — M8's 방 + M6's 문, two words you already own: 방문을 닫다 (M13's 닫다), 방문을 두드리다 (M66's 두드리다). Two grade-B words, one spelling, and only the verb tells them apart: a 방문 you 하다 is a visit; a 방문 you 닫다 is a door.

en: to indicate, mark; to show (a feeling)
notes: 表示 surface-show: the surface-表 of M33's 표현 ('表現 surface-appear') that M44's 발표 note reused ('the 표 is 표현's surface-表 (M33)') and M34's 표정 wears + 示 (show — frozen). To indicate, to mark: M12's 지도 + 에 표시하다 = mark it on the map; M42's 감정 + 을 표시하다 = show a feeling, one register above 표현하다. NIKL's C-row 標示 (signpost-mark) is the label: M21's 가격 + 표시 on a price tag — same spelling, a different 표. So, three 표s: 表 surface (표현, 표정, this), 票 ticket (M12's 표), 標 signpost (the label). 표시 rides free, and it erupts: 표시가 나다 (M28's 나다) = it shows.

鑑賞 mirror-appreciate: 鑑 (frozen — the bronze mirror you inspect a thing in) + the prize-賞 that M40's 상 note filed ('the prize-상 (賞) that award shows hand out'). To appreciate, in the museum register: M2's 영화 + 를 감상하다 is watching a film the way a critic does; M15's 그림 + 을 감상하다 at M23's 미술관. M1's 보다 watches; 감상하다 watches with intent — the verb on the program, not the couch. The noun stands next.

鑑賞: the hobby noun on every form — 음악 감상 with M2's 음악, 영화 감상 with M2's 영화, listed beside M17's 독서 under M17's 취미. RADAR, mandatory and three-deep: 감상 (感想) = impressions, the thoughts after — 감상문 (riding frozen) is the reflection essay every Korean schoolchild owes after a field trip, with the feel-感 of M42's 감정; and 감상적 (感傷 — the wound-傷 of M36's 상처) = sentimental, wearing the -적 badge (M45). Three 감상s, one spelling; this module owns 鑑賞 — the one you can put on a résumé.

反復 flip-again: the flip-反 of M24's 반대 (that note glossed its 반 as 'flip') + the again-復 of M44's 복습 ('this 복 is again-復, not M25's luck-福') — fully decodable from two receipts, nothing frozen. To repeat: 같은 문장을 반복하다 with M33's 문장, 반복해서 듣다 with M2's 듣다 — the app's whole method in one verb. 반복 rides free: 반복 연습 (the 연습 inside M10's 연습하다) = drill, 반복 학습 (M44's 학습). Radar vs M29's 또: 또 is again, once more; 반복하다 is again as a machine.

en: to yield, give way, give up (a seat)
notes: 讓步 yield-a-step: 讓 (frozen — to let another go first) + 步 (a step — frozen). To yield: M12's 자리 ('자리 있어요?') + 를 양보하다 = give up your seat — THE sentence of M6's 지하철, and the reason the gap deck holds 노약자석; 길을 양보하다 = let someone pass. 양보 rides free: 양보 운전 (the 운전 inside M10's 운전하다) is painted on highway signs — yield-driving — and 양보 없는 사람 (M1's 없다 under the badge from M24) = someone who never gives an inch, said of toddlers and drivers alike.

節約 section-promise: M72's 에너지 note wrote the IOU — '에너지 절약 (절약 — saving, riding frozen)' — and today it pays. The 절 is a joint/section-節: the same 절 in M11's 계절 (季節, the year's sections) and M25's 명절 (名節, the named ones), neither decoded until now; the 약 is the promise-約 of M5's 약속 that M52's 예약 note filed as '약속's promise-約'. To economize is to promise yourself smaller portions: M1's 시간 + 을 절약하다, M9's 돈 + 을 절약하다, M36's 전기 + 를 절약하다. Radar vs M17's 모으다: 모으다 gathers money up, 절약하다 spends less of it. The native 아끼다 (to be sparing — riding frozen) is what a grandmother says; 절약하다 is what the light switch says. 절약 rides free.

en: a report (to the authorities); a declaration
notes: 申告 state-and-tell: the 申 of M64's 신청 ('申 (state)') + the tell-告 of M32's 광고 ('廣告 wide-tell') — to state it officially. A report to the authorities: M16's 경찰 + 에 신고하다, 112에 신고하세요 (Korea's police number — M2's 일, 일, 이); M36's 사고 + 신고, 분실 신고 (분실 — loss, riding frozen) at the lost-and-found; and the office kind, M43's 세금 + 신고 every May. 신고하다 rides free. Radar vs M64's 신청: 신청 asks for something; 신고 tells on something.

飜譯 flip-carry-over (both frozen — 飜 turns a page, 譯 carries the meaning across). Translation, the written kind: 번역하다 rides free (M1's 한국어 + M6's 로 번역하다), 번역 앱 (M20's 앱), and 번역기 = the translator app — the machine-기 of M13's 세탁기 ('the same 기 as 비행기') on a phone. Its spoken twin rides frozen: 통역 (通譯 — the through-通 of M12's 교통 that M44's 필통 note refused as '교통's through-通 (M12)') = interpreting: 번역 is the page, 통역 is the voice. Radar, a third 역: M6's 역 is the station (驛), M43's 무역 is trade (易 — 'this 역 is 易, not the subway's 역 (M6)'), 번역 carries (譯).

en: advance into, expansion (into a market, a field)
notes: 進出 advance-out: 進 (frozen — the advance in M61's 진행되다, '進行 advance-go') + the out-出 of M12's 출구 that M43's 수출 note decoded ('出 is the out-door of 출구'). Expansion into a new arena: 해외 진출 — M31's 해외, 'beyond-the-sea' — is what K-pop and 삼성전자 did (M72's 전자 note printed it 'on the back of half the world's phones'); 세계 시장 진출 with M23's 세계 and M3's 시장. 진출하다 rides free. Radar vs 수출: goods 수출, companies (and idols, and players) 진출 — 자동차를 수출하다, 해외에 진출하다.

解釋 untie-explain: the untie-解 of M56's 해결하다 ('untie it AND rule on it') + 釋 (frozen — to loosen, to explain). An interpretation: M8's 꿈 + 해석 = dream-reading; M33's 문장 + 해석 = parsing a sentence, the reading-class word one register above M24's 설명하다; 해석하다 rides free. NIKL's C-row 解析 = analysis, the mathematician's (M15's 수학) — same spelling, a different 석. Radar vs 번역: 번역 carries a text into another language; 해석 tells you what it meant in this one — you can 번역하다 a line and still fail to 해석하다 it.

en: to run counter to; (homograph) to fall for
notes: NIKL's B-row is 反하다 — to run counter to: M39's 규칙 + 에 반하다, M39's 법 + 에 반하다 — the verb behind M64's 위반 ('違 (go against) + 反 (turn back)'), and behind the frame every editorial needs: 이에 반해 = in contrast to this — M56's 한편 and 또한 finally get their contrast-sibling; the gap deck holds it. The flip-反 is M24's 반대. MANDATORY radar, and the one everyone knows: the homograph 반하다 = to fall for — 첫눈에 반했어요 = it was love at first sight, where the 눈 is M14's 눈 (the eye), not the first snow of M26's 첫눈 (whose note already ran 첫사랑). Same shape, opposite temperature: on paper you 반하다 a rule; in dramas you 반하다 a face. Taught last on purpose — the hinge's one 하다 that will not dismount: there is no bare 반 to stand alone.

M5's 넷 ('Before a counter: 네 — 네 명') in the 흘-family uniform: four days — and the shelf's first missing member, paid. M52's 사흘 note ended 'four days is 나흘, five 닷새 — the shelf's untaught tail', and the M52 md filed the same debt ('with 나흘 and 닷새 as the untaught tail'). 나흘 동안 (M28's 동안) 여행했어요 = traveled for four days; by the logic M52's 이틀 note ran ('The famous TV itinerary 1박 2일 (one night, two days) is 이틀 with a bed in the middle'), 3박 4일 is 나흘 with three beds. The family now reads 하루 (M8) · 이틀 (M52) · 사흘 (M52) · 나흘 · 닷새 (next) — then 엿새, 이레, 여드레, 아흐레 (six through nine, riding frozen; only calendars say them) — and 열흘 (M52: 'the shelf's roundest span').

M5's 다섯 + the family's day-syllable, welded and said 닫쌔 — the ㅅ shuts the first syllable and hardens the next. Five days: 닷새 동안 (M28's 동안) 비가 왔어요 (M11's 비) — five days of M11's 장마 in one sentence. With 나흘 above, the receipt M52's 사흘 note wrote ('four days is 나흘, five 닷새 — the shelf's untaught tail') is cleared: the native count runs 하루 (M8) · 이틀 (M52) · 사흘 (M52) · 나흘 · 닷새, every span a native trip. 닷새 만에 = after five days — that 만 is the after-a-gap 만 (untaught glue, riding frozen), not the only-만 of M30, so the deck keeps to 동안.

The before-前 that M46's 이전 set loose ('finally standing alone' — the 전 inside M5's 오전 and the 전에 from M13) + M11's 날: the day before — always before SOMETHING. 시험 전날 (M10's 시험) = the day before the exam, 결혼식 전날 (M25's 결혼식), 명절 전날 (M25's 명절) = the day the whole country is on the road. The 날-shelf now reads in order: 전날 / 그날 (M29) · 이날 (M46: 'It's newspaper anaphora') / 이튿날 (next) / 첫날 (M46) / 마지막 날 (M15's 마지막). Radar: 전날 is relative — the day before THAT; for the day before today you still say 어제 (M2).

이틀 (M52) + M11's 날 with the ㄹ swapped for ㄷ at the weld — the same ㄷ M18's 숟가락 wears ('Note the ㄷ batchim where 젓가락 has ㅅ'): 숟가락 is 술 (a spoonful, riding frozen) + 가락 through the identical swap, and the spelling rule behind both also writes 사흗날 and 섣달 (riding frozen). The next day, in STORY register: 이튿날 아침 (M2's 아침) = the next morning, the line every folktale turns on. Said 이튼날 — the ㄷ slides to ㄴ before ㄴ, the slide M25's 작년 note ran ('said 장년 — the nasal slide again'). Radar: 다음 날 (M8's 다음 + 날, two words) is the plain version you use for tomorrow's plans; 이튿날 belongs to narration and datelines.

M29's 그 ('Korean's closest thing to THE: 그 영화 — the movie we both mean') + M8's 다음 ('다음 주 (next week), 다음 역 (next station — listen for it on the subway)') welded into one dictionary word — the spacing interlude's rule that compounds 'weld solid' 'when they've fused into one concept'. 그다음에 = and then, after that — the storyteller's connective, and the listener's whole question: 그다음에 어떻게 됐어요? = and then what happened? 그다음 날 = the day after that, 그다음 주 = the week after. The 그-weld rail now runs 그때 (M25: 'the storyteller's pivot') · 그동안 (M29) · 그날 (M29) · 그다음 · 그해 (next).

그 + M11's 해 — the sun moonlighting as 'year', the job its note filed under 새해 and M25's 올해 note ran ('올 + M11's 해 — the year we're standing in'): THAT year, in narrative. 그해 여름 (M11's 여름) = that summer, 그해 겨울 (M11's 겨울) = that winter — how memoirs and news retrospectives set a scene, where speech would say 그때 (M25). The 2021 drama 그 해 우리는 spaced it for the poster; the dictionary welds it, and so does every anchor reading 그해 12월. A cousin of M46's 지난해 ('anchors say 지난해, the break room says 작년 (M25)') — one register up, one pointer back.

M2's 어제 + M8's 밤 with the linking ㅅ wedged between them — the wedge M40's 고춧가루 note filed and M46's 오랫동안 reused ('with the linking-ㅅ wedged in — the same wedge M40's 고춧가루 note filed'): last night, said 어제빰. 어젯밤 꿈 (M8's 꿈) = last night's dream, 어젯밤에 잠을 못 잤어요 (M28's 잠) = I couldn't sleep last night — the sentence M38's 늦잠 answers the next morning. Radar: 어제 저녁 (two words, M2's 저녁) is yesterday EVENING, the dinner hour; 어젯밤 is welded and late. Rom eojetbam — the ㅅ written as t at the weld, the way 고춧가루 became gochutgaru.

再昨年 again-last-year: 再 (again — a FIRST; no shipped note has decoded it, and it is neither the timber-材 of M40's 재료 nor the 재 inside M7's 재미있다 — three 재s on the radar now) + M25's 작년 ('The year that just left, said 장년 — the nasal slide again'). The year before last, said 재장년 — the same slide, one syllable deeper. The year ladder finally has both ends: 재작년 → 작년 (M25) → 올해 (M25) / 금년 (below) → 내년 (M25) → 내후년 (the year after next, riding frozen). 재작년 겨울 (M11's 겨울) = two winters ago; and the 再 returns wherever something happens again — 재방송 (a rerun) and 재시험 (a retake) ride frozen.

今年 now-year: the now-今 of M2's 지금 and M38's 금방 ('今方 — 방금 flipped, and looser') + M25's 년. This year, on paper — tax notices, forms, and the news say 금년 where the break room says M25's 올해, whose note shrugged 'no Sino version needed'; here it is, and it stays in print. Radar, MANDATORY: NOT the gold-金 of M5's 금요일 ('금 = metal/gold') and M60's 금 ('金 the metal itself, at last') — 今 and 金 are identical in Hangul, and only the neighbor tells them apart: 금년 counts, 금값 costs. Said as written — ㅁ before ㄴ has nothing to slide.

這番: M29's 저 ('The far pointer: 저 건물 — that building yonder') + M12's 번 ('Also counts times — 한 번 (once, native)'): the far turn = last time, SPOKEN — 저번에 = last time, 저번 주 = last week, 저번 달 = last month. It holds the slot M46's 지난번 holds one register up ('The 지난- prefix M25's 지난주 note promised would work the whole calendar (지난달, 지난번) — paid in full'), and M16's 이번 ('this-turn') is its partner: 이번 / 저번 / 다음번 (riding frozen). Hanja footnote: 這 means 'this' in Chinese and drifted to 'that one before' in Korean — a borrowed pointer that turned around on the crossing.

M10's 오래 ('오래 기다렸어요? — did you wait long?') + the before-前 that 전날 carries above: long-before = long ago. 오래전에 = a long time ago, 오래전부터 (부터 from M6) = since way back — 오래전부터 알았어요 = I've known for ages. The 오래 family M73's 오래도록 assembled ('오래 (M10) / 오랜만 (M19) / 오랫동안 (M46) / 오래도록 / and the determiner next door') gets its backward member, and the recent-past ladder M38's 아까 built ('방금 (seconds), 아까 (hours, same day), 어제 (M2)') runs on past the horizon: 아까 → 어제 → 저번에 → 오래전에 → 옛날에, where M24's 옛날 starts the folktales.

數年 several-years: the number-數 of M15's 수학 ('수 (number) + 학') doing its OTHER job — 'a number of' — + M25's 년. Several years, print register: 수년 전 = some years ago, 수년간 = over several years — the between-間 of M1's 시간 run as a span, the way M38's 기간 runs it ('期間 term-between'). Speech says 몇 년 (M5's 몇); the news says 수년. The same 數 scales up: 수십 년 = decades, 수백 명, 수천 개 (수십/수백/수천 — several tens, hundreds, thousands — riding frozen). 수년 is said as written; 수십 년 is said 수심 년, the ㅂ sliding before ㄴ.

M25's 때 ('The when-noun. Bare after events: 추석 때, 시험 때') welded onto M3's 점심 ('both the time and the meal'): around lunch — the fuzzy hour, not the slot. 점심때 전화할게요 = I'll call around lunch; 점심때가 됐어요 = it's about lunchtime. Radar: 점심시간 — M3's 점심 + M1's 시간 — is the SCHEDULED break, twelve to one on the office door; 점심때 is whenever the stomach says so — vague the way M46's 무렵 is ('때 pins a moment; 무렵 admits that dusk has no timestamp'), but everyday. And 아침때 does not exist: the morning is simply 아침에.

M2's 저녁 ('Same double duty as 아침: the time and the meal') + M25's 때: around evening, when the light goes and dinner starts being negotiated — 저녁때 봐요 = see you this evening, 저녁때 다시 전화하세요 (M8's 전화하다, M10's 다시) = call again around dinner. Its literary twin is 저녁 무렵 — M46's 무렵 note ran '저녁 무렵 (M2's 저녁, going amber)' — and 저녁때 is the same hour in slippers. The 때-welds stop here: 아침때 is not a word and 밤때 is not a word — the day's soft spots are lunch and dinner, the two hours a family actually bargains over.

M8's 밤 + S2's 중 ('중국's middle-中, hung after any noun'): the middle of the night — 밤중에 전화하지 마세요 (M20's 전화, -지 마세요 from M14) = don't call in the dead of night; 밤중에 깼어요 (M36's 깨다, the waking sense) = I woke in the night. 한밤중 (the dead of night, with 한 as 'peak') rides frozen and is the drama version. Radar vs M38's 새벽 ('in Korea it starts at midnight: 새벽 두 시 = 2 a.m.'): 새벽 is the clock's word, with hours attached; 밤중 is the feeling — dark, late, and nobody should be calling.

M8's 밤 + M28's 낮 ('The day's missing timeslot: 아침 → 점심 → 낮 → 저녁 → 밤, complete at last'): night-and-day — Korean puts the night first where English says day-and-night, and it means it: 밤낮으로 = around the clock, 밤낮없이 (M32's 없이 — '없다 + -이: without') = nonstop, no night, no day. The diagnosis everyone eventually receives: 밤낮이 바뀌다 (M35's 바뀌다) = your nights and days got switched — jet lag, night shifts, and the gamer's school break; the gap deck files it. M38's 종일 ('usually as 하루 종일') measures one day; 밤낮 spans the whole cycle; M38's 밤새다 ('Korean for pulling an all-nighter') is what flips it. Said 밤낟, rom bamnat.

M11's 여름 + M49's 철 ('The native season-word — 계절 (M11) is the calendar's term; 철 is the market's: 딸기 철 (딸기 M30) = strawberry season'): summer as a PERIOD with rules — 여름철 건강 (M14's 건강) on every pharmacy poster, 여름철 음식 (M1's 음식) = summer food, 여름철 과일 (M3's 과일). The 철-welds run the calendar: 봄철 and 가을철 ride the same rail, and 장마철 (M11's 장마 — 'The weeks-long summer rains') = the rainy season, nested inside this one. M11's 방학 ('Work takes 휴가, school takes 방학') splits the same summer by who gets to leave.

M11's 겨울 + M49's 철: winter as a season with a to-do list — 겨울철 난방 (heating — riding frozen) drives the gas bill, 겨울철 건강 관리 (M14's 건강, M57's 관리) headlines every December, and 겨울철 간식 (M40's 간식) is the 군고구마 M40's 고구마 note smelled ('군고구마 (roasted) is the smell of a Korean winter street'). 환절기 (換節期 — the change-of-season weeks, riding frozen) is what separates 겨울철 from 봄철, and the word every cold gets blamed on. Radar: 계절 (M11) names the season; 철 is the season as a set of habits — coats out, 김장 (M26) done, 딸기 (M30) in.

四季節: M2's 사 in hanja + M11's 계절 — and that note's receipt, paid: 'Korea is proudly a land of 사계절 — four distinct seasons'. The national self-description in one word: 사계절이 뚜렷하다 (뚜렷하다 — distinct, riding frozen) is in every textbook and tourism brochure, 사계절 내내 (M73's 내내 — '여름 내내 (M11's 여름) = all summer long') = all year round, and 사계절용 (four-season, of a jacket or a tire) rides frozen. The running joke, filed for accuracy: with springs and autumns shrinking, the country is said to be down to two seasons — a hot one and a cold one — and the brochures have not been told.

물 (M1) + M49's 더위 ('덥다 (M11) pressed into a noun') with the ㄹ of 물 stepping out at the weld — the exact move M49's 소나무 showed ('솔 (the old pine word) + 나무 (M22), the ㄹ stepping out at the weld'): water-heat = the wet, heavy heat of a Korean July. That note called 더위 'THE heat, the season-long thing you survive rather than describe'; 무더위 is the humid grade of it, the forecaster's word — 무더위가 계속되겠습니다. Radar, MANDATORY: NOT the nothing-無 of M20's 무료, M39's 무조건, and M75's 무시하다 — this 무 is water, and it drips. 무덥다 (the adjective) rides frozen; 열대야 (熱帶夜 — the tropical night that never cools, riding frozen) is what 무더위 does after dark; 더위를 타다 (the M49 gap deck) is what it does to you.

日常生活: M38's 일상 + M29's 생활 — and M38's receipt, paid: '일상생활 = daily life (M29's 생활 welded on)'. The textbook phrase is 일상생활에서 = in everyday life — 일상생활에서 자주 쓰는 표현 (M33's 표현) = expressions used often in daily life, the subtitle of half the phrasebooks ever printed; 일상생활에 필요한 (M16's 필요하다 under the badge from M24) = needed for daily life. M75's 생활하다 ('생활하다 runs a life') is its verb. Radar vs M38's 평소 ('the baseline — 평소에 = usually, on a normal day'): 평소 is WHEN — an ordinary day; 일상생활 is WHERE — the ordinary itself.

M39's 규칙 through the -적 factory from M45 (M45's 적: 'a dependent noun that bolts onto a Sino noun and turns it into a quality-word') — and the IOU M39 wrote, paid: '규칙적인 생활 = a regular routine (the -적 suffix Ring 2 owes you, previewing itself)'. 규칙적인 운동 (운동 — M8's 운동하다, dismounted) = regular exercise; 규칙적으로 = regularly, the adverb form M45's 개인적 ran ('개인적으로 = personally, in my own view'). Its negative is 불규칙 (riding frozen), built by the rule M43's 부동산 note filed ('不 reads 불 except before ㄷ and ㅈ, where it slims to 부') — and 불규칙 동사 is the grammar table's own name for the ㅂ, ㄷ, and 르 families M7 and M14 taught: 'irregular verb', now readable.

'Schedule' through the converter: sch- → 스케 with the ㅡ-cushion M32's 프로그램 filed ('P→ㅍ and the ㅡ-cushion twice'), -dule → 줄 with the ㅈ the Konglish interlude assigned to English z/j (size → 사이즈). Radar, three schedules: M23's 일정 ('일정이 어떻게 돼요? — what's the schedule? Works for trips and Tuesdays alike') is the itinerary you are handed, M8's 계획 ('주말 계획 — weekend plans') is what you intend, 스케줄 is the calendar you keep — and the celebrity's: 스케줄이 많아요 is the complaint of every 스타 (M51). Fullness borrows M62's 가득 and the full-차다 M66's 차다 note filed ('full (가득 차다)'): 스케줄이 가득 찼어요 = my schedule is packed. 시간표 (the school timetable) rides frozen.

臨時 facing-the-hour: 臨 (to face, to be upon — riding frozen) + the time-時 M46's 시절 filed ('時節 time-season: 시간's 時 (M1)'): for the hour at hand = temporary, provisional. 임시 공휴일 (공 public + 휴일, the pattern M25's 연휴 note glossed) = a one-off public holiday the government declares on short notice — the gap deck has it; 임시로 = for now, provisionally; 임시 정부 (M32's 정부) = the Provisional Government of 1919, Korea's government-in-exile in Shanghai, the phrase on every history exam. Radar: M28's 잠깐 and M29's 잠시 ('M28's 잠깐 in uniform') are MOMENTS; 임시 is a STATUS — a thing that holds until the real one arrives; M46's 당분간 ('For now, until things settle') is its adverb. And this 임 (臨) is not the charge-任 of M39's 책임.

本來 origin-come: the origin-本 of M27's 일본 ('본 (origin)') and M57's 기본 ('基本: base-基 + 일본's (M27) origin-本') + the coming-來 M25's 미래 carries and M57's 원래 decoded ('元來: origin-元 + 미래's (M25) coming-來'). 본래 = M57's 원래 ('원래 그래요 = that's just how it is: the national shrug') one notch more written: 본래의 목적 (M33's 목적) = the original purpose, 본래 모습 (M34's 모습) = its original form — essay and editorial words; the shrug itself stays 원래. Said 볼래 — the same ㄴ+ㄹ→ㄹㄹ merge 원래's note ran ('says 월래 — the ㄴ+ㄹ→ㄹㄹ merge'), which is why the rom is bollae.

en: if by any chance (announcing a condition)
notes: 萬一 ten-thousand-one: M9's 만 (10,000) + M2's 일 (one) — a one-in-ten-thousand chance = if, by any chance. The twin of M33's 만약 ('萬若 ten-thousand-if: M9's 만 (10,000) counting hypotheticals. It's an adverb that ANNOUNCES a -(으)면 clause (M20)') — and 만일 announces exactly the same clause, one shade more written and more serious: 만일 비가 오면 (M11's 비) in a notice, 만약에 비가 오면 in a text. Its own habitat is the sign: 만일의 경우 (M32's 경우 — 'News-speak's favorite if: 비가 올 경우') = in case of emergency, 만일의 경우에 대비해서 (대비 — preparing against, riding frozen) = as a precaution. M24's 혹시 ('Also 'just in case': 혹시 몰라서') is the spoken softener; 만일 is the printed one. Taught last because it opens a door the rest of the shelf walks through: 만일 스케줄이 바뀌면 — the sentence deck runs it.

Gram, through the converter: the same 그램 that M32's 프로그램 note built ('Program through the converter: P→ㅍ and the ㅡ-cushion twice') — the gram inside pro-gram, now sold on its own. Sino numbers in front, the way M30's 미터 taught ('Rides like a counter, Sino numbers in front'): 백 그램 (M9's 백) is the unit M3's 반찬 shop prices by — 백 그램에 얼마예요? (M9's 얼마). The whole metric shelf obeys one line from M30's 서른 note — 'Ages native, money Sino — the split holds' — and every unit here sides with money.

킬로 + 그램: a thousand grams, and the unit every Korean scale reads out — M35's 몸무게 note already ruled 'Scales in Korea speak kilograms; the anxiety is universal'. 오 킬로그램 (M2's 오), 몸무게가 육십 킬로그램이에요 (M2's 육), and M57's 무게 ('무게가 나가다 = to weigh — weight GOES OUT, says Korean') is what the number measures. Six syllables is a lot to say about a bag of onions, so the next entry is what people actually say.

The 준말 clip — the interlude's law, 'frequency is pressure' — and it clips TWO words at once: 킬로 is 킬로그램 on the scale and 킬로미터 on the road, the way M51's 프로 note ran 'One clip, two careers'. 몸무게 몇 킬로예요? (M35's 몸무게, M5's 몇) asks weight; 십 킬로 달렸어요 (M17's 달리다) covers distance — context decides, and nobody says the long form aloud. M40's 고춧가루 note already counted in it ('Kimjang math: kilos per household'), and M40's 무 'weighs a kilo and sweetens after frost'. Sino in front: 오 킬로, 십 킬로 — never 다섯 킬로.

The small end of M30's 미터 — that note filed 센티미터 'for the small stuff'; 밀리미터 is smaller still, a thousandth. The ㄹㄹ run in 밀리 is the typing drill M13's 엘리베이터 note warned about ('Konglish, five syllables, and a typing-drill boss fight') — five syllables here too. Its home is the forecast: 비 십 밀리미터 (M11's 비 — '비가 와요 — rain COMES') is how much rain fell, the number every umbrella decision runs on. Clipped in speech to 밀리: 오 밀리.

킬로 + M30's 미터: a thousand meters — the road's unit. 서울에서 부산까지 사백 킬로미터: M12's 부산 note already drew the bracket ('서울에서 부산까지 — the classic KTX bracket'); today it gets a number. 시속 (per hour — riding frozen) puts it on a speedometer: 시속 백 킬로미터. Radar: 킬로 alone means this on the highway and 킬로그램 in the kitchen — see two entries up; the long form is for road signs and the news.
