The converter's ton: the Konglish interlude ran th → ㅅ/ㄸ on 'marathon → 마라톤', so the unit was already sitting inside the race. 이 톤 = two tons (M2's 이 — Sino, like every unit on this shelf); 일 톤 트럭 (트럭 — truck, riding frozen) is the small blue pickup that moves every Korean apartment and every market stall, a national object with the unit in its name. 톤 also weighs the abstract: 쓰레기 몇 톤 (M13's 쓰레기) in an environmental headline.

攝氏 — and the 씨 is M4's 씨, the name suffix ('After a full or given name: 민수 씨'): Celsius entered Chinese as 攝爾修斯, got clipped to its first character, and kept the honorific — 섭씨 is literally Mr. 섭. 화씨 (Fahrenheit — Mr. 화, riding frozen) is the pair. It fronts the number M49's 온도 taught ('The counter it reads out is that same 도: 이십 도 = twenty degrees'): 섭씨 이십오 도. Both ㅆ hard — seopssi; the forecast says it, thermostats print it, and speech drops it: 이십오 도 alone is already Celsius in Korea.

零下 zero-under: 零 is a first — no shipped note has decoded zero — and as a NUMBER, 영 is a new job for a syllable you know three ways (M10's 영어, M2's 영화, M27's 영국 — three different hanja, none of them zero); the 하 is the down-下 of M12's 지하 ('지하 일 층 = B1') and M39's 이하 ('以下 from-here-down'). 영하 십 도 = −10°C, the coldest phrase in M49's 기온 forecast; 영하로 떨어지다 (M36's 떨어지다, 'The great faller, three jobs deep') = to drop below zero. Radar: 영상 (零上, above zero) is the pair and rides frozen — it is NOT M20's 영상, the video clip; the forecast means the temperature, your phone means the file.

億: M9's 만 ('Korean counts in 만-units, not thousands') times itself — 만 × 만 = 100,000,000 — and UNLIKE 만, it takes the 일: 일억, 이억, 십억. M9's 만 note said 'never 일만'; that rule stops at 만, and 억 wants its one. The unit of M13's 아파트 ('whole skylines of numbered towers'): 십억 = a billion won, and Seoul prices are quoted in it; 조 (trillion — riding frozen) sits above it in the national budget. Radar, mandatory: not the 억 of M34's 기억 or M19's 추억 — that 憶 remembers, this 億 counts. Sino all the way up: 일, 십, 백, 천, 만, 억, 조.

M5's 몇 ('Always paired with a counter') + M2's 십 ('Stack to count: 십일 11, 이십 20'): some-tens = dozens of, scores of. 몇십 명 (M5's 명) = dozens of people; 몇십 년 (M25's 년) = decades — the vagueness is the point, as in English tens-of. The pattern runs up the ladder: 몇백, 몇천, 몇만 — read them as a pattern, not as words. Said 멷씹; the rom keeps the letters, myeotsip. Radar: 몇 십 with a space is a question (how many tens?); welded, it stops asking.

M55's 한두 ('Korean estimates by welding neighbors' — 'the weld IS the approximation') in its standalone form: 하나 and 둘, both M5, welded with no counter after. Before a counter it is M55's 한두 (한두 개, 한두 번); alone, sentence-bearing, it is 한둘 — 한둘이 아니에요 = it's not just one or two, there are many; 한둘씩 (씩 from M43) = one or two at a time. M55 called 한두 the 'First rung of the ladder'; the rail continues 두세, 서너 (two-three, three-four — riding frozen), always neighbors, never a gap.

數字 number-character: the 수 of M15's 수학 ('수 (number) + 학 (study-of)') and M15's 점수 ('점 (points) + 수 (number)') + the 자 of M27's 한자 ('자 (character)') and M20's 문자 — a number written down. M36's 행운 note already ran it: '행운의 숫자 = lucky number'. The spelling wears the linking-ㅅ — the wedge M46's 오랫동안 note filed ('with the linking-ㅅ wedged in') — so it is said 숟짜; rom sutja. Korea's unlucky 숫자 is 4: M2's 사 sounds like 死, death, so elevators skip 4층 for F — the gap deck rides it.

計算 count-reckon: the bare noun of M9's 계산하다 ('계산해 주세요 — check, please' — 'the math IS the transaction') and the front half of M43's 계산기 ('計算器 count-machine') — the M75 move, 'Dismount — verb → bare noun, the way print writes'. Dismounted it does both jobs: 계산이 빠르다 (M12's 빠르다) = quick with numbers; 계산 좀 해 주세요 at the counter; 계산대 (the checkout — riding frozen) is where it happens. M73's 각자 note already stood it bare: '각자 계산해요 (M9's 계산하다) = everyone pays their own'. And 계산적 (the -적 badge from M45) = calculating, said of people, never kindly.

折半 fold-half: 折 (fold, break — riding frozen) + M5's 반 ('두 시 반 = 2:30') — the half you get by folding in two, exact. M56's 나누다 ran '반으로 나누다 (M5's 반)'; 절반 is the result, in print: 절반 이상 (M32's 이상, '以上 from-here-up') = more than half, 절반 이하 (M39's 이하) = under half — the news figures. The fraction trio M57 built — 전체 ('The fraction trio opens here: the whole, a part, the rest'), 일부, 나머지 ('The trio closes: 전체 − 일부 = 나머지') — gains its exact middle. Radar: bare 반 is also M15's 반, the homeroom ('3학년 2반 — grade 3, class 2'); 절반 is never a classroom.

多數 many-number: the many-多 of M26's 다양하다 ('다 (many) + 양 (kinds): many-kinded') + the number-數 of 숫자 above — the majority, counted in heads: 다수의 의견 (M24's 의견) = the majority opinion. Radar vs M32's 대부분 ('대 (big) + 부분 (part) = the big part: most'): 대부분 measures share — most of the cake; 다수 counts people — most of the room. Its pair rides frozen: 소수 (the minority, 少數), and together they make 다수결 (majority rule), the word every class vote and every parliament runs on.

一等 one-rank: M2's 일 + 等 — a first for the hanja: the 등 of S2's list-closer ('The list-closer: 사과, 포도, 딸기 등') is this 等 doing its and-the-like job; here it ranks. 일등 하다 = to come first; 일등석 = first class (the seat-席 riding frozen); 이등, 삼등 ride as pattern, and 꼴찌 (dead last — riding frozen) is the floor. Radar, three firsts: M30's 첫째 ('first-in-order — and the firstborn child') orders a list, 일등 ranks a race, and M51's 우승 ('you 이기다 six times and 우승 once') takes the title — a 일등 in one race, a 우승 for the season.

人分 person-portion: the person-人 of M32's 인간 ('人間 person-between') + the portion-分 of M32's 부분 ('部分 section-portion') — and the same 分 inside M5's 분, the minute counter ('Hours native, minutes Sino — the hybrid clock'): a minute is an hour's portion, a serving is a table's. Sino in front: 일 인분 = one serving, 이 인분 = two — and the grill rule: most 고기 (M3) places will not fire the grill under 이 인분, so a solo diner orders for two or eats elsewhere. Radar vs M58's 인원 ('몇 명 (M5) counts the people; 인원 is what the clipboard calls the answer'): 인원 counts eaters, 인분 counts plates — 세 명이 오 인분을 먹었어요 is a perfectly normal Korean sentence.

部 the section: the 부 of M32's 부분 and M58's 부장 ('部長 section-chief'), as a counter for whole copies of a document — 보고서 두 부 (M43's 보고서), 신문 한 부 (M8's 신문), 이력서 세 부 (이력서 — résumé, riding frozen). The split with M30's 장: M75's 복사 note counted a copy in sheets (복사 한 장), and 장 still counts the paper — a ten-page report is 열 장 (M5's 열, the sheet count) and 한 부 (the set); native numbers in front of both. NIKL's C-row is a different 부: the wealth-富 of M43's 부자 ('富者 wealth-person'), as in 부를 쌓다 — to build wealth — a noun you will read, not count with.

Two hanja, both counted. The bucket-桶 that M54's 쓰레기통 decoded ('M13's 쓰레기 + 통 (桶, the bucket)') and M44's 필통 named ('the all-purpose container syllable (물통, 쓰레기통) — NOT 교통's through-通 (M12)') counts whole containers: 수박 한 통 (M30's 수박 — sold whole, that note says), 김치 한 통 (M3's 김치). And the through-通 the 필통 note excluded returns as the counter for things that go THROUGH: 편지 한 통 (M27's 편지), 전화 한 통 (M20's 전화), 문자 한 통 (M20's 문자). One bucket, one call — native numbers in front of both, and context tells you whether you are holding a melon or a message.

en: counter — flowers, bunches, blossoms; a snowflake
notes: The blossom counter, already run twice: M30's 포도 ('포도 한 송이 — one bunch') and M40's 버섯 ('the pine mushroom priced like jewelry and gifted like it too' — 송이 is that mushroom's name). Today it counts on its own: 꽃 한 송이 (M7's 꽃) = one flower, the florist's unit — 장미 백 송이 (장미 — rose, riding frozen; M9's 백) is the drama-proposal cliché; 포도 두 송이 = two bunches. And weather: 눈송이 (M11's 눈 — the snow) = a snowflake, one blossom of snow. Native numbers, like every counter of things you can hold.

號線 number-line: the number-號 of M38's 신호 ('信號 trust-mark') and M20's 번호 ('Numbers that LABEL, not count') + 線 line — a first for 線, though M36's 넘다 note already ran the word: '선을 넘다 (over the LINE — the boundary idiom Korea loves: 선 넘었어 = you went too far)'. Sino in front, because the number labels: 이호선 = Line 2 — Seoul's green circle line, the one that loops the city and most people's lives; 몇 호선이에요? (M5's 몇) at every transfer in M6's 지하철. 노선 (a route, any line — riding frozen) is the general word; 호선 is the numbered one on the map.

en: the year (as a label: fiscal, academic)
notes: 年度 year-degree: M25's 년 ('Sino numbers in front: 이천이십육 년' — '년 does the paperwork') + the degree-度 M49's 온도 reused ('정도's degree-度 (M32)') — the year as a LABEL on a document: 2026년도 입학 (M44's 입학), 2025년도 예산 (예산 — budget, riding frozen), 년도별 (-별, by- — riding frozen; not M22's 별, the star) = by year. Radar, three years: 년 dates (올해는 2026년), 년도 files (2026년도), and M46's 년대 ('the decade machine') narrates (90년대). The rom keeps the spelled ㄴ, nyeondo — and since the word always rides a number, you will read it as 이천이십육년도.

円 the yen — Japan's 원: M27's 일본 ('sun-origin, where the day starts seen from the continent') keeps its own currency, and Korean spells it in one syllable. Money is Sino, per M30's 달러 ('십 달러 — ten dollars, Sino like all money'): 백 엔, 만 엔. The currency shelf now reads 원 (M9) · 달러 (M30) · 엔, with 유로 and 위안 riding frozen — all of it what M23's 환전하다 ('환 (exchange) + 전 (money)') converts. Radar, and it will catch you: -엔 is also 에는 clipped by the 준말 law — 겨울엔, 이번엔 — the way M61's 넘어가다 note wrote 이번엔 넘어갈게요. The yen has a space before it and a number in front; the particle has neither.

M29's 때문 ('[noun] 때문에 — because of it: 눈 때문에, 너 때문에 (credit or blame; tone decides)') pressed flat by the 준말 interlude's law, 'frequency is pressure' — the same clip M47's 애 note credited ('the same clip that made M27's 아줌마 from 아주머니'). 너 땜에 = because of you; 일 땜에 못 가 = can't go, work. Register is the whole lesson: 땜 lives in texts and in M19's 반말 ('half-speech — the register with the endings snapped off'); in a report, an email to a 부장님, or anything graded, it is 때문 in full. NIKL files it as a dependent noun; the app tags it noun. Taught last in this drawer because it is the outlier: every other word here goes on a form, and this one never should.

The horizontal — and its partner 세로 is next, because Korean names the two axes as a pair. 가로 십 센티미터 (센티미터 rides via M30's 미터 note) = 10 cm wide; the ruler shelf M57 built — 크기 ('Korean builds its rulers out of its adjectives'), 길이, 높이, 무게 — gets its width. Together they are the crossword: 가로세로 (낱말 — word, riding frozen). And a writing direction: 가로쓰기 (M10's 쓰다 through the -기 nominalizer from M13) = horizontal writing, which is how everything you read in this app is set. Radar: the 가로 of 가로등 (streetlight) is 街路, the street — a different word that happens to stand on the same two syllables.

The vertical, 가로's partner: 세로 이십 센티미터 = 20 cm tall; on a form, 가로 × 세로 is how every box, photo, and parcel gets its size. 세로쓰기 = vertical writing — the direction old newspapers and every 조선 시대 (M26's 시대) book ran, top to bottom, right to left, until the late 1990s flipped the dailies to 가로. The phone did the rest: a 세로 영상 (M20's 영상) is a vertical video, the shape phones made the default. Radar: this 세 is not the 세 of 세 명 (the M5 counter contraction) and not M22's 세상 — a native word, no hanja to decode.

en: up and down; top and bottom
notes: M6's 위 + M6's 아래 welded, the way M65's 앞뒤 was ('One word, a small axis'): the vertical axis as one noun. 위아래로 흔들다 (M41's 흔들다 — '손을 흔들다 (hello, goodbye, taxi)') = shake up and down; 위아래를 보다 = look someone up and down, the once-over. The idiom is the culture: 위아래가 없다 = to have no up-and-down — no sense of rank — the harshest thing an elder says about a junior, because Korean, as the M47 lesson put it, 'runs TWO politeness ladders', and M24's 어른 is 'The person 존댓말 (M19) was invented for'; the gap deck files it. 아래위 is also heard; the meaning does not flip.

中間 middle-between: the middle-中 S2's 중 filed ('중국's middle-中, hung after any noun') + the between-間 of M32's 인간 ('間, between') and M1's 시간 — the middle as a point or a stage. 중간에 = midway, partway through (영화 중간에 나갔어요, M2's 영화); 중간 크기 (M57's 크기) = medium; 중간고사 = midterms (고사 — exam, riding frozen; 기말고사, the finals, its bookend). Radar, three middles: M28's 가운데 ('M6's position nouns finally get their center') is where you stand, M50's 중심 is what matters, and 중간 is halfway — in space, in time, or on a size chart.

頂上 crown-top: 頂 (the crown of the head — riding frozen) + the top-上 M54's 옥상 found ('The 상 is top-上, hiding inside M22's 세상 (世上, the world) all along') and M32's 이상 wears. The summit: 산 정상 (M11's 산), 정상에 오르다 (M22's 오르다 — 'Mountains, stairs, and prices — all things that 오르다'). And the pun the news lives on: 정상 회담 (회담 — talks, riding frozen) = a summit meeting — the mountaintop borrowed for diplomacy, exactly as English did it. RADAR, mandatory, NIKL's C-row: 正常 = normal — 정상이에요 = it's normal, the doctor's best sentence — with the 正 of M63's 정확하다 ('정답's 正 (M44 — the one hiding inside 정말 since M11)'); 비정상 (abnormal) rides frozen. One spelling: a peak you climb, a state you hope for.

The native top: 산꼭대기 = the mountaintop, 나무 꼭대기 (M22's 나무), 건물 꼭대기 (M22's 건물) — where the thing ends and the sky starts. Register sorts the three tops: 정상 is the climber's and the news anchor's word, 꼭대기 is the child's and the storyteller's, and M55's 맨 위 ('The edge-finder: 맨 위 (M6), 맨 앞 (M6), 맨 처음 (M15) = the VERY top / front / first') is the plain description. Radar: it shares a syllable with M29's 꼭 ('The promise-hardener: 꼭 오세요') and nothing else — no promise in a peak.

en: one's side (of a person); by, beside (intimate)
notes: One's side — the intimate 옆. M6's 옆 ('옆에 — beside') is geometry: a desk has an 옆, a chair has an 옆. 곁 is company: only people and pets have one. 곁에 있어 주세요 (-아/어 주다 from M9) = stay by my side; 곁을 지키다 (M26's 지키다 — 'Traditions, promises, secrets, goals: 약속을 지켜요') = to stay by someone through it, the hospital-corridor verb; 곁을 떠나다 (M23's 떠나다) = to leave someone's side. The ballad word — half of Korean love songs turn on it — and the one position noun on this shelf that measures nothing.

M36's 넘다 ('산을 넘다 (over the mountain)') frozen into a noun: the far side. 산 너머 = beyond the mountain, 창문 너머 (M6's 창문) = through the window, 국경 너머 (국경 — the border, riding frozen). Like every position word since M6's 위 ('A NOUN, not a preposition'), it hangs after its noun and takes 에 or 로: 산 너머에 있어요, 창문 너머로 보여요 (M36's 보이다). SPELLING LAW, mandatory: 너머 (noun — the far side) vs 넘어 (the verb's -아/어 form — the crossing): 산 너머에 있어요 / 산을 넘어 가요. Natives get this wrong constantly — the spacing interlude admitted 'spacing is the part of Korean orthography natives get wrong most often', and 너머/넘어 is the same humility, one rule over. 어깨너머로 배우다 (M14's 어깨, M2's 배우다) = to learn over someone's shoulder — the gap deck closes on it.

姨母: 姨 (mother's sister — riding frozen) + the mother-母 that M47's 고모 note decoded ('the 모 is mother-母, 부모님's (M4) second syllable') — and that note wrote the IOU this entry pays: 'Her mirror is 이모, mom's sister: the word you've been shouting at restaurant servers since M18's gap deck taught the summons'. The M18 gap deck still holds the shout, and M27's 아줌마 note gave the tactic ('Address one as 이모 (M18) in a restaurant and eat better'); today the actual aunt arrives — your mother's sister, who outranks the 반찬 (M3) refills. The aunt shelf, by side: 고모 (dad's sister) / 이모 (mom's sister) / 숙모 and 외숙모 (aunts by marriage — riding frozen); Korean has no plain word for aunt. Taught first on purpose: the whole module files people by their coordinates, and 이모 is the one coordinate you already use.

四寸 four-degrees: M2's 사 + the 寸 that M47's 삼촌 note decoded ('三寸 three-degrees: M2's 삼 + 촌 (寸), the kinship-distance unit — Korea MEASURES family') — and that note promised this exact entry: 'Your cousin lives one step further: 사촌, the four-degree relative — same arithmetic'. The M54 gap deck carried it frozen in 이웃사촌 ('The 사촌 (四寸, four-degrees-removed: a cousin — untaught, frozen here)'), itself paying M13's 이웃; today the word lands and both receipts close. Cousins wear sibling titles — 사촌 형, 사촌 언니, 사촌 동생 (all M4) — and the side files them: 외사촌 (mom's side, on the 외- axis M47 drew) and 고종사촌 (through a 고모), both riding frozen. Count on your fingers: parent 1촌, sibling 2촌, uncle 3촌, cousin 4촌 — and 팔촌, eight degrees out, is where Korean says family ends.

en: older sister's husband (said by a woman)
notes: 兄夫: the 兄 that M47's 형제 note surfaced ('형 (M4) finally shows its hanja 兄') + 夫, husband — a FIRST: no shipped note has read this character, though it has been the front half of M25's 부부 all along (夫婦 — the back half is the 婦 M58's 주부 decoded as 'the bride-婦 of 신부 (M47)'). Older-brother-husband: what a WOMAN calls her 언니's (M4) husband — 형부, 언제 오세요? — and the speaker-gender grid M4 started with 형/오빠 and 누나/언니 runs straight into the in-laws: a man calls his 누나's (M4) husband 매형 (riding frozen), and the gap deck files the fork. He is not blood, but he is 형 by title, so 께서 (M47) and -(으)세요 from M4 apply the moment he outranks you in age — which he does by definition.

M47's 고모 + the husband-夫 the entry above just landed: dad's sister's husband. This is the -부 rail, and it runs on one rule — husbands are filed by WHOSE husband they are: 형부 (언니's), 고모부 (고모's), 이모부 (이모's — riding frozen, the mirror this module's first word implies). Korean never needed a plain word for uncle-by-marriage; it needed a suffix and a coordinate. To his face 고모부 works as-is — kinship words are their own titles, per the address system M58 ran — while M27's 아저씨 (its note: 'Technically an uncle-by-marriage; practically every man over forty') is what the language does with every other man his age.

長男 eldest-son: the chief-長 of M58's 부장 ('部長 section-chief') and 반장 ('班長: M15's 반 (the 3학년 2반 classroom) + 長'), here meaning ELDEST rather than boss — the first-born is the family's chief by birth — + the man-男 that M47's 남매 decoded ('남자's (M4) man-男'). M30's 첫째 warned that 'Birth order is a lifelong job title in Korean families', and M47's 막내 closed the ladder ('첫째, 둘째, … 막내 — birth order as a lifelong job title, exactly as 첫째's note warned'); 장남 is that job title in its formal register — 첫째 아들 (M4's 아들) = 장남 — and the daughters' side runs 장녀 (riding frozen). The K-drama plot word: the 장남 inherits the company and the duty — 부모님을 모시다 (M47's 모시다) lands on him first — and the sentence deck runs exactly that.

次男 next-son: the next-次 of M46's 차례 ('次例 next-in-line: order and turns') + the same 男 — the second son, 둘째 아들 in the formal register (M4's 아들 after M30's 둘째), with 차녀 (riding frozen) for a second daughter. The pair 장남/차남 is how family registers, obituaries, and inheritance lawyers count sons; speech says 첫째/둘째 (M30) and lets the 막내 (M47) be the punchline. Drama law: the 장남 inherits, the 차남 is free — to marry for love, leave for Seoul, or run the rival company. Radar: this 차 is next-次, not the car-車 of M50's 자동차 nor the tea-茶 of M2's 차 — a third 차, and it only ever means second place.

en: husband's parents, parents-in-law (from the wife's side)
notes: The 시- axis the M47 md drew ('시- stamps his whole family — 시어머니, 시아버지, 시집') + 부모 — the bare 부모 inside M4's 부모님, whose note said 'You basically never drop it'; and indeed the 님 comes back the moment you speak: 시부모님 (the M47 md: 'M16's 님-ladder reaches home'). The husband's parents as ONE word — M47's 시어머니 and 시아버지 filed together for forms, statistics, and the sentence 시부모님을 모시고 살아요, with M47's 모시다. The wife's side is quieter in the language: 처가 (her family home) and 처부모 (her parents) run on 妻, wife — both riding frozen — and appear a tenth as often, which is the sociology the M47 gap deck already read off 시집살이. The 시 is 媤, the husband's-side character M47's 시집 note filed; it is not the market-市 of M3's 시장.

新婚夫婦, four characters you already own in pairs: M25's 신혼여행 unpacked the front ('신 (new — 신문's new-신) + 혼 (marriage — 결혼's 혼) + M11's 여행') and M25's 부부 is the back ('M19's 커플, upgraded by paperwork') — with 夫 finally read at 형부 above and 婦 read at M58's 주부. Newlyweds, as a unit: 신혼부부 특별공급 — the housing lottery's special allotment (특별공급 riding frozen, M57's 특별 in front) that gives new couples first claim on apartments, which tells you how badly the state wants them to stay married and multiply — and 신혼집 (riding frozen), the first apartment M1's 집 becomes. The word expires quietly: after a year or two the couple is just 부부, and the 신 goes back to newspapers.

愛人 love-person: 愛, love — a FIRST (M7's 사랑하다 is native, so no shipped note has ever needed the character) + the person-人 of M23's 외국인 ('외국 + 인 (person)') that M47's 노인 reused ('old-老 + the person-人 of 외국인 (M23)'). RADAR, mandatory: NOT M47's 애 ('아이 (M4) worn smooth by speech') — 애인 is not kid-person; the 애 here is a full hanja syllable, and 애인 있어요? asks about your love life, not your childcare. The register: ballads, older speakers, and forms — today's speech says 남자 친구 / 여자 친구 (M1's 친구 after M4's 남자/여자), and the 준말 interlude's clipping law makes them 남친 / 여친 (both riding frozen). How you acquire one is M19's 사귀다, whose note warned '사귀자 is a confession'.

en: a rich household, a wealthy family
notes: M43's 부자 ('富者 wealth-person') + M1's 집 with the linking-ㅅ wedged between — the same wedge M46's 오랫동안 filed ('with the linking-ㅅ wedged in — the same wedge M40's 고춧가루 note filed'): rich-person's house = a wealthy family, said 부자찝. Its whole career is adjectival: 부잣집 아들, 부잣집 딸 (M4's 아들/딸) = the rich kid — K-drama's second lead by law, the one with the car and the disapproving mother. The opposite is M43's 가난하다 nouned, as its note said ('Nouned as 가난'): 가난한 집 — and the drama needs exactly one of each. Rom radar: the ㅅ is written, so the app spells it bujatjip; the ear hears the tensing it causes.

en: a young child, a little kid
notes: M21's 어리다 wearing the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 + M4's 아이 — the two-word phrase 어린 아이 welded into one dictionary word, the way M58's 젊은이 ran the same weld one age up ('젊다 (M24) wearing the badge -(으)ㄴ (M24)'). A young child, in the register of books and pediatric leaflets: 어린아이처럼 (처럼 from M41) = like a small child, said of adults who sulk; 어린아이도 알아요 = even a child knows. M46's 시절 note already ran the badge on this adjective ('어린 시절 = childhood, M21's 어리다 wearing M24's badge'); here the badge stops being grammar and becomes spelling. The children shelf, sorted by room: 어린이 (M35 — its note: 'the word on museums, menus, and crosswalk signs') / 어린아이 (books) / 어린애 (kitchens, next entry) / 아이 (M4) and 애 (M47), everywhere.

The same weld with M47's 애 in the child seat — and that note drew the register line this entry sits on: '아이 is for writing and pediatricians; 애 is for living rooms'. So 어린애 is the living-room form, and it leans dismissive: 어린애처럼 굴지 마 = stop acting like a kid (굴다 — to behave, riding frozen; -지 마 is -지 마세요 from M14 with the ending snapped off, M19's 반말), 어린애 취급하지 마세요 = don't treat me like a child (취급 — treatment, riding frozen). Aimed at a real toddler it is neutral; aimed at an adult it is the insult. Both spellings are NIKL grade B — Korean ranks the polite child and the scolded one within a few hundred places of each other, which is about right for how often each gets said.

女, standing alone as a PREFIX: the female-女 that M32's 여성 decoded ('女性 woman-nature'), that M47's 손녀 spelled 녀 mid-word ('the same 女 that runs 여자 (M4), spelled 녀 here by the initial-sound law M44's 토론 note documented for 論'), and that M58's 소녀 carried — now bolted to the front of jobs and ranks: 여의사 (on M4's 의사), 여교수 (on M27's 교수), 여기자 (on M16's 기자), and this shelf's 여대생, 여고생, 여직원. M4's 동생 note already showed the mold ('Genderless — 여동생 / 남동생 specify sister / brother'), M26's 왕 note ran 여왕 for the queen, and 여학생/남학생 assemble the same way. One honest culture line: Korean marks the FEMALE as the exception — 여직원 exists, an everyday 남직원 does not — a live debate, and newsrooms have begun dropping the prefix. Radar: this 여 is not the travel-旅 of M11's 여행 or M52's 여관 — same syllable, different character; the noun 여자 (M4) is this prefix with its child-子 still attached.

여 + M15's 대학생 ('대학 + 학생, overlapped into one word') clipped to 대생 — the overlap overlapping again: 女大生. A female university student — the word of campus dramas, old magazine covers, and crime-news headlines, which is the register warning: 여대생 marks gender where 대학생 would do, and the marked form tends to appear when the story is about her being female. The unmarked plural is 대학생들; if you mean a specific woman at your university, 대학생 or her name serves better. The male mirror 남대생 exists on paper and almost never in speech — the asymmetry the 여 entry named, measured on one word.

高校: pays M15's 고등학교 note verbatim — 'Shortened to 고등학생's 고교 in headlines — Korean compresses what it says often'. The high-高 of M19's 최고 ('최 (most) + 고 (high)') + the school-校 that M32's 교육 pinned as the building ('NOT 학교's (校, the school building)'): high-school, two syllables instead of four. The clip breeds: 고교생 (riding frozen) for the student, 고교 야구 (M17's 야구) for the summer tournament, and the grade shorthand every Korean knows by heart — 고1, 고2, 고3 — where 고3, the third year, is the year the M15 gap deck's 수능 ('the exam that stops the nation') is aimed at; this module's gap deck files it as the identity it becomes. Print and speech split: 고등학교 in a sentence, 고교 in a headline or a compound.

여 + 고교 + 생: the student-生 that M58's 신입생 decoded ('student-生 (학생, M4)'), on the clipped school above — 女高生, a prefix, a clip, and a suffix with no root noun left standing, which is how compressed Korean compounds get. The teenage-girl word of school dramas and 교복 (M21) commercials; the male form 남고생 rides frozen and is said about as often, because for schoolchildren both genders get marked — the asymmetry the 여 entry named eases where uniforms are involved. Radar: 여고 alone is a girls' high school (riding frozen), so 여고생 is either a girl at high school or a student at a girls' school, and only the sentence tells you which.

여 + M16's 직원 ('직 (duty) + 원 (member — the one in 회사원)'): the female staff member — and the entry the 여 note's culture line was written for. On an org chart 여직원 marks what 직원 already covers; in a shop, 여직원한테 물어보세요 = ask the woman at the counter, where the prefix is doing description, not policy. The member-員 is the one M43's 사원 staffed ('the member-員 already staffing 회사원 (M4) and 직원 (M16)') and M58's 종업원, 공무원, and 회원 wear — the payroll's most reliable suffix, now with a gender stamp the language is slowly unlearning. Rom radar: 직원 liaises across the syllable — yeojigwon, said 여지권.

en: homeroom teacher (in charge of a class)
notes: 擔任 carry-the-charge: the carry-擔 of M64's 담당하다 ('擔 (carry on the shoulder) + 當 (face)') + the charge-任 of M39's 책임 ('責任 duty-charge'): the one who shoulders the class. The homeroom teacher — 담임 선생님 (M4's 선생님), one per 반 (M15's 반, whose note said '3학년 2반 — grade 3, class 2 — is how Korean schools address a kid') for the whole year: the adult who calls home, signs the forms, and keeps the 고3 in their seats; 담임을 맡다 (M37's 맡다, in its take-a-role sense) = to be assigned a class. M58's 반장 ('elected every semester and in charge of quiet and roll call') answers to the 담임; the 학부모 (parents of students — riding frozen) phone the 담임. Rom: damim — the ㅁ liaises, 다밈.

M15's 대학교 ('대 (big) + 학교: the big school') + M27's 교수 ('교 (teach — 교실/교과서's 교, M15) + 수. Address as 교수님, always') welded into the full title: 大學敎授. The version on M16's 명함 and in the newspaper byline — 김민수 대학교수 — where 교수 alone would be speech; Korean print likes the institution attached to the rank. Above it sits M58's 총장 ('The head of a 대학교 (M15) — the campus's final boss: M15's 교수님 answers to the 총장님'); below it, the 강의 (M44) it gives and the 대학원생 (from M44's 대학원 + 생) who grade for it. To the face, still and only 교수님 — the four-syllable form is for paper.

店員 shop-member: the shop-店 of M27's 서점 ('서 (writing) + 점 (shop)') — the very 店 that M32's 점 radar'd away ('NOT 서점's 점 (店, shop — M27)') — + the member-員 of 여직원 two entries up. The clerk ON PAPER: 편의점 점원 (on M6's 편의점) in a news story, 점원이 친절해요 in a review. To the face, never: you call over M16's 직원 ('Also who you call over in any shop: 직원'), or use M6's 저기 in its 저기요! job, or promote whoever it is to 사장님 (M9) and watch the service improve. Same rule as M58's 종업원: the counting word and the calling word are different words.

The English waiter through the converter: w → 웨, and the agent -er → 어, the tail of M10's 컴퓨터 and M30's 미터. A waiter — in a Western-style restaurant, in a job listing, and in old films where someone snaps 웨이터! across a room; that snap is exactly what not to do today. M58's 종업원 note set the rule ('signs and statutes say 종업원, faces get warmer words'): to summon, use M6's 저기 in its 저기요! job, M9's 여기요 ('flags a server (like 저기요)'), or — where floor seating and aprons allow — this module's 이모. 웨이트리스 (waitress) rides frozen, and the 여 prefix takes the day off: the loanword carries its own gender in English, so Korean does not stamp it.

運轉技士: 운전 — the bare noun inside M10's 운전하다, which M50's 운전자 split open ('carry-運, turn-轉') — + M48's 기사 in its 技士 sense, paying that note's radar verbatim: '기사님 the driver is a different word (技士, a licensed-skill title) — the taxi 기사님 has never read your 기사'. The job title — 버스 운전기사, 택시 운전기사 (on M6's 버스/택시) on the licence, the union banner, and the news; face to face the same person is 기사님, exactly as M50's 운전자 ruled ('On paper a 운전자, in the mirror a 기사님'). 技 is the skill-技 of M44's 기술 ('技術 craft-skill'); 士 is the 士 of M44's 박사 ('博士 broad-scholar') — a licensed person — and that opens the RADAR of the two job-사s: teacher-師 (M4's 요리사, M14's 간호사, the 師 that M58's 사모님 left frozen, M69's 목사 — '牧師 shepherd-teacher') vs licensed-士 (박사, 기사, and M16's 변호사 — 辯護士, which that note filed by sound: 'The job-사 family grows: 요리사, 간호사, 변호사'). One teaches a craft, one holds a licence; 운전사 (the older form) rides frozen.

外交官: M64's 외교 ('外 (outside) + 交 (meeting): the meeting of outsiders, nations with nations') + 官, official — a FIRST: the bureaucrat's character, which M57's 관리 only glimpsed as a homograph ('a historical homograph 관리 (官吏) is the Joseon official'). RADAR, mandatory, because the syllable is a trap: this 관 is NOT the hall-館 of M23's 박물관 ('The -관 suffix builds public buildings: 박물관, 미술관, 영화관'), M27's 대사관 ('대사 (ambassador) + M23's -관 (public building)'), or M52's 여관 ('the hall-館') — the 외교관 is the official-官 who works INSIDE the building-館: a diplomat in an embassy, 대사관의 외교관. The same 官 stamps 경찰관 (from M16's 경찰 + 官 — the pattern the taught-as ledger already runs) and 장관, a government minister (riding frozen). 외교관이 되다 (M10's 되다) is the dream the 외교관 시험 (M10's 시험) gatekeeps; the sentence deck counts the years after.

歷史家: M15's 역사 + the maker's 家 — the house-家 that M48's 작가 read as a skill you live in ('作家 make-house: the 家 is 가족's (M4) house-家 — in the maker-suffix reading, a skill so practiced it's the house you live in') and M58's 전문가 filed as 'the maker's house-家 of 작가/음악가/예술가 (M48)'. A historian: 역사가들은 …라고 본다 = historians hold that …, the frame of every documentary; M45's 역사적 ('역사적인 날 = a historic day') is the adjective they hand out. RADAR, the subject particle: 역사가 길어요 = history is long — the identical spelling, M15's 역사 wearing 가 — the trap M57's 길이 filed for another word ('Radar: M12's 길 (road) wearing the subject particle spells 길이 too'). If a verb follows directly, someone is talking about history; if 들 or a name follows, someone is a historian.

The English design through the converter: z → ㅈ, the rule the Konglish interlude tabled as size → 사이즈 (M9's 사이즈), and the -gn tail flattened to 인. Design — the noun on every product page (디자인이 예뻐요, M1's 예쁘다), the department (디자인 팀, M16's 팀), the major (디자인 전공, M44's 전공) — and the verb by the hinge M75 ran on thirty words: 디자인하다. Radar vs the Sino shelf: 설계 (blueprint-design, the engineer's word — riding frozen) is what an architect does; 디자인 is what makes you buy it. The person is next.

디자인 + the converter's agent -er, which lands as 너 because 디자인's coda ㄴ carries over into the 어: 디자이너, beside 웨이터, M10's 컴퓨터, M30's 미터, and M48's 아나운서, which its note filed as Konglish. The designer: 패션 디자이너 (패션 riding frozen — M72's 모델 note ran it the same way: '패션 모델 — 패션 riding frozen'), 게임 디자이너 (on M8's 게임), 디자이너 브랜드 on the shopping channel. This is the loanword wing of the title machine: where Sino jobs end in 者/家/員/士/官, English jobs come through the converter with their own -er attached — so 디자이너 gets no 자, and no 여 either.

初步 first-step: the beginning-初 of M46's 최초 ('beginning-初 — the third 초, exactly the one M25's candle note radar'd') + the step-步 that M75's 양보하다 left frozen last module ('讓步 yield-a-step: 讓 (frozen — to let another go first) + 步 (a step — frozen)') — landed today, one module later. A beginner, or the beginner LEVEL: 초보 운전 = the sticker on every new driver's rear window (the gap deck explains what it buys you), 한국어 초보 = a Korean beginner, 초보 요리사 (M4's 요리사) = a rookie cook. The upgrade is M26's 왕 — 'modern slang's favorite prefix: 왕만두 are king-sized dumplings' — 왕초보 = total beginner, the king-size applied to inexperience. Radar: the third 초 — M25's 초 melts, the clock's 초 ticks, this one takes the first step.

초보 + the person-者 of M27's 환자 ('The -자 is a person-suffix (기자, 학자 — reporter, scholar)') — the payroll that M43's 소비자 formalized ('者 is the person-suffix M27's 환자 note introduced (기자 M16 records, 환자 suffers, 소비자 spends)') and M58's 책임자 and M72's 과학자 extended: the beginner as a PERSON. 초보자를 위한 (위한 + noun from M44) = for beginners — the phrase on this app's own shelf and on every textbook spine; 초보자도 할 수 있어요 = even a beginner can do it, the ad copy. 초보 alone can modify (초보 운전) or name the level; 초보자 is only ever the human. You were one at Module 1; the suffix is how Korean says so politely.

使用者: S2's 사용 ('사용 중 (in use — the bathroom door's word)' — whose note ended 'The verb is 사용하다 — 쓰다 (M10) in a lab coat') + 者: the user. 사용자 이름 (M1's 이름) = username, 사용자 설정 (설정 — settings, riding frozen), 사용자가 많아요 = it has a lot of users — the software word. Radar per M72's 이용 ('사용 uses a thing, 이용 uses a service'): apps and machines have 사용자, libraries and subways have 이용자 (riding frozen); and M58's 고객 ('what the company calls you TO YOUR FACE, always as 고객님') is the same human once money changes hands. Three names for one person, sorted by what they are doing to the product.

The English champion through the converter: ch → ㅊ, -pion → 피언. The champion — the person who has done M75's 우승하다, which M51's 우승 pre-announced ('우승하다 = to take the title; 우승컵 = the trophy'): 세계 챔피언 (on M23's 세계) = world champion, 챔피언 벨트 (벨트 riding frozen) in boxing and wrestling, 디펜딩 챔피언 in sports pages that enjoy their loanwords. Sort the podium: M17's 선수 is any athlete (and, per its note, 'Also slang for anyone suspiciously good at anything'); 챔피언 is the one holding the title; the Sino synonym 우승자 (우승 + 者 — riding frozen) is what the official record writes. The title machine's third wing: English ranks arrive through the converter and skip the hanja suffixes entirely.

en: robber, armed robbery (强盜); (homograph) intensity (强度)
notes: 强盜 strong-steal: the strong-強 that M63's 강하다 landed ('強 strong — the hanja M56's 강조하다 note carried frozen finally lands its own word') + 盜, steal (riding frozen): the robber who uses force, and the crime itself. M36's 도둑 is the stealth version ('The thief — who ENTERS: 도둑이 들었어요'); 강도 is the threat version — 은행 강도 (on M6's 은행) = a bank robbery, 강도를 당하다 = to get robbed (당하다 — to suffer, riding frozen), and the news pairs it with M36's 잡히다: 강도가 잡혔어요. SENSE COLLAPSE, mandatory: NIKL's C-row 强度 is intensity — same 强, a different 도 (度, degree) — 강도 높은 훈련 = high-intensity training (훈련 riding frozen), 운동 강도 = workout intensity, on M8's 운동하다 dismounted. The verb tells them apart: a 강도 who 들다 (M28) is a robber; a 강도 that is 높다 is a level.

首相 head-minister: the head-首 of M31's 수도 ('首都 head-city: where a country keeps its head') + 相 — the mutual-相 of M57's 상대 ('相對 mutual-facing') in its other job, the minister who faces the throne. The prime minister of a parliamentary country: 영국 수상 (on M27's 영국), 일본 수상 (on M27's 일본) — Korea's own head of cabinet is the 총리 (riding frozen), under M32's 대통령, so 수상 in Korean news is almost always someone else's. SENSE COLLAPSE, mandatory and three deep: 수상하다 (受賞) = to win an award — 受, receive (a FIRST) + the prize-賞 that M40's 상 filed ('the prize-상 (賞) that award shows hand out — 상을 받았어요 = I won a prize'), so 수상 소식 = award news and the awardee is a 수상자 (riding frozen); and 수상하다 (殊常, riding frozen) = suspicious — 수상한 사람 = a suspicious person, the drama's stock line. A PM, a prize, and a prowler: the particle and the verb decide.

en: lack, shortage (不足); (homograph) a tribe (部族)
notes: Two NIKL grade-B words in one spelling, and both are yours. 不足: the noun under M39's 부족하다 ('不足 not-enough-foot: falling short — 잠이 부족해요 (sleep-deprived: the national condition, M28's 잠)') — 운동 부족 (on M8's 운동하다, dismounted) = too little exercise, 수면 부족 = sleep deprivation (수면 riding frozen), 인력 부족 = a labour shortage (인력 riding frozen), 경험 부족 (on M33's 경험) = inexperience: the diagnosis noun, stacked bare the way print stacks; M43's 부동산 explained the spelling ('不 reads 불 except before ㄷ and ㅈ, where it slims to 부'), and M53's 모자라다 is the native groan for the same condition. 部族: the section-部 of M32's 부분 + the tribe-族 of M32's 민족 ('民族 people-tribe: 대한민국's 민 + 가족's 족 (M4)'): a tribe — 아프리카 부족 (on M31's 아프리카), 부족 사회 (on M32's 사회). The shortage is far commoner; the tribe turns up in documentaries — and 부족이 부족해요 (the tribe is short of something) is grammatical, unkind, and a good memory hook.

性別 nature-separate: the nature-性 of M32's 여성 and 남성 ('女性 woman-nature') + the separate-別 that M57's 특별 decoded ('the 별 is separate-別: special = set apart'): the field on every form — 이름 (M1), 나이 (M4), 성별. Gender as a category, not a person: 성별에 관계없이 (from M32's 관계 + M32's 없이) = regardless of gender, the anti-discrimination clause; 성별을 선택하세요 (with M33's 선택하다) = select your gender, the dropdown. Radar, twice: this 별 is not M22's 별, the star; and M23's 성 note logged the triple ('Also the 성 in 성격 (M19) and family names; the radar logs a triple') — this 性 is the middle one, the nature inside 성격 itself, not the castle and not the surname. Taught last on purpose: after thirty-three people-words filed by side, rank, and title, here is the word the form uses to file YOU.

M18's 볶다 said it — "The 볶 in 떡볶이 and 볶음밥 (fried rice)" — and here the rice lands. 볶다 + the -(으)ㅁ freezer (M33's 웃음 named the factory; M40's 얼음 note said "the -ㅁ factory (웃음 M33, 걸음 M38) ships its coldest product") + M1's 밥: fried-thing-rice — the name is the recipe. 김치볶음밥 — M3's 김치 in front — is the dish every Korean can cook from leftovers; 새우볶음밥, with M59's 새우, is the Chinese-place order, served with a fried egg on top. Said 보끔밥.

醋 + 밥: the vinegar-초 M40's 식초 decoded ("食醋 food-vinegar: 식사's food-食 + 초 (vinegar)") on M1's 밥 — vinegared rice, which is what sushi IS. That makes a FOURTH 초 for the radar M25's 초 note opened ("초 is also 'second' (the clock's tick) and the start-syllable of 초등학교 (M15)") and M46's 최초 counted: candle, second, beginning, vinegar. The Korean word says the recipe; the Japanese loan 스시 (frozen) says the brand. M18's 회 ("sliced and dipped in 고추장-vinegar") is the fish without the rice.

en: rice bowl; (idiom) one's livelihood, one's job
notes: M1's 밥 + M18's 그릇 ("Also the counter for servings: 밥 한 그릇 — one bowl of rice"): the rice bowl — and, because rice is livelihood, the JOB. 밥그릇 싸움 (M67's 싸움) = a turf war, two departments fighting over one bowl; 밥그릇을 지키다 (M26's 지키다) = protect your position. The gap deck files the fight. Rom radar: written bapgeureut, said 밥끄릇 — the ㄱ tenses after ㅂ.

食 + 빵: the food-食 of M18's 한식 ("한 (Korea) + 식 (food — 식당's 식)") on M2's 빵 ("Starts with tense ㅃ — puff-free and tight"; the Konglish interlude tracked the loaf itself, which "sailed from Portuguese (pão) to Japan to Korea centuries ago"): meal-bread — the plain sliced loaf for toast and sandwiches, as opposed to the pastry case. The 빵집 (frozen — the bread-house) sells both. Radar: this 식 is food-食, not the way-式 of M55's 식.

M18's 된장 ("The fermented backbone of Korean cooking") + M18's 찌개, whose note already served it ("served bubbling in stone or steel: 김치찌개, 된장찌개"): the stew named by its engine, with M18's 두부 as "된장찌개's soft white heart", a handful of 파 (M40), and whatever the fridge had. The default home stew — the smell of a Korean kitchen at seven — and the first dish anyone asks an 엄마 (M4) how to make. Say the ㅉ tight.

M3's 김치 + M18's 찌개: the stew made from kimchi gone sour — old kimchi is the ingredient, not a fault, and M18's 돼지고기 or a can of 참치 (frozen — tuna) is the partner. Where 된장찌개 is the everyday pot, 김치찌개 is the one on every foreigner's list: red, bubbling, set on M40's 상 with the lid still rattling. The M28 sentence already ran the verdict — 김치찌개는 별로 맵지 않아요 — and the verdict is what Koreans tell guests.

설렁 (native; the folk etymology ties it to the 선농단 altar where kings prayed for harvests — a story, not a derivation) + 탕: the hot-water-湯 M54's 목욕탕 decoded ("hot-water-湯, the same syllable that ends soup names (M40's 감자 note litigated 감자탕)"). M3's 국 note promised it — "Fancier stews are 찌개 and 탕 — later" — and today the suffix lands: milky ox-bone broth, unsalted in the kitchen and salted at the table with the salt jar and a fistful of 파 (M40), the hangover breakfast of the nation. The register ladder: 국 (M3) at home, 찌개 (M18) thick and shared, 탕 in a restaurant bowl. The ㄹㄹ is audible: 설렁.

M30's 갈비 ("Ribs, grilled tableside") + 탕: the same ribs, boiled instead of grilled — clear broth, glass noodles, a rib you eat with your hands — the wedding-hall lunch and the reason 결혼식 (M25) guests leave full. The 탕 family runs by the same rule: 감자탕 from M40's 감자, and the 삼계탕 M59's 인삼 note held frozen ("the 삼 floating in 삼계탕 (ginseng-chicken soup — riding frozen)") — still frozen, but now you can read it: ginseng-chicken-soup.

M60's 녹색 note pre-poured it — "녹차 (green tea, riding frozen) is this 綠 poured over M2's 차" — and today it lands: 綠茶 green-tea, with 차 in its tea sense (that note's other sense, the car, is a homograph; context decides). Boseong's terraced 녹차밭 (frozen — tea fields) is the postcard; 녹차 아이스크림 (M9's 아이스크림) is the café's version. Counted in M5's 잔: 녹차 한 잔.

紅茶 red-tea: 紅 is a FIRST — no note has read it until now — and it explains why Korean (and Chinese) call black tea RED: the liquor gets named, not the leaf. The same 紅 was waiting inside 홍삼, which M59's 인삼 note left frozen ("steamed and aged it becomes 홍삼 (red ginseng — riding frozen)") — red ginseng now decodes itself. 홍차 is the teabag-and-milk register, the 카페 (M2) menu's least-ordered line and the 밀크티 (frozen) it hides inside.

M59's 인삼 ("人蔘 person-root") + 차: the gift-box tea — sachets of it fill every 명절 (M25) parcel, and hotel lobbies serve it to arriving guests. The radar from that note still holds: "this 삼 is root-蔘, not three (M2)". Bitter, earthy, sweetened with 꿀 (M40); the drink Korea pours when it wants you to feel looked after.

Lemon through the converter — the l lands as ㄹ, the vowels settle: 레몬. On this shelf it makes 레몬차 — lemon slices packed in honey in a jar, spooned into hot water — the 차 shelf's loan, beside 유자차 (frozen — the citron kind). M30's 오렌지 note set the precedent ("the native citrus is 귤"): imports keep their English names, the native fruit keeps its own. Count it with M5's 개: 레몬 한 개.

M2's 차 + M5's 잔 ("커피 한 잔, 물 두 잔") with the linking-ㅅ wedged in — the wedge M46's 오랫동안 filed ("with the linking-ㅅ wedged in") and M78's 부잣집 and M76's 숫자 both wore: 茶盞, the teacup — said 찯짠, rom chatjan. Radar, three cups: M18's 컵 is the object, M5's 잔 the count, 찻잔 the porcelain one with a saucer; 커피잔 (frozen) is its café twin.

차다 in its cold sense — M66's 차다 note listed it: "cold (바람이 차다 — also on your B-list, riding along here)" — wearing the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 on M1's 물, welded solid: cold water. M40's 얼음 note's "얼음물 arrives free at every 식당" is the iced kind; M18's 뜨겁다 is the opposite bowl. Two idioms: 찬물도 위아래가 있다 (even cold water has an order — the elder drinks first; the gap deck files it) and 찬물을 끼얹다 (끼얹다 frozen) = to throw cold water on a mood.

The persimmon, native: autumn's orange fruit, eaten crisp, left to soften into 홍시 (frozen), or dried into 곶감 — the one M49's 호랑이 note already starred ("the tiger flees a 곶감 (dried persimmon), having judged it scarier than himself"). The NIKL row here is the fruit; the C-row 감 is feeling-感, the suffix M57's 가능성 note described ("the way -감 bottles a feeling"). Radar in one sentence: 감이 좋다 = the persimmons are good — or I have a good feeling about this.

M9's 술 ("The umbrella word over 맥주 and 소주") + M5's 잔: the glass the alcohol goes in — 盞, the same hanja that ends 찻잔. Its verbs are the etiquette: 술잔을 채우다 (M37's 채우다 — that note ran "잔을 채워요 (the 건배 before-photo — 비우다's mirror)"), 술잔을 비우다 (M37's 비우다) = drain it, 술잔을 돌리다 (M37's 돌리다) = pass one cup around the table, the old ritual. M18's 건배 note has the clink ("Juniors clink lower and turn slightly away to drink"); M71's 한잔 ("close the space and the count becomes an occasion") is the invitation; the gap deck has the pour.

M9's 술 + M5's 병 — the bottle counter whose note also calls it the standalone word for a bottle: the liquor bottle — 소주병, 맥주병, the green glass Korea returns by the billion. Radar: M14's 병 — its note warned "get well before you count bottles" — gives 술병 a second reading, 酒病, the sickness from drinking: 술병이 났어요, with M28's 나다 = the drink made me ill. Same spelling, two hanja; the empties on the table tell you which.

M9's 술 + M12's 자리 (seat, spot): a drink-seat = the drinking OCCASION — the seat becomes the event. 술자리에서 is where careers and friendships get negotiated; M16's 회식 ("officially optional and practically not") is the office kind, and the night has floors — 이차, 삼차 (frozen — the second and third venues, read with M2's 이 and 삼), each one smaller and later. 오늘 술자리가 있어요 — on M1's 있다 — = I have drinks tonight, said with the exact tone of an obligation.

M9's 술 + M1's 집: the drink-house — the bar. M40's 치즈 note already sat you down there ("corn-cheese at every 술집"). The -집 shop suffix names a house by what it sells: 빵집, 꽃집, 고깃집 (all frozen — bread, flowers, meat), and M18's 맛집 by what it has. Nobody lives in a 술집; it is the M1 house-word wearing an apron.

en: wine (the Sino word: on labels, at church)
notes: M30's 포도 note pre-poured it — "포도주 the drink it becomes (주 = alcohol, 소주's 주 — the compound machine pours)" — and today the 酒 gets read: 葡萄酒 grape-alcohol, the alcohol-酒 that has been sitting inside M3's 맥주 (barley-酒) and 소주 (burned-酒) since Ring 1. The church's word and the label's word — 포도주 is what the priest pours and what the bottle prints; the menu says the next entry.

Wine through the converter: w becomes 와, the landing M78's 웨이터 note mapped ("w → 웨") one vowel over. 포도주 and 와인 are one liquid in two registers — 포도주 on paper and at Mass, 와인 at the 술집 and on the date: 와인 한 잔 (M5's 잔), 와인바 (frozen). The pair is this shelf's law in miniature: the Sino compound names the recipe, the loan names the scene.

M27's 중국 ("the Middle Country") + 집: not a house in China — the -집 rule again — but the Chinese-Korean restaurant, home of the delivery trinity: 자장면 (the noodles M30's 초콜릿 note fed the single — "Black Day in April, eating 자장면"), 짬뽕 and 탕수육 (both frozen). It is M18's 배달 ("anywhere, anything, absurdly fast") in its oldest form, and 이사 (M54) day is 중국집 day by custom: nobody unpacks a kitchen before the noodles arrive.

Curry — via Japan (カレー), which is why the r landed as ㄹ and the vowel as 에 rather than the English-route 커리 (frozen — the Indian-restaurant spelling): 카레 means the thick, mild Japanese-style curry over rice, 카레라이스 (라이스 frozen), the school lunch and the bachelor's Sunday pot. Two spellings, two cuisines; the converter's route decides the dish.

Sausage through the converter — the s lands as ㅅ, the soft g as ㅈ: 소시지. The lunchbox's pink standby (비엔나 소시지 — the little Vienna kind, frozen), a 편의점 (M6) counter snack, and the reason 부대찌개 (frozen — the army-base stew built from post-war American rations) exists. Beside M18's 돼지고기 it is the same animal, processed.

Native — an old word for a small woven box — now the packed meal itself. Two kinds: the school 도시락 M22's 소풍 note described ("김밥 mandatory, mothers up at dawn rolling it"), and the 편의점 도시락 — M6's 편의점 in front — that feeds the night shift for a few thousand 원 (M9). Its verb is 도시락을 싸다 — to pack — a homograph of M7's 싸다 (cheap), so 싼 도시락 is a cheap lunchbox or a packed one; context decides. M40's 챙기다 packs it for someone else.

M15's 종이 + M18's 컵 ("Konglish 'cup', one syllable"): the paper cup — the office water cooler's cup, the 자판기's cup, the church's after-service coffee. The plainest compound on the shelf, and the one 일회용품 (below) is mostly about: Korea burns through billions a year, and the café rule two entries down was written to stop it.

M72's 자동 note built it in passing — "자동 판매기 → clipped to 자판기 (the vending machine, riding frozen)" — and today it takes coins: 自販機, the self-自 of M72's 자동 + the sell-販 of M43's 판매 ("販賣 sell-sell") + the machine-機 M72's 기계 named ("the machine-機"), clipped to three syllables. M43's 동전 note already fed it ("The 500원 coin is the vending machine's favorite"). 커피 자판기 — the paper-cup coffee at a few hundred won in every office lobby — is the classic; the new ones take cards and sell everything.

en: bag (the one the product comes in); counter for bags
notes: 封紙 seal-paper: the seal-封 of M43's 봉투 ("封套 seal-sheath") + 紙, paper — the 지 of M27's 편지 and M30's 휴지 ("휴 (discard) + 지 (paper)"), read as a hanja here for the first time. RADAR, mandatory: M43's 봉투 is the envelope and the shop's carrier bag ("at every counter, the bag question: 봉투 필요하세요?"); 봉지 is the bag the product comes IN — 라면 봉지 with M3's 라면, 과자 봉지 with M9's 과자 — and a counter: 과자 한 봉지 = one bag of snacks.

The Konglish interlude's false-friend table filed it — English hears records, Korean means "a plastic bag (비닐봉지)". Vinyl came to mean any thin, crinkly plastic: 비닐 장갑 (M21's 장갑 — the clear gloves the 김장 (M26) crew wears), 비닐하우스 (frozen — the plastic greenhouse that is half of Korea's farmland skyline). Rule of thumb for the next entries: 비닐 crinkles, 플라스틱 snaps.

비닐 + 봉지: THE plastic bag — the checkout question rephrased. One honest line of culture: it has cost money for years and has been banned outright in supermarkets and big shops since 2019, so the bag now has a price and a politics, and the answer to 비닐봉지 필요하세요? (M16's 필요하다) is increasingly a shrug and a 가방 (M6). The black 비닐봉지 from the market stall is old Korea; the reusable 장바구니 (frozen — the shopping basket) is the new.

Plastic with the ㅡ-cushions installed — five syllables from two, the interlude's law that "Konglish is often LONGER than its source". This is the rigid kind: 플라스틱 병 (M5's 병), 플라스틱 컵 (M18's 컵), 플라스틱 용기 (frozen — container). Radar vs 비닐: 비닐 is what crinkles, 플라스틱 is what snaps — and both end up where M13's 쓰레기 note said ("Korea sorts it strictly"), in the 분리수거 (frozen — sorted collection) bins every apartment block polices on its own night.

Dismounted from M9's 포장하다 ("포장해 주세요 — to go, please. Also gift-wrapping; context decides") the way s9_togo already split it ("포장 (wrapping) + 하다 + 주세요 — the takeout sentence"): 包裝 wrap-dress — the wrap-包 M52's 소포 landed ("小包 small-wrap") + 裝 (to dress, to fit out — frozen; NOT the 粧 of M6's 화장실). Three jobs: 포장 = takeout (포장 돼요? — can I get it to go?), 선물 포장 — M9's 선물 in front — = gift wrapping, and the packaging on everything in this drawer. And the tent M18's 떡볶이 note pitched — "sold from every orange tent (포장마차)" — is a WRAPPED cart (마차 frozen): a 포장마차 is packaging you can eat in.

一回用: M2's 일 (one) + 回 (a round, a time — the turn-back-回 M53's 회복하다 read as "回復 turn-back-restore"; as a counter it rides frozen — 일회, 이회 — doing in print what M12's 번 does in speech) + the use-用 M43's 비용 filed ("the use-用 you've owned since 사용하다 (M10) and pocketed in M37's 용돈 (use-money)"): one-round-use. It sits bare in front of the thing: 일회용 컵, 일회용 젓가락 (M18), 일회용 비닐봉지. Radar on the 회: M18's 회 (raw fish) is 膾, the gather-會 inside M16's 회식 is a meeting, this 回 is the round.

일회용 + the goods-品 of M43's 제품 ("品 stacks three boxes into 'goods'"): single-use goods as a category — the word on the sign, not the cup. 일회용품 사용 금지 (S2's 사용 and 금지) is the 2022 café rule that took the paper cup off the counter for anyone sitting down; 일회용품 줄이기 — M37's 줄이다 nominalized with -기 from M13 — is the campaign on every 편의점 (M6) door. The packaging drawer closes on its verdict: Korean names food by assembly and packaging by judgment, and this word is the judgment.

The bare noun inside M36's 안전하다 — that note decoded it ('peace-entire: safe. Two owned roots collide beautifully') and already ran it bare ('drive safe; 안전벨트 = the belt'): 安全, the peace-安 of M33's 안부 + the all-全 of M31's 전국. This is the M75 move, 'Dismount — verb → bare noun, the way print writes', run on an adjective: 안전 제일 (M22's 제일) = safety first, the slogan on every construction fence; 안전을 위해서 with M32's 위하다 = for safety; 안전 운전 on the highway sign, where the mouth says 안전하게 운전하세요 — the -게 adverbializer from M33 on M10's 운전하다. 안전벨트 keeps its 벨트 (riding frozen). The gap deck has the slogan and its named failure.

有名 have-name: the having-有 the S3 appendix tabled ('without / having | 무료 · 무궁화 · 유료 · 유명하다') + the name-名 of M5's 명 and M25's 명절, which M75's 절약하다 note read as 名節 ('the named ones'). M17's 유명하다 said 'For now: 이 선수가 유명해요' — dismounted, the root is a determiner in print: 유명 배우 (M48's 배우), 유명 브랜드 (브랜드 riding frozen); 유명인 (frozen) = a celebrity, and 유명세 (frozen) = the tax of fame, what the 유명 pay in privacy. Speech keeps the 하다: 유명해요, 유명한 with the badge from M24.

親切 close-earnest: the close-親 the S3 appendix tabled ('close | 친구 · 친절하다') + 切, a FIRST — earnest, wholehearted; the same hanja means cut elsewhere, one line. M4's 친절하다 ('Polite: 친절해요') mounts it, and M24's 착하다 drew the line ('M4's 친절하다 is kind BEHAVIOR; 착하다 is kind NATURE'). It is the review word — M78's 점원 note put 점원이 친절해요 in a review — and bare it is the banner word: 친절 교육 (M32's 교육) = courtesy training, 친절한 직원 (M16's 직원) on the poster; 불친절 (frozen) is the one-star complaint.

en: importance (as a bare determiner: important, key)
notes: 重要: M41's 체중 weighed the first half ('The 중 is heavy-重, the same weight sitting inside 중요하다 (M16)'), M57's 주요 named the second ('essential-要 — the 요 that has been sitting inside 중요하다 (M16) and 필요하다 (M16) all along') and drew the radar — 중요 'says it MATTERS', 주요 says it leads the list. M16's 중요하다 ('For now: 회의가 중요해요') is where you met it. Bare, print's determiner: 중요 서류 (M16's 서류) = important documents, 중요 사항 (사항 — items, riding frozen) on every form; the mouth says 중요한 with the badge from M24. Its -성 product is next.

Pays M57's 가능성 verbatim: the -성 factory 'ships 중요성 and 필요성 off the same belt' — here is the first product. 重要性: 중요 + the nature-性 that M57 named, which bottles a thing's nature the way M39's 자신감 bottles a feeling with -감. M32's 교육 + 의 중요성 = the importance of education — the opening line of every essay; 중요성을 강조하다 (M56's 강조하다) = to stress the importance, the news verb. 필요성 (frozen) is the belt's other product.

en: being active, positive drive (the root of 적극적)
notes: M45's 적극적 decoded it ('piled-to-the-pole: effort stacked as high as it goes') and ran the stutter line ('root 적극 + suffix 적 — the machine stamps without listening'): here is the root, bare. 적극 추천 (the 추천 inside M18's 추천하다, dismounted the same way) = highly recommended, the sticker on the shelf; 적극 지지 (지지 — support, riding frozen) in the editorial; M45's 적 + M6's 으로 make 적극적으로 = actively, in the mouth. The mirror still rides frozen — M45 said 'Its mirror 소극적 (pulled-back, passive — not yet taught)', and 소극 waits with it.

高速: M50's 고속도로 decoded it ('high-speed-way-road: 최고's high-高 (M19) + speed-速 (new — the 속 inside everything fast Korea builds)') — today, minus the road; M57's 속도 ('the factory's one Sino ruler') carries the same 速. Bare on the timetable: 고속버스, which M50's 터미널 note parked at its terminal; 고속열차, which M50's 열차 note called 'the high-speed one'; 고속 충전 (충전 — charging, riding frozen) on the phone box. Radar holds from M57: 'this 속 is speed-速, not M28's inside-속'.

事務 affairs-duties — and four receipts, paid: M16's 사무실 ('office work'), M43's 근무 ('the 사무 was office-TASKS all along'), M43's 사업 ('the 사 of 사무실 (M16's office was an 事務-room)'), M57's 업무 ('the duty-務 of 사무실 (M16, an 事務-room)'). Bare: 사무직 (frozen) = desk jobs, 사무용 (the use-用 of M43's 비용) = for office use, 사무를 보다 = to handle office business — M1's 보다 in its take-care-of job. M58's 총장 note left 사무총장 frozen; it still rides that way.

移動: the move-移 of M54's 이사 ('move-migrate') + the move-動 of M57's 활동 ('the move-動 that 자동차 (M50) decoded out of 운동하다 (M8)'). The sign word: 이동 중 (the busy-sign 중 from S2), M12's 자리 + 이동 = a seat change, 이동 통신 (M48's 통신) = mobile telecom. 이동하다 is M50's 움직이다 ('The everything-mover') in print — the sentence deck moves a concert indoors with it. Radar trio: M50's 옮기다 moves a thing, M54's 이사 moves a household, 이동 moves a position.

保護: the 保 M43's 보험 decoded ('keeping-safe — insurance, decoded, is protection purchased against the drop') + 護 guard — a FIRST by decode: M78's 운전기사 note only spelled M16's 변호사 as 辯護士, and M14's 간호사 is 看護, watch-guard, a decode that note never gave. 환경 보호 — M32's 환경 note kept it with M26's 지키다, the native verb; 보호하다 is the Sino one, and print prefers it. 보호자 (the person-者 of M43's 소비자) = the guardian on every hospital form; M22's 동물 + 보호 on the shelter banner.

共同: 共 together — a FIRST, and NOT the 公 of M6's 공원, which M43's 공장 note filed as public ('rests on public-公 M6') — + the same-同 of M38's 동시 ('The 동 is same-同, not east-東'). Together as a unit, on paper: 공동 구매 (구매 — purchase, riding frozen) = group buying, 공동 생활 (M29's 생활) = communal living, 공동 명의 (frozen) on the deed; 공동체 (frozen) = a community. Radar vs M9's 같이 and M29's 함께: the adverbs say together, 공동 files it.

en: formal, official, regular (正式); (homograph) a set meal (定食)
notes: 正式: the correct-正 M63's 정확하다 landed ('correct-solid: 정답's 正 (M44 — the one hiding inside 정말 since M11)') + M55's 식 ('the way-hanja'): the proper way. 정식 직원 (M16's 직원) = a regular employee, not a contract one; M6's 으로 makes 정식으로 = formally, officially. RADAR, mandatory: the restaurant's 정식 is 定食 — the set-定 of M33's 정하다 + the food-食 of M18's 한식 — the set meal, and 한정식 (frozen) is the full Korean spread. NIKL lists 正式; your street lists both, and only the 하다 or the tray tells you which.

Pays M32's 글 verbatim: that note filed 글자 = 'a written character'. 글 + 字 — the character-字 that M76's 숫자 traced through M27's 한자 and M20's 문자. A letter on the page: 한 글자 (the 한 that M5's 하나 contracts to) = one character, M1's 작다: 글자가 작아요 = the print is small, the reading-glasses complaint. Radar: not M71's 자 (breath), not the thing-子 that M54's 상자 note capped its box with. 글자 is what M26's 한글 is made of.

M32's 글 + M10's 쓰다 'through the -기 nominalizer from M13' — the weld M76's 가로 note ran for 가로쓰기, now standing on its own. Writing as a SKILL: the language-class quartet 말하기, 듣기, 읽기, 쓰기 (all frozen — the four boxes on every syllabus) and this one, the one nobody practises: 글쓰기 수업 (M10's 수업), 글쓰기 실력 (M26's 실력). 띄어쓰기, the spacing interlude, came off the same machine — 띄다 + 쓰기.

en: our language — Korean, from the inside
notes: M4's 우리 + M4's 말 — that note filed 말 as the 말 of 반말 and 한국말, the colloquial 한국어 — welded solid the way M27's 우리나라 was ('One word, written solid — the possessive pronoun fused into the map'). M44's 국어 drew two doors ('foreigners study 한국어; Korean kids sit through 국어 시간 — same language, different door'); 우리말 is the third door, the warm one: 우리말 사랑 on the classroom poster, 우리말 쓰기 = the purist campaign for Korean words over loanwords. Say it and you are speaking from inside the house.

M55's 각 ('each: 각 나라 (M23) = each country') + the country-國 of M31's 국가: the notice-board version of 각 나라. M23's 세계 + 각국 = the countries of the world — the frame every foreign-desk story opens with; 각국 정부 (M32's 정부) = governments everywhere. The register line in M55's 각 note holds: speech trails 마다 from M31 after the noun (나라마다), print stamps 각국 in front.

Pays M48's 대중 — that note already spelled it out, 대중문화 = pop culture, on M26's 문화. 大衆文化: the crowd-衆 of 대중 + culture, filed as a field: 대중문화 평론 (평론 — criticism, riding frozen), 한국 대중문화 = K-culture on the syllabus. M26's 한류 ('the wave that carried 드라마, 케이팝, and probably you to this app') is its export wing; the sentence deck quotes a newspaper on it.

M29's 생활 (life as it is actually lived) + M32's 환경 ('ring-boundary: the environment'): the ring around a life — the housing-survey phrase. 생활환경이 좋다 (M1's 좋다) = good living conditions, the estate agent's line; 생활환경 개선 (개선 — improvement, riding frozen) in the city plan. Four-syllable welds are print's habit: M77's 일상생활 is the sibling, welded the same way from M38's 일상.

M64's 등록 ('climbing your detail up onto the official record') + the money-金 M60's 금 landed ('the metal itself, at last'): the fee for being on the books = tuition. M44's 장학금 pays it — that note said the scholarship is 'aimed at tuition'. 등록금 인상 — the 인상 M41 warned about ('the news-인상 of 가격 인상 (price hike) is a different hanja') — = a tuition hike, the campus-protest word. Says 등녹끔: the ㄹ bows to the ㅇ before it — the rule M32's 대통령 note filed ('ㄹ after ㅇ nasalizes') — rom deungnokgeum.

M1's 한국 + M45's 적 ('a dependent noun that bolts onto a Sino noun'): Korean-ish. 한국적인 것 (M17's 것 under the badge from M24) = something quintessentially Korean; M29's 가장 + 한국적인 = the most Korean — the tourism slogan, and the sentence deck's verdict on a painting. M45's 세계적 is the precedent — same stamp, aimed at home. Print keeps the bare 한국적; the mouth adds 인 or 으로 (한국적으로 = in a Korean way).

Pays M27's 독일 verbatim — that note listed 독일어 first and ruled 'every machine applies'. [나라] + 어, the language machine M27 taught (the ledger's 일본어 and 중국어 rows are the same machine): the 어 is the language-語 M42's 어색하다 traced ('the language-語 of 한국어 (M1), 단어 (M10), 언어 (M26)'). Here because the NIKL list bothered to list it, and because it says 도기러 — the liaison M27 filed as 'said 도길', carried one syllable further.

M8's 신문 + the company-社 M32's 사회 flipped ('gather-meet: society. Flip the syllables and you get 회사') and M52's 여행사 stamped onto M11's 여행: the newspaper as a company. 신문사 기자 (M16's 기자) = a staff reporter; 신문사 조사 (M44's 조사) = a newspaper's survey, the sentence deck's source. M48's 언론 note left 언론사 frozen ('a news organization') — the wider word; 조선일보 and 한겨레 (frozen) are the two ends of the shelf, one line.

野 field — the field-야 of M17's 야구 that M18's 야채 called 'the SAME field-야 as 야구' — + M55's 외 ('the outside-root, finally solo'): out in the field = outdoors. 야외 공연 (M48's 공연), 야외 활동 (M57's 활동), 야외 결혼식 (M25's 결혼식) — the sentence deck rains one out. Radar: M71's 야 is breath; the 야 of M16's 야근하다 is night; and M65's 실내 gave the mirror ('inside / outside') — 실외 (frozen) is merely not-inside, 야외 is the open sky.

市 — the city-市 of M31's 시청 and M50's 시민 — + 외: outside the city. 시외버스 is the bus that shares M50's 터미널 with the 고속버스; 시외 전화 (M20's 전화) = a long-distance call, the phrase your parents paid by the minute for. Radar pair with M12's 시내: 시내버스 / 시외버스 — same bus, different map — and the 시 radar M31 opened (city, o'clock, exam) keeps its three rows.

種 kind: the seed-種 M63's 각종 found inside M57's 종류, which decoded it ('seed-sort: things filed by what they grew from'). Bare, it counts kinds: M5's 셋 contracts before it — 세 종 = three kinds — and M29's 여러 + 종 = several kinds — and it is the species on a zoo sign. SENSE COLLAPSE, mandatory: NIKL's C-row 종 is 鐘, the bell of M31's 종로 ('Bell Road — named for 보신각') — 종을 치다 (M17's 치다) = ring the bell. And M38's 종일 is a third ('The 종 is end-終'). Seed, bell, end: three 종s, one spelling.

質: the substance-質 M45's 성질 found ('the substance-質 hiding inside 질문 (M10 — a question asks after the substance)'). Quality, bare and spoken: M1's 좋다 and M29's 나쁘다 grade it (질이 좋다, 질이 나쁘다); M7's 높다 under the badge from M24, on M32's 교육, gives 질 높은 교육 = quality education; M63's 양 on the 보다-particle from M22 gives 양보다 질 = quality over quantity. 품질 (frozen) is the label's word; 질 is the mouth's. Radar: M10's 질문 asks after this 質; M57's 질서 is rank-秩, a different 질.

高級: the high-高 of M19's 최고 + 級 grade — a FIRST: the step in 학급 (a class), 등급 (a rating), 초급 and 중급 (beginner, intermediate — all frozen). High on the ladder: 고급 레스토랑 (레스토랑 riding frozen — it belongs to the loanword shelf), 고급 한국어 = advanced Korean, which is what this app's last ring is. Radar: M38's 급하다 is urgent-急, not grade-級 — the rush and the rank share a sound.

預金: 預 deposit — a FIRST; radar vs the beforehand-豫 of M52's 예약 ('ahead-promise') and M33's 예 (yes; example) — + M60's 금. Money entrusted to M6's 은행: 예금하다 = to deposit, 예금 통장 (M43's 통장: 'the little booklet the ATM fills line by line'), 예금 이자 (이자 — interest, riding frozen). M43's 저축 ('saving as a discipline') is the habit; 예금 is the account it lands in — the sentence deck feeds one half a salary at a time.

住宅: 住 live — a FIRST, the 주 M12's 주소 never decoded; not the master-主 of M27's 주인, not M8's 주 (week) — + 宅 house, a FIRST too: the 댁 of M27's 댁 ('upgraded for elders') is this hanja read honorifically, and the 택배 M54's 상자 note left frozen is this 宅 as well — home delivery. A house as a category — the census, the mortgage: 주택 가격 (M21's 가격), 단독주택 (frozen) vs M13's 아파트, the Korean housing binary; 주택가 (frozen) = a residential street. The mouth says M1's 집.

en: motive, motivation (動機); (homograph) a peer from the same intake (同期)
notes: 動機 motive: the move-動 of M57's 활동 + the machine-機 of M72's 기계 and M33's 기회 — what MOVES you. M44's 학습 + 동기 = learning motivation; 동기 부여 (부여 — granting, riding frozen) = motivating people, the HR word. SENSE COLLAPSE, mandatory: NIKL's C-row 동기 is 同期 — same period — the cohort: 입사 동기 (입사 — joining a company, riding frozen) = the people hired the same year, M15's 대학교 + 동기 = the people who entered with you — the bond M69's 동창 drew ('A schoolmate from back then, forever'), one rung tighter. The gap deck files the cohort; the sentence deck meets it ten years on.

副作用: 副 secondary — a FIRST, NOT the copies-部 of M76's 부 nor the section-部 of M32's 부분 — + 作用, the make-作 of M48's 작가 + the use-用 of M43's 비용: a secondary working = a side effect. M10's 약 + 의 부작용; 부작용이 있어요/없어요 on the 있다-chassis — the pharmacy question, the one the sentence deck answers with a trip to M6's 병원. Off the shelf it is the policy metaphor too: every law has its 부작용.

國立: the country-國 of M31's 국가 + 立 stand — a FIRST: the hanja under M14's 서다 and M12's 세우다, which M14 glossed as 'make it stand'. Made to stand by the state: 국립 박물관 (M23's 박물관), 국립 대학교 (M15's 대학교); the family 사립, 시립, 도립 (frozen — private, city, provincial) reads by its first syllable. Said 궁닙: the ㄹ bows to the ㄴ the way M57's 종류 note filed it ('the ㄹ bows to the ㄴ'), then the ㄱ nasalizes the way M32's 국민 says 궁민 — rom gungnip. Taught last on purpose: the notice board's proudest word.

Fashion through the converter — f → ㅍ, sh → ㅅ+ㅕ — and the shelf's oldest IOU, paid three times at once: the 잡지 note (M48) ran '패션 잡지, 시사 잡지', the 모델 note (M72) filed '패션 모델 — 패션 riding frozen', and the 디자이너 note (M78) ran '패션 디자이너 (패션 riding frozen'. All three collocations are yours today, plus 패션쇼 (쇼 — riding frozen). Neighbor-word radar, the module's law: 패션 is the industry and the field; M21's 스타일 ('제 스타일이에요 — it's my style') is what YOU wear; M21's 유행 ('유행이에요 — it's in style') is the trend itself. 패션 감각 (감각 — a sense, riding frozen) is having taste in all three.

Belt, with the converter's ㅡ-cushion on the final t — the 테스트 rule, one syllable short. Three notes have carried it frozen: M36's 안전하다 ('안전벨트 = the belt'), M60's 매다 ('안전벨트를 매세요 (seatbelt, riding frozen)'), and M78's 챔피언 ('챔피언 벨트 (벨트 riding frozen)') — all paid today, and 매다 is its verb: 벨트를 매다. The native word for the same strip of leather is 허리띠 — M14's 허리 + 띠, a band, riding frozen: grandparents say 허리띠, shops sell 벨트, and 허리띠를 졸라매다 (tighten the belt — riding frozen) is the recession idiom in either register.

Button — but only the kind you PRESS: M20's 누르다 ('르-family: 눌러요. Buttons, links, elevator floors, and the 좋아요 below') is its verb, 버튼을 누르다, and the 취소 note (M75) left it frozen ('취소 버튼 (버튼 — riding frozen)') beside the 확인 button every screen pairs it with. Radar, Rule 4 of the interlude: the button sewn on a shirt is native 단추 (riding frozen) — 버튼 is pressed, 단추 is done up. 시작 버튼 (M8's 시작하다, dismounted), the elevator's floor buttons, the phone's 홈 버튼: the loan took the machines and left the sewing box alone.

The interlude's own specimen — 'test → 테스트 (one syllable becomes three)' — and the rule M51's 콘서트 note named after it ('the 테스트 rule: crowded consonants get vowels'). RADAR, mandatory, against 시험 (M10): a 시험 is sat and graded (시험을 보다); a 테스트 is TRIED — 테스트하다 = to test a product, 테스트를 받다 = to get tested, and the 심리 note (M67) filed the one Korea does for fun ('심리 테스트 is the personality quiz Korea loves'). M44's 검사 ('檢査 check-examine') is the inspection, medical or mechanical. Three words for one English one: the exam, the trial, the check.

Box, cushioned to two syllables — and the Rule 4 pair that opens the module's thesis: M54's 상자 ('箱子 box-thing') is the dictionary's word, 박스 is the shop sign's, and both live. That note's 택배 상자 is 택배 박스 on the delivery slip; 사과 한 박스 — M3's 사과 — counts by the box the way M5 counts by the bottle; and M50's 교통사고 note already installed one on your windshield ('every Korean windshield carries a 블랙박스 (Konglish: dashcam)') — a made-in-Korea sense English never had. The loan took the counting and the compounds; 상자 kept the dictionary.

The counter — NIKL glosses it 계산대, the checkout the 계산 note (M76) left frozen ('계산대 (the checkout — riding frozen) is where it happens'). 카운터에서 계산하세요 with M9's 계산하다 ('계산해 주세요 — check, please') = pay at the counter; the front desk of M23's 호텔 and the bar's row of stools are 카운터 too — 카운터 자리 (M12's 자리) is the seat facing the cook. Rule 4 radar: it is never a person who counts, and the register itself is 계산대 on the sign, 카운터 in the mouth.

Mail — the word the 이메일 note (M16) pre-paid: '메일 alone also works — Korean rarely means postal mail by it.' So 메일 = email, nearly always: 메일을 보내다 (M16's 보내다), 메일을 확인하다 (M20's 확인하다), 메일 주소 (M12's 주소) = your email address, 메일함 (the inbox — riding frozen). The paper kind stays native and Sino: M27's 편지 ('편지를 쓰다/받다') is the letter, M52's 소포 the parcel, and M27's 우체국 handles both. Rule 4 in its cleanest form — the loan took the screen and left the post office.

Media, in the academic and newsroom register: 소셜 미디어 is what the West says where M20's 에스엔에스 note filed Korea's word ('Korea says SNS — es-en-es — where English says social media'). Sort the shelf: M48's 언론 ('The press as an institution') is the institution, M32's 방송 is the act of broadcasting, the Sino synonym 매체 (媒體, the medium — riding frozen) is what the dictionary says, and 미디어 is the channels taken together as a field — 미디어 회사 (M2's 회사), 미디어 아트, 뉴미디어. The loan lives in compounds and syllabi; the news you actually watch is still M24's 뉴스.

Underwear, not trousers — the British-English trap, and Rule 4 at its most embarrassing: 팬티 is what goes under M21's 바지. M51's 팬 note showed the f → ㅍ rule landing two English words on one syllable ('The converter's f → ㅍ rule runs twice and lands both English words on one syllable'); this is a third landing, unrelated to either — no fandom, no skillet. The category word 속옷 (underwear — riding frozen, on M7's 옷) is what the shop-floor sign says; 팬티 is the item. Say it about laundry and children, never about what a colleague is wearing.

Home page, specialized by Rule 4: in Korean a 홈페이지 is the WHOLE website, not its front door — 회사 홈페이지 with M2's 회사, 학교 홈페이지 with M1's 학교, 홈페이지에서 확인하세요 with M20's 확인하다 = check on the website. M20's 사이트 is the same thing one register down and one syllable shorter: the official notice says 홈페이지, the friend says 사이트. 홈 alone rides frozen — the phone's 홈 버튼, baseball's home plate.

Film — the roll inside M20's 카메라 and the stock M2's 영화 was shot on; M48's 촬영 ('撮影 snatch-shadow: filming is catching shadows before they move on') is what it caught. The l-m pile gets a cushion: 필름, two syllables. Today the roll is retro — 필름 카메라 is the hipster's — the window tint is 선팅 필름 (riding frozen), and the word's real Korean life is a metaphor: 필름이 끊기다, with M36's 끊기다 ('modern life is a list of things that 끊기다'), is the film cutting out mid-reel = blacking out drunk. The gap deck pours it.

Group — rank 879, the highest word on this shelf, because it works three jobs: the K-pop 아이돌 그룹 (아이돌 — riding frozen), 걸그룹 and 보이그룹; the conglomerate — 삼성그룹, the 대기업 M64 filed ('The big firm is the big one, not the counted one'); and any bunch of people. Put it against its Korean neighbors: M16's 팀 ('우리 팀 — M4's warm 우리 extends to the office') has a job, M23's 단체 ('단체 여행 — the guided tour') has a registration, M69's 모임 ('any recurring get-together') has a calendar — 그룹 is the loose one, a set of people with nothing but the set in common. The sentence deck splits a 팀 into 그룹s.

PC, spelled the way the mouth says it — NIKL lists the word as PC and the sign says PC방, but the syllables are 피시, and sentence Korean writes them: 피시방. M8's 방 note filed the room ('Also in 노래방 (karaoke room) and PC방') beside M17's 노래방, and g17_bang owns the rented-room economy; 피시 is the machine itself in initials — M10's 컴퓨터 for short. Say 피시 for the desktop tower and the gaming café; say M20's 노트북 for the one on your lap — Korean keeps the two apart the way English does not.

Monitor — the screen as HARDWARE: 모니터를 사다, 모니터가 크다, 듀얼 모니터 (riding frozen) on every developer's desk. M20's 화면 ('화 (picture) + 면 (surface): picture-surface') is what is ON it — the picture, the display, the thing you tap: 화면이 안 나와요 complains about the image, 모니터가 고장 났어요 (S2's 고장) about the box. Verbed it keeps its English: 모니터하다 / 모니터링 (riding frozen) = to keep watch over, said of markets, patients, and interns.

Tape — the sticky roll that M37's 붙이다 ('스티커를 붙여요') sticks: 테이프로 붙이다, 박스를 테이프로 감다 (M41's 감다, wind). The brand-as-noun is 스카치테이프 (riding frozen), the way English says Scotch tape; the other sense is the cassette — 녹음 테이프 with M48's 녹음, 비디오테이프 — which is what grandparents still mean by the word. Cushion count: t-a-p-e is one syllable in English, three in Korean — the interlude's law that 'Konglish is often LONGER than its source'.

File — and the 날아가다 note (M49) already mourned it: '파일이 날아갔어요 = the unsaved file, mourned in every office'. Its verbs are all taught: 파일을 저장하다 (M20's 저장하다 — the fix), 파일을 보내다 (M16's 보내다), 파일을 지우다 (M20's 지우다), and the sentence deck runs the loss through -아/어 버리다 from M52. Radar: the paper folder with the clip is ALSO a 파일 — the plastic one on every 사무실 (M16) desk — and M16's 서류 is what goes inside it. One loan, both the digital and the cardboard sense; English split them, Korean kept one.

Accessory, five syllables of cushion — the interlude's warning that 'Konglish is often LONGER than its source' at its longest: ac-ces-so-ry becomes 액-세-서-리, an 스 wedged into the middle. M21's 넥타이 note set the verb ('An accessory, so it takes 하다'): 액세서리를 하다 = to wear accessories — the umbrella over M21's 목걸이, 귀걸이, and 반지, none of which take M8's 입다. Shops sign it 악세사리; the misspelling is more common than the standard — the app teaches the dictionary form and expects the street to disagree.

Blouse: the b-l pile cushioned to 블, the final s to 스 — four syllables from one. A woman's dress shirt, in the office register: 블라우스 beside M21's 셔츠 (the shirt), under M21's 코트, over M21's 치마, and beside M21's 원피스, the interlude's Rule 3 specimen. Worn with M8's 입다, like every garment with sleeves. The department store's sign reads 블라우스 and the dictionary has no Korean synonym for it — this is a loan that filled a gap, not one that took a job.

Restaurant — with the French r-tail Korean kept: 레스토랑, never 레스토런, because the word came through the kitchen and not the classroom. Rule 4 by register: M2's 식당 is any place that serves food; 레스토랑 is the Western or upscale one — 이탈리안 레스토랑, 호텔 레스토랑 with M23's 호텔, and the 1990s chains that were 패밀리 레스토랑 (riding frozen). M52's 예약 goes with it more than with 식당; so does 와인 (riding frozen — a later shelf). A 김치찌개 is eaten at a 식당, a steak at a 레스토랑, and the same room can be both depending on who is paying.

Golf, cushioned: g-o-l-f → 골프. M17's 치다 note listed the racket and the keyboard ('The strike-play verb: 피아노를 치다, 기타를 치다, 테니스를 치다') and the club joins the list: 골프를 치다. Korea's golf is corporate and expensive — the business round is how deals used to close — and the crowd that actually plays does it indoors: 스크린 골프 (riding frozen), the simulator bars the gap deck files. The sentence deck makes a weekend habit of it with -기로 하다 from M48.

골프 + the place-場 that M37's 주차장 note paved ('The -장 (場, grounds) also paves 정류장 (M12) and 운동장'): the golf course. Same rail as M51's 경기장 and M37's 주차장 — the -장 takes any activity and grants it ground. 골프장에 가다 is the executive's Saturday; 골프장 회원 (M58's 회원) is the status symbol, since a course membership costs what an apartment does. Radar: this 장 is 場, not the chief-長 of M58's 부장 nor M30's 장, the counter for flat things.

Badminton, five syllables — d-m cushioned to 드민, the final n kept. M17's 치다 again (배드민턴을 치다), and the most democratic sport in the country: nets strung across every 공원 (M6) at dusk, 아파트 (M13) courtyards, school gyms — no 골프장 fee, one 셔틀콕 (riding frozen) per family. Korea's badminton is also elite (Olympic medals every cycle), but the word mostly means the retired couple in matching tracksuits at seven in the morning.

M11's 스키 ('스키를 타다 — ride skis, like every vehicle since M6') + the place-場 of 골프장 above: the ski resort. M31's 강원도 note already placed them ('ski country, summer beaches, and the 2018 Winter Olympics (평창)'); the resorts are a two-hour bus from Seoul, and 스키장에 가다 is the December plan of every 대학생 (M15). Same rail: 골프장, 스키장, 경기장 (M51), 주차장 (M37) — the -장 does not care whether the ground is grass, snow, or asphalt.

Skate, cushioned front and back: s-k → 스케, final t → 트. M6's 타다 is its verb — 스케이트를 타다 — on M40's 얼음, at the rink or on the frozen 한강 (M22). The kinds ride frozen: 피겨 스케이팅 (figure skating — the sport 김연아 made a national religion at the 2010 Olympics), 스피드 스케이팅, and 인라인 (the wheeled kind). Radar: 스케이트 is the boot and the act; 스케이트장 is the rink — the -장 rail, one more time.

Oven — the converter's v → ㅂ, then a cushion: 오븐. The immigrant appliance: Korean kitchens ran on the stovetop the 가스 note (M40) filed (가스레인지) and the microwave the 전자 note (M72) left frozen ('전자레인지 (the microwave — riding frozen'), and the oven arrived with M2's 빵 and M19's 케이크 — most apartments still have none. M18's 굽다 is its verb: 오븐에 굽다 = to bake, the same verb that grills 삼겹살. And the 에어프라이어 (air fryer — riding frozen) took the oven's job in the 2020s before it ever fully had one.

Lighter — l → ㄹ, the -er → 터, the same -er as M78's 디자이너 and M10's 컴퓨터. The smoker's tool: M14's 담배 and 피우다 need it, and the two asks are 라이터 있어요? and 불 좀 빌려주세요 — M13's 불 ('One word for fire and the lights') through M69's 빌리다 ('빌려주다 = to lend'): in Korean a light is borrowed, not given. Radar: the writer is M48's 작가 ('if it gets written, a 작가 signed it'); English lighter and writer both arrive as 라이터 (카피라이터 — the copywriter), and only one of them is sold at the 편의점 (M6) counter.
