Lens, z → ㅈ: 렌즈. Two jobs: the contact — 콘택트렌즈 clipped to 렌즈 by Rule 2, the clip machine — and the glass on a 카메라 (M20). The 안경 note (M21) gave the verbs ('안경을 쓰다 OR 끼다'), and the contact takes only the fitted one: 렌즈를 끼다 with M21's 끼다 in the morning, 렌즈를 빼다 with M53's 빼다 at night. Radar: 안경 is the frame on your face, 렌즈 the glass in it — 안경 렌즈 is the pair together, and 안경 renders 렌즈 unnecessary, which is the whole sales pitch.

Poster, cushioned: p-o-s-t-er → 포스터. On M13's 벽 with M37's 붙이다 (포스터를 붙이다), advertising with M32's 광고 ('廣告 wide-tell'), announcing M48's 공연 — whose note warned what happens when you read one badly ('When the poster says 공연 연기, read carefully: the show is postponed, not acting'). 영화 포스터 on M2's 영화, 콘서트 포스터 on M51's 콘서트, and 벽보 (the wall notice — riding frozen), the older register's name for the same sheet.

Memo — but in Korean a 메모 is a jotted note, not the office circular: 메모하다 = to jot down, 메모를 남기다 with M37's 남기다 = to leave a note. M15's 공책 ('공 (blank) + 책 (book): a blank-book') holds it, M10's 쓰다 writes it, and M34's 기억 ('기억이 안 나요 = it's not coming to me') is why you needed one. 메모지 (the pad — riding frozen) is the sticky square on the 냉장고 (M13). Radar: 메모리 (the phone's memory — riding frozen) shares five letters and nothing else.

Pack — NIKL's gloss — and two Korean jobs the English word never held together: the carton, 우유 팩 with M2's 우유, and the sheet mask, 마스크팩 — M14's 마스크 + 팩 — K-beauty's biggest export, the face-shaped sheet you leave on for twenty minutes. 팩을 하다 = to do a face mask, a phrase every cosmetics ad runs. The carton counts too: 우유 한 팩. Radar: 팩스 (fax, one syllable longer — riding frozen) is a different machine entirely.

Gum — with a tense ㄲ the converter does not usually install: English g lands on ㄱ (골프, 그룹), but 껌 tensed, the way M2's 빵 ('Starts with tense ㅃ') did on its way from Portuguese. M41's 씹다 ('잘 씹어 드세요 — chew well') is its verb: 껌을 씹다. The culture: 껌 is what you chew to hide M9's 술 or M14's 담배 on your breath, and what 껌값 — gum money — measures: dirt cheap, the gap deck's idiom on M7's 싸다. Last word on the shelf and the shortest: one syllable, one tense consonant, the whole converter in miniature.

M22's 강 + M1's 물 with NO linking-ㅅ — the wedge only goes between two open syllables, and 강 already ends in a consonant: river-water, the river as a moving thing rather than a line on a map. 강물이 흐르다 runs on M35's 흐르다 ("Water, time, tears, music — Korean lets them all 흐르다"), M74's 흘러가다 carries it downstream, and 강물처럼 (처럼 from M41) is the ballad simile for anything that keeps going. M22's 한강 is the 강 Seoul means, and M40's 얼다 note already froze it: "most winters 한강이 얼어요" — that is 강물, stopped.

M11's 바다 + linking-ㅅ + M1's 물 — the same wedge M23's 바닷가 wore ("M11's 바다 + 가 (edge): the sea's edge"), now on the water itself. Says 바단물: the ㅅ lands as a ㄷ, then nasalizes before the ㅁ — the assimilation the rom keeps, as M49's 나뭇잎 did. 바닷물이 짜요 — M3's 짜다, the kitchen's salty, tasted at the beach — is the first thing every child reports; 바닷물에 발을 담그다 (M40's 담그다) is the second.

M11's 비 + linking-ㅅ + 물: rain-water — says 빈물, by the same ㄷ-then-ㄴ route as 바닷물. 빗물이 고이다 (고이다 — to pool, riding frozen) is the puddle; 빗물을 받다 (M9's 받다) is the bucket under the leak. RADAR: this 빗- is rain wearing its linking form, not the comb 빗 (riding frozen) — same spelling on the dresser, different weather. The wedge shows up again in 빗소리 (with M19's 소리) and, two entries down, in 빗줄기.

M22's 나무 + linking-ㅅ + 가지: the branch — and a THIRD 가지 for the radar M32's 가지 note opened ("A counter for varieties", then "Homograph: 가지 is also the eggplant"): kind, eggplant, branch — three words, one spelling. Says 나묻까지: the ㅅ lands as ㄷ and tenses the ㄱ, unwritten in rom. 나뭇가지가 부러지다 (부러지다 — to snap, riding frozen) is the storm; 나뭇가지에 새가 앉다 — M22's 새 on M9's 앉다 — is the morning after. Sister to M49's 나뭇잎 — same trunk, same mortar.

Pays M49's 빛 to the letter: "햇빛 (sun's), 달빛 (달 M16), 별빛 (별 M22)" — the middle one lands. M16's 달 — "One 달 orbits, the other invoices" — is the orbiting one here. No wedge needed: 달 ends in ㄹ, and the linking-ㅅ only fits between vowels, though the ㅂ still tenses (달삗, unwritten). 달빛 아래 (M6's 아래) = under the moonlight, the ballad's opening shot; look up by it and M49's 토끼 ("the one IN the moon") is pounding rice cake.

en: the hill behind (the house, the village)
notes: M6's 뒤 + linking-ㅅ + M11's 산: the back-mountain — the hill behind the house or the village, and every Korean village has one; every 아파트 (M13) complex claims one too. 뒷산에 오르다 (M22's 오르다: "Mountains, stairs, and prices — all things that 오르다") is the retiree's dawn routine, M17's 등산 at its most modest: no summit, home by breakfast. Says 뒫싼, the ㅅ landing as ㄷ and tensing what follows. The walk at the end of this shelf leads here.

M22's 새 (the bird — "M13's 새 (new) has a flying homograph") + M19's 소리: bird-sound, birdsong. No wedge this time — 새소리 says exactly what it spells; the linking-ㅅ is a habit of compounds, not a law. Its verb is M36's 들리다 ("듣다 + 리: to be heard"): 새소리가 들려요 = birdsong reaches me — perception running passive, the way M36 said it does. Beside the joke in M19's 소리 note ("무슨 소리야?"), this is the one 소리 nobody objects to; 빗소리 and 물소리 build the same way.

M7's 꽃 + 잎: the leaf M49's 나뭇잎 note left waiting ("나무 + linking-ㅅ + 잎 (leaf — the bare word waits its own turn; today it rides the compound)") rides a second time, still bare-untaught, now on the flower: a flower-leaf = a petal. Says 꼰닙 by the same party — "an ㄴ sneaks into 잎 and the ㅅ matches it — 나뭇잎 says 나문닙" — except here it is the ㅊ of 꽃 that gives way to the ㄴ; rom kkonnip. 벚꽃 (M11) 꽃잎이 떨어지다 (M36's 떨어지다) is the two-week snowfall every April; 꽃잎을 세다 (the count-세다, riding frozen — M41's 세다 is the strong one) is he-loves-me-not.

The X-속 factory M65 built — "The X-속 factory: noun + 속 = inside the [noun], the deep-inside M28 owns" — fed M11's 산: M65's 물속, 꿈속, 머릿속, 가슴속 were the factory's four, and 산속 is the fifth. 산속 마을 (M22's 마을) is where the folk tales open; 산속에서 길을 잃다 (M28's 잃다: "길을 잃다 — lose the way") is how they get going. Not 산 안: M6's 안 is inside a boundary, M28's 속 is inside the substance, and a mountain's substance is trees. Says 산쏙, the ㅅ tensing after ㄴ — unwritten.

M13's 불 + M7's 꽃: fire-flower — the flame, the spark, and the whole sky show. Pays M25's 축제 verbatim: "The 불꽃축제 fills M22's 한강 every autumn" — the Seoul International Fireworks Festival, a million people on the riverbank one October night. 불꽃놀이 (with M26's 놀이: "M19's 놀다 turned noun") is fireworks as play, the sparkler in a child's hand; 불꽃 튀다 (튀다 — to fly off, riding frozen) = sparks fly: a fierce contest, a quarrel, or a first date, depending on the drama. Says 불꼳.

Pays M22's 동물 to the letter: "동물원 — the animal-house — is the zoo; the 원 you know from 병원 and 학원". That note pointed at the sound; today the hanja: 動物園, and this 園 is a GARDEN — the same 원 that ends M6's 공원 (公園, the public garden) — while 병원 wears the house-院 M14's 병 note decoded ("병 (illness) + 원 (house) = 병원"). Two 원s, one sound: animals get a garden, patients get a house, and neither is M9's 원, the one you pay with. The nine animals below live in one — 서울대공원 (riding frozen), the national zoo in 과천. Rom liaises the ㄹ: dongmurwon, the way 학원 goes hagwon.

en: stem, stalk; a stream, a streak
notes: M55's 줄 ("a rope or a line") grown a syllable: the line a plant grows along — 나무 줄기 — M22's 나무 — is the trunk, 꽃 줄기 the stalk — and then any long running thing: 물줄기 (a jet of water), 빗줄기 (a streak of rain, with 빗물's wedge), 산줄기 (a mountain range — the 백두대간, the peninsula's spine, riding frozen). It counts too: 한 줄기 빛 (M49's 빛) = one ray of light, the subtitle at every drama's turning point. NIKL also lists 줄기 as the gloss of 대 (the older stalk-word, riding frozen) — same meaning, one entry, both senses covered.

Pays M11's 미세먼지 — "미세 (fine) + 먼지 (dust)" — the bare dust lands, and M22's 공기 note's reason ("because M11's 미세먼지 made air quality a conversation topic") still holds every spring. Its verbs are all shipped: 먼지가 쌓이다 (M61's 쌓이다: "it piles up on its own, nobody stacking") is the shelf you forgot, and M66's 털다 already ran the cure — "먼지를 털다, the dust off the coat". The proverb welds them: 털어서 먼지 안 나는 사람 없다 — M66's 털다, M28's 나다, M1's 없다 — = shake anyone hard enough and dust comes out — nobody is clean.

Pays M41's 쥐다 verbatim: "Homograph bonus: 쥐 = mouse, and 다리에 쥐가 났어요 (M28's 나다) = a cramp" — the animal lands, and the cramp keeps its name. Korean does not split mouse from rat: one 쥐, sized by context (생쥐, the small one, riding frozen); the one on your desk is the loan 마우스 (riding frozen). First animal of the zodiac — 쥐띠, the birth-year band on the 띠 M79's 벨트 note left frozen ("허리띠 — M14's 허리 + 띠, a band, riding frozen"; still frozen) — and the M42 gap deck already dug its hole: 쥐구멍에 숨고 싶다 — M60's 구멍, M37's 숨다. 쥐 죽은 듯 (riding frozen) = as if the mice had died = dead quiet.

The snake — sixth animal of the zodiac (뱀띠), and the drama's shape for cunning: 뱀 같은 눈 — M24's 같다 in its badge form, on M14's 눈 — is the villain's close-up, 뱀처럼 (처럼 from M41) is how he moves. Korea has no lions but plenty of snakes: the 구렁이 (the big harmless rat-snake, riding frozen) lives in the old tales as the house guardian under the roof beam, and 구렁이 담 넘어가듯 (riding frozen) = the way a 구렁이 slides over a wall = gliding past a problem without ever addressing it. One native syllable, nothing to decode.

Pays g22_umul by unfreezing its animal: 우물 안 개구리 ("someone who thinks their small world is the whole world") — and that deck's own line, "저는 우물 안 개구리였어요 is a humble way to say travel changed you", now parses word by word (only 우물, the well, still rides frozen). RADAR: not M5's 개 (the counter) and not the dog — native, one word; 개굴개굴 is the croak. The 청개구리 (the green tree-frog — its 청 is the hanja twin M49's 푸르다 note filed; riding frozen) is the folk tale's contrary child who does the opposite of everything he is told, and the gap deck buries the story.

The fox — sly, charming, and the wife-typology every Korean has heard: 여우 같은 아내 vs 곰 같은 아내 — M49's 곰 ("The bear — and Korea's first mother"), M24's 같다 in the badge form — the fox-wife charms, the bear-wife endures; the gap deck weighs them. 구미호 (九尾狐, the nine-tailed fox — M2's 구 counts the tails; riding frozen) is the drama's shape-shifter, from the old ghost-story hour to 2020's 구미호뎐. RADAR: M78's 여 prefix is not in here — 여우 is native, one word — and 여우비 (fox-rain, riding frozen) is a sunshower: the fox, folklore says, is getting married.

The butterfly — and the bow tie: 나비넥타이 (with M21's 넥타이: "An accessory, so it takes 하다") is a butterfly-necktie, the compound machine at the tuxedo counter. 나비효과 (the butterfly effect, riding frozen) reached Korean unchanged; 호랑나비 (with M49's 호랑이 striped onto wings — the swallowtail, riding frozen) is the one in the folk song. RADAR: not M11's 비 (rain) — native, one word. And 나비야! is what a Korean calls any cat (M22's 고양이) that has not yet been given a name; the nursery song made it the default.

M31's 베이징 note already roasted one: "북경 오리 (Peking duck) kept the old name". 오리고기 (with M3's 고기) is on the grill — duck restaurants line the road out of every city — and it counts with M5's 마리: 오리 두 마리. 오리발 (with M14's 발: the duck's foot) is the swimmer's flipper, and the idiom 오리발 내밀다 (내밀다 — to stick out, riding frozen) = to hold out a duck's foot = to deny flatly, feign innocence: the interrogation room's verb, the gap deck holds it out. RADAR: not the 오 (five) from M2 — native, one word.

Pays g_m59_wonsungi to the letter: "원숭이 (the monkey) rides frozen; everything else is owned" — today it lands, and 원숭이도 나무에서 떨어진다 — M22's 나무, M36's 떨어지다 — is fully yours, comfort included. Ninth animal of the zodiac (원숭이띠). The playground's own chain-rhyme starts here: 원숭이 엉덩이는 빨개 (with M49's 빨갛다 in casual form; 엉덩이 = bottom, riding frozen) — red is the apple, the apple is tasty, and so on link by link to 백두산 — the compound machine, sung. 동물원's most-watched enclosure, and the one kids are told not to imitate.

獅子: the lion-獅 (a FIRST) + the noun-capping 子 M54's 상자 note pointed out ("the -자 is the noun-capping 子 that also ends 의자 (M6) and 모자 (M9)"). No lions in Korea, so the word is all 동물원, 라이온킹 (riding frozen), and 사자머리 — a mane of a haircut on M8's 머리. RADAR, three 사자s: this one roars; the 사자성어 g_m73_gakjadosaeng filed is 四字, four characters; and 저승사자 (使者, the envoy — riding frozen) is the black-hatted grim reaper of every drama, come to collect. The zodiac has no lion — 띠 skips it.

Named by its nose: M14's 코 + an old form of M7's 길다, worn smooth — nose-long — the same naming logic M22's 물고기 note found ("Korean names the animal by its destiny"), aimed at a feature instead of a fate. Every Korean child's first big word: 코끼리 아저씨는 코가 손이래 (the nursery song — the elephant's nose is his hand; riding frozen). 코끼리 코 (riding frozen) is the MT drunk-spin game — forehead on a thumb, ten turns, try to walk — and the old joke needs only owned parts: 코끼리를 냉장고에 넣는 법 — M13's 냉장고, M28's 넣다 — open the door, put in the elephant, close the door.

Pays M49's 노랗다 verbatim: "The color of 개나리 (the forsythia that yellows every Korean spring)" — the flower lands. First bloom of March, ahead of 진달래 and M11's 벚꽃: the hedge along every riverbank path and school fence, 개나리가 피다 (M22's 피다). RADAR: not M5's 개 and not the dog — this is the lesser-개 prefix on 나리 (the lily, riding frozen): the wild lily, the way 개꽃 is the flower you cannot eat (next entry). Native, one word; the 노란 badge form from M49 is built in.

The second bloom of spring, and the poem: 김소월's 진달래꽃 (see M48's 시인 note: "윤동주 and 김소월 are the names every Korean carries") — 나 보기가 역겨워 가실 때에는 (when you tire of me and leave — riding frozen, one line) is the opening every Korean can recite. Edible: 화전 (the petal pancake, riding frozen) is fried on the third day of the third lunar month. RADAR: 철쭉 (the royal azalea, riding frozen) is the poisonous lookalike — country names call 진달래 참꽃 — M29's 참, the true flower — and 철쭉 개꽃, the flower you leave alone. Not M16's 달 — native, one word.

M1's 크다 wearing the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 + M12's 길, welded solid the way M67's 큰일 was ("크다 (M1) wearing the badge (M24) + the work-일"): the big road, the main street. 큰길로 나가다 (M8's 나가다) = go out to the main road — the first line of every set of directions; 큰길가 is where the bus stops (길가, three entries down). Its opposite is M50's 골목길: Korean addresses used to be given alley-first, big road last. 대로 (the Sino boulevard — 세종대로, riding frozen) is 큰길 in print.

The native four — M5's 넷, contracted the counter way ("Before a counter: 네 — 네 명") — + M27's 거리 ("The raw street inside M23's 사거리 (four-streets), extracted"): the native twin of M23's 사거리 ("사 (four — M2's Sino) + 거리 (streets)"). Same crossroads, two counting systems, and 삼거리/세거리 split the same way. Seoul's signs say 사거리; 대구's still say 네거리 — the native count survived in the south. RADAR: not M1's 네 (yes), though 네거리에서 왼쪽 (M6's 왼쪽) is the kind of instruction you answer 네 to.

M12's 길 + 가 (the edge — the 가 M23's 바닷가 decoded: "M11's 바다 + 가 (edge): the sea's edge"): the road's edge, the roadside. 길가에 세우다 (M12's 세우다: "세워 주세요 — please pull over"), 길가에 주차하다 (with M50's 주차), 길가의 가게 (M1's 가게 — the shop with its stock on the pavement). RADAR: this 가 is the edge-noun, not the subject particle — 길가가 is legal Korean, one edge and one particle. 개나리 grows on it; the bus stops on it; 큰길가 is the busy version. Says 길까, tensed and unwritten.

停車場 stop-car-place: 停 (stop — a FIRST) + M2's 차 in its car sense (M50's 자동차 note: "M2's 차, whose tea-note flagged the car meaning on day two") + the place-場 that M37's 주차장 paved — and 주차장 is "駐車場 park-car-place": two 車場s, one parked, one stopped. M12's 정류장 ("The IOU from Module 6's 역 note, paid. 버스 정류장 in full") is the modern bus stop; 정거장 is older and wider (trains too), and it COUNTS: 두 정거장 더 가세요 — M9's 더 — = two more stops — the subway sentence. M6's 역 is the building; 정거장 is the interval between two of them.

理髮所: the ordering-理 M67's 심리 note traced ("the ordering-理 of 정리 (M54)") + 髮 hair (a FIRST) + the place-所 of M27's 장소 ("장 (place) + 소 (place — 안내소's 소)") and M72's 연구소 ("the place-所 that M52's 숙소 note decoded"): the hair-ordering place. The striped pole, the hot towel, the 아저씨 clientele; men under fifty go to the 미용실 (the salon, riding frozen) for the same cut at twice the price. Its verb is M21's 깎다 ("Peels apples, trims hair, and — at markets — cuts prices"): 이발소에서 머리를 깎다, on M8's 머리.

M1's 책 + M8's 방: book-room — the little bookshop, and M54's 헌 note already shelved one: "헌책방 = the secondhand bookstore, smelling of every previous owner". Register pair with M27's 서점 ("서 (writing) + 점 (shop)"): 서점 is the sign and the chain, 책방 is the neighborhood word — 동네 책방 — M22's 동네 — the indie bookshops that came back in the 2010s with a cat and a coffee machine. Hanja exists (冊房) but nobody hears it; the word reads as native. Says 책빵, the ㅂ tensing after ㄱ — unwritten.

M17's 등산 ("등 (climb) + M11's 산") + the road-路 of M31's 종로 ("종 (鐘 bell) + 로 (路 road)") and M38's 도로 ("welded to 종로's road-路"): the climb-mountain-road, the trail. 등산로 입구 (M12's 입구) = the trailhead — the signboard at the bottom of every 뒷산, with a map nobody reads and a stretching bar everybody uses. Says 등살로: the ㄴ of 산 gives way to the ㄹ that follows, the same handshake that makes M25's 설날 say 설랄 — rom deungsallo.

M29's 이곳 ("여기's written twin") + 저곳 (built from M29's 저 + M12's 곳, the same mold) welded: this-place-that-place. The third member of the set M50's 여기저기 note drew ("Print writes 곳곳; mouths say 여기저기"): 곳곳 (M50) is everywhere, 여기저기 (M50) is the spoken all-over, 이곳저곳 is the written here-and-there — the travel brochure's and the diary's word: 이곳저곳 구경하다 (M22's 구경하다), 이곳저곳을 다니다 (M16's 다니다). Says 이곧저곧. The walk on this shelf ends where all walks do: here and there.

電話機: M20's 전화 ("M8's 전화하다 was this noun wearing 하다") + 機, the motor-machine of M12's 비행기 ("비행 (flight) + 기 (machine)") and M13's 세탁기: the phone as an OBJECT. 전화 is the call; 전화기 is the thing it comes out of — 전화기를 바꾸다 (M9's 바꾸다) = get a new phone, and 공중전화기 (the payphone — riding frozen) is the museum piece. Today's 전화기 is M20's 스마트폰, and nobody calls it that — M6's 핸드폰 took the job; the word survives on the office desk and in every drama that needs a landline to slam. Shelf rule, opening: a MOTOR gets 機.

受話器: the receive-受 that M78's 수상 note decoded for 受賞 + the talk-話 M33's 회화 filed ("전화's talk-화") + 器, the tool-器 of M51's 악기 — a receiver for talk: the handset. 수화기를 들다 (M28's 들다) picks up, 수화기를 놓다 (M28's 놓다) hangs up — the landline gestures, alive in every office and every drama slam-down. Radar: 수화 without the 기 is sign language (hand-talk, on the hand-手 of M37's 세수 — riding frozen). Shelf rule: no motor inside, so the vessel-器.

寫眞機: M17's 사진 — whose hanja M75's 복사 note finally read ("寫眞, write-the-real: a photo is reality written down") — + the motor-機 of 비행기: the camera, in Sino. M20's 카메라 is what the mouth says; 사진기 is what the museum label, the manual, and the grandfather say — the same register split M50 ran for 차 and 자동차. Still 사진을 찍다 (M17's 찍다) whichever word names the box.

淸掃機: M8's 청소하다 ("Polite: 청소해요. Rooms and houses — wiping objects is 닦다") dismounted to 청소, + 機: the cleaning-machine = the vacuum. Its verb was booked long ago — M37's 돌리다 note ran "청소기를 돌려요" beside the washer, and the IOU clears here: appliances are RUN, not used. 로봇 청소기 (로봇 — riding frozen) is the one that bumps into M13's 소파 and gets a name.

陶瓷器: 陶 earthenware + 瓷 porcelain (both firsts) + the vessel-器 of M51's 악기 ("The 기 is tool-器 — a different hanja from 비행기's machine-機 (M12), same career") — 器 in its literal job at last: a vessel. Ceramics as a category: 고려청자 (Goryeo celadon, the grey-green glaze — riding frozen) and 조선백자 (white porcelain, on M26's 조선 — riding frozen) are the two dynasties' signatures, and the 이천 도자기 축제 (M25's 축제) sells the living trade every spring. The shelf rule closes: a MOTOR gets 機 (전화기, 사진기, 청소기), a VESSEL or a hand-tool gets 器 (수화기, 도자기, 악기).

學生證: M4's 학생 + 證 proof — a first by hanja, though the 증 has been closing M9's 영수증 (the receiving-proof) since Ring 1. The student ID: what 학생 할인 demands at the counter — M43's 할인 note called it "the student discount your ID exists for". The family rides frozen: 신분증 (the ID card — 신분 is status) and 자격증 (a licence, a certificate). Radar: M53's 증상 is 症, illness — a different 증; this one certifies.

連絡處: 연락 — M19's 연락하다 ("연락해! — text me!") dismounted, the M75 move — + 處 place — the 처 M36's 상처 decoded ("傷處 wound-place") and M69's 부처 note radared as the ministries. The contact-place = contact details: the form field after M1's 이름 and M12's 주소. With M37's 알리다 through the favor machine, 연락처 좀 알려 주세요 is how you ask for it; 비상 연락처 (비상 — emergency, riding frozen) is the line on every school form and hotel card.

座席: 座 seat (a first) + 席, the seat-席 of M64's 참석하다 ("參 (mix in) + 席 (seat)") that M76's 일등 note parked in 일등석 and the M75 gap deck sat in 노약자석 — the NUMBERED seat: 좌석 번호 (M20's 번호), 좌석을 예약하다 with M52's 예약, 좌석 버스 (the seated commuter bus — riding frozen as a compound). Radar vs M12's 자리 ("자리 있어요? — is this seat taken?"): 자리 is the spot you ask about, 좌석 is what the ticket prints.

自家用 own-house-use: the self-自 of M72's 자동 ("自動 self-moving") + the house-家 of M31's 국가 ("가 (家 house — 가족's 가, M4)") + the use-用 of M43's 비용: the car that is yours, as opposed to M6's 버스 and 지하철. 자가용으로 출근하다 (M16's 출근하다) = drive yourself to work, the commute the sentence deck measures against the bus. Register, completing the column M50 built: M2's 차 is what you say, M50's 자동차 is what the form says, 자가용 says whose it is.

準備物: 준비 — M8's 준비하다, dismounted — + 物 thing — the thing-物 of M22's 동물 ("동 (moving) + 물 (thing)") and M48's 인물: the things-to-bring. The line under every school notice — 준비물: 물 (M1), 모자 (M9), 도시락 (M80) — and the 알림장 (the notice notebook — riding frozen) every parent checks at ten at night. 준비물을 챙기다 (M40's 챙기다, the provisioning verb). Radar: not M1's 물 (water), though water is usually on the list.

化粧品: 化 (the becoming-化 M32's 변화 decoded) + 粧 adorn — the 粧 M80's 포장 note kept apart from its own 裝 ("NOT the 粧 of M6's 화장실") — + the goods-品 of M43's 제품: makeup-goods = cosmetics. M6's 화장실 is literally the makeup room, that note said, so 화장 is makeup and 화장하다 (to put on makeup — riding frozen as a verb) is what happens in it. K-beauty's whole export in one word: the 올리브영 aisle (the drugstore chain — riding frozen), 화장품 가게 (M1's 가게), and the 한국 화장품 that fills every visitor's 짐 (M13).

香水 fragrance-water: the incense-香 M41's 향기 decoded + the water-水 M17's 수영 found ("수 (water — the 수 in 수요일's water-day!)") — and M41's 향기 note promised this word in passing: "Flowers and perfume (향수) carry 향기; garbage only ever manages 냄새". 향수를 뿌리다 (M40's 뿌리다 — sprinkle, spray): you spray it; 향수 냄새 (M41's 냄새) is what the elevator complains about. Radar, one clause: a homograph 향수 (鄕愁, on the home-鄕 of M27's 고향 — riding frozen) is homesickness, and 향수병 with M14's 병 is homesickness as a diagnosis — the exchange student's word. Shelved beside 화장품, where the shop puts it.

運動服: 운동 — M8's 운동하다 ("운동 (movement) + 하다"), dismounted — + 服 clothing — the suffix's character shown for the first time: M21's 교복 named it ("교 (school) + 복 (clothing): the -복 suffix dresses whole categories") and M21's 한복 wore it. Workout clothes: 체육복, on M44's 체육, is the school kit, 운동복 the gym's, and 츄리닝 is the slang — the Konglish interlude filed it as sweatpants that came from training by way of Japanese. RADAR: not M25's 복 (luck-福, the kind you 받다); 운동복 brings no luck, only M54's 빨래.

國旗: the country-國 of M31's 국가 + 旗 flag — a first by hanja, the 기 M26's 태극기 glossed ("태극 (the red-blue yin-yang) + 기 (flag)"): the national flag as a category. 태극기 is Korea's 국기; 국기에 대한 경례 (the salute to the flag — riding frozen) opened every school morning for decades and still opens the ceremonies. Radar, the 기 file on this shelf: machine-機 (전화기), tool-器 (악기), energy-氣 (M41's 향기), and now flag-旗 — four hanja, one syllable, and the compound tells you which.

手票 hand-ticket: the hand-手 M37's 세수 filed ("洗手 wash-HANDS") and M68's 악수 confirmed + the ticket-票 M75's 표시하다 note sorted ("票 ticket (M12's 표)"): a cheque. The 십만 원 수표 — M9's 원, a hundred thousand of them — was the biggest paper money in the wallet until the fifty-thousand-won note arrived in 2009 — now a bank-counter word, 수표로 주세요 said by nobody under forty. Radar: M12's 표 is the ticket you tear; 수표 is money that needs your signature on the back.

The needle — and M36's 도둑 note already quoted its proverb: "바늘 도둑이 소 도둑 된다 — the needle-thief becomes the cow-thief" — small sins grow (M59's 소 is the cow; the gap deck files the sentence). 바늘과 실 (실 — thread, riding frozen) = needle and thread, the inseparable pair; 시계 바늘, on M5's 시계, is the clock's hand; 주사 바늘, on M14's 주사, is the one every Korean kid fears; 바늘방석 (a cushion of needles — riding frozen) is the seat you cannot sit still on.

The comb — the wide-tooth one in every 목욕탕 (M54) locker room. Its verb 빗다 (to comb — riding frozen) is its own root: 머리를 빗다 on M8's 머리. Sound radar: 빗, M49's 빛 (light), and 빚 (debt — riding frozen) all say 빋 alone; the final consonant wakes before a vowel — 빗이 (the comb), 빛이 (the light). Spelling radar: M11's 비 + the linking-ㅅ makes 빗물 (rainwater — the parallel M82 word, riding frozen here), so the comb and the rain meet in compounds only; 빗 by itself is always the comb.

담 (毯, the woollen kind — riding frozen) + 요 (the native floor-mat you sleep ON — riding frozen): the thin blanket — the airplane one, the office-chair one, the one you wrap around yourself on the 소파 (M13). Radar vs M13's 이불 ("Thick enough to sleep under ON the floor"): 이불 is bedding, 담요 is a wrap. 담요를 덮다 (M54's 덮다) covers you; 무릎 담요 — M14's 무릎 — is the lap blanket that lives on every Korean office chair from October to April — the gap deck owns it.

M28's 속 ("inside-the-substance") + M7's 옷: inside-clothes = underwear — a debt paid: M79's 팬티 note filed it frozen ("The category word 속옷 (underwear — riding frozen, on M7's 옷)") and today it is a word. 겉옷 (outerwear, on M41's 겉 — riding frozen) is the mirror: 겉 is the face of the thing, 속 the substance, and the wardrobe agrees. Wear-verb: 입다 (M8), like everything on the body in the M21 table; says 소곧 alone, 소고시 before a vowel.

M1's 책 + M6's 가방: the schoolbag — 책가방을 메다, with M66's 메다 ("The shoulder-carry verb"), the verb M60's 매다 note held a seat for ("가방을 메다 — a pool word for later"). The first status object of the 초등학교 (M15) years: 가방 is any bag; 책가방 has a timetable and a 필통 (M44) in it. Native weld, and the thesis in one word — the weld tells you what is inside, not what it is for.

Paid to the letter: M36's 유리 note filed "유리창 = glass window (M6's 창문's fancier cousin)". The 창 is 窓, the window M65's 창밖 decoded ("窓 (window)"): 창문 is the window as a hole with a frame, 유리창 is the pane itself — what you 닦다 (M8: "Teeth, windows, shoes — anything you rub clean") and what M36's 깨지다 was born for: 유리창이 깨졌어요, and the ball a few entries down is usually the suspect. Native weld: glass tells you what it is MADE OF.

新聞紙: M8's 신문 + 紙 paper — the 지 M80's 봉지 read as a hanja ("封紙 seal-paper"). Newsprint as MATERIAL: 신문 is what you read, 신문지 is what the newspaper becomes the next morning — spread under the 삼겹살 (M18) grill, wrapped around the 생선 (M3), stuffed into wet shoes: 신문지를 깔다 (깔다 — to spread on the floor, riding frozen). The Sino tail rule in one pair: same object, renamed by what it is now FOR.

M32's 글 + 씨, a native suffix — RADAR: not M4's 씨, the name suffix; no politeness in it. Beside M81's 글자 (the character on the page) and M81's 글쓰기 (writing as a skill), 글씨 is how YOUR hand made the letters: 글씨가 예쁘다 (M1's 예쁘다), 글씨를 잘 쓰다 (M10's 쓰다). 손글씨 (handwriting on purpose — riding frozen) is the café-menu aesthetic; 악필 (terrible handwriting — riding frozen) is the doctor's.

The app's oldest technical word, finally a word: the bottom consonant of a syllable — the sound interlude ran it ("Whatever letter sits in the 받침, only seven sounds are allowed to actually close a syllable") and M5's 여덟 note said "That ㄼ 받침 reads as ㄹ here". From M9's 받다 + -침, a native noun-maker: the thing that receives from below = a support — which is why it is also the saucer under a cup (컵 받침, M18's 컵) and the stand under anything. Grammar first: 받침이 있으면 은, 없으면 는 — the first rule of M1, now nameable; the coaster second.

M17's 축구 ("축 (kick) + 구 (ball)") + M17's 공 ("this one bounces"): the football — a native ball welded onto a Sino sport, and the two ball-words side by side: 구 is the Sino ball inside the game's name, 공 is the native ball you can hold. 축구공을 차다 (M66's 차다 — "The foot-swing kick verb"); the -공 rail runs 농구공, 야구공 by pattern. And the 유리창 above — every 축구공 story ends at a broken window.

拳鬪 fist-fight: the fist-拳 M26's 태권도 decoded ("태 (stomp) + 권 (fist) + 도 (way)") + 鬪 fight, a first (전투 = combat, riding frozen): boxing — the Sino word on the Olympic schedule; the gym says 복싱 (riding frozen). 권투 선수 (M17's 선수). Radar: M5's 권 counts books; this 권 makes a fist.

排球 push-ball: 排 push aside (a first — radar: not M3's 배 (stomach, boat, pear) nor the 배 of M18's 배달) + the ball-球 of the -구 family M17 built. M17's 농구 note declared "The -구 family complete: 축구, 야구, 농구" — 배구 reopens it, and 탁구 (table tennis — riding frozen) is still waiting. Volleyball: the school-gym sport, the beach one, and the one Korea watches in the Olympics with the sound up.

M81's 고속 + M6's 버스: the intercity express — paid twice: M50's 터미널 parked it ("고속버스 터미널, the set piece of every hometown visit and army send-off") and M81's 고속 note pointed back ("고속버스, which M50's 터미널 note parked at its terminal"). The 명절 (M25) bus: booked weeks ahead, 좌석 numbered, the one half the country boards on the same morning. Radar with M81's 시외: 시외버스 stops in every town; 고속버스 stops nowhere.

M12's 시내 + 버스: the city bus — paid: M81's 시외 note drew the pair ("시내버스 / 시외버스 — same bus, different map"). Seoul colour-codes the fleet — blue for the trunk lines, green for the branches, and the 마을버스 (the village bus — riding frozen) that climbs the hill nothing else will — all tapped with the 교통카드 M12's 교통 note built ("교통 + M9's 카드"). 좌석 is what you hope for; 자리 is what you get.

M12's 공항 + 버스: the airport limousine (리무진 — riding frozen — is painted on its side): the first Korean bus most learners ride, from 인천공항 into town, stop by stop past every 호텔 (M23). 좌석 numbered, 짐 (M13) in the belly, and the 공항버스 정류장 (M12's 정류장) is on every hotel's directions page. It connects the two airports below as well — the domestic one and the front door.

地下道: M12's 지하 ("The 지하 in 지하철 — now you own both halves") + the way-道 of M38's 도로 ("道路 way-road: the official road") — the same 道 that ends the provinces M31 mapped: the underpass — how you cross a big road (큰길 — the parallel M82 word, riding frozen) when the 횡단보도 (M23) is a hundred metres away. The 지하상가 (the underground shopping arcade — riding frozen) grew inside it; its mirror, the 육교 (the footbridge — riding frozen), is dying out as the crossings come back up to street level.

金浦空港 gold-inlet airport: M60's 금 + 浦, an inlet (a first — the 포 of 목포 and 포항, the port cities, riding frozen) + M12's 공항: Seoul's OLD airport, the one 인천 replaced as the front door in 2001. Domestic flights — M31's 국내 note listed the word: "국내선 = domestic flights" — and the short shuttles to Tokyo and Shanghai; the 제주도 (M22) flight leaves from here. 김포 is also the city it sits in, west of Seoul on the way to the sea.

M31's 인천 + 공항: paid to the letter — M31's 인천 note called the city "Korea's front door" and named this airport as "where you'll land", and M31's 국제 note glued itself onto it. The sign says 인천국제공항; everyone says 인천공항. The pair: 김포 flies 국내선, 인천 flies 국제선 (international flights — riding frozen), and the 공항버스 above connects them. The last module of the B-list ends here, where the next trip starts.

M31's 동대문 + M3's 시장: paid — M31's 동대문 note promised "동대문시장 for fashion at 3 a.m., 남대문시장 for everything else". The wholesale fashion market that runs all night: the 새벽 (M38) trade is 도매 (wholesale — riding frozen) — shop owners from every city with carts and cash, buying next season before dawn — and DDP (the spaceship-shaped design plaza next door — riding frozen) is the daytime landmark. 남대문시장 is the same machine pointing south, the gate the M27 md decoded. The B-list closes here, at the market that never closes.

級 the grade — the step M81's 고급 note filed as a FIRST ("高級: the high-高 of M19's 최고 + 級 grade — a FIRST: the step in 학급 (a class), 등급 (a rating), 초급 and 중급 (beginner, intermediate — all frozen)") now stands bare, with Sino numbers in front, because it labels: the 한국어능력시험 (TOPIK — M44's 능력 on M10's 시험, the name riding frozen) runs 일 급 to 육 급, and 삼 급 is where this app's Ring 2 lands you; M26's 태권도 counts its coloured belts in 급, descending toward the black-belt 단 (riding frozen). The idiom: 급이 다르다 = on a different level, out of one's league (gap deck). THREE 급s, radar: this grade-級; M16's 월급 ("월 (month — the one starting 월요일) + 급 (pay): month-pay") is pay-給, a character shown here for the first time; M38's 급하다 ("急하다: urgent") is urgent-急 — and the next four entries run all three.

學級 study-grade: the study-학 M11's 방학 glossed ("학 (study) released") + 級 — the class as an administrative unit, the first of the frozen three in M81's 고급 note to thaw. Radar: M15's 반 is the everyday word — that note's "3학년 2반 — grade 3, class 2 — is how Korean schools address a kid" — and nobody says 삼학년 이학급; 학급 is the paperwork's word: 학급 회의 (M10's 회의) = the class meeting, 학급 문고 (the class bookshelf — 문고 riding frozen), 학급당 학생 수 in the ministry's statistics. Says 학끕, the tensing every 학-compound wears.

特級 special-grade: M57's 특별 ("特別: M24's 특별하다, rootward — M32's 특히 already split out the special-特") lends the 特, 급 above the 級: the top rung. Two shelves wear it — 특급 호텔 (M23's 호텔 — the five-star tier) and 특급 열차 (M50's 열차, "列車 row-of-carts", the limited express that skips the small stations; the KTX outranks even that). Slang promotes it: 특급 칭찬 = top-grade praise, 특급 비밀 (M19's 비밀) = a secret above secret. Radar: not the express-급행 of a train timetable (riding frozen) — 특급 is a rank, 급행 is a speed; and the 급 is grade-級 still, not the 急 of hurry.

急 + the adverb-히 — M32's 특히 note named it ("the adverb-히 of 천천히/열심히 (M10)") — on the urgent-急 of M38's 급하다: in a hurry, urgently. The written adverb: 급히 연락 바랍니다 on the notice board (M34's 바라다, formal), 급히 떠나다 in the news copy (M23's 떠나다). Radar: the mouth says 급하게 — M38's 급하다 with -게 from M33 — and the page says 급히; same 急, two registers, the way 천천히 and 특히 both ride the 히 that turns a Sino root into manner. Adverb, house pos noun.

緊急 tight-urgent: M34's 긴장하다 ("緊張 tight-stretched") supplies the tight-緊, M38's 급하다 the urgent-急 — an emergency is urgency pulled taut. It prefixes: 긴급 뉴스 (M24's 뉴스) breaks into the broadcast, 긴급 회의 (M10's 회의) empties the office, and 긴급 재난 문자 — the phone's emergency alert (재난 disaster, riding frozen; M20's 문자) — is the 2020s' most-heard buzz, every rainstorm and heatwave arriving as a siren in your pocket. Radar: 비상 (emergency — riding frozen; M83's 연락처 note left it frozen too, "비상 연락처 (비상 — emergency, riding frozen)") is the noun on the exit sign (S2's 비상구); 긴급 is the adjective-noun on the headline.

en: counter — number (of a room, issue, typhoon); no.
notes: 號 the label counter, the number-號 finally alone: M76's 호선 note read it inside the compound — "號線 number-line: the number-號 of M38's 신호 ('信號 trust-mark') and M20's 번호 ('Numbers that LABEL, not count') + 線 line" — so 호 is the 號 bare, 번호 is number + 號, 호선 is 號 + line. Sino numbers in front, and it names rather than counts: 삼백일 호 = room 301 (what the door says), 제일 호 = issue no. 1 of a magazine, 제팔 호 태풍 = typhoon number eight on the evening news. Dependent noun — house pos noun, like M76's 송이. Radar, three other 호s on the shelf: M27's 호주 is 濠 (module-27.md filed it as "濠洲, for Australia"), M22's 호수 is the lake-湖, and M23's 호텔 is Konglish with no hanja at all.

號室 number-room: 호 above + the room-室 of M15's 교실 ("교 (teach) + 실 (room) — the room-실 family from 화장실/침실/거실 goes to school") — now it goes to the hospital and the hotel: 삼백일 호실 = room 301 in full, the form the nurse's chart and the front desk use; the door itself just says 삼백일 호. 몇 호실이에요? (M5's 몇) is the question at every ward and every 고시원 corridor. Radar: M8's 방 is the room as a room; 호실 is the room as an address.

番地 number-land: M12's 번 + the land-地 of M31's 지역 ("地 earth/land — the 지 grounding 지도"): the numbered lot. This is the old address system — 서울시 종로구 … 번지, city, district (M31's 종로 sits inside its 구), lot — that the road-name system (도로명 주소, on M38's 도로 and M12's 주소) replaced in 2014; the 번지 still prints on every old form, deed, and drama letter. And the idiom: 번지수가 틀리다 (M15's 틀리다) = wrong lot number = barking up the wrong tree (gap deck). Radar: M12's 번 counts turns and buses; 번지 is only ever ground.

The leaf, at last on its own — M49's 나뭇잎 note filed the debt ("나무 + linking-ㅅ + 잎 (leaf — the bare word waits its own turn; today it rides the compound)") and M82's 꽃잎 rode it a second time ("the leaf M49's 나뭇잎 note left waiting"); this is the turn. Native; the Sino twin is the leaf-葉 of M49's 낙엽 ("落葉 fall-leaf") and M52's 엽서 ("葉書 leaf-writing"). Alone it says 입 — RADAR: M14's 입 (mouth) is its exact homophone, and only a following vowel tells them apart: 잎이 = 이피, 입이 = 이비. The family: 나뭇잎 (M49), 꽃잎 (M82), 찻잎 (tea leaves — M2's 차 with the linking-ㅅ M80's 찻잔 wore), 깻잎 (the perilla leaf on every BBQ table — riding frozen). 잎이 나다 (M28's 나다) in April, 잎이 떨어지다 (M36's 떨어지다) in November.

洋服 Western-clothes: the ocean-洋 of M31's 서양 ("서 (compass west) + 양 (洋 ocean): the west-ocean world"), stamping imports the way M40's 양파 note said ("The 양- prefix stamps whatever arrived by ship; the kitchen kept the receipts") + 服, the clothing-服 M83's 운동복 decoded ("the suffix's character shown for the first time"): the suit. 양복을 입다 (M8's 입다, the body zone of the wear-verb table M21 drew), with M21's 넥타이, which that note says quietly rules the 출근 dress code; 양복점 is the tailor (riding frozen). Radar, the 양- prefix family: 양파 (M40), 양배추 (M59), 양말 (M21 — M40's 양파 note: "the same 양- that starts 양말, M21"), now 양복, 양식, 양주 — NOT M63's 양 (量 amount) and NOT the sun-陽 of M49's 태양.

en: formal wear, a suit (the dress code)
notes: 正裝 correct-dress: the correct-正 M63's 정확하다 read ("정답's 正 (M44 — the one hiding inside 정말 since M11)") + 裝 — the dress-裝 M80's 포장 note held frozen ("裝 (to dress, to fit out — frozen; NOT the 粧 of M6's 화장실)") lands. Formal wear, any gender: 정장을 입다, 면접 정장 (interview wear, on M43's 면접), 정장 차림 (차림 — attire, riding frozen) on the invitation. Radar vs 양복: 양복 is the (men's) suit as an object on a hanger; 정장 is the dress code — a woman in a jacket and skirt is in 정장, never in 양복.

en: a form, format (樣式); Western food (洋食)
notes: Two words, one spelling — the NIKL list carries both. 樣式 (rank 1831) = a form, a format: the pattern-樣 of M34's 모양 ("模樣 pattern-form") + the way-式 of M55's 식 ("式 the way-hanja") — 신청 양식 — M64's 신청, "the paper you file when you want a thing done" — is the application form, 양식에 맞게 — M15's 맞다 — = per the form, 양식을 작성하다 (작성하다 — to fill in, riding frozen). 洋食 = Western food: the ocean-洋 of 양복 + the food-食 of M18's 한식, whose note pre-printed the sign — "The set: 한식, 중식 (Chinese), 일식 (Japanese), 양식 (Western). Four cuisines, one suffix." (중식/일식 riding frozen). Radar: the verb decides — 양식을 작성하다 is paperwork, 양식을 먹다 is pasta.

洋酒 Western-alcohol: the ship-prefix again + the alcohol-酒 M80's 포도주 read ("葡萄酒 grape-alcohol, the alcohol-酒 that has been sitting inside M3's 맥주"): whisky, brandy, cognac — the distilled imports, as a category. The gift-box bottle at M25's 명절, the duty-free bag at M83's 인천공항, the bottle-keep shelf behind the bar. Sits under M9's 술 ("The umbrella word over 맥주 and 소주") beside 포도주: 소주 is what the table drinks, 양주 is what the table is impressed by. Radar: 洋 again, not the 量 of M63's 양.

公衆電話 public-crowd-telephone: M83's 전화기 note filed it frozen ("공중전화기 (the payphone — riding frozen)") — thaw it. 公 is the public-公 of M6's 공원 as M48's 공연 read it ("公演 public-perform: 공원's (M6) public-公") + 衆 the crowd-衆 of M48's 대중 ("大衆 great-crowd") + M20's 전화: the public's telephone. Culture: the 1990s queue with a 삐삐 (pager — riding frozen) in one hand, the drama's rain-soaked call, and the 공중전화 부스 (booth — riding frozen) that now doubles as a 안심 부스 (safety booth — riding frozen) with an emergency button and a defibrillator inside (gap deck); the phones survive because the law says a public line must. 공중전화를 걸다 — M20's 걸다, the hang-a-call verb.

空中 sky-middle: the SAME spelling as the 공중 in 공중전화, the OTHER hanja — the sky-空 M43's 공장 note filed ("공항 flies on sky-空 M12, 공원 rests on public-公 M6") + the middle-中 of S2's 중 ("중국's middle-中"): in the air. 공중에 뜨다 (M38's 뜨다: "물에 뜨다 (float)" — here the ground lets go), 공중그네 (the trapeze — riding frozen), 공중부양 (levitation — riding frozen, the comedian's word for anything that floats when it shouldn't). RADAR, the module's best: 공중화장실 (the public restroom, on M6's 화장실) is 公衆; 공중에서 is 空中 — two 공중s, and the compound tells you which. The NIKL list carries only this sky sense; the public one rides on 공중전화 above.

薔薇 — two hanja FIRSTs that name one flower and nothing else, the way 葡萄 spells M30's 포도: the rose. M76's 송이 note promised it ("장미 백 송이 (장미 — rose, riding frozen; M9's 백) is the drama-proposal cliché") — paid. 장미꽃 doubles the flower with M7's 꽃, as 벚꽃 does; May is 장미의 계절 (M11's 계절), with the 장미 축제 (M25's 축제) along 중랑천 (riding frozen); the drama title 장미의 전쟁 (M32's 전쟁) is the War of the Roses, domesticated. 장미 가시 is the thorn (가시 — riding frozen), and 장밋빛 — M49's 빛 with the linking-ㅅ — is rosy: 장밋빛 미래, a rosy future. Ring 2 ends here, on a flower.

en: to be due to (因-); only in -(으)로 인해(서) / -(으)로 인한
notes: 因 cause — a FIRST, and the character that sits inside 원인 below — with the -하다 that makes a verb of anything: to be due to. You will never conjugate it raw; like M32's 대하다 ("You'll almost never conjugate it raw — it lives in the frame [noun]에 대해서 (about)") it lives in a frame: [cause]으로 인해(서) = because of, owing to, and [cause]으로 인한 + noun with the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24. 태풍으로 인해 (M11's 태풍) = owing to the typhoon; 사고로 인한 피해 (M36's 사고; 피해 is on this shelf) = damage caused by the accident. The written twin of M29's 때문 — that note's "[noun] 때문에 — because of it: 눈 때문에, 너 때문에 (credit or blame; tone decides)" — 때문에 is the mouth's because-of, 로 인해 the report's, and the report has no tone: 로 인해 files a cause and moves on. The 로 is M6's 로 in its by-means-of job, 으로 after a consonant.

en: to compare (比-); only in 에 비해(서) / 에 비하면
notes: 比 compare — the first character of M56's 비교하다 ("比較 compare-compare — both characters mean it, so the word can't mean anything else") standing alone with -하다 — and, like 인하다, never conjugated raw. Two frames: [standard]에 비해(서) = compared to, and [standard]에 비하면 = if you set it beside, with -(으)면 from M20 built in. 작년에 비해 (M25's 작년) = compared with last year — the first line of every quarterly report; 나이에 비해 젊어 보여요 (M4's 나이, M24's 젊다 through M36's 보이다) = looks young for his age. Sort it against M22's 보다-particle, which does the same job in the mouth: 작년보다 is spoken, 작년에 비해 is printed; M73's 비교 is the noun both of them share. RADAR: not M11's 비 (rain) — 비에 비해 means compared with the rain, and only the 에 keeps the two apart.

en: to not be bound by (不拘-); only in 에도 불구하고
notes: 不拘 not-hold: the not-不 of M39's 부족하다 ("不足 not-enough-foot") — 不 reads 불 before most consonants and 부 before ㄷ and ㅈ, the same character the un-prefix 불- runs on — + 拘 hold, restrain (a FIRST; 구속, detention, is a C word riding frozen on it). To not be held by a thing = in spite of it, and the verb has exactly one frame: [obstacle]에도 불구하고 = despite, notwithstanding — 도 from M2 on the 에, then the verb in -고 from M10. 비에도 불구하고 (M11's 비) = despite the rain; 나이에도 불구하고 (M4's 나이) = despite his age. It is the written twin of -아/어도 from M39 and of M39's 그래도 — that note glossed the fossil "even it being so" — so 비가 와도 speaks and 비에도 불구하고 prints. A verb form exists too, -(으)ㅁ에도 불구하고 (늦었음에도 불구하고): recognize it; the noun frame is the one to produce. Says 불구하고 with a plain ㄱ — the page writes no tensing, and neither does the romanization.

en: to include as the first of; ~을/를 비롯한 = including, starting with
notes: Native, no hanja, and again a verb that only lives in a frame: [chief example]을/를 비롯해(서) = including, starting with; [chief example]을/를 비롯한 + noun with the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24. 서울을 비롯한 대도시 (M12's 서울, M50's 대도시) = the big cities, Seoul first among them; 부모님을 비롯해 가족 모두가 왔어요 (M4's 부모님 and 가족, M29's 모두) = the whole family came, parents at the head of the list. The order is the point: what stands before 비롯한 is the headline member and the rest follow behind it. The mouth says 서울 같은 대도시 with M24's 같다; the report wants its list to have a first name. Says 비로탄 — the ㅅ of 비롯 sliding onto the ㅎ — birothada.

en: to originate (from), stem from; ~에서 비롯된 = arising from
notes: 비롯하다 through the 되다-flip that M70's 마련되다 described ("되다 doesn't check pedigree, only the 하다 it replaces"): to originate, to stem from — [source]에서 비롯되다. 작은 실수에서 비롯된 사고 (M1's 작다, M63's 실수, M36's 사고) = an accident that began with a small slip; 오해에서 비롯된 싸움 (M24's 오해, M67's 싸움) = a quarrel born of a misunderstanding; 그 문제에서 비롯된 갈등 (M7's 문제; 갈등 — conflict, riding frozen; it belongs to M95) = the conflict that started there. Where M28's 생기다 says a thing arose and M56's 발생하다 files that it occurred, 비롯되다 points upstream at what it came out of — the verb the whole cause-shelf stands on. Says 비롣뙤다 in the mouth; the page and the romanization keep birotdoeda.

en: to suffer, undergo; to have (something bad) done to one
notes: 當 face, meet — the 當 of M64's 담당하다 ("擔 (carry on the shoulder) + 當 (face)"), of M32's 당신 ("當身 that-body") and of M34's 당연하다 ("當然 fitting-so") — with -하다: to meet a thing head-on, to have it land on you. M78's 강도 note filed it frozen — "강도를 당하다 = to get robbed (당하다 — to suffer, riding frozen)" — and today it lands. It takes a bad noun as its object and turns the noun into a passive: 사고를 당하다 (M36's 사고) = to be in an accident, 사기를 당하다 (사기 — fraud, riding frozen) = to get scammed, 피해를 당하다 (this shelf's 피해) = to suffer harm. Compare the passive party of M36: 이/히/리/기 bolt onto a VERB (잡다 → 잡히다); 당하다 bolts onto a NOUN — Korean's get-[noun]-ed, and print's favourite one, written as a single word once the noun is a 하다-noun: 무시당하다 (무시 — being ignored, riding frozen), 거절당하다 (거절 — refusal, riding frozen). RADAR: M73's 적당하다 carries the same 當, but that verb is 適當하다 whole — nobody suffers a fitting.

原因 source-cause: 原 the source, the origin (a FIRST) + the cause-因 that 인하다 above welded into -(으)로 인해. M72's 발생 note filed it — "발생 원인 (원인 — cause, riding frozen) in the report" — paid. It is the cause that IS, as against M24's 이유 ("이유가 뭐예요? — what's the reason?"), which is the reason you GIVE: 이유 is what a person says, 원인 is what the investigation finds — 사고의 원인 (M36's 사고), 화재 원인 (화재 — fire, riding frozen). Its partner is M32's 결과 ("結果 tie-fruit: a result is the fruit your efforts tied off"): 원인과 결과 = cause and effect, on M30's 와/과. 원인을 밝히다 (밝히다 — to bring to light, riding frozen) is the headline's verb. RADAR: not M9's 원 (won) — an 원인 is never a price — and this 인 is 因, not the person-人 of M23's 외국인.

根據 root-rely: 根 root (a FIRST — the Sino twin of M49's 뿌리, the native root that note called "literal (나무 뿌리) and every metaphor you'd hope for") + 據 to rely on, to be based on (a FIRST): what an argument stands on. 근거가 있다/없다 on the 있다-chassis = there are / are not grounds; 근거 없는 소문 (M24's 소문 — "Things-heard: the 문 of M8's 신문 (new-hearings), minus the fact-checking") = a baseless rumour, the phrase every denial reaches for; 과학적 근거 (M15's 과학 through the -적 factory of M45) = a scientific basis; [fact]을/를 근거로 = on the grounds of, M6's 로 doing its by-means-of job. In the essay it is the word the teacher writes in the margin — 근거는? — where is your evidence? RADAR: this 거 is 據, not the 거 of M17's 것 (이거, 그거) — 근거 is not a root-thing, it is the root itself.

Native — the one word on the grounds shelf with no hanja: the ground a thing is laid on, whether a canvas, a background, or a basis. Its frame is [ground]을/를 바탕으로 = on the basis of, again M6's 로 as by-means-of: 경험을 바탕으로 (M33's 경험) = drawing on experience, 사실을 바탕으로 한 영화 (M24's 사실, M2's 영화) = a film based on a true story — the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 on 하다 closes the frame. 바탕화면 (M20's 화면) = the desktop wallpaper, literally the background-screen, the word on every right-click menu in the country. Where 근거 is the evidence you cite, 바탕 is the ground you build on; said of a person, 바탕이 좋다 = good raw material, good bones — and 바탕이 나쁜 사람 (M29's 나쁘다) is a bad one underneath.

en: blame; fault (the cause of something bad)
notes: Blame, as a noun — the accusatory cause. Two IOUs, both verbatim: the M63 gap deck rode it frozen ("탓 (blame — the accusatory cousin of this module's 잘못)") and M69's 조상 note said where the debt lay ("M63's gap deck already blamed them (못되면 조상 탓, with this word riding frozen)") — today the word lands, and the second half of that proverb goes into the gap deck. [Culprit] 탓 = X's fault: 남 탓 (M74's 남) = blaming others, 날씨 탓 (M7's 날씨) = the weather's fault, 내 탓이에요 (M19's 내) = my fault, with 제 탓 (M17's 제) as the humble form g_m63_jal_tat used. 탓하다 = to blame: 남 탓하지 마세요, on -지 마세요 from M14. As a clause ending, -(으)ㄴ/-는 탓에 = because of (something bad) — Part 3 pairs it with its mirror, M69's 덕분 ("[Person] 덕분에 = thanks to them, and it ONLY credits"): 탓 only blames, 덕분 only credits, and M29's 때문 sits between them with its tone undecided.

影響 shadow-echo: 影 shadow — the 영 M48's 촬영 decoded ("撮影 snatch-shadow") — + 響 echo, resound (a FIRST): influence is the shadow a thing throws and the echo it leaves behind. M61's 미치다 note filed the collocation frozen — "영향을 미치다 (影響 = influence, frozen) is how news-Korean says 'affects'" — paid: 영향을 미치다 = to affect (the print verb), 영향을 주다 (M9's 주다) = to influence (the everyday one), 영향을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be influenced. 좋은/나쁜 영향 (M1's 좋다, M29's 나쁘다), 큰 영향 (M1's 크다); 영향력 = clout, with the strength-力 of M39's 노력 riding frozen on the end. RADAR: M2's 영화 hides a different 영 — M48's 촬영 note drew the line, "영화 (M2) hides a different 영 (映, projecting onto screens)" — so three 영s share one screen business: 影 the shadow, 映 the projection, and neither is the 英 of 영어.

作用 make-use: the make-作 of M48's 작가 ("作家 make-house") + the use-用 of M43's 비용 ("the use-用 you've owned since 사용하다 (M10)"): a working — what one thing does to another. M81's 부작용 built on it before it existed, decoding 副 + 作用 as "a secondary working = a side effect" and running "M10's 약 + 의 부작용"; the bare 작용 is that note's missing half, and 부작용 = 副 + 작용 is now a split you can read at a glance. 상호 작용 (상호 — mutual, riding frozen) = interaction, the textbook's word; 약의 작용 = the drug's action, the pharmacist's; 화학 작용 (화학 — chemistry, riding frozen) the lab's. RADAR: not the 작 of M1's 작다 (small) — 작용 is the Sino make-作, and a 작용 is never small.

en: to act (on), to work, to have an effect
notes: 작용 with -하다, the verb: to act on, to be at work. [Factor]이/가 [target]에 작용하다 = X acts on Y: 약이 몸에 작용해요 (M10's 약, M14's 몸) = the drug works on the body; 여러 원인이 함께 작용했어요 (M29's 여러 and 함께) = several causes were at work together — the sentence the report writes when it cannot pick one. 유리하게/불리하게 작용하다 (유리 and 불리 — favourable and unfavourable, riding frozen; -게 from M33) = to work for or against someone, the analyst's verb of record. Where M61's 미치다 aims influence at a target, 작용하다 describes the mechanism doing the aiming.

結論 tie-argument: the tie-結 of M32's 결과 ("결혼's knot-결 (M25 — 結, literally tying)") + the argument-論 of M44's 논문 ("論文 argument-writing"), reading 론 mid-word by the initial-sound law — the argument tied off. M38's 이르다 note ran the collocation and told you to wait: "결론에 이르다 = arrive at a conclusion) — recognize, don't chase" — now chase it. 결론을 내리다 (M6's 내리다 in its bring-down job) = to reach a conclusion, 결론이 나다 (M28's 나다) = a conclusion emerges, 결론부터 말하면 (M6's 부터, M4's 말하다) = to cut to the chase, the meeting's favourite opener; 결론적으로 = in conclusion — the -적 factory of M45 + 으로 — the last line of every essay. Says 결론 with the ㄹㄹ intact: gyeollon.

必要性: M16's 필요하다 ("Korean needs backwards: 돈이 필요해요 — 'money is needed (to me).'") dismounted to its noun 필요 + the nature-性 that M57's 가능성 named — the belt that "ships 중요성 and 필요성 off the same belt" — and that M81's 중요성 half-paid, leaving "필요성 (frozen) is the belt's other product". The last product ships. 필요성을 느끼다 (M32's 느끼다) = to feel the need, 필요성이 있다/없다 = there is / isn't a need for, 교육의 필요성 (M32's 교육) = the necessity of education — the essay's second paragraph, after 중요성 has opened the first. The 성 is the 性 of M32's 여성 and 남성, never M23's 성 (castle).

en: to correspond to, fall under, be applicable
notes: 該當 that-fit: 該 the said, the one in question (a FIRST) + the 當 of 당하다 above, here in its fit-sense — M34's 당연하다 ("當然 fitting-so"): to be the one that fits. [Case]에 해당하다 = to fall under, to correspond to: 다음 경우에 해당하는 사람 (M8's 다음, M32's 경우) = anyone to whom the following applies — the sentence every eligibility notice opens with. Bare 해당 is a determiner: 해당 지역 (M31's 지역) = the region in question, 해당 사항 없음 (사항 — item, riding frozen; M1's 없다 nouned) = not applicable, N/A — the three characters on every form you have ever half-filled. Radar: M64's 담당하다 is to be in charge of; 해당하다 is to be the case. The ㅎ stays soft: haedanghada.

en: circumstances (personal, the ones you explain) (事情)
notes: 事情 affair-feeling: the affair-事 of M36's 사건 ("事件: the incident") and 사고 ("事故: the accident") + 情, the 情 of M26's 정 (jeong) — the same character M32's 정치 note drew its line against, since that word's 정 is 政 — circumstances with feeling in them, the situation as it presses on a person. The one you explain: 사정이 있어요 = I have my reasons, 사정이 생겨서 못 가요 (M28's 생기다) = something came up, 집안 사정 (M65's 집안) = family circumstances, the reason nobody asks about. 사정을 봐주다 = to make allowances, to cut someone slack (gap deck); 사정하다 = to plead. The circumstance shelf, sorted: M33's 상황 ("狀況 state-of-things") is the neutral one you already own; 사정 is personal; 형편 is means; 처지 is plight; 실정 is the audit; 여건 is the givens. RADAR: this 정 is 情 — not the 政 of 정치, not the 正 of M63's 정확하다.

en: one's means; how things stand (形便)
notes: 形便 shape-convenience: the shape-形 of M37's 인형 ("人形 person-shape") + the 便 of M12's 편하다 and M42's 편안하다 ("便安: M12's 편하다 grows an 안"): the shape things are in — and most often the shape of the money. 형편이 어렵다 (M7's 어렵다) = hard up, 형편이 좋아지다 (M1's 좋다 on -아/어지다 from M35) = to get back on one's feet, 형편에 맞게 (M15's 맞다, -게 from M33) = within one's means, 형편이 안 되다 = can't afford it — M10's 되다 declining. And the adjective every bad review reaches for: 형편없다 = terrible, dreadful — literally no shape at all (gap deck). Register: 사정 is why, 형편 is whether you can pay for it.

處地 place-ground: the place-處 of M83's 연락처 ("連絡處") and M36's 상처 ("傷處 wound-place") + the land-地 of M31's 지역 ("地 earth/land — the 지 grounding 지도"): the ground you stand on — and the word leans toward the bad ground. 같은 처지 (M24's 같다) = in the same boat; 어려운 처지 (M7's 어렵다) = a tight spot; 처지가 딱하다 (딱하다 — pitiable, riding frozen) = in a sorry state; 남의 처지를 생각하다 (M74's 남, M10's 생각하다) = to put yourself in someone's shoes, and 처지를 바꿔 생각하다 (M9's 바꾸다) = to trade places in thought — Korean's walk-a-mile. RADAR: not M36's 상처 whole — the 처 is the same place, but the 지 is ground, not a wound.

en: the actual state of affairs (實情)
notes: 實情 real-feeling: the real-實 of M72's 실제 ("實際 real-between") and M34's 확실하다 ("確實 firm-real") + the 情 of 사정 above: the situation as it actually is — the report's word, with no person in it, only the facts on the ground. 실정에 맞다/맞지 않다 (M15's 맞다) = to fit / not fit the realities — 우리 실정에 맞지 않아요 is the sentence every imported policy gets told; 실정을 파악하다 (파악하다 — to grasp, riding frozen; it belongs to M93) = to get the picture; and the survey's closing frame, -는 실정이다 = the situation is that… — 돈이 부족한 실정이에요 (M9's 돈, M39's 부족하다). Shelf position: 사정 is my circumstances, 실정 is the country's — 實 audits what 事 only pleads.

與件 given-item: 與 to give, to grant (a FIRST) + the item-件 of M36's 사건 ("事件: the incident"): the given items — the conditions you did not choose and must work inside. 여건이 되다/안 되다 (M10's 되다) = the conditions allow / don't allow: 여건이 안 돼서 못 갔어요; 여건을 마련하다 (M56's 마련하다) = to create the conditions, the ministry's favourite promise; 경제적 여건 (M32's 경제 through the -적 factory of M45), 주거 여건 (주거 — housing, riding frozen). Shelf: 상황 is how things look, 여건 is what you have to work with. RADAR: not M78's 여 ("女, standing alone as a PREFIX") — there is no woman in 여건 — and not the travel-旅 of M11's 여행 either; 與 is its own character, seen here for the first time.

反應 turn-respond: the turn-back-反 of M64's 위반 ("違 (go against) + 反 (turn back)") + 應 respond, answer (a FIRST): what turns back at you. 반응이 좋다/없다 = the response is good / there is none — the first thing every launch and every joke is measured by; 반응을 보이다 (M36's 보이다) = to show a reaction; 반응이 뜨겁다 (M18's 뜨겁다) = a hot response, the press's way of saying the crowd liked it; 화학 반응 (화학 — chemistry, riding frozen) is the lab's; 반응 속도 (M57's 속도) = reaction time; 반응하다 the verb. RADAR: the 응 is 應, not M71's 응 ("The casual yes") — though a good 반응 usually starts with one.

要求 need-seek: M56's 요구하다 dismounted — that note decoded it ("要求 need-seek: the need-要 hiding inside M16's 필요하다 + seek-求 (frozen)") and set the verb at the top of its ladder ("말하다 says, 주장하다 insists, 강조하다 underlines, 요구하다 sends the bill"). The bill itself, as a noun: 요구를 받아들이다 (받아들이다 — to accept, riding frozen) = to meet a demand, 요구 사항 (사항 — item, riding frozen) = the list of demands, 고객의 요구 (M58's 고객) = what the customer requires. Sort it against M33's 부탁: a 부탁 asks a favour and can be refused kindly; a 요구 states a claim and expects the bill paid. RADAR: the 구 is 求, seek — not M2's 구 (nine).

被害 suffer-harm: 被 to be subjected to (a FIRST — the passive character itself; it is the 피 of 피동, the grammar word for the passive party of M36, riding frozen) + 害 harm (a FIRST): harm received. It comes with M8's 입다 in its second job — 피해를 입다 = to suffer damage: the wear-verb, worn as a wound — or with this shelf's 당하다: 피해를 당하다. 피해를 주다 (M9's 주다) = to cause harm; 피해자 = the victim — the person-者 that M27's 환자 note introduced ("The -자 is a person-suffix (기자, 학자 — reporter, scholar)"), the one name on that payroll nobody wants; 태풍 피해 (M11's 태풍), 큰 피해 (M1's 크다). RADAR: not M14's 피 (blood) + M11's 해 (sun) — the syllables are old friends, the characters are new; there is no blood and no sun in 피해, only harm.

負擔 bear-carry: 負 to bear on the back (a FIRST) + the carry-擔 of M64's 담당하다 ("擔 (carry on the shoulder)"): a load carried on back and shoulder — a burden, financial or emotional. 부담이 되다 = to be a burden, 부담을 느끼다 (M32's 느끼다) = to feel the pressure, 부담을 주다 = to put someone under obligation; 부담스럽다, through the -스럽다 factory of M45, = burdensome, awkward — the adjective for a gift too big or a compliment too warm. And the sentence every host says: 부담 갖지 마세요 (M56's 갖다, -지 마세요 from M14) = don't feel obliged. 경제적 부담 in the report, 마음의 부담 (M19's 마음) in the chest. RADAR: not the section-部 of M32's 부분 nor the copies-部 of M76's 부 — this 부 is 負, the one that bears.

壓力 press-force: 壓 press down (a FIRST) + the strength-力 of M39's 노력 ("努力 exert-strength"): pressure, on a lid or on an official. M40's 밥솥 note wrote the compound before the word existed — "전기밥솥, 압력밥솥: job-description naming" — and M54's 전기밥솥 repeated it; 압력밥솥, the pressure cooker, is decoded at last. 압력을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be under pressure, 압력을 넣다 (M28's 넣다) = to apply pressure — the lobbyist's verb; 압력을 가하다 (가하다 — to apply, riding frozen) the newspaper's. Says 암녁: the ㅂ nasalizes to ㅁ before ㄹ and the ㄹ turns to ㄴ — amnyeok, the sound change the romanization writes out. RADAR: the pressure of a bad week is M14's 스트레스; 압력 is a force from outside — physics, or politics.

危機 danger-moment: 危 danger — the 위 of M12's 위험하다, whose character is shown here for the first time (that note stopped at the sign: "위험해요! Also on every warning sign: 위험") — + 機, the machine-機 of M12's 비행기 in its other sense: the pivot, the critical moment. A crisis is a dangerous hinge. 경제 위기 (M32's 경제) = the economic crisis — the 1997 one, called IMF 위기, is the reference point for every Korean over forty; 위기를 넘기다 (넘기다 — to get past, riding frozen; it belongs to M94) = to weather a crisis; 위기에 빠지다 (M35's 빠지다) = to fall into crisis; 위기감 = a sense of crisis, on the -감 that M39's 자신감 bottles. RADAR: not M6's 위 (top) — a 위기 is not an up-moment — and not M26's 분위기 (atmosphere), whose 기 is 氣, the breath, not this 機.

憂慮 worry-ponder: the worry-憂 of M34's 우울하다 ("憂鬱 worry-dense") + the ponder-慮 of M61's 고려하다 ("考慮 examine-ponder"): worry that has been thought through — the editorial's worry. M29's 걱정 ("걱정하지 마세요 — don't worry") is the mouth's; 우려 is the headline's: 우려가 있다 = there are concerns, 우려를 낳다 (M47's 낳다, in its give-rise job) = to raise concerns, 우려하다 = to be concerned (the minister is concerned), 우려의 목소리 (M19's 목소리) = voices of concern. Nobody says 우려돼요 to a friend; everybody writes it about interest rates. RADAR: not the post-郵 of M27's 우체국, not the rain-雨 — 憂 is the heart's character.

對策 face-plan: the face-對 of M32's 대하다 ("對하다 to-face") and of M55's 대 in its versus job ("Second job, 對 versus") + 策 a plan, a scheme (a FIRST): a plan drawn up facing a problem. Two notes carried it frozen — M56's 마련하다 ("대책을 마련하다 (대책, countermeasures — riding frozen)") and M70's 마련되다 ("대책이 마련되다 = measures are put in place — the government's") — both paid. 대책을 마련하다/세우다 (세우다 — to set up; M12's 세우다 taught only the stop-the-car sense) = to draw up measures; 대책이 없다 = there is no plan — and, of a person, hopeless; 안전 대책 (M81's 안전), 사후 대책 (사후 — after the fact, riding frozen) = the measures that arrive one 사고 too late, which is what the M56 gap deck's barn proverb is about. RADAR: not M1's 책 (book) — 策 is a plan, though it was once a bamboo slip, which is where books came from.

方案 way-plan: the direction-方 of M31's 방향 ("방 (方 direction)") + the plan-案 of M52's 안내하다 ("案內 plan-inside: a guiding paper (案)"): a proposed way through. 해결 방안 (M72's 해결) = a solution, the committee's phrase; 방안을 찾다 (M6's 찾다) = to look for a way; 방안을 제시하다 (제시하다 — to put forward, riding frozen; it belongs to M93) = to propose one. Sort it against M32's 방법 — 방법 is HOW you do a thing, 방안 is a plan on the table that may not be chosen — and against 대책: a 대책 answers a problem that has already struck, a 방안 is any way forward. RADAR: not M8's 방 (room) and not M6's 안 (inside) — 방안 is not the inside of a room, though 방 안에 is.

en: to depend on, rely on (依存-)
notes: 依存 lean-exist: the lean-依 of M56's 의하다 ("依 lean-on") + 存 exist (a FIRST — 존재, existence, rides frozen; it belongs to M92): to exist by leaning on something. [Support]에 의존하다 = to depend on: 부모님에게 의존하다 (M4's 부모님), 한 가지 방법에만 의존하지 마세요 (M32's 가지 and 방법, M30's 만) = don't rely on a single method. 의존도 = the degree of dependence — the degree-度 M78's 강도 note read ("a different 도 (度, degree)"), riding frozen on the end; 의존적 through the -적 factory of M45. Sort it: M19's 믿다 trusts a person; 의존하다 rests a whole weight on them — the doctor's word (알코올 의존 — 알코올 riding frozen) and the economist's. RADAR: the 의 is 依, not the doctor-醫 of M4's 의사.

The column's 그래서: M7's 그래서 ('Cause, then 그래서, then result.') is the mouth's, 따라서 is the paragraph's — M32's 정부 and M8's 계획 in 따라서 정부는 계획을 바꿨습니다 opens the sentence that draws the conclusion, and S2's 그러므로 ('in a judge's robe') sits one rung more formal still, for proofs and sermons. RADAR: M33's 상황 note already ran the OTHER 따라서 — '상황에 따라서 (M32's 따르다) = depends on the situation' — that one is M32's 따르다 — to follow; to pour — in its -아/어서 coat. One spelling, two jobs, and the comma referees: 따라서, alone at the head of a sentence, concludes; [noun]에 따라서 mid-sentence follows. Ring 3 opens on the word every editorial turns its corner on.

M9's 더 ('더 주세요 — more, please') with a second syllable of weight: 더 is more, 더욱 is all the more — 날씨가 더욱 추워졌어요 (the cold deepening on -아/어지다 from M35), 더욱 열심히 (M10's 열심히, redoubled). Print's intensifier; the mouth says 더 or M38's 훨씬 (far, much more). Its cousin 더욱이 (moreover — riding frozen) opens the next point of an argument; 더욱 sharpens the current one.

en: first of all, for now (一旦)
notes: 一旦 one-dawn: M2's 일 (one) + 旦 (dawn, daybreak — a FIRST): 'once', 'for the moment' — 일단 먹자 = eat first, worry later (the -자 let's-ending from M19); 일단 해 보세요 = just try it for now (the try-machine -아/어 보다 from M16). Twin: M56's 우선 ('first of all — M8's 먼저 with an agenda') runs the agenda; 일단 suspends it — 일단은 = for now, at least. The one adverb on this shelf the mouth uses exactly as much as the page does.

M24's 다르다 (to be different) through the adverb press that M62's 멀리 note described ('M6's 멀다 through the adverb press') — a 르-stem unpacks to ㄹ+리: 다르- → 달리. 달리 말하면 (M4's 말하다 on -(으)면 from M20) = in other words; 예상과 달리 = unlike what was expected; 달리 방법이 없어요 (M32's 방법) = there is no other way. The spoken twin is 다르게, the -게 adverbializer from M33 on the same stem — 다르게 is the mouth's, 달리 the page's. RADAR, three 달s: M16's 달 (the month, the moon), M17's 달리다 (to run), and this 달리 — 달리 뛰어요 is 'runs differently', not 'runs runs'.

M30's 만 (only, just) wearing a 다 in front — the limiting particle turned into a sentence-opener that narrows what came before: 좋은 계획이에요. 다만 돈이 없어요 = a good plan; only, there is no money. Contracts, reviews and rulings all turn on 다만 (the fine print's first word); the mouth says M53's 근데 or M7's 하지만 for the same pivot. Radar: the 만 inside is the particle's 만, not M9's 만 (ten thousand — 만 원), and the 다 is not M9's 다 (all) — 다만 limits, it never totals.

en: never, by no means (with a negative)
notes: 決코: the decide-決 that M33's 결정하다 decoded ('決定 decide-fix') and M56's 해결하다 reused, with a native 코 tail — 'decidedly [not]': 결코 잊지 않겠습니다 (M15's 잊다, the will -겠- from M49) = I will never forget. RADAR: not M14's 코 (the nose). Twin: M39's 절대 ('absolutely (never)') — 절대 is the mouth's oath, 결코 the memoir's — and like 절대 and M39's 전혀 ('Another negative-polarity item') it demands its 안/못/없다/-지 않다 partner; 결코 without a negative is a sentence missing its floor.

M72's 실제 note wrote the receipt — '실제로 = actually, in reality — the adverb rides free on M6's 으로, and NIKL lists it as its own entry' — and today the entry lands: 實際 + 으로, the fact adverb: 실제로 봤어요 = I saw it with my own eyes; 실제로는 (with the 는 of contrast) = in reality, though. That note's three-way radar holds — M24's 사실 confesses ('사실은…'), M11's 진짜 feels, 실제 measures — and 실제로 is the ruler in adverb form. Its shelf-mate 사실상 (below) is different: 실제로 is what actually happened, 사실상 is what the facts amount to.

果然 fruit-so: the fruit-果 of M32's 결과 ('結果 tie-fruit') + the so-然 of M34's 당연하다 ('當然 fitting-so') — as the fruit turned out: indeed. Twin: M32's 역시 (as expected, sure enough) is the mouth's applause; 과연 is the essay's nod — 과연 훌륭해요 (M63's 훌륭하다) = excellent indeed. Second job, in questions: 과연 그럴까요? = but is it really so? — the doubting 과연 every column raises before answering it. Never spoken outside a reading; read daily.

都大體 all-big-body: 都 (all — the same character M31's 수도 spells as city), big-大 (M50's 대도시: 'the big-大'), body-體 (M53's 신체: '身體 the body') — all told, in the whole — which is how 대체 (riding frozen as the short form) came to mean what, all told?, and 도 doubles the exasperation: 도대체 왜요? = why on earth?; 도대체 어찌 된 일이에요? = what on earth happened? RADAR: the 도 is NOT M2's 도 (also), the 대 is NOT M55's 대 (the machine counter) — three hanja, one syllable of fury. Twin: none — this is the mouth's word that print also keeps, and its 대체 is the 大體 inside 대체로 below, with a very different temper.

多少 many-few: the many-多 M26's 다양하다 carries ('다 (many) + 양 (kinds): many-kinded', per M76's 다수 note) + the few-少 M35's 청소년 decoded ('靑少年 green-few-years') — more-or-less = somewhat: 다소 어려워요 (M7's 어렵다), 다소 비싸요 (M7's 비싸다). Twin: M56's 약간 (slightly, a bit — 'the measured 조금 (M9)') — 약간 measures with instruments, 다소 hedges in print; a recipe says 약간, a report says 다소. Radar: the 소 is few-少, not M48's 소설 (small-小) — that split M58's 소년 note drew ('少 counts FEW, 小 measures SMALL').

Just, and nothing more: 그저 웃었어요 (M7's 웃다) = just smiled; 그저 고맙습니다 = simply, thank you. Twin: M24's 그냥 (just, no reason) is the mouth's just; 그저 is the page's, with a sigh folded in. RADAR: one native word — the 저 is neither M1's 저 (I) nor M29's 저 (that yonder), and it has no kin in the 그저께 (the day before yesterday) M52's 엊그제 note carried 'untaught, carried inside the compound'. 그저 그래요 = so-so — the shrug even the mouth keeps.

M62's 그리 (not that much; so — the 그리 of 그리 오너라, the period drama's thither) + 하여, the formal -아/어 coat of 하다 that M72's 관련하다 note showed in the wild ('관련해서 / 관련하여 = in relation to'): so-doing = and so. The storyteller's 그래서 (M7): 그리하여 왕은 … (M26's 왕) = and so the king… — nobody says it, every folktale writes it. Sort the three: 그래서 in speech, 그리하여 in the once-upon-a-time register, 따라서 (above) in the argument.

M68's 앞서다 note wrote the IOU: 'Its fossil 앞서 (beforehand — riding free and glossed) opens formal sentences: 앞서 말한 것처럼 = as mentioned earlier'. Today the fossil is a word — M6's 앞 + M14's 서다 in its -아/어 coat, standing in front in TIME: 앞서 본 것처럼 (처럼 from M41) = as we saw earlier, 앞서 밝힌 대로 (대로 from M54, on M56's 밝히다) = as stated above. The news says 앞서 where the mouth says M38's 아까 or M8's 먼저; a second frame, [noun]에 앞서 = prior to — M10's 회의 in 회의에 앞서 — is the notice board's 전에 (M13).

M38's 때때로 clipped to one 때 — that note drew the register line: 'essays and lyrics say 때때로; texts say 가끔' — M25's 때 + the -로 tail M62's 정말로 note counted ('an adverb-maker hiding in plain sight'). 때로는 (with the 는 of contrast) = at times, though; 때로 슬프고 때로 기뻐요 (verb--고 from M10, M7's 슬프다, M34's 기쁘다) — the ballad's two-beat line. Ladder: M8's 가끔 says it, 때때로 writes it, 때로 sings it.

M72's 이용되다 note paid it forward — '널리 이용되다 (널리 — widely, riding frozen)' — and s_m72_method_hospitals said the rest: 'Print says 널리 here; M17's 많이 says the same thing without a frozen word.' Now it is yours: kin of M13's 넓다 (wide), through the -리 press that made M62's 멀리 — an older stem 너르- gives 널리 where 넓다 would give 넓게 (the -게 adverbializer from M33). 널리 알리다 (M37's 알리다) = spread the word; 널리 알려진 (M56's 알려지다 in the badge) = widely known — the headline's formula. Says 널리 as spelled, ㄹㄹ and all.

en: only then, for the first time
notes: The adverb that points back at the condition: 그때 비로소 이해했어요 (M25's 그때, M10's 이해하다) = only THEN did I understand — after that, not before. Sort the three finallys: M35's 드디어 ('finally! (spoken)') cheers, M35's 마침내 (at last, finally — written) concludes, 비로소 marks the threshold that made it possible — it loves to follow -아/어야 from M39 ('only if'): 직접 봐야 비로소 알아요 (M56's 직접) = only once you see it yourself do you know. Written, native, and quiet.

en: altogether, from the start; at all
notes: The all-the-way adverb: 아예 안 갔어요 = didn't go at all — never even set out; 아예 몰라요 = has no idea whatsoever. Twin: M39's 전혀 (not at all) measures the amount (none); 아예 measures the attempt (none was made) — and unlike 전혀 it also runs positive: 아예 이사했어요 (M13's 이사하다) = moved out altogether, 아예 처음부터 (M15's 처음, M6's 부터) = right from the very start. Native, and spoken as freely as written — this shelf's second mouth-word after 일단.

The root three notes pre-decoded — M33's 어쨌든 ('Built from 어찌+했+든'), M34's 어쩌면 ('어찌 + -(으)면 fossilized'), M42's 어쩐지 ('어찌 (how — the stem of M33's 어쨌든 and M39's gap-deck 어쩔 수 없어요)') — and M61's 어쩌다 called it '어찌하다 (do-how) compressed'. Today the root lands: how — the archaic, rhetorical M10's 어떻게: 어찌 된 일이에요? = what on earth happened? (M10's 되다 in the badge, on M2's 일 in its 'work, matter' sense); 어찌 그럴 수가! = how could that be! The mouth says 어떻게; fiction, sermons and outrage say 어찌 — and 도대체 above loves to walk in front of it.

相當히: the mutual-相 of M57's 상대 ('相對 mutual-facing') + the fitting-當 of M34's 당연하다 ('當然 fitting-so') + the -히 tail — to a matching degree = considerably: 상당히 어려워요, 상당히 많아요. Twin: M62's 꽤 ('quite, fairly' — 'It grades one honest notch below 아주') is the mouth's; 상당히 is the report's, the same notch with a suit on, and M29's 매우 ('very (formal)') sits one rung above both. The adjective 상당하다 (a considerable amount) is a few modules down the C-list; recognize the 相當 when it comes.

M29's 참 ('the warm truly (날씨가 참 좋네요)') + 으로 — the -로 tail M62's 정말로 note counted — the truly of prose, prayer and the podium: 참으로 감사합니다, 참으로 아름다워요 (M22's 아름답다). Ladder the truly-family by dress: M11's 진짜 (the mouth), M11's 정말 ('진짜's slightly dressier sibling'), M62's 정말로 ('the sworn-testimony upgrade'), 참으로 (the speech), and 실로, three entries down (the essay). Radar: not the oh-right! 참 — 참으로 never remembers anything, it only affirms.

大體로 by-the-big-body: big-大 (M50's 대도시) + body-體 (M53's 신체) + 로 — taken as a whole = in the main: 대체로 맑음 (M11's 맑다 frozen into the forecast's noun) = mostly clear; 대체로 만족해요 (M39's 만족하다) = satisfied on the whole. Twin: M8's 보통 ('usually') is the mouth's average; 대체로 is the survey's. RADAR: this 大體 is the same 대체 inside 도대체 above — 'all told' with the temper removed — and NOT 대체하다 (to replace, 代替 — riding frozen), a different pair of characters on the same sound.

en: suddenly, out of nowhere (of a thought)
notes: Suddenly — but only for what happens inside the head: 문득 생각났어요 (M67's 생각나다, to occur to one), 문득 떠올랐어요 (M49's 떠오르다, to come to mind), 문득 옛날 친구가 그리웠어요 (M24's 옛날, M42's 그립다). M28's 갑자기 ('The plot-twist adverb') is for rain, cars and screams; 문득 is for the thought that arrives without knocking — a novelist's word. RADAR: no kin to M6's 문 (the door), though a 문득 thought does come through one uninvited.

大槪 big-outline: the big-大 again + 槪 (an outline, a rough sketch — a FIRST) = in rough outline = usually, for the most part: 대개 아침에 운동해요 (M8's 운동하다). RADAR: the 개 is NOT M5's 개 (the counter — 사과 두 개), and the shape 대개 has nothing to do with a dog. NIKL sense collapse: the list files 대개 twice, adverb and NOUN — 대개의 경우 (M32's 경우) = in most cases, 대개는 = most of them — so hold both. Twin: M8's 보통 speaks it, 대개 writes it, and M32's 대부분 ('the big part: most') counts it.

事實上 on-the-facts: M24's 사실 (fact; actually) + top-上, the character M32's 이상 ('以上 from-here-up') and M54's 옥상 ('The 상 is top-上') filed — in effect, de facto: 사실상 끝났어요 (M8's 끝나다) = it's effectively over; 사실상 불가능해요 (M39's 불가능하다) = virtually impossible. The hair every columnist splits: 실제로 (above) is what actually happened; 사실상 is what the facts amount to, whatever the paperwork says. Radar: the 상 is 上, not the state-狀 of M33's 상황 nor M57's 상대 — M54's 옥상 note opened that file.

Three taught parts welded: M20's 끊다 (to hang up, cut off) through the -(으)ㅁ noun freezer from M67 → 끊임 (a cutting-off), + M32's 없이 ('없다 + -이: without') = without a cutting-off = ceaselessly: 끊임없이 노력하다 (M26's 노력하다) — the sentence every graduation speech and every company slogan contains; 끊임없이 변해요 (M26's 변하다) = keeps changing. Says 끄니멉씨 — the ㅎ of ㄶ goes silent before the ㅁ, and the ㅅ of 없 slides onto the 이. Ring 3's first fully decodable adverb.

The ministry's 그리고 (M7): in addition, and at the same time — 아우르다 (to embrace, to gather in — riding frozen) in its -아/어 coat, the same welding that made 앞서 above. It opens the second demand of every press release: 아울러 정부는 … (M32's 정부). Twin: M56's 또한 (moreover, also — written) adds; 아울러 adds and binds the two together. Spoken never; read weekly; said aloud only by a minister at a lectern.

徐徐히 slow-slow-ly: 徐 (slow, unhurried — a FIRST) doubled, the doubling M38's 때때로 note called 'The doubling trick from 빨리빨리 and 점점', + the -히 tail of M10's 천천히. Twin: M10's 천천히 ('the learner's shield') is the pace you ask for; 서서히 is the pace things change at — 서서히 좋아져요 (M53's 좋아지다), 서서히 어두워져요 (M13's 어둡다 on -아/어지다 from M35). Your car goes 천천히; the sunset goes 서서히; M35's 점점 ('The creep adverb') is the spoken word for the same slow slope.

M29's 그 + -나마 (the even-if-only-that particle — riding frozen): even that little = at least, thank goodness for small things: 그나마 다행이에요 (M36's 다행, '多幸 much-fortune') = at least that's something; 그나마 비가 안 와서 = at least it didn't rain. The consolation adverb — the shrug that finds the silver lining and refuses to call it silver. Radar: not the (이)나 particle from M43 (or; a whole), though both settle for less.

en: literally, truly, the very word for it
notes: M29's 그 + 야말로 — the emphasis particle, that-of-all-things (a Band 7 pattern still in the mail, so hear it here, don't build with it yet), and inside it M4's 말 + 로: that, indeed, by the very word = the word for it is exactly: 그야말로 완벽해요 (M39's 완벽하다) = perfect, literally; 그야말로 전쟁이었어요 (M32's 전쟁) = it was, truly, a war. The essayist's 'literally' — used where English abuses the word, and a shade more honestly. Says 그야말로 with the ㄹㄹ intact.

The it-was-always-so adverb: 워낙 바빠서 (M4's 바쁘다) = being so busy — as ever; 워낙 조용한 사람이라 (M13's 조용하다) = a quiet person by nature. It explains rather than measures — M11's 너무 says too much; 워낙 says that is how it has always been — the built-in excuse Korean hands you before the apology. Native, spoken as much as written, and almost always followed by a reason ending: 워낙 … -아/어서.

實로: the real-實 M34's 확실하다 decoded ('確實 firm-real') and M72's 실제 reused, + 로 = in reality, truly — the essay's 참으로: 실로 놀라운 일이에요 (M26's 놀라다 in the badge) = a truly astonishing thing. RADAR: the 실로 in M61's 찾아가다 note ('사무실로 직접 찾아갔어요') is M16's 사무실 + 로 (to the office), not this word — same three letters, an office visit versus an oath. Says 실로 with ㄹㄹ.

M29's 그 + 女, the female-女 that M78's 여 stands for ('female- (prefix)'), spelled 녀 mid-word by the rule M47's 손녀 note gave ('spelled 녀 here by the initial-sound law'). A twentieth-century coinage modelled on Japanese 彼女 — before it, Korean prose used 그 for both sexes, and bare 그 still means HE in a novel (M29 taught it as the pointer before a noun; standing alone in print, it is a pronoun). WRITTEN only: nobody says 그녀 aloud except when reading — the mouth says 그 사람, M55's 걔, or the name with M4's 씨. Gap deck.

M29's 그 + 이 (person — the bound noun inside 이분 and 저이, riding frozen): 'that one'. The word a wife uses for her husband to a third party — 그이는 대개 늦게 와요 — warmer than M27's 남편 and older than the borrowed 오빠 (M4) that a younger wife says; fiction and older speakers keep it, and it is affection, not distance. Radar: 저이 (that one over there — riding frozen) is the same build on M29's 저; 그이 is the one that carries the affection.

en: you (senior to a grown junior; courtly)
notes: The professor's and the father-in-law's you — 자네, 잘 왔네 — said DOWN, warmly, by a senior to a grown junior: the student, the young colleague, and above all the son-in-law (M47's 사위 hears it most). It pairs with the 하게 speech level (-네, -게, -나 — riding frozen), the courtly register between M19's 반말 and 요. RADAR: not M1's 네 (yes) and not M19's 네 ('your (casual)'). The ladder of you's: M19's 너 (equals, casual), 자네 (senior to junior, courtly), M32's 당신 (you — formal, spousal, careful), and the name+씨 or title M4 gave so you need none of them. Learn to be called it; do not say it yet. Gap deck.

The drama's all-purpose villain word: M29's 나쁘다 in 나쁜 놈 = bastard, 이 놈! = you rascal — a dependent noun, so it needs a word in front (이/그/저 from M29, or a badge adjective from M24).
