Also affection: 우리 놈 for a little boy, M74's 귀엽다 in 귀여운 놈 for a scamp. NIKL files 이놈 and 그놈 as entries of their own — pointer + 놈 welded — so this one word pays three. Its female twin 년 is a plain slur: it exists, it is spelled like M25's 년 (the year), and it stays in the drama. Radar: M5's 명 and its honorific 분 COUNT people; 놈 judges them. Gap deck.

The bare form M55's 듯이 note promised — "Headlines clip it to bare 듯: 비 올 듯." — lands as a word: a dependent noun, badge from M24 in front, that names the LOOK of a thing. 비가 올 듯 = looks like rain (the headline, the weather app's one-liner); 아는 듯 모르는 듯 = as if knowing, as if not — the hover between two looks; 그럴 듯 = plausible-looking, which the next entry will conjugate. That note drew the line it still keeps: "Radar vs M41's 처럼: 처럼 rides a noun (피부처럼); 듯이 rides a claim." 듯이 is the adverb grown from this noun, 듯하다 the verb grown from it, and this is the root under both — the noun Korean uses to measure how something SEEMS, the way 것 같다 from M34 used 것. Hard ㅅ at the end: says 듣 alone, 드시 before a vowel.

듯 + 하다, and the chassis is the one 것 같다 from M34 built — badge + noun + closer: 비가 올 듯해요 = it looks like rain, 아는 듯했어요 = seemed to know, 벌써 떠난 듯해요 (M23's 벌써, 떠나다) = seems to have left already. Same meaning as 것 같다, different coat: 것 같다 is SAID, 듯하다 is WRITTEN — the newspaper's, the novel's, the report's, and in the mouth it sounds like someone reading. The seeming-family, five members now: 것 같다 from M34 ("[badge] + 것 같다 — I think / it seems"), -나 보다 from M34 ("-나 보다 wants a clue you can point at"), M34's 모양 ("~모양이에요 can also mean 'seems'"), -(으)ㄹ 수도 있다 from M84, and 듯하다 — the essay's hedge. Always spaced from the badge (올 듯하다), and its twin 듯싶다 (riding frozen) is the same word in a softer voice. Auxiliary; house pos verb.

en: to be worth (doing); to be about the size of (auxiliary)
notes: Prospective badge + 만하다 = worth the doing: 볼 만해요 = worth seeing (M1's 보다 — the reviewer's verdict), 믿을 만한 사람 (M19's 믿다) = someone you can trust, 먹을 만해요 = edible, decent — the diner's faint praise, and 갈 만해요 = it's worth the trip. M63's 그만하다 (about that much — or, as a verb, to stop doing) pre-ran the 만 — 그 + 만하다, about that much — and its gap deck measured damage with it ("그만하다's adjective reading in its natural frame"); today 만하다 stands free. NIKL files this 만 as its own dependent noun, dictionary example 화를 낼 만도 하다 (there is reason enough to be angry): a thing has ENOUGH of what it takes. RADAR: not the only-만 from M30 (하나만), not M9's 만 (ten thousand) — this 만 is the about-that-much of M47's 만큼 (as much as, to the extent of) wearing 하다. Spaced from the verb: 볼 만하다. Auxiliary; house pos verb.

The count-세다 M82's 꽃잎 note left frozen ("꽃잎을 세다 (the count-세다, riding frozen — M41's 세다 is the strong one)") through the -ㅁ factory (M33 — the belt that shipped M34's 느낌 and 믿음): counting, nouned. Bare it is arithmetic — 셈이 빠르다 (M12's 빠르다) = quick at figures — and framed it is the essay's 'effectively': -(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다 = it amounts to — 다 끝난 셈이에요 (M9's 다, M8's 끝나다) = as good as done, 그런 셈이에요 (M24's 그런) = that's about the size of it; and 셈 치다 = to count it as — 없는 셈 치고 (riding as a frame) = counting it as gone, the budget's kindest lie. RADAR: not the three-세 of M5's 셋 and not M41's 세다 (strong) — the counting verb is the strong verb's quiet twin, and 셈 is its only child on the list.

The noun under M56's 마련하다 — that note ran "자리를 마련하다 (M12's 자리 — set up the occasion), 돈을 마련하다 (scrape it together — 어렵게 마련한 돈 carries the sweat in M24's badge)" and the headline's "대책을 마련하다 (대책, countermeasures — riding frozen)", and M70's 마련되다 flipped it. NIKL lists the bare word twice, and both are yours: the plain noun — 내 집 마련 (M1's 집) = getting a home of one's own, the national project, 돈 마련 = raising the money — and the dependent noun in its frame, -기 마련이다 = is bound to, naturally happens: 사람은 누구나 실수하기 마련이에요 (M16's 실수하다) = everyone slips sooner or later, 겨울에는 춥기 마련이에요. Read it as provision: there is a provision for it in the order of things, so it happens — the noun of arranging, used to say the world has already arranged it. RADAR: S4's 마 (the Busan hey!) is not in it.

en: the verge, the point (of a bad state)
notes: 地境 land-boundary: the land-地 of M31's 지역 ("地 earth/land") + the boundary-境 of M32's 경우 ("境遇 boundary-meeting") and 환경 ("環境 ring-boundary") — the edge of the ground you are standing on. -(으)ㄹ 지경이다 = at the point of, on the verge of: 죽을 지경이에요 (M14's 죽다) = I'm dying — of work, of heat, of hunger (gap deck); 울 지경이에요 (M7's 울다) = about to cry; and 이 지경이 되다 (M10's 되다) = to come to this pass, said over a mess. Always bad: the verge is a cliff, never a summit. RADAR: not M46's 지 (the time-since noun) and not the 경 of M17's 경기 — this 경 is the boundary M32 drew.

en: one's own way; (frame) it depends on
notes: In its own way — three settings. With 대로 from M54 ("The conformity particle"): 나름대로 열심히 했어요 (M10's 열심히) = I did my best, in my own way — the modest defense and the modest praise. With 이다: 사람 나름이에요 = it depends on the person (gap deck), 생각하기 나름이에요 (the -기 nominalizer from M13 on M10's 생각하다) = it's how you look at it. And bare, the 2010s' adverb: 나름 괜찮아요 (M7's 괜찮다) = it's decent, actually — a shrug of a compliment. Each thing measured by its own ruler: the noun for as-far-as-that-goes. RADAR: not M1's 나 (I) and not the 나 particle from M43 — 나름 is one word, and it never splits.

en: what, the thing which (formal dependent noun)
notes: The formal 'what': M24's badge + 바 = the thing which — 아는 바가 없습니다 = I have no knowledge of it, the official's line in the -습니다 register; 바라는 바 (M34's 바라다) = what one hopes for; 뜻하는 바 (this shelf's 뜻하다) = what is meant. Plain speech says 것 (M17): 아는 게 없어요 is the same sentence with its tie off. Today the NOUN only — the connective -(으)ㄴ/는 바 that opens a formal clause belongs to Module 91. RADAR: not the 바 of M4's 바쁘다 or M28's 바로; and NIKL's other 바 is the loan bar (riding frozen), where you drink.

en: to not (formal auxiliary; the long form of 않다)
notes: The long form of the long negation: -지 않다 from M28 ("안 is for speed, -지 않다 for writing and weight") is this word after the squeeze — 아니ㅎ pressed into 않, the 준말 press M55 named at work on grammar. -지 아니하다 survives where the page is heavy: law (…하지 아니한다 in every statute), notices, hymns, the pledge; the mouth never says it. M34's 괜히 note pre-ran the fossil: "both from 관계하지 아니하다, 'not related'" — 괜찮다 and 괜히 are 아니하다 worn smooth. RADAR: M19's 아니다 is the copula's not-be (학생이 아니에요); 아니하다 negates a verb, and only on paper. Auxiliary; house pos verb.

To hold something AS something: the -게 adverbializer from M33 in front does the job — 소중하게 여기다 (this shelf's 소중하다) = to hold dear, 당연하게 여기다 (M34's 당연하다) = to take for granted, 가족처럼 여기다 (처럼 from M41) = to treat as family; and 으로 여기다 (M6's 으로) = regard as — 친구로 여겨요. Where 생각하다 (M10) has a thought, 여기다 files a standing verdict: how you rank a thing in your own heart. RADAR, a homograph: M6's 여기 (here) is a place, 여기다 is a verb — 여기서 여겨요 is two different words touching. The passive is next.

en: to be considered, be regarded as
notes: 여기다 through -아/어지다 from M35: to be regarded. 중요하게 여겨진다 (M16's 중요하다) = is considered important, 당연한 것으로 여겨져요 = is taken as given — the print sentence where English says is-thought-to-be, with no thinker named. NIKL gives it its own row because the paper uses it more than the active: a 여겨진다 in a report is a verdict nobody has to sign. Same 여기 radar as its parent: not M6's 여기.

M10's 뜻 ("meaning") + 하다: to mean. 이 말은 무엇을 뜻해요? (M29's 무엇) = what does this mean?, and the indirect form 무엇을 뜻하는지 (-는지 from M33) is how the essay asks it. Register pair with M72's 의미하다 ("Speech says 뜻이에요; paper says 의미한다"): 뜻하다 is the native 'to mean', 의미하다 the Sino — the same split M32's 의미 drew against 뜻 ("the formal register of M10's 뜻"). And 뜻하지 않게 (riding frozen) = unexpectedly, the sign that 뜻 also means intention — what you meant to happen. Says 뜨타다 — ㅅ meeting ㅎ.

M34's 판단 ("判斷 judge-cut: the call you make") dismounts to its verb — that note already ran 판단하기 어려워요. 스스로 판단하세요 (M56's 스스로) = judge for yourself; 상황을 판단하다 (M33's 상황) = size up the situation; 잘못 판단하다 (M63's 잘못) = to misjudge. The judge-判 is the one M75's 비판하다 struck with ("批判 strike-judge"). Not the courtroom (that judge has other words) — the call any person makes with the facts in hand, and the verb the four adjectives of worth on this shelf are made for: 올바르게 판단하다.

評價 judge-price: 評 (a FIRST — to weigh a thing in words; the 평 of 비평 and 평론, riding frozen) + 價 price (a FIRST as a decode — M21's 가격 never read its hanja, and this is its price-價): to put a price on a thing is to assess it. 평가를 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be evaluated; 수행평가 (riding frozen) = the school's performance assessment every Korean child dreads; 저평가/고평가 (frozen) = under- and over-valued, the stock page's pair. RADAR: not M1's 가 (the subject particle) — this 가 costs money.

평가 + 하다: to rate. 높이 평가하다 (M57's 높이) = to rate highly — the reviewer's and the boss's verb; 나름대로 평가하다 = to judge by one's own lights; 결과를 평가하다 (M32's 결과). RADAR vs the entry above it: 판단하다 makes a CALL (yes or no, safe or not); 평가하다 assigns a GRADE (how good, how much) — a 판단 can be wrong, a 평가 can only be low.

en: to recognize, perceive, be aware of
notes: 認識 recognize-know: the 認 of M64's 확인 ("確 (certain) + 認 (recognize)") + the 識 of M44's 지식 ("知識 know-recognize"). To register a thing as real: 문제를 인식하다 (M7's 문제) = to recognize the problem — the first line of every fix; 위험을 인식하다 (the 위험 of M12's 위험하다) = to perceive the danger; 얼굴 인식 (M8's 얼굴; 인식 the noun riding frozen) = face recognition, what your phone does before it unlocks. RADAR vs M4's 알다: 알다 knows; 인식하다 realizes and files it — knowing with a timestamp.

意識 intent-know: the 意 of M32's 의미 ("意味 intent-flavor") and M39's 의지 ("意志 intent-aim") + the knowing-識 above. The ER's first question: 의식이 있어요? — is he conscious?; 의식을 잃다 (M28's 잃다) = to lose consciousness, 의식이 돌아오다 (M23's 돌아오다) = to come round. Widen it and it is awareness: 환경 의식 (M32's 환경) = environmental awareness, 무의식 (frozen) = the unconscious. RADAR, mandatory — NIKL files a second 의식 as its own C-row: 儀式 = a ceremony, the -식 of M25's 결혼식 — 결혼식은 의식이에요, a wedding is a rite. One spelling, one hanja apart: the hospital's word and the temple's.

en: to be conscious of, to mind (others)
notes: 의식 + 하다, and its object is nearly always other people: 남을 의식하다 (M74's 남) = to mind what others think — the Korean condition, gap deck; 카메라를 의식하다 (M20's 카메라) = to play to the camera; 의식하지 않고 (-지 않다 from M28) = without minding, the freedom every self-help book sells. It pairs with M42's 눈치 ("눈치를 보다 = anxiously reading the room"): 눈치 is the organ, 의식하다 is the act — and 의식하지 마세요 (-지 마세요 from M14) is the friend's advice before the interview. Says 의시카다 — ㄱ meeting ㅎ.

觀點 view-point: the see-觀 of M23's 관광 that M35's 습관 note named ("관광's see-觀") and M72's 관찰하다 rode + M32's 점 ("點 dot: a point") — the dot you look from. 다른 관점에서 (M24's 다르다) = from a different point of view; 관점의 차이 (M57's 차이) = a difference of standpoint, the polite name for a fight. The four views, sorted: M24's 의견 is what you SAY in a meeting; 견해 (two entries down) is what an expert HOLDS; 관점 is where you STAND; 시각 (next) is the ANGLE you look from. English has opinion and point of view; Korean has the whole geometry.

en: angle of view, perspective; (homograph) the time, the hour
notes: 視角 see-angle: the watch-視 of M48's 시청자 ("watch-視") and M75's 무시하다 ("無視 no-see") + 角 angle, a FIRST (the corner in 삼각형, frozen). 새로운 시각 (M35's 새롭다) = a fresh angle; 비판적 시각 (M75's 비판하다 with -적 from M45) = a critical eye; 시각이 다르다 (M24's 다르다) = we see it from different angles. RADAR, mandatory — NIKL files a second 시각 as its own C-row: 時刻 = the time, the point on the clock — M1's 시간's 時 + 刻 (carve, frozen): 도착 시각 (the 도착 of M8's 도착하다) is the timetable's arrival TIME, where the mouth says 시간. 시간 is a span, 시각 is a point; and the angle-시각 is the one this shelf teaches.

en: opinion, view (held by someone who knows)
notes: 見解 see-untie: the view-見 M56's 발견하다 lifted ("the view-見 inside M24's 의견") + the 解 of M34's 이해 ("理解") that M56's 해결하다 called untie-解 and M75's 해석 spelled out ("解釋 untie-explain") — a view that has untied the knot. The expert's opinion: 전문가의 견해 (M58's 전문가), 견해 차이 (M57's 차이) = a difference of views, 견해를 밝히다 (M56's 밝히다) = to state one's position — the press-conference verb. RADAR vs M24's 의견: an 의견 anyone can have; a 견해 is held by someone who has thought — the news quotes 견해, the class discussion collects 의견.

論理 argument-order: the argument-論 of M44's 논문 ("argument-論") + the 理 M45's 이성 filed ("the reason-理 of 이유 (M24) and 이해하다 (M10)") and M67's 심리 called "the ordering-理 of 정리 (M54)" — argument, put in order. 논리적 (-적 from M45) = logical; 논리에 맞다 (M15's 맞다) = it holds together; 논리가 없다 = it doesn't add up — the debate club's kill shot. Says 놀리 — ㄴ meeting ㄹ becomes ㄹㄹ, the same assimilation M44's 토론 note documented for 論 in the other direction.

常識 constant-knowledge: the constant-常 of M38's 일상 ("日常 day-constant") — the same 常 M8's 항상 has carried unread, and the 常 of the 異常 M32's 이상 note set against itself — + the knowing-識 of M44's 지식. What everyone knows, always: 상식이 없다 = no common sense (the verdict on the person who talks in the cinema); 상식적으로 (-적 from M45, then 으로) = by common sense; 일반 상식 (M57's 일반) = general knowledge, the quiz show's category; 비상식적 (frozen) = absurd. RADAR: 지식 is what you learned; 상식 is what you are assumed to have.

疑問 doubt-ask: the doubt-疑 of M34's 의심 ("疑心 doubt-heart") + the ask-問 M75's 방문하다 read out of M10's 질문 ("the ask-問 inside M10's 질문"). A question that has not been asked aloud: 의문이 생기다 (M28's 생기다) / 의문이 들다 (M28's 들다) = a doubt arises; 의문을 풀다 (M36's 풀다) = to resolve it; 의문점 (M32's 점) = the questionable point. RADAR: M10's 질문 is asked to someone; 의문 sits in your own head — and M34's 의심 suspects a person, where 의문 only doubts a claim.

PAYS M74's 거짓: that note said "the formal pair is 진실 (truth — riding frozen) / 거짓" — the ride ends here. 眞實 true-real: the 眞 M74's 가짜 note showed ("眞 true and 假 false") — the same 眞 inside M17's 사진, whose 寫眞 M75's 복사 note read — + the real-實 of M34's 확실하다 ("確實 firm-real") and M72's 실제. 진실을 말하다 (M4's 말하다) = to tell the truth; 진실은 하나 = the truth is one, the detective's line; 진실이 밝혀지다 (the passive of M56's 밝히다, riding free) = the truth comes out. RADAR: M24's 사실 is a fact; 진실 is the truth the facts add up to; M11's 진짜 is the mouth's 'really'.

眞理 true-order: 眞 above + the 理 of M45's 이성 and M67's 심리 ("the ordering-理 of 정리 (M54)") — the truth that is the ORDER of things. The philosopher's, the scientist's, the church's: 진리를 찾다 (M6's 찾다) = to seek truth; 진리는 변하지 않아요 (M26's 변하다, -지 않다 from M28) = truth does not change. RADAR vs 진실: 진실 is what happened (one case, one courtroom); 진리 is what always holds (every case, no courtroom). Says 질리 — ㄴ before ㄹ turns to ㄹㄹ.

觀念 view-thought: the see-觀 of 관점 + the think-念 M67's 염려하다 decoded ("念慮 think-and-ponder") — the same 념 that M23's 기념품 and M25's 기념일 carry as 'commemoration', and the one M40's 양념 note read in a folk etymology ("藥念, 'medicine-mindset'"). An idea that has set in the head rather than been tested: 고정관념 (고정 fixed, riding frozen) = a stereotype — the word every Korean uses for one; 시간 관념이 없다 (M1's 시간) = no sense of time. RADAR: 생각 (M10's 생각하다) is a thought passing; 관념 is a thought that has hardened.

理念 order-thought: the 理 of 진리 + the 念 of 관념 — the idea a system is ordered by. 정치 이념 (M32's 정치) = political ideology; 이념 대립 (대립 — opposition, riding frozen) = the ideological standoff the peninsula has run since 1945; 이념 교육 (M32's 교육). The loan 이데올로기 (a C-word saved for Module 96, riding frozen) is its foreign twin, and the press uses both. RADAR vs 관념: a 관념 is any set idea in one head; an 이념 is the set idea a party, a state, or a movement runs on.

價値 price-worth: the price-價 of 평가 (M21's 가격, read at last) + 値 worth, a FIRST. On the 있다-chassis: 가치가 있어요/없어요 = worthwhile / worthless — 볼 가치가 있어요 is 볼 만해요 with the noun showing; 가치를 인식하다 with this shelf's verb; 가치관 (the see-觀 again — a C-word riding frozen) = one's values, the interview question. RADAR, mandatory: M9's 같이 note said "Pronounced 가치 — a sound-change bonus" — 같이 SAYS 가치, and this 가치 is spelled so: 같이 가요 and 가치가 있어요 are homophones to the ear and strangers on the page. The shelf ends on it because everything above it — a judgment, a view, a truth — is something Korean weighs.

所重 place-of-weight: the place-所 M52's 숙소 filed ("장소's place-所 (M27)") + the heavy-重 of M41's 체중 ("體重 body-heavy") — the place where the weight is. 소중한 사람 (M24's badge) = someone dear, 소중한 시간 (M1's 시간), 소중한 추억 (M19's 추억) = cherished memories; and 소중하게 여기다 = to hold dear — the frame this shelf's 여기다 was made for. RADAR vs M16's 중요하다: M41's 체중 note said important things are heavy things — 중요하다 is heavy, 소중하다 is heavy AND yours; a 중요한 회의 (M10's 회의) matters to the company, a 소중한 사람 matters to you.

en: to be right, correct, upright (in conduct)
notes: M63's 바르다 (upright and proper — or spread on, its second reading) with 올- in front — whole, entire, a native prefix riding frozen (kin to M55's 온) — wholly upright. 올바른 태도 (M33's 태도) = the right attitude, 올바른 판단 = sound judgment, 올바르게 (the -게 from M33) = correctly, properly. Runs the 르-family table (M7): 올발라요. RADAR, three rights: M15's 맞다 checks answers, M63's 옳다 judges choices (that note's line: "an answer can be 맞다, only a decision can be 옳다"), and 올바르다 grades conduct — the posture-word 바르다 for the way a person stands in life.

M34's 바라다 (to hope, to wish) through the -ㅁ factory (M33) — 바람, a wish, the noun NIKL lists beside the wind — + 직하다, the fit-to-be suffix (riding frozen; it turns a noun into 'worthy of'): fit to be wished for. 바람직한 방향 (M31's 방향) = the desirable direction; 바람직하지 않아요 (-지 않다 from M28) = not advisable — the committee's mildest no, and the way a report says 'don't'. RADAR: not M11's 바람 (wind) — the wish-바람 and the wind-바람 are one spelling and two nouns, and 바람직하다 grows from the wish. Says 바람지카다 — ㄱ meeting ㅎ.

適切 fit-earnest: the fit-適 of M64's 적용하다 ("適 (fit) + 用 (use)") + the 切 M81's 친절 called a FIRST ("親切 close-earnest") — fitting, to the point. 적절한 표현 (M33's 표현) = the apt expression, 적절한 때 (M25's 때) = the right moment, 적절히 (frozen) = properly. RADAR, the fit-family sorted: M63's 알맞다 fits on the nose, M73's 적당하다 is the mouth's 'suitable' (that note: "where 알맞다 fits, 적당하다 suffices"), and 적절하다 is the memo's — 적당히 해 means take it easy, 적절히 해 means do it properly. The written 적당하다, and the word a review reaches for when it means yes.

M4's 살다 through the -(으)ㅁ noun freezer from M67 ("### 2. -(으)ㅁ — the noun freezer" — 살 + ㅁ, the ㄹ kept): the living of a life, frozen into a noun. 삶을 살다 = to live a life; 삶의 의미 (M32's 의미) = the meaning of life; 행복한 삶 (M7's 행복하다) = a happy life. RADAR, mandatory: M40's 삶다 is a different word that happens to share the spelling of its stem — that note's "Boil the THING: 달걀을 삶다, 감자를 삶다" — 삶을 살다 lives, 삶다 boils, and both say 삼 (that note: "Says 삼따"). M25's 인생 ("one person's run through time") is the Sino twin: 인생 is the span, 삶 is the living of it, and the essay keeps both. Says 삼 alone, 살미 before 이.

en: process, course (of events); a course of study
notes: 過程 pass-through-measure: the 過 of M35's 과거 ("過去 passed-gone") and M33's 사과하다 ("謝過 apologize") + the 程 of M32's 정도 ("程度 measure-degree") — the measured stretch a thing passes through. 과정을 거치다 (this shelf's 거치다) = to go through a process; 결과보다 과정 (M32's 결과) = the process over the result, every teacher's line; 그 과정에서 = in the course of it. NIKL SENSE COLLAPSE, both yours: a second 과정 is 課程 — the task-課 of M44's 과제 ("課題 task-topic") + 程 — the curriculum: 석사 과정 (석사 — a master's, riding frozen) = a master's programme, 교육 과정 (M32's 교육) = the syllabus. One spelling: the road you travel and the course you enroll in.

段階 step-stairs: the step-段 that M55's 단 note filed as the other 단 ("Radar: M13's 계단 climbs a different 단 — step-段.") + 階, a FIRST — and M13's 계단 is 階段, the SAME two characters reversed: 계단 = stair-steps, the thing you climb; 단계 = step-stairs, the stage you are at. 첫 단계 (M46's 첫) = the first stage; 다음 단계 (M8's 다음) = the next step; 단계를 거치다 (this shelf) = to pass through a stage; 마지막 단계 (M15's 마지막) = the final phase. Everything in Korean planning happens 단계적으로 (the -적 factory from M45) — in stages. RADAR: not the single-單 of M55's 단 하나.

en: a period, a time; the right moment, timing
notes: NIKL SENSE COLLAPSE, two rows, one spelling, both yours. 時期 (a period): 時, the hour-時 of M5's 시 and M1's 시간, + the 期 of M34's 기대 ("期待 appointed-time-await") and M38's 기간 ("期間 term-between") — 어려운 시기 (M7's 어렵다) = a hard time, 그 시기에 = in that period, 사춘기 시기 = the adolescent years. 時機 (the moment): the same 時 + the 機 of M33's 기회 ("機會 machine-meeting") — 시기를 놓치다 (M12's 놓치다) = to miss the moment, 좋은 시기 = good timing. A period you live through and a moment you must catch — the essay uses both. RADAR, one clause: a third 시기 (猜忌 — riding frozen) is jealousy, 시기하다 = to envy; the word 시기심 on the drama's villain is that one.

時點 time-dot: the hour-時 of M5's 시 + M32's 점 ("點 dot: a point") — a dot on the timeline. 이 시점에서 = at this point (in time), the presenter's and the manager's phrase; 그 시점에 = at that moment; 현재 시점 (M35's 현재) = as of now. Where M38's 순간 is a moment felt, 시점 is a moment marked on a chart — the written register's 그때. RADAR: 시점 is also the narrator's point of VIEW in a novel (視點, riding frozen — the watch-視 of M87's 시각): 일인칭 시점 = first-person narration. On the timeline it is 時, in the literature class it is 視.

en: the early period, the initial stage
notes: 初期 first-period: the beginning-初 that M46's 최초 decoded ("最初 most-first") + the 期 of M38's 기간 ("期間 term-between"). 초기에는 = in the early days; 초기 단계 (this shelf's 단계) = the initial stage; 감기 초기 (M14's 감기) = the first days of a cold, when the pharmacist says catch it now; 조선 초기 (M26's 조선) = early Joseon. Its mirror is 후기 (the late period — riding frozen), and 중기 sits between. RADAR: M25's 초 (candle — "This one melts.") and the clock's second are different 초s; this one is the start-syllable of 초등학교 (M15), the one M25's 초 note already flagged.

直後 straight-after: the 直 of M56's 직접 ("直接 straight-touch") + the after-後 of M13's 후에 ("후 = the time after") and M46's 이후. Rides a noun or a past badge and then takes a particle: 사고 직후 (M36's 사고) = right after the accident, 졸업 직후에 (M44's 졸업) = right after graduation, 무너진 직후 (this shelf's 무너지다) = just after it collapsed. Where M46's 이후 is any time after, 직후 is the moment after — no gap. Its mirror 직전 (right before — riding frozen) does the same job on M13's 전에 side: 시험 직전 = just before the exam. The newsroom's pair for the seconds around an event.

以來 from-then-coming: the 以 of M32's 이상 ("以上 from-here-up") + the 來 of M2's 내일 ("來 coming") — from that point, coming forward to now. A dependent noun: it needs a time in front — 그 이래 = since then, 졸업한 이래 (M44's 졸업 on the past badge from M24) = ever since graduating, 유사 이래 (riding frozen) = since history began, the editorial's grandest opener. M46's 이후 note gave you the spoken twin — "그 이후로 = ever since" — and 이래 is the same span in the written register, always reaching to the present. RADAR: the 이래 of S4's 왜 이래 is 이렇게 해 squeezed, and the 이래 in M82's 코끼리 note ("코끼리 아저씨는 코가 손이래") is the quoting -(이)래 ("they say it's") — neither is this noun. Three 이래s; only this one is 以來.

en: flow, current, the drift (of time, talk, events)
notes: M35's 흐르다 through the -(으)ㅁ noun freezer from M67 — 흐르 + ㅁ, the 르 kept whole in the noun (흘러요 conjugates; 흐름 does not). That note let everything flow — "시간이 흘러요 (time flows)" — and the noun collects it: 시간의 흐름 = the flow of time, 대화의 흐름 (M24's 대화) = the thread of a conversation, 이야기의 흐름 (M24's 이야기) = the story's drift. 흐름을 타다 (M6's 타다) = to ride the current — of a trend, a market, a game; 흐름을 끊다 (M20's 끊다) = to break the flow. The essay's favorite abstract noun after 과정: history, money, and the second half of a football match all have a 흐름.

轉換 turn-swap: the turn-轉 that M50's 자동차 note found in the bicycle ("자전거 (M10) is 自轉車, the self-TURNING cart") and M50's 운전자 split ("carry-運, turn-轉") + the 換 of M64's 교환 ("換 (swap)"). 기분 전환 (M7's 기분) = a change of mood — the reason for the walk, the haircut, the trip; 전환점 (M32's 점) = the turning point; 방향 전환 (M31's 방향) = a change of direction, on the road and in a career; 전환하다 = to switch over. Where M32's 변화 is change as it happens, 전환 is change with a hand on the switch — a turn made, not a turn suffered.

M53's 회복하다 dismounted — that note read it "回復 turn-back-restore" and set the frame "건강을 회복하다" (M14's 건강). The bare noun runs the headlines: 경기 회복 (M17's 경기 in its economy sense) = economic recovery, 피로 회복 (M53's 피로) = the little brown bottle's promise, 회복이 빠르다/느리다 (M12's 빠르다, M12's 느리다) = a fast or slow recovery — the doctor's sentence; 회복 단계 (this shelf's 단계) = the recovery phase. 회복되다 is the happen-form from M53; 회복력 (riding frozen) is resilience, the 2020s' word. The turn-back-回 is the same round as M80's 일회용.

運命 carry-life: M36's 운 ("運: luck") + the 命 of M64's 명령 ("命 (life) + 令 (deed)") — the life you are carried through. s_m37_dry_cleaner's note already sent it out in a ballad — "your fate (운명에, in ballads)" — and here it stands: 운명이에요 = it was meant to be; 운명적인 만남 (the -적 factory from M45, M2's 만나다 nouned) = a fated meeting; 운명을 받아들이다 (M56's 받아들이다) = to accept one's fate; 운명을 바꾸다 (M9's 바꾸다) = to change one's destiny — the drama's thesis and antithesis. Where M36's 운 is a coin flip, 운명 is the whole run. Says 운명 as written — the ㄴ and ㅁ are both nasals, nothing slides.

en: a bond, a tie between people; a karmic connection
notes: 因緣 cause-tie: the 因 M86's 인하다 introduced ("因 cause — a FIRST") + 緣, a first — the thread of cause that ties two people together, Buddhism's word for why you met. 인연이 있다/없다 = to be, or not be, meant to cross paths (the 있다 factory, at its most fatalistic); 좋은 인연 = a good connection, said of a spouse, a mentor, a business partner; 인연을 맺다 (맺다 — to tie, riding frozen) = to form a bond; 인연을 끊다 (M20's 끊다) = to cut ties. The proverb on the gap deck — 옷깃만 스쳐도 인연 — says even sleeves brushing is one. Where M32's 관계 is the relationship you have, 인연 is the reason you have it. Says 이년 — mind the ㄴ, it is not the insult 이년, which is a different word and not for you.

en: a mate, the other half of a pair; one's partner
notes: The other half: 짝이 맞다 (M15's 맞다) = to match, to be a pair (the NIKL row's own frame, ~이 맞다); 짝이 없다 = odd, unmatched — a sock, a chopstick, a person; 짝을 짓다 (M54's 짓다) = to pair up, the teacher's command; 짝꿍 (riding frozen) = your seatmate, the desk-partner of every Korean primary school; 짝사랑 (M7's 사랑하다 nouned) = one-sided love, a pair with only one half in it. Also the counter for pairs: 양말 한 짝 (M21's 양말) = one sock. RADAR: the 짝 inside M62's 깜짝 (M26's 놀라다 note: "깜짝 is the jump itself") is a mimetic syllable, not a mate — and the 짝짝 of the M51 gap deck's clapping is a sound. This 짝 is the one that matches.

M5's 하나 in its counter shape 한 + 마디 (a joint of bamboo, a bar of music, a single word — riding frozen): one word's worth of speech. 한마디로 (M6's 로) = in a word, the summarizer's opener (gap deck); 한마디도 못 했어요 (M2's 도, M3's 못) = I couldn't get a word out; 한마디만 할게요 (only-만 from M30) = just one thing — the toast is never one thing; 한마디 하다 = to say a word, and in the office, to have a word with someone. Written solid, one noun, and NIKL ranks it 804 — the size of a remark, not of a word: 한마디 can be a whole sentence, and 말 한마디로 천 냥 빚을 갚는다 (riding frozen) says one can pay off a debt of a thousand coins.

M50's 움직이다 ("The everything-mover") through the -(으)ㅁ noun freezer from M67 — 움직이 + ㅁ. The body's: 움직임이 빠르다 (M12's 빠르다) = quick-moving, the coach's word; the camera's: 움직임을 지켜보다 (this shelf) = to watch the motion; the newsroom's: 새로운 움직임 (M35's 새롭다) = a new move, a stirring — a party's, a market's, a protest's. That verb's note filed "마음이 움직였어요 = I was moved"; the noun keeps the reach: 마음의 움직임 = a stirring of the heart. Says 움지김 — the ㄱ steps over to the ㅁ syllable's vowel.

en: to undergo, go through, experience (something hard)
notes: To live through a thing, usually a hard one: 어려움을 겪다 = to go through hardship — M7's 어렵다 in the -(으)ㅁ noun freezer from M67 (that md's "어렵다 → 어려움"); 전쟁을 겪다 (M32's 전쟁) = to live through a war; 위기를 겪다 (M86's 위기) = to weather a crisis; 변화를 겪다 (M32's 변화) = to undergo change. M33's 경험 ("experience is what passing through things leaves on you") is the noun; 경험하다 experiences neutrally, 겪다 leans toward suffering — you 경험하다 a culture, you 겪다 a divorce. Says 격따 — the ㄲ batchim reads as ㄱ. The verb the retrospective endings were made for: 겪어 보니까 알겠더라고요 = having been through it, I understood.

en: to pass through, go via; to go through (a stage)
notes: Through and out the other side: 단계를 거치다 (this shelf's 단계) = to go through a stage, 과정을 거치다 (this shelf's 과정) = to go through a process, 부산을 거쳐 (M12's 부산) = via Busan — the itinerary's word, 여러 사람의 손을 거치다 (M29's 여러, M8's 손) = to pass through many hands. Where 겪다 (above) suffers the passage, 거치다 just records it — a checkpoint, not a wound; the -아/어 form 거쳐 is its commonest coat (거쳐서 = via, by way of). RADAR: M17's 치다 (to hit, to play) is inside the spelling and nowhere in the meaning — 거치다 is one verb, not 거 + 치다.

en: to realize, come to see (a truth)
notes: To wake up to a thing: the 깨 of M36's 깨다 (to break, to wake — that note's "잠에서 깨다 — sleep is a thing you break OUT of") with an old verb for reaching welded on — you wake, and you arrive at the truth. ㄷ-irregular, the family of M6's 걷다 ("ㄷ-irregular like 듣다: 걸어요, 걸었어요.") and M2's 듣다: 깨달아요, 깨달았어요, 깨달은. 잘못을 깨닫다 (M63's 잘못) = to realize one's mistake; 의미를 깨닫다 (M32's 의미) = to grasp the meaning; 뒤늦게 깨달았어요 (M6's 뒤 + M8's 늦다, welded) = I realized too late. RADAR: M13's 닫다 is the law-abiding one ("A law-abiding ㄷ — 닫아요, unlike 듣다/걷다."); 깨닫다 is not 깨다 + 닫다 and does NOT behave — the ㄷ flips to ㄹ before a vowel. Where M4's 알다 knows, 깨닫다 comes to know — the verb of the moment the penny drops.

en: to have lived (up to now), to come through life
notes: M4's 살다 + M1's 오다, welded: to live one's way up to the present — life as a road that arrives at today. Almost always in the past badge from M24 or the past tense: 지금까지 살아온 인생 (M25's 인생) = the life I've lived so far, 평생 살아온 동네 (M22's 동네) = the neighborhood I've lived in all my life, 열심히 살아왔어요 (M10's 열심히) = I've lived hard, the retiree's summary. The 오다 is the same coming-toward-now that M28's 가져오다 and M23's 돌아오다 carry: the past walks TOWARD the speaker. Its twin walks away — next entry.

en: to live on, go on living, make one's way through life
notes: M4's 살다 + M1's 가다: to live onward from here — life as a road that leaves today. 앞으로 살아갈 날들 (M25's 앞으로, M11's 날 with the plural 들) = the days still to live; 함께 살아가다 (M29's 함께) = to live together in the world, the public-service ad's verb; 살아가는 이야기 (M24's 이야기) = the stories of getting by, the neighbor's small talk; 어떻게 살아가야 할까요? (M10's 어떻게, -아/어야 from M39) = how should we live? 살아오다 looks back from now, 살아가다 looks forward from now — one verb, two directions, both present in every memoir's first page. The 가다 also says the living is WORK: 살아가다 is making a living as much as being alive.

en: to carry (on one's person); to possess (a quality, a meaning)
notes: To have about you: 의미를 지니다 (M32's 의미) = to carry a meaning, 가치를 지니다 (M87's 가치) = to have value, 특징을 지니다 (M45's 특징) = to bear a feature, 힘을 지니다 (M14's 힘) = to hold power — and literally, 늘 지니고 다니는 사진 (M38's 늘, M16's 다니다) = a photo I always carry. Sort against M28's 가지다 (that note: "가지다 grips it") and M56's 갖다 ("the written register trusts it with abstractions"): 가지다 holds in the hand, 갖다 holds on the page, 지니다 carries in the character — a quality you would not put down. The verb of essays about what a work of art or a nation possesses; you will read it far more than you say it.

en: to be equipped with, have in place; to meet (conditions)
notes: To have everything in its place: 조건을 갖추다 (M39's 조건 — "the strings attached") = to meet the conditions, 자격을 갖추다 (M64's 자격) = to hold the qualifications, 실력을 갖추다 (M26's 실력) = to have the skills in hand, 시설을 갖추다 (M50's 시설) = to be fitted out with facilities — the job posting's verb and the hotel brochure's. Kin of M56's 갖다 (to have, held): 갖다 has, 갖추다 has ALL of it and in order — the -추 is the same completing tail that turns 낮다 into 낮추다 (M37). 갖출 것을 갖추다 = to have what one ought to have; 예의를 갖추다 (예의 — courtesy, riding frozen) = to observe the proprieties, the bow included. Says 갇추다.

en: to join, connect; to continue, carry on (a line)
notes: To join end to end — a rope, a road, a lineage: 뒤를 잇다 (M6's 뒤) = to succeed someone, to carry on after them; 말을 잇다 (M4's 말) = to go on speaking (말을 잇지 못했어요 = I was lost for words); 전통을 잇다 (M26's 전통) = to carry a tradition forward; 두 도시를 잇는 다리 (M22's 도시, M14's 다리) = the bridge that links two cities, in the badge. ㅅ-irregular — M14's 낫다 ("ㅅ vanishes before vowels"), M40's 젓다 and M54's 짓다 (that note: "M14's 낫다 and M40's 젓다 finally seat their third member") now seat a fourth: 이어요, 이었어요, 이은, but 잇고, 잇는. RADAR: says 읻따 alone, exactly like M1's 있다 — 잇다 joins, 있다 exists, and only the vowel forms tell them apart (이어요 vs 있어요). Its happen-form is next.

en: to be connected, lead on; to continue, go on
notes: 잇다 (above) + -아/어지다 — the ㅅ gone before the vowel (이어 + 지다), the shape M35's 이루어지다 note built ("이루다 + -아/어지다: the glue as a vocabulary word"): the do-form joins, the happen-form IS joined. 길이 이어지다 (M12's 길) = the road continues; 회의가 세 시간 동안 이어졌어요 (M10's 회의, M28's 동안) = the meeting went on for three hours; 이야기가 이어지다 = the story picks up again; 대대로 이어지다 (대대로 — generation to generation, riding frozen) = to be handed down. The newsroom's verb for anything that keeps going — a drought, a strike, a losing streak — and the badge form 이어지는 = ongoing, continuing. Where M28's 계속 is the adverb, 이어지다 is the verb.

en: to advance, move forward, press on
notes: M28's 나다 (to emerge, to sprout) in its -아 form + M1's 가다: to come out and go on — forward. 앞으로 나아가다 (M25's 앞으로, or M6's 앞 with 으로) = to move ahead; 한 걸음 나아가다 (M38's 걸음) = to take a step forward; 목표를 향해 나아가다 (M26's 목표, 향해 — toward, riding frozen) = to press on toward the goal — the commencement speech's verb. Prose also uses the bare -아 form as a connector: 나아가 = furthermore, and beyond that — the essay's next rung after M85's 더욱. RADAR: says 나아 exactly like the 나아요 of M14's 낫다 (to get better — 나 + 아요), but this is 나다 + 가다: no illness improves in 나아가다, though the drama would like you to think so.

M52's 머무르다 note wrote the receipt — "르-family (M7's table): 머물러요 — and it even clips to 머물다" — and the clip turns out to be a NIKL headword of its own, ranked 2469: same meaning, one syllable lighter, and a plain ㄹ-stem where the long form was 르-family: 머물어요 is wrong — the clipped verb conjugates 머물러요 too, but its dictionary form and its badge (머무는, ㄹ dropping like 살다 → 사는) are its own. 호텔에 머물다 (M23's 호텔) = to stay at a hotel; 서울에 며칠 머물 거예요 (M25's 며칠) = I'll stay in Seoul a few days; 제자리에 머물다 (제자리 — one's original place, riding frozen) = to stay put, to stagnate — the report's verdict on a flat economy; 시선이 머물다 = a gaze lingers, the novel's. Radar from that note still holds: M23's 묵다 counts the nights, 머물다 spans the stay.

維持 tie-hold: 維 (a rope, a tie) + 持 (to hold) — both FIRSTs — + 하다: to hold a thing where it is. 건강을 유지하다 (M14's 건강 — the frame M53's 회복하다 set as "건강을 회복하다", one verb later) = to keep one's health; 관계를 유지하다 (M32's 관계) = to keep a relationship going; 질서를 유지하다 (M57's 질서) = to keep order — the police statement's verb; 체중을 유지하다 (체중 — body weight, riding frozen) = to hold one's weight, the diet's hardest stage. Its happen-form 유지되다 = to be sustained; the noun 유지 alone runs the compound 현상 유지 (M35's 현재's kin 현상, riding frozen) = the status quo. Where M26's 지키다 keeps a promise, 유지하다 keeps a level.

en: to watch over, keep an eye on; to watch (how things go)
notes: M26's 지키다 ("약속을 지켜요 — keep your word" — but also to guard) in its -어 form + M1's 보다: to guard-and-see — to watch closely, without stepping in. 아이를 지켜보다 (M4's 아이) = to keep an eye on a child; 상황을 지켜보다 (M33's 상황) = to watch how the situation develops — the diplomat's and the doctor's verb (좀 더 지켜봅시다 = let's wait and see); 조용히 지켜보다 (M13's 조용하다 through the -히 adverbializer) = to watch quietly; 지켜봐 주세요 = please keep watching (me) — the debut interview's last line, said to the fans. Not a passive looking: the 지키다 inside means you are ON it. The verb of the eyewitness — and the ending this module teaches, -더라고요, is what you say after you have 지켜본 it.

en: to strive, take pains, make an effort
notes: 애 (effort, one's inmost strain — riding frozen: the 애 of 애를 쓰다, 애가 타다) + M10's 쓰다 (to use): to spend one's effort. 애써 = with effort, taking pains — 애써 웃었어요 (M7's 웃다) = I forced a smile; 애쓰지 마세요 (-지 마세요 from M14) = don't trouble yourself; 애쓰셨어요 / 애쓰셨습니다 (the honorific -(으)시- from M4) = you worked hard — the thank-you for effort that, unlike M71's 수고하다 ("never up at a boss"), etiquette lets you send upward (gap deck). RADAR: M47's 애 is a kid ("아이 (M4) worn smooth by speech") — 애가 애쓰다 is a child trying hard, two different 애s in three syllables. Where M26's 노력하다 makes an effort, 애쓰다 makes it visibly and at a cost.

en: to achieve, bring about (on a grand scale)
notes: M35's 이루다 ("To make real: 꿈을 이루다") in a bigger coat: to achieve something the size of a nation. 경제 발전을 이룩하다 (M32's 경제; M57's 발전, whose note "pre-filed 경제 발전") = to achieve economic development — the textbook sentence about the 1970s; 통일을 이룩하다 (M31's 통일) = to achieve reunification, the speech's; 평화를 이룩하다 (M32's 평화) = to bring about peace; 눈부신 성장을 이룩하다 (눈부시다 — dazzling, and 성장 — growth, both riding frozen) = to achieve dazzling growth. You 이루다 a dream; a country 이룩하다-s a miracle — the verb never fits a small object, and it never sounds spoken. Says 이루카다 — the ㄱ and ㅎ merge. The ceremonial sibling of a household verb.

M41's 흔들다 + 리, the passive party of M36 — and that note pre-ran the exact sentence: "Feed it to M36's machine and the bus does it to you: 버스가 흔들려요 — shaken, not shaking." Today the shaken verb gets its own card, and the reach is what NIKL ranks: 마음이 흔들리다 (M19's 마음) = to waver, to be tempted; 나무가 흔들리다 (M22's 나무) = the trees sway; 믿음이 흔들리다 (M34's 믿음) = one's faith is shaken; 흔들리지 않는 (-지 않다 from M28, in the badge) = unwavering, on the brand and on the resolution. The subject is what gets shaken; put the shaker in with 에 or M29's 때문 with 에. The verb of the retrospective: 그때 마음이 많이 흔들리더라고요.

Down all at once: 건물이 무너지다 (M22's 건물) = the building collapses — the 1995 Sampoong department store is the sentence's national memory; 다리가 무너지다 (M14's 다리) = the bridge falls; 회사가 무너지다 (M2's 회사) = the company goes under; 마음이 무너지다 (M19's 마음) = to be crushed — the heart as a building; 질서가 무너지다 (M57's 질서) = order breaks down, the editorial's. Its do-form is 무너뜨리다 (riding frozen — the 뜨리다 tail that M66's 떨어뜨리다 wears): to bring down. Where M36's 깨지다 breaks a cup and M36's 떨어지다 drops a thing, 무너지다 takes a structure down — and the retrospective ending fits it like a glove: 다 무너지더라고요.

水準 water-level: the 水 of M54's 수돗물 ("水道 water-channel") + the 準 of M39's 기준 ("基準 base-level") — where the water stands is the level, and the level is the standard. 수준이 높다/낮다 (M7's 높다 and 낮다) = the standard is high/low; 생활 수준 (M29's 생활) = standard of living; 수준 높은 교육 (M32's 교육, the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 in between) = high-level education. M57's 높이 measured how tall one thing is; 수준 measures where a thing stands against everyone else's — the first of this module's ten rulers.

規模 rule-pattern: the 規 of M39's 규칙 ("規則 rule-standard") + the 模 of M34's 모양 ("模樣 pattern-form") — the measured outline of a thing is its scale. 규모가 크다/작다 (M1's 크다 and 작다) = large-/small-scale; 사업 규모 (M43's 사업) = the size of the business; 대회 규모 (M51's 대회) = how big the tournament is. It sizes undertakings, not objects — a truck has a 크기 (M57), a project has a 규모 — and the next entry bolts the big-大 onto it.

範圍 pattern-enclosure: 範, a first, is the pattern-mould; 圍 is the enclose-圍 of M57's 주위 ("周圍") — the fence drawn around what counts. M72's 확대되다 note wrote the phrase on credit — "범위가 확대되다 (범위 — scope, riding frozen)" — and the ride ends here. 시험 범위 (M10's 시험) = what the exam covers, the question every student asks first; 범위를 넘다 (M36's 넘다) = to go beyond the scope; 넓은 범위 (M13's 넓다) = a wide range. Where 규모 says how BIG, 범위 says how FAR.

平均 flat-even: the 平 of M32's 평화 ("平和 flat-harmony") + 均, a first meaning even — level everything out and read the number. 평균 이상 (M32's 이상, "以上 from-here-up") = above average, 평균 이하 (M39's 이하) = below it; 평균 점수 (M15's 점수) = the average score; 평균적으로 = on average, the -적 factory from M45 wearing 으로. The 均 returns two shelves down in 균형, where evenness becomes balance.

單位 single-position: M55's 단 ("單 single") + the 位 of M31's 위치 ("位置 place-put") — the one place you count from. 미터 단위 (M30's 미터) = in meters; 가족 단위 (M4's 가족) = by family, in family units — the museum ticket's word; 단위가 크다 = the unit is large, the won's daily problem (everything is thousands). Every 평균, 규모 and 범위 on this shelf is measured in some 단위.

大型 big-mould: the big-大 whose 대- prefix M50's 대도시 note said "sizes up whatever it touches; it is not done working" + 型, a first — the mould a thing is cast in, its type. 대형 마트 (M3's 마트) = the big-box store, 대형 사고 (M36's 사고) = a major accident, 대형 화면 (M20's 화면) = a big screen; 중형 and 소형 (mid- and small-size, both riding frozen) fill out the car lot. RADAR: this 형 is 型 the mould — not M4's 형 the brother, and not the 衡 inside 균형 below.

The same big-大 of M50's 대도시 stamped onto this module's 규모: large-scale. It stands bare in front of a noun the way M57's 특별 does — 대규모 공사 (S2's 공사) = major construction, 대규모 행사 (M69's 행사) = a big event, 대규모 조사 (M44's 조사) = a large-scale survey; 소규모 (small-scale, riding frozen) is its mirror. Sort against 대형: 대형 is the size of one THING (a truck, a store, a screen); 대규모 is the size of an UNDERTAKING (a project, a survey, a protest).

比重 compare-heavy: the 比 of M86's 비하다 + the heavy-重 of M41's 체중 ("體重 body-heavy") — how heavy one part weighs against the whole. 비중이 크다/높다 = carries a lot of weight, counts for much; 비중을 두다 (M40's 두다) = to put weight on, to prioritize; the physics sense (specific gravity) is the same word, and the metaphor never left the lab. RADAR: not M11's 비 (rain) + S2's 중 (in the middle of) — nothing is raining in the middle of anything.

均衡 even-scale: the 均 of 평균 above + 衡, a first — the beam of a balance scale. 균형을 잡다 (M28's 잡다) = to find your balance; 균형을 잃다 (M28's 잃다) = to lose it — on a bicycle and in a budget alike; 균형 잡힌 식사 (M36's 잡히다 in the badge, M3's 식사) = a balanced meal, the nutrition poster's phrase. RADAR: the 형 is 衡 the scale-beam — not M4's 형 the brother and not the 型 of 대형 two entries up; three 형s, three characters.

增加 add-add: 增, a first, + the 加 of M51's 참가하다 ("參加 join-add"). The statistic's noun: 인구 증가 (M64's 인구) = population growth, 수출 증가 (M43's 수출) = a rise in exports, 증가 추세 (추세 — a trend, riding frozen) = an upward trend. Its mirror 감소 (減少 — decrease) rides frozen here, and every chart in the newspaper has both columns.

증가 + 하다: the print twin of M35's 늘다 and M56's 늘어나다 — 인구가 증가하다 is the report, 사람이 늘었어요 is the mouth. Intransitive despite the 하다 (things 증가하다 on their own; nobody 증가하다-s them), so the 되다-row never touches it. 크게 증가했어요 = rose sharply; 점점 증가하고 있어요 (M35's 점점, the -고 있다 progressive) = keeps rising. The verb the chart's arrow points with.

M35's 줄다 + M28's 들다 (entering): shrinking, watched — the decrease as a trend you can see, the way M56's 늘어나다 note said 늘어나다 "grows where everyone can see". 인구가 줄어들다 (M64's 인구) = the population is dwindling; 소리가 줄어들다 (M19's 소리) = the sound fades away; 관심이 줄어들었어요 (M24's 관심) = interest has tailed off. ㄹ-drop like 들다: 줄어듭니다. Sort: 줄다 is the fact, 줄어들다 the trend, and the report's own word, 감소하다, rides frozen.

The IOU M85's 상당히 wrote: "The adjective 상당하다 (a considerable amount) is a few modules down the C-list; recognize the 相當 when it comes" — it came. 相當 mutual-fitting, and it lives in the badge: 상당한 돈 (M9's 돈) = a considerable sum, 상당한 시간 (M1's 시간) = a good while; as a closer, 차이가 상당해요 (M57's 차이) = the gap is sizable. Second job, the fitting-當 doing its old work: [noun]에 상당하다 = to be equivalent to.

Native, and the mouth's own giant: 엄청난 돈, 엄청난 인기 (M17's 인기), 규모가 엄청나요. M73's 굉장히 note picked the spoken strong very; 엄청나다 is the adjective under the same breath, and its clipped adverb 엄청 (riding frozen) — 엄청 커요, 엄청 맛있어요 — is what young Seoul actually says where the textbook prints 아주 (M11). Calibration: 크다 is big; 거대하다 (next) is vast on the page; 엄청나다 is vast with your eyebrows up.

巨大 giant-big: 巨, a first — the giant character — + the big-大 of 대형. Vast, and written: 거대한 도시 (M22's 도시), 거대한 회사 (M2's 회사), 거대한 산 (M11's 산). The page's word for size that the mouth would hand to 엄청나다: 거대한 규모 is the editorial, 엄청난 규모 is the same fact told at dinner. And its 위대하다 cousin, next, is 大 with a different first character — big the other way.

en: to be great (of a person, a work) (偉大-)
notes: 偉大 great-big: 偉, a first — greatness of a person, never mere size. 위대한 세종대왕 (M26's 세종대왕 — whose 대 that note traced as "대 (great — 대학교's big-대)") = Sejong the Great; 위대한 작가 (M48's 작가) = a great writer; 위대한 인물 (M48's 인물) = a great figure. Only people and what they make are 위대하다; a mountain is 거대하다. Both are 大; the first character decides whether you look up at it or bow to it.

M28's 뛰다 + M28's 나다: leaps out = stands out. The M68 md welded 뛰다 onto 들다, 나가다, 오다 and 다니다; this is the fifth weld, and the only one that came out an adjective. 실력이 뛰어나다 (M26's 실력) = exceptionally skilled; 뛰어난 선수 (M17's 선수) = a top athlete; 뛰어난 작품 (M48's 작품) = an outstanding piece. Pair it with 못지않다, next: 뛰어나다 says better than the field; 못지않다 says not behind the best.

en: to be no less than, as good as
notes: M3's 못 (can't) + -지 않다 from M28: not-unable = not falling short, one spaceless word. Frame: [X]에 못지않게 / [X] 못지않게 = no less than X, as well as X — 형 못지않게 잘해요 (M4's 형) = as good as his brother; 프로 못지않은 실력 (M51's 프로, M26's 실력) = skill worthy of a pro. The -게 adverbializer from M33 is its usual coat. Sort against M47's 만큼: 형만큼 잘해요 is a tie measured; 형 못지않게 잘해요 is a tie conceded — the younger one caught up.

en: to be merely, no more than (不過-)
notes: 不過 not-exceed: the 不 of M39's 부족하다 ("不足 not-enough-foot") + the 過 that M33's 사과하다 spells — does not go past = is merely. Frame: [noun]에 불과하다 — 열 명에 불과해요 (M5's 열, the counter 명) = a mere ten people; 시작에 불과해요 (M8's 시작하다, nouned) = it's only the beginning; 소문에 불과해요 (M24's 소문) = it's just a rumor. Sort: 만 (M30) and 뿐 (M55) say only; 불과하다 says only, and it is not much — the disappointment is built into the verb.

Native: 드문 일 = a rare thing, 드문 경우 (M32's 경우) = an unusual case, 보기 드문 (M1's 보다 through the -기 nominalizer from M13) = rarely seen; 드물게 = rarely, with the -게 adverbializer from M33. ㄹ-drop: 드뭅니다, 드문. RADAR: there is no 물 in it — M1's 물 (water) is a syllable coincidence. Sort: 흔하다, next, is its mirror, and M8's 가끔 is a different axis — 드물다 grades how often the world does a thing, 가끔 how often you do.

Native: 흔한 이름 (M1's 이름) = a common name, 흔한 일 = an everyday thing, 요즘 흔해요 (M26's 요즘) = it's everywhere these days. M62's 흔히 arrived first — "흔히 states the world's — what is typical, not what is habitual" — and this is the adjective it was pressed from. 드물다 is its mirror; the pair grades how often the world does a thing, and neither one grades you.

en: to be abundant, rich in (豊富-)
notes: 豊富 plentiful-rich: 豊, a first — the harvest character, a full vessel — + the 富 of M43's 부자 ("富者 wealth-person"). 경험이 풍부하다 (M33's 경험) = richly experienced; 표현이 풍부하다 (M33's 표현) = expressive; 자원이 풍부하다 (자원 — resources, riding frozen) = resource-rich. The written twin of M7's 많다 for whatever counts as wealth: 경험이 많아요 is the résumé said aloud, 경험이 풍부합니다 is the résumé.

强力 strong-strength: the force-强 of M64's 강제 + the 力 of M39's 노력 ("努力 exert-strength"). 강력한 태풍 (M11's 태풍) = a powerful typhoon; 강력한 힘 (M14's 힘) = tremendous force; 강력하게 반대하다 (M64's 반대하다) = to oppose strongly. Sort against M63's 강하다: 강하다 is strong (a team, a will, a signal); 강력하다 is powerful — strong with force behind it, the weather bureau's and the police's word. Said 강녁하다, the ㄹ nasalizing after ㅇ.

en: to be constant, fixed, regular (一定-)
notes: 一定 one-fixed: M2's 일 (one) + the fix-定 of M33's 결정하다 ("決定 decide-fix") — set at one value and kept there. 온도가 일정하다 (M49's 온도) = the temperature is constant; 일정한 속도 (M57's 속도) = a steady speed; 수입이 일정하지 않아요 (M43's 수입) = the income is irregular — the freelancer's sentence. RADAR: M23's 일정 (itinerary / schedule) is 日程, day-course, a different pair of characters on the same sound; 일정이 일정하지 않아요 = the schedule isn't regular, both at once.

en: to be complete, whole, perfect (完全-)
notes: 完全 complete-whole: the 完 of M39's 완벽하다 ("完璧 complete-jade") + the all-全 of M31's 전국. M56's 완전히 arrived first and "is the form that passes the editor"; this is the adjective under it: 완전한 문장 (M33's 문장) = a complete sentence; 완전하지 않아요 = imperfect; 불완전하다 rides the 불- machine that M44's 합격 note kept paying. Sort: 완벽하다 is flawless; 완전하다 is whole — nothing missing rather than nothing wrong.

徹底 pierce-bottom: both characters firsts — go all the way through, down to the bottom. 철저한 검사 (M44's 검사) = a thorough inspection; 철저한 준비 (M8's 준비하다, nouned) = thorough preparation; 철저하게 (the -게 adverbializer from M33) or 철저히 (the -히 adverb, riding frozen) = thoroughly. The auditor's adjective, and the 底 (bottom) returns in 도저히 at the end of the shelf — the same bottom, reached in defeat.

嚴格 strict-frame: 嚴, a first — the stern character — + the frame-格 of M44's 합격 ("合格 fit-the-frame"). 엄격한 규칙 (M39's 규칙) = strict rules; 엄격한 선생님 (M4's 선생님) = a strict teacher; 엄격하게 = strictly. Said 엄껴카다 — the ㄱ + ㅎ merging as it does in 합격하다. Sort against M39's 심하다: 심하다 is harsh (the person went too far); 엄격하다 is strict (the frame is narrow, and it is applied without exception).

en: to be specific, particular; to specify (特定-)
notes: 特定 special-fixed: the special-特 of M57's 특별 + the 定 of 일정하다 above. It mostly stands bare as a determiner: 특정 지역 (M31's 지역) = a specific region, 특정 인물 (M48's 인물) = a particular person, 특정한 조건 (M39's 조건) = specific conditions. Its verb face is the detective's: 위치를 특정하다 (M31's 위치) = to pin down the location. Sort: M24's 특별하다 is special as in remarkable; 특정하다 is specific as in this one and not the others.

眞摯 true-sincere: the 眞 M74's 가짜 note X-rayed ("the heads are 眞 true and 假 false") + 摯, a first. 진지한 태도 (M33's 태도) = an earnest attitude; 진지하게 생각하다 (M10's 생각하다) = to think seriously; 진지한 이야기 (M24's 이야기) = a serious talk. RADAR: the 진지 in M47's 잡수시다 note ("진지 잡수셨어요?") is the honorific rice — a different word on the same sound. Sort against M63's 심각하다: 심각하다 is grave (the situation); 진지하다 is earnest (the person).

到底 reach-bottom: both characters firsts — having gone all the way to the bottom, still nothing. Negative-only, always: 도저히 못 하겠어요 = I simply can't; 도저히 이해할 수 없어요 (M10's 이해하다) = I cannot possibly understand; 도저히 안 돼요 (gap deck) = it just won't work. It joins the polarity family the M39 md filed — "절대 and 전혀 also travel only with negatives" — as the third member. Sort: 전혀 is not at all (a fact); 도저히 is not possibly (a defeat) — the bottom has been reached and the thing still isn't there.

假令 suppose-let: the 假 of M74's 가짜 + the 令 of M64's 명령 — let it be false for a moment = supposing. 가령 비가 오면 (M11's 비, -(으)면 from M20) = say it rains; 가령 이런 경우에는 (M32's 경우) = take a case like this. The lecturer's for-instance, and it leans toward the hypothetical — it sets up a case rather than listing one; 예컨대, next, lists.

M33's 예 in its second job ("예 = example — 예를 들면") + -컨대, a fossil ending riding frozen that survives in a handful of formal words. The essay's for example, one word, comma after: 예컨대, 서울이나 부산 (M12's 서울 and 부산, (이)나 from M43) = for example Seoul or Busan. Sort: 예를 들면 is said and written; 예컨대 is only written; 가령 supposes rather than lists. The 例 is M39's 예외 ("例外 example-outside") with the outside removed.

M85's 더욱 wrote it down — "Its cousin 더욱이 (moreover — riding frozen) opens the next point of an argument; 더욱 sharpens the current one" — and the ride ends. Sentence-initial, comma after: 더욱이, 비용도 많이 들어요 (M43's 비용, M28's 들다 in its cost job) = moreover, it costs a lot. The column's and-what's-more; M62's 게다가 (on top of that) is the mouth's, and M85's 아울러 binds where 더욱이 escalates.

en: side by side, in a row
notes: Native, the -히 tail on a root that never stands alone: 나란히 서다 (M14's 서다) = stand side by side; 나란히 앉다 (M9's 앉다) = sit together in a row; 나란히 걷다 (M6's 걷다) = walk abreast. Also the tie: 나란히 일등 (M76's 일등) = joint first place — two things shoulder to shoulder, and neither ahead. The one adverb on this shelf that measures nothing; it is here to keep the comparison level.

企業 plan-work: 企 (stand up to; to plan) + the work-業 of M43's 사업 ("事業 affairs-work"). M64's 대기업 decoded it in advance — "大 (big) + 企 (stand up to) + 業 (business)" — and today the bare word lands: 기업 is the firm as an institution, the newspaper's word for what M2's 회사 is in the mouth. 중소기업 (small and medium firms — riding frozen) is the other half of every economic headline; 기업가 is the entrepreneur, with the -가 of the 사업가 M43's 사업 note mentioned. Radar: 사업 is what you DO (사업을 하다); 기업 is what you ARE.

國會 country-gather: the country-國 of M31's 국가 + the gather-會 of M32's 사회 ("社會 gather-meet"). M58's 국회의원 note decoded the member and pointed here — "국회 is the assembly itself (the domed building in 여의도 — frozen landmark)" — and today the building gets its own entry: 국회에서 (in the Assembly), 국회를 통과하다 (통과 — passing, riding frozen) is what a 법률 does on its way to becoming law. Rom gukhoe: the ㄱ and ㅎ contract in the mouth (구쾨); the spelling keeps them apart.

政黨 govern-faction: the govern-政 of M32's 정치 ("政治 govern-manage") + 黨, the party-character — a first. The newsroom's pair rides frozen and the gap deck files it: 여당 (the ruling party) and 야당 (the opposition). RADAR, mandatory: 정당하다 (正當 — just, fair; riding frozen) is a different 정 and a different 당 — 정당한 요구 (M86's 요구) is a fair demand, not a party's.

法院 law-house: M39's 법 + the house-院 that M14's 병 note decoded ("병 (illness) + 원 (house) = 병원") and that M82's 동물원 note sorted from the garden-園 ("animals get a garden, patients get a house"). The court, building and bench: 법원에 가다, 법원의 판결 (this shelf). 대법원 (the Supreme Court — riding frozen) wears the big-大 of M64's 대기업 in front. Radar: 법원 is the building; the trial inside it is 재판, a few entries down.

機關 pivot-gate: the pivot-機 of M33's 기회 ("機會 machine-meeting") + the gate-關 of M32's 관계 ("關係 connect-tie"). An institution is machinery with a gate on it: 교육 기관 (M32's 교육) an educational institution, 정부 기관 (M32's 정부) a government agency, 공공 기관 (공공 — public, riding frozen) a public body. The same 機關 names an engine — 기관차, the locomotive (riding frozen) — and the newspaper sense is the one to file: the agency that ACTS.

en: organization, body (機構); apparatus, equipment (器具)
notes: Two words in one spelling, and NIKL lists both, so both are yours. 機構 (rank 1250): the pivot-機 of 기관 above + 構, to construct (a first) — an organization as a built structure: 국제 기구 (M31's 국제) an international body, 정부 기구. And 器具 (rank 3178): the vessel-器 of M51's 악기 and M83's 도자기 ("a VESSEL or a hand-tool gets 器") + 具, a tool (a first) — an implement: 운동 기구 gym equipment (M8's 운동하다, dismounted), 실험 기구 (실험 — an experiment, riding frozen) lab apparatus. Context sorts them: a 기구 you JOIN is 機構; a 기구 you LIFT is 器具.

組織 assemble-weave: 組 (to assemble; a group) + 織 (to weave), both firsts — an organization is a fabric. 조직을 만들다, 조직하다 to organize (the -하다 rides free), and 조직 생활 (M29's 생활) = life inside an organization, the phrase every new 사원 (M43) learns the hard way. The second sense is the biologist's: tissue — the same weave, read literally. Radar: 조직 is the body you are IN; 기관, above, is the body that acts ON you.

集團 gather-lump: the gather-集 of M44's 집중 ("集中 gather-middle") + the 團 M62's 단지 note kept in its radar ("團地 — 아파트 단지"). A group with a boundary around it: 집단 생활 (M29's 생활) is barracks and dormitories, 집단 행동 (M57's 행동) is collective action, 이익 집단 (M43's 이익) an interest group. RADAR: not M1's 집 — nobody lives in a 집단; the 집 here is 集, not a house.

民間 people-between: the people-民 of M32's 국민 ("國民 country-people") + the between-間 of M32's 인간 ("人間 person-between"). What lies among the people — everything that is NOT the state: 민간 기업 (a private company), 민간 단체 (단체 — an organization, riding frozen), 민간인 (a civilian — the person-인 M32's 정치 note put to "suffix work"), the headline's word when the army is not the subject. Its opposite is the state itself: 정부와 민간이 함께 (M29's 함께).

議員 discuss-member: M58's 국회의원 came "國會議員, decoded end to end" — discuss-議, the syllable inside M10's 회의, + the member-員 of M43's 사원 ("社員 company-member"). Today the tail dismounts: 의원 is the lawmaker on their own, 국회 의원 the same person written apart, and the address is the one M58 filed — "의원님 is the address". Radar: this 의원 (議員) sits in the Assembly; the 의원 (醫院, riding frozen) with the 의 of M4's 의사 is a neighbourhood clinic — same spelling on the sign, opposite buildings.

長官 chief-official: the long-長 of M39's 장점 ("사장님/부장님's chief-장") + the official-官 that M78's 외교관 note introduced ("官, official — a FIRST") and that M57's 관리 note glimpsed ("a historical homograph 관리 (官吏) is the Joseon official"). That 외교관 note left this word on the step — "장관, a government minister (riding frozen)" — and today it walks in: 교육부 장관 (the education minister; -부 the ministry, riding frozen), 장관님. The 官 of 외교관, 경찰관 and 장관 is one civil-service character; the 장 in front is the chief.

候補 wait-fill: 候 (to wait for, to watch for) + 補 (to fill in, to supplement), both firsts — the one waiting to fill the seat. 대통령 후보 (M32's 대통령), 후보자 with the person-者 M27's 환자 note introduced ("The -자 is a person-suffix (기자, 학자 — reporter, scholar)"), 후보로 나오다 (M28's 나오다) = to run. RADAR: this 후 is 候, not the after-後 of M13's 후에 — a candidate is not 'after' anything, however long they wait.

委員 entrust-member: 委 (to entrust — a first) + the member-員 of M43's 사원 — a member entrusted with a task. The committee itself is 위원회 (with the 會 of M10's 회의 — riding frozen): 선거 관리 위원회 (this shelf's 선거 + M57's 관리) runs every election in the country. Radar against 의원, above: an 의원 is ELECTED to the Assembly; a 위원 is APPOINTED to a committee — one syllable apart, one ballot apart.

위원 + the chief-長 of 장관: the head of a committee. The address is 위원장님, exactly as M9's 사장님 is the chief with 님 attached — the 長 that closes 사장, 부장 and 장관 now closes a committee. The 長 is the same character M39's 장점 stretched to mean 'long': the chief is the long one, the one who has been there longest. 국회 위원장 chairs a standing committee; 위원장을 맡다 (M37's 맡다) = to take the chair.

住民 live-people: the live-住 that M81's 주택 introduced ("住 live — a FIRST") + the people-民 of M32's 국민. The people who live somewhere: 지역 주민 (M31's 지역), 아파트 주민 (M13's 아파트), 주민 여러분 (M27's 여러분) — the notice-board's addressee. And the card in every wallet: 주민등록증, the resident registration certificate — M64's 등록 + the proof-證 of M83's 학생증 — the national ID; the gap deck has it. Radar, in the words of M50's 시민 note: "국민 answers to the country; 시민 answers to the town" — and 주민 answers to the street.

百姓 hundred-surnames: M9's 백 + the surname-姓 of M33's 성함 ("姓銜 surname-title") — the hundred surnames, the old word for the people as seen from the throne. M26's 왕 has 백성; a 대통령 (M32) has 국민 — the sageuk says 백성, the news says 국민, and the gap between them is four centuries. 백성을 위하다 (M32's 위하다) is the good king's job description. Not a word you will use about anyone alive; a word every historical drama uses about everyone.

en: charge, responsibility for; the person in charge (擔當)
notes: 擔當 carry-face: M64's 담당하다 ("擔 (carry on the shoulder) + 當 (face)") with the 하다 taken off — the noun M78's 담임 note already leaned on ("the carry-擔 of M64's 담당하다"). 담당자, the person in charge (the person-者 of M27's 환자), is who the front desk sends you to; 담당 직원 (M16's 직원), 담당 의사 (M4's 의사) pin the noun on a person like a badge. 제 담당이 아니에요 = not my department — the sentence bureaucracy runs on. M86's 당하다 shares the 當: 담당 faces a duty; 당하다 gets faced BY one.

法律 law-rule: M39's 법 + 律 (a rule, a measure — a first) — the law AS WRITTEN: what 국회 passes and a 법원 reads out. M39's 법 is the law in general and also the way of doing (its note: "김치 만드는 법 = how to make kimchi"); 법률 is only ever the statute — nobody makes kimchi by 법률. 법률을 만들다, 법률에 따라 (Part 3), 법률 전문가 (M58's 전문가). Rom beomnyul: ㅂ before ㄹ turns ㅁ and the ㄹ turns ㄴ — say 범뉼.

判決 judge-decide: the judge-判 of M34's 판단 ("判斷 judge-cut") + the decide-決 of M33's 결정하다 ("決定 decide-fix"). The court's decision, handed down: 판결을 내리다 (M6's 내리다 — the same DOWN M57's 결정 note used for 결정을 내리다), 판결이 나다 (M28's 나다). A 판단 is anyone's call; a 판결 is the bench's — a 판단 with a robe on. The 판사 (the judge — riding frozen) makes it.

裁判 cut-judge: 裁 (to cut cloth; to decide — a first) + the judge-判 of 판결 above. The trial: 재판을 받다 (M9's 받다 — you RECEIVE a trial the way you receive an exam), 재판을 하다, 재판이 열리다 (M36's 열리다 in its be-held sense). The set closes: 법원 is the building, 재판 is what happens inside it, 판결 is what comes out of it.

規定 rule-fix: the rule-規 of M39's 규칙 ("規則 rule-standard") + the fix-定 that M57's 결정 note named ("The 정 is fix-定"). A rule an organization has set down: 회사 규정 (M2's 회사), 학교 규정, 규정에 따라 (Part 3), 규정 위반 (M64's 위반), 규정을 어기다 (어기다 — to break a rule, riding frozen). Register: 규칙 is any rule, down to a board game (M39: "게임 규칙 = how to play"); 규정 is the rule that has a document number.

權利 authority-benefit: the authority-權 of M64's 권하다 ("權 (authority)") + the profit-利 of M43's 이익 ("利益"). A right is authority that benefits you: 권리가 있다/없다, 권리를 지키다 (M26's 지키다), and the phrase M69's 행사 note filed early — "권리를 행사하다 (권리 = a right, riding frozen)" — to exercise a right; today the frozen half thaws. Its twin is 의무 (duty — riding frozen): 권리와 의무, the pair on every civics test; 인권 (human rights, frozen) is 人 + this 權. Rom gwolli: ㄴ before ㄹ assimilates — say 궐리.

統制 unify-control: the unite-統 of M31's 통일 ("統 unite") and of M32's 대통령 + the control-制 of M64's 제한 ("制 (control)"). Control from above: 통제하다 (the 하다 rides free), 교통 통제 (M12's 교통 — a road closed for a parade), 출입 통제 (출입 — coming and going, riding frozen: keep out), 언론 통제 (M48's 언론 — press control, the word that dates a government). Radar: M64's 강제 is force applied once; 통제 is control kept up.

罪, the character for wrong — and the 죄 inside M4's 죄송합니다 all along (罪悚, wrong-plus-dread: the formal sorry is, literally, guilt and fear), never decoded until now. Alone it is guilt and sin: 죄를 짓다 (M54's 짓다 — a wrong is BUILT, like a house or a pot of rice), 죄가 있다/없다 (guilty / innocent — the verdict's two words), 죄인 a sinner (the person-人). The church says 죄; the courtroom says 범죄, next. Rom joe — one syllable, said 줴.

犯罪 commit-wrong: 犯 (to commit, to violate — a first) + 죄 above. 죄 is the wrong; 범죄 is the wrong the law has a name for: 범죄자 the criminal (the person-者 of M27's 환자), 범죄율 the crime rate (율 — rate, riding frozen), 청소년 범죄 (M35's 청소년) and 사이버 범죄 the sub-headings. 범죄를 저지르다 (저지르다 — to commit, riding frozen) is the collocation the report uses; the mouth says 죄를 짓다. Radar: 범 alone is also the tiger of folk tales (riding frozen), who never committed anything.

暴力 violent-strength: 暴 (violent, sudden — a first) + the strength-力 of M39's 노력 ("努力 exert-strength"), which is M14's 힘 in hanja. Force used to harm: 폭력을 쓰다 (M10's 쓰다 in its use-sense), 가정 폭력 (M47's 가정 — domestic violence), 학교 폭력 (M1's 학교 — school bullying, the news's standing headline), 폭력적 (the -적 factory of M45). RADAR: not M60's 폭 (幅, width) — 폭이 넓다 is wide, 폭력 is violent; and the same 暴 opens the 폭설 (heavy snow) M86 left frozen. Rom pongnyeok: ㄱ meets ㄹ and both nasalize — 퐁녁.

選擧 select-raise: the select-選 of M33's 선택하다 ("選擇 select-pick") + 擧 (to raise, to put forward — a first): to choose someone by raising them up. M46's 앞두다 note set the scene — "선거를 앞두고 = with the election ahead" — and today the noun arrives: 선거를 하다, 선거에 나가다 (M8's 나가다 — to run), 선거 결과 (M32's 결과), 대통령 선거 (M32's 대통령), 국회의원 선거 (M58's 국회의원). M61's 뽑다 is the spoken verb underneath: 대통령을 뽑다 = to elect the president.

示威 show-might: the show-示 that M75's 표시하다 note left frozen ("示 (show — frozen)") + 威 (might, authority — a first): to show your strength in public. 시위를 하다, 시위에 나가다 (M8's 나가다), 시위대 (the demonstrators — the unit-隊 of M58's 군대, riding frozen). Korea's word for the street as a political instrument, and the reason 촛불 시위 — M25's 초 + M13's 불 with the linking-ㅅ of M82's 바닷물 — has its own gap entry. Radar: this 시 is 示, not the city-市 of M50's 시민.

輿論 crowd-argument: 輿 (a carriage; the many, the public — a first) + the argument-論 of M44's 논문, spelled 론 here by the sound law M44's 토론 note laid out ("word-initial ㄹ softens to ㄴ (論文 → 논문) but keeps its ㄹ mid-word (討論 → 토론)"). What the many argue: 여론 조사 (M44's 조사) the opinion poll — the sentence deck runs one — 여론이 좋다/나쁘다, 여론에 따라 (Part 3). RADAR, mandatory: not M78's 여 (女, the female prefix) — there is no woman in 여론, only a crowd — and not the travel-旅 of M11's 여행.

公式 public-form: the public-公 of M6's 공원 as M48's 공연 note read it ("공원's (M6) public-公") + the form-式 of M55's 식 ("式 the way-hanja"). Two senses, one logic. Official — the public form of a thing: 공식 발표 (M44's 발표), 공식 입장 (입장 — a stated position, riding frozen), 공식적으로 (the -적 of M45 + 으로) officially. And the maths teacher's formula, 수학 공식 (M15's 수학) — a public form that always works. 비공식 (unofficial — the not-非 riding frozen) is the leak; 공식 is the press release.

名譽 name-praise: the name-名 inside M17's 유명하다 (有名 — to have a name) and inside the 명절 M75's 절약하다 note wrote out ("M25's 명절 (名節, the named ones)") + 譽 (praise — a first). Honour is a name well spoken of: 명예를 지키다 (M26's 지키다), 명예를 걸다 (M20's 걸다 in its hang-sense — to stake one's honour), 명예 훼손 (defamation — 훼손 damage, riding frozen: the charge every celebrity files), 명예 교수 (M27's 교수 — emeritus). Radar: M5's 명, the person counter, IS this 名 — to count people is to count names.

意圖 intent-plan: the intent-意 of M32's 의미 ("意味 intent-flavor") + the plan-圖 of M64's 시도하다 ("圖 (plan)"), which is also the drawn-圖 of M12's 지도, the map. Intent as the newspaper weighs it: 의도적으로 (deliberately — the -적 of M45), 나쁜 의도는 없었어요 (M29's 나쁘다 — there was no bad intent), 의도를 알다 (M4's 알다). -(으)려고 from M50 is intent in the mouth; 의도 is intent as a noun a court can examine. RADAR: M58's 국회의원 note parked the Assembly in 여의도 — that 의도 is an island's name and shares not one character with this one.

民主主義 people-master-ism: the people-民 of M32's 국민 + the master-主 of M38's 주로 ("主로 main-ly") and M27's 주인 + 主義, the -ism, closed by the 義 of M44's 강의 ("講義"). 민주 (the people as masters) + 주의 (a doctrine): the people rule, as a creed. RADAR, mandatory: the 주의 here is 主義; S2's 주의 is 注意, caution ("미끄럼 주의") — 민주주의 asks no one to be careful. The same -주의 builds 자본주의 (capitalism) and 사회주의 (M32's 사회 + -ism), both riding frozen. Rom minjujuui — five syllables, the last ㅢ said 이.

민주 + the becoming-化 of M32's 변화 ("變化 change-becoming") — the note that said "The suffix industrializes: 세계화 globalization". The becoming-democratic of a country, and in Korea a proper noun as much as a word: 민주화 운동 (M8's 운동하다, dismounted) is the movement, and June 1987 is its date — a month of nationwide 시위 that turned a military government into direct presidential 선거. 민주화 이후 (M46's 이후) dates the modern republic; 민주화되다 (the 되다-row) is the verb. 세계화, 민주화, 노령화 — one -화, three eras.

en: to rule, dominate; to control (支配)
notes: 支配 branch-allot: the branch-支 of M65's 지점 ("支 (support, branch-off)") + 配 (to distribute, to allot — a first): to hold the branches and hand out the shares. The 配 that M18's 배달 never decoded (that note's radar stopped at the belly of M3's 배) is this one — 配達, allot-and-deliver. To rule: 나라를 지배하다 (M23's 나라), 시장을 지배하다 (M3's 시장 — to dominate a market), 지배적 (dominant — the -적 of M45), 지배자 the ruler (the person-者 of M27's 환자). Register: M26's 왕 rules his 백성 with 다스리다 (the native verb, riding frozen); 지배하다 is what the textbook says an empire did, and what a 대기업 (M64) does to a market.

構造 construct-make: the 構 that M90's 기구 note filed as a first ("構, to construct (a first)") + 造, to make, to build — a first. How a thing is put together: 사회 구조 (M32's 사회) the structure of society, 구조적 (through the -적 factory of M45) structural, 구조 조정 (조정 — adjustment, riding frozen) the corporate euphemism for layoffs. RADAR, one clause: a homograph 구조 (救助, rescue) drives the 구조대 — the rescue squad, riding frozen — and NIKL lists only 構造, so the rescuers ride frozen too. This is the shelf's first word because every other word on it is one of its parts.

形態 shape-posture: the shape-形 of M37's 인형 ("人形 person-shape") + the 態 of M33's 태도 ("態度 posture-degree") and M34's 상태 ("狀態 form-posture"). The form a thing takes, as opposed to what it is made of: 다양한 형태 (M26's 다양하다 in the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24) = various forms, 새로운 형태의 가족 (M35's 새롭다, M4's 가족) = a new kind of family, [noun]의 형태로 = in the form of. RADAR: three 형-words open this shelf — 형태, 형식, 형성 — and none of them is M4's 형, the older brother; the character is 形, a shape.

形式 shape-way: 形 again + M55's 식 ("式 the way-hanja"). The form as a way of doing — a format, a template, and, when the way has outlived its point, a formality: 보고서 형식 (M43's 보고서) = the report format, 형식에 맞추다 (M37's 맞추다) = to fit the format, 형식보다 내용 (M32's 내용, with the than-보다 from M22) = substance over form. 형식적 through the -적 factory of M45 is where the word turns sour: 형식적인 인사 (the 인사 of M19's 인사하다) = a perfunctory greeting, 형식적으로 = for form's sake. 형태 is the shape a thing HAS; 형식 is the shape it is REQUIRED to have.

方式 direction-way: the 方 of M31's 방향 ("방 (方 direction)") + 式, the way-hanja from M55. M32's 방법 ("方法 direction-law: a method is a direction with rules") is the HOW that gets a thing done; 방식 is the STYLE it is habitually done in — 생활 방식 (M29's 생활) = a lifestyle, 사고 방식 (사고 — thinking, 思考, riding frozen; RADAR: not M36's 사고, the accident) = a way of thinking, 접근 방식 (this shelf's 접근) = an approach. 그런 방식으로 (M24's 그런, M6's 로) = in that manner — the sentence M55's 식 note ran as 그런 식으로, with the 방 put back. RADAR: not M8's 방, the room — M32's 방송 note counted three 방s already, and this is the direction one.

構成 construct-complete: 構 from 구조 above + the 成 of M35's 성공하다 ("成功 achieve-merit"). What a thing is made up of: 가족 구성 (M4's 가족) = family makeup, 구성원 (the member-員 of M43's 사원 — 구성원 riding frozen) = a member of a group, 이야기의 구성 (M24's 이야기) = the plot's construction. The noun of the pair below, and the shelf's first 하다/되다 flip. RADAR: not M23's 성 (the castle) — the 성 of 성공 was 成 all along.

en: to compose, to make up, to form (構成)
notes: The 하다 side: [parts]로 [whole]을 구성하다 = to make up the whole out of the parts — 전문가들로 위원회를 구성했어요 (M58's 전문가, the 위원 of M90 with the 회 of M10's 회의 — 위원회 riding frozen as the committee) = formed a committee of experts. The subject is whoever did the assembling — a government, an author, a coach. The news rarely names one, which is why the next entry is the one you will read.

en: to be composed of, to consist of (構成)
notes: The 되다 side, and the one the report writes: [whole]은/는 [parts]로 구성되다 = consists of — 세 부분으로 구성되다 (M32's 부분, M6's 로 marking the parts) = consists of three parts. The flip M70's 마련되다 note described — "되다 doesn't check pedigree, only the 하다 it replaces" — runs down this whole shelf: 구성하다/구성되다, 형성하다/형성되다, 실시하다/실시되다, three pairs in one module. The state form 구성되어 있어요 is the usual one, for the reason M70's 포함되다 note gave ("포함되어 있어요 far more than 포함돼요"): a composition is a standing condition, not an event.

形成 shape-complete: 形 + 成 — the shape coming to be. 인격 형성 (인격 — character, personhood, riding frozen) = character formation, the phrase on every school's mission statement; 여론 형성 (M90's 여론) = the forming of public opinion; 습관 형성 (M35's 습관) = habit formation. Sort against 구성: 구성 is what a thing IS made of; 형성 is the process of its coming to have a shape at all.

The 하다 side: to form something that has no shape yet — 좋은 관계를 형성하다 (M32's 관계) = to form a good relationship, 자신의 가치관을 형성하다 (M26's 자신, 가치관 — values, riding frozen) = to shape one's own values. Takes 을/를 like any 하다-verb; the object is the thing that ends up with a shape.

en: to be formed, to take shape (形成)
notes: The 되다 side, the report's and the textbook's: 습관은 어릴 때 형성돼요 (M35's 습관, M21's 어리다 under -(으)ㄹ 때 from M25) = habits are formed when you are young; 여론이 형성되다 = public opinion takes shape; 성격이 형성되다 (M19's 성격) = a personality forms. Nobody is named as the shaper — M35's 이루어지다 note called that the happen-form, and this is the same grammar with a Sino root.

en: function, feature (機能); a skill (技能)
notes: NIKL SENSE COLLAPSE — two words in one spelling, both yours. 機能 (rank 531): the machine-機 of M33's 기회 ("機會 machine-meeting") + the 能 of M39's 가능하다 ("可能 can-able") — what a machine is able to do, its function: 기능이 많다 = has a lot of features (the phone review), 새 기능 (M13's 새) = a new feature, 기능을 하다 = to serve a function. And 技能 (rank 5325): the craft-技 of M44's 기술 ("技術 craft-skill") + 能 — a skill in the hands: 기능을 익히다 (익히다 — to master, riding frozen; M40's 익다 note met it as the cooking causative, "익히다 cooks it through on purpose", and a skill is cooked through the same way) = to learn a trade, 기능 대회 (M51's 대회) = a skills competition. Context sorts them the way M90's 기구 note sorted 機構/器具: a 기능 a DEVICE has is 機能; a 기능 a PERSON has is 技能.

節次 section-sequence: the 節 of M37's 예절 ("禮節 courtesy-section") + the 次 of M46's 차례 ("次例 next-in-line") — the sections in the order they must come. 절차를 밟다 (M66's 밟다) = to go through the procedure — Korean STEPS through it; 절차가 복잡하다 (M22's 복잡하다) = the procedure is complicated, the line at every 구청 (frozen — the district office); 정해진 절차 (M33's 정하다 in the badge) = the set procedure. Sort the three order-words: M33's 순서 ("順序 order-sequence") is the order things come in, M46's 차례 is your turn in it, 절차 is the order that is REQUIRED. RADAR: not M26's 절 (the bow, the temple) and M2's 차 (the tea) — a bow over tea is a 차례, not a 절차.

Native — the shelf's one word with no hanja: the frame a thing is cast in, then the frame it can't get out of. 사진 틀 (M17's 사진) = a picture frame; 창틀 (M6's 창문, clipped) = a window frame; 틀을 깨다 (M36's 깨다 — the break-job, not the wake-job) = to break the mould; and the gap deck's 틀에 박히다 (박히다 — to be driven in, stuck, riding frozen) = stereotyped, stuck in a rut. Sound radar, three native 틀s: M15's 틀리다 (to be wrong) and M51's 틀다 (to turn on, to set flowing) share the syllable — dictionaries do trace 틀리다 back to a twisting-off-the-frame, but file the three by sound and keep this one as the noun.

土臺 earth-platform: 土, earth, soil — a first — + the 臺 of M51's 무대 ("舞臺 dance-platform") and the counter 대 of M55 (臺): a platform raised on the ground. 토대를 마련하다 (M56's 마련하다) = to lay the foundation, [noun]을/를 토대로 = on the basis of, M6's 로 doing its by-means-of job — 경험을 토대로 (M33's 경험). The grounds shelf now has three words, and M86's 바탕 note drew the first line ("Where 근거 is the evidence you cite, 바탕 is the ground you build on"): 바탕 is the ground, 토대 is the platform built on it, 근거 is the evidence you cite from it. In a building it is literal — the 토대 is the footing M57's 기초 note called 기초 공사.

核心 kernel-heart: 核, the kernel, the nucleus — a first (the bare 핵 belongs to Module 92 and rides frozen here) — + the heart-心 of M34's 의심 ("疑心 doubt-heart"). The seed inside the fruit: 핵심 내용 (M32's 내용) = the key points, 핵심 인물 (M48's 인물) = the key figure, 핵심을 찌르다 (M66's 찌르다, the needle-in verb) = to hit the nail on the head, 핵심은 이거예요 = here's the crux. The presenter's word — every 발표 (M44) has a slide called 핵심 정리 (M13's 정리하다, dismounted).

焦點 scorch-point: 焦, to scorch — a first — + the dot-點 of M32's 점 — the point where a lens brings the sun down to a burn. 초점을 맞추다 (M37's 맞추다, the tuning verb) = to focus on, of a camera and of an argument alike: 이 연구는 청소년에 초점을 맞췄어요 (M32's 연구, M35's 청소년) = this study focused on teenagers; 초점이 안 맞다 = out of focus, the verdict on a blurry photo; 초점 없는 눈 (M14's 눈 in the badge) = a vacant stare. RADAR: not M25's 초, the candle — though both burn — and not the 초 of 초등학교.

本質 origin-substance: the 本 of M57's 기본 ("基本: base-基 + 일본's (M27) origin-本") + the 質 of M45's 성질 ("性質 nature-substance"). What a thing IS underneath what it looks like: 문제의 본질 (M7's 문제) = the real issue, 본질적으로 (-적 from M45, then 으로) = essentially, 본질을 잃다 (M28's 잃다) = to lose sight of what it was for. 형태 is the shape you see; 본질 is what would remain if you took the shape away — the philosopher's word, and the columnist's.

根本 root-origin: the root-根 that M86's 근거 decoded ("根據 root-rely") + 本 again — a root under a root. 근본 원인 (M86's 원인) = the root cause, 근본부터 (M6's 부터) = from the ground up, 근본이 없다 = ill-bred — the insult that says a person has no roots (one clause, and never to a face). 본질 is what a thing is; 근본 is where it comes from — and the report reaches for 근본 when it wants to say the fix so far has been cosmetic.

根本的 — 근본 through the -적 factory of M45, and tagged noun by that module's house rule: 근본적인 해결 (M72's 해결) = a fundamental solution, 근본적인 변화 (M32's 변화) = a radical change, 근본적으로 = fundamentally. The word every editorial uses to say that the problem is the structure, not the people in it — which is this module's whole subject.

基本的 — M57's 기본 through the same -적 factory: 기본적인 예의 (M26's 예의) = basic manners, 기본적인 기능 = the basic features, 기본적으로 = basically, the word Korean presenters open a caveat with. Sort against its shelf-mate: 기본적 is what is EXPECTED of everyone (the floor); 근본적 goes down to the ROOT (the footing) — M57's 기초 note already split 기본 from 기초 the same way, and the -적 forms keep the split.

領域 command-domain: the 領 of M32's 대통령 ("大統領 big-unify-command" — the command-領) + the 域 of M31's 지역 ("역 (域 domain)"): the territory something has command over. 전문 영역 (M57's 전문) = one's area of expertise, 연구 영역 (M32's 연구) = a field of research, 개인의 영역 (M57's 개인) = one's private sphere, 영역을 넓히다 (M54's 넓히다) = to expand one's territory. Sort the three fields: 분야 is what you WORK in, 부문 is a division of an economy or a prize, 영역 is a territory of knowledge or law — one with a border.

部門 section-gate: the 部 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion") + the 門 of M54's 대문 ("大門 great-gate"): a section with its own gate. 각 부문 (M55's 각) = each division, 서비스 부문 = the service sector, 수출 부문 (M43's 수출) = exports; and the awards show: 남우주연상 부문 (riding frozen — best actor) = the best-actor category. 부분 is a piece of a thing; 부문 is a piece that has been given a door and a name.

分野 divide-field: the 分 of M32's 부분 + the field-野 of M81's 야외 ("野 field"): the fields divided up. 전공 분야 (M44's 전공) = one's field of study, 다양한 분야에서 (M26's 다양하다) = in various fields, 이 분야의 전문가 (M58's 전문가) = an expert in this field — the noun M58's 전문가 was waiting to be an expert IN. Of the three, the one you will say about yourself: 어느 분야에서 일하세요? = what field do you work in?

en: work, a task, a job of work (作業)
notes: 作業 make-work: the make-作 of M48's 작가 ("作家 make-house") + the work-業 of M43's 사업 ("事業 affairs-work"). Work as a piece of work, a task with a start and a finish: 작업 중 (S2's 중 — the busy-sign machine) = work in progress, 작업실 (the room-실 of M16's 사무실) = a studio, 공동 작업 (공동 — joint, riding frozen) = collaboration, 작업을 시작하다/끝내다 (M8's 시작하다, M16's 끝내다). RADAR: the 일 of M2's 일하다 is work in general; 작업 is one job of it. And the slang, one clause: 작업 걸다 (M20's 걸다) = to make a move on someone — a task with a start, if not a finish.
