實施 real-lay-out: the 實 of M34's 확실하다 ("確實 firm-real") + the 施 of M50's 시설 ("施設 lay-out-and-set-up"): to lay something out for real. The ministry's noun — 실시 여부 (여부 — whether or not, riding frozen), 실시 기간 (M38's 기간) = the period of implementation — and the noun of the pair below. Sort against 시행 (riding frozen): 시행 is the ENFORCEMENT of a law from a date; 실시 is the CARRYING-OUT of a thing that was planned. RADAR: not M63's 실수 with the o'clock-시 of M5 — 실시 is 實施, no mistake and no o'clock.

en: to carry out, to conduct, to implement (實施)
notes: The 하다 side: 시험을 실시하다 (M10's 시험) = to hold an exam, 조사를 실시하다 (M44's 조사) = to conduct a survey, 교육을 실시하다 (M32's 교육) = to run a training programme. The verb the notice board uses where the mouth uses 하다: 시험을 봐요 is the student's sentence, 시험을 실시합니다 is the school's. Whoever 실시하다s is an institution.

en: to be carried out, to be conducted (實施)
notes: The 되다 side, and the headline's: 조사가 실시되다 = a survey is conducted, 전국에서 실시된 시험 (M31's 전국, in the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24) = an exam held nationwide, 다음 달부터 실시돼요 (M8's 다음, M16's 달, M6's 부터) = takes effect from next month. The third 하다/되다 pair on the shelf, and the one with the most passive headlines to its name: something was carried out; the report does not say by whom, and the reader knows it was the state.

處理 place-manage: the 處 of M36's 상처 ("傷處 wound-place") + the 理 of M34's 이해 (理解): to manage a thing in its place — to deal with it. 쓰레기 처리 (M13's 쓰레기) = waste disposal, 일 처리가 빠르다 (M2's 일하다's 일, M12's 빠르다) = gets things done fast — the compliment every office wants, 정보 처리 (M33's 정보) = data processing, 사고 처리 (M36's 사고) = handling an accident. The verb 처리하다 is not on the slice but rides free: 빨리 처리해 주세요 = please take care of it quickly.

接近 contact-near: the 接 of M43's 면접 ("面接 face-contact") + the 近 of M31's 부근 ("근 (近 near)"): coming into contact by coming near. 접근 방식 (this shelf's 방식) = an approach, in the analyst's sense; 접근 금지 (S2's 금지) = keep out, on the fence; 접근이 쉽다/어렵다 (M7's 쉽다 and 어렵다) = easy/hard to get at. The noun a report uses for how it got at its problem, and the sign a substation uses for how you should not get at it.

Takes 에, not 을: 문제에 접근하다 (M7's 문제) = to approach a problem, 자료에 접근하다 (M44's 자료) = to access the data, 접근하기 쉽다 (M7's 쉽다 through the -기 nominalizer from M13) = easy to approach, said of a website and of a person. Sort against M62's 가까이 (near, as an adverb): 가까이 가다 is walking up to it; 접근하다 is the same walk in a report.

en: unfolding, development (of a plot, events) (展開)
notes: 展開 unfold-open: the 展 of M35's 발전하다 ("發展 unfold-expand") + the 開 of M72's 개발하다 ("開發 open-launch"): to unfold and open out. How a story goes: 이야기 전개 (M24's 이야기) = the plot's development, 빠른 전개 (M12's 빠르다 in the badge) = fast pacing — the drama review's highest praise — 사건 전개 (M36's 사건) = how events unfolded, 논리 전개 (논리 — logic, riding frozen) = the line of argument. 전개하다/전개되다 ride frozen; the noun is the one you will read. Sort against 발전: 발전 grows; 전개 unrolls.

統合 unify-fit: the 統 of M31's 통일 (the unite-통) + the 合 of M44's 합격 ("合格 fit-the-frame"): unified and fitted together. 두 회사의 통합 (M2's 회사) = the merger of two companies, 사회 통합 (M32's 사회) = social integration, 통합 검색 (M20's 검색하다, dismounted) = the all-in-one search. 통합하다/통합되다 are not on the slice and ride frozen. Sort against 통일: 통일 makes two into ONE; 통합 makes two into one BODY that still has parts — the peninsula wants the first, the merger gets the second.

導入 lead-in: 導, to lead, to guide — a first — + the in-入 of M43's 수입 ("輸入 ship-IN"). To lead a thing in from outside and install it: 제도 도입 (제도 — a system, an institution, riding frozen) = the introduction of a system, 새 기술 도입 (M44's 기술) = the adoption of a new technology, 도입 초기 (M88's 초기) = the early days after rollout. 도입하다/도입되다 ride frozen. RADAR: not M2's 도 (the also-particle) with M14's 입 (the mouth) — 導入 leads something in through the gate, not the mouth.

en: to install, to set up (設置)
notes: 設置 set-place: the 設 of M50's 시설 ("施設 lay-out-and-set-up") + the 置 of M31's 위치 ("位置 place-put"): to set a thing in its place. 앱을 설치하다 (M20's 앱) = to install an app — the verb under every 설치 button on your phone — 에어컨을 설치하다 (M11's 에어컨), 카메라를 설치하다 (M20's 카메라). The noun 설치 rides free and NIKL lists it too: 설치 중 (S2's 중) = installing. Where 도입 brings a SYSTEM in, 설치하다 bolts a THING to the wall — and M50's 시설 is what you get once enough of them are bolted.

生命 life-mandate: the life-生 M25's 인생 note read as "생 (life — 생일's 생)" + the 命 that opened M64's 명령 — "命 (life)" — the span heaven allots. 생명이 있다/없다 = to be alive / inanimate, the line a biology textbook draws; 생명을 구하다 = to save a life, with M43's 구하다 in the job that note filed second ("The same spelling's second job is rescue"). Three lives, sorted: M25's 인생 is the span of one person's years, M88's 삶 is the living of them (that note: "인생 is the span, 삶 is the living of it"), and 생명 is the force that makes a body alive at all — a sparrow has 생명, only a person has 인생. RADAR: not the counter 명 of M5 (네 명) — that is 名, the name-character, and this is 命.

存在 exist-be-at. M86's 의존하다 note paid the first half in advance — "存 exist (a FIRST — 존재, existence, rides frozen; it belongs to M92)" — and this is M92: the second half is the 在 of M35's 현재 ("現在 appear-exist"). Two jobs: the abstract noun (신의 존재 — M69's 신 — the existence of god) and the concrete one, a being (작은 존재 = a small being; 소중한 존재 — M87's 소중하다 — someone precious). 존재감 = presence, the feeling of being there, with the -감 that M39's 자신감 note traced ("the feeling-stuff suffix from M37's 장난감 note"): 존재감이 없다 = to be invisible in a room. Its verb is next door.

존재 + 하다: to exist, in the essay's voice. M1's 있다 PLACES a thing (책상 위에 있어요) and 존재하다 ASSERTS it: 신은 존재하는가 = does god exist — the philosophy seminar's question, never the kitchen's. Its negative is the long one from M28: 존재하지 않는다 = does not exist, the plain closer the page uses ("the plain form" the M32 md named). In the mouth it is 있어요 every time; the moment a sentence needs a THING to be rather than to be somewhere, the pen reaches for 존재하다.

en: life (the one you can lose; native)
notes: Native, and the anatomy is on the surface: M14's 목 (neck / throat) + M41's 숨 (breath — that note: "숨을 쉬다 = to breathe") — life is the breath in the throat. 목숨을 걸다 (M20's 걸다, the hanging job) = to stake one's life, to hang your life on it; 목숨을 잃다 (M28's 잃다) = to lose one's life; 목숨을 구하다 (M43's 구하다) = to save a life, the drama's version of 생명을 구하다. The sort: 생명 above is the force any living thing has — the scientist's word; 목숨 is the one YOU can lose — the mouth's word and the sageuk's, where it is always being spared or taken.

靈魂 spirit-soul: both characters firsts — 靈 the numinous, 魂 the soul that leaves the body. 영혼을 팔다 (M28's 팔다) = to sell one's soul; 영혼이 없다 = soulless, which is where the office joke lives — 영혼 없는 대답 (gap deck), the reply given with nobody home behind the eyes. Sort it from M34's 정신 ("精神 essence-spirit" — the mind, what you lose when 정신이 없어요) and from M19's 마음 (the heart you feel with): 정신 thinks, 마음 feels, 영혼 is what the priest and the horror film are talking about.

現實 appear-real: the appear-現 of M33's 표현 ("表現 surface-appear") + the real-實 of M34's 확실하다 ("確實 firm-real"). What is actually the case, as against what you hoped: 현실을 직시하다 (직시하다 — to look straight at, riding frozen) = face reality; 꿈이 현실이 되다 (M8's 꿈, M10's 되다) = a dream comes true; 현실은 달라요 (M24's 다르다) = reality is different, the sentence that closes every argument about a plan. Kin: M11's 진짜 and M74's 가짜 grade a THING as real or fake; 현실 is the real itself, the thing you wake up into.

현실 through the -적 factory of M45 — NIKL files it as a noun, as it files every -적 word, and it works like one: 현실적인 계획 (M8's 계획) = a realistic plan, 현실적으로 = realistically (the word that opens the sentence in which someone lowers your hopes), 현실적인 사람 = a practical person. Its negative wears the not-非 prefix: 비현실적 (unrealistic — riding frozen) is the verdict on the plan that assumed no traffic. Pairs with M45's 정신적 and 물질적 (four entries down) on the same -적 shelf.

現象 appear-image: 現 again + the image-象 of M41's 인상 ("印象 stamp-image") — a thing that appears and can be observed. 자연 현상 (M22's 자연) a natural phenomenon, 사회 현상 (M32's 사회) a social one — the noun a report puts after anything it has noticed but not explained. M88's 유지하다 note ran the compound 현상 유지 and called it "the status quo" with 현상 riding frozen — paid today. RADAR: not M40's 상 (床, the table dinner arrives on); NIKL lists only this 現象 row, so the prize-懸賞 of a wanted poster is not your problem yet.

宇宙 roof-and-ridge-beam: both characters firsts, and both originally mean the house — 宇 the eaves (space in every direction), 宙 the beam (time from past to future). The universe is a house, says the hanja. 우주선 = spaceship (船 the ship-character, riding frozen), 우주인 = astronaut (the person-人 of M32's 인간), 우주 여행 (M11's 여행). Three worlds, sorted: M22's 세상 is the world as lived, M23's 세계 is the world as mapped, and 우주 is everything the map is inside of.

人類 person-kind: the person-人 of M32's 인간 ("人間 person-between") + the kind-類 of M57's 종류 ("種類 seed-sort") — humans as a species, the essay's collective. 인류 역사 (M15's 역사) = human history; 인류의 미래 (M25's 미래) = the future of humankind; 전 인류 = all of humanity. Sort against 인간: 인간 is a human, one or many; 인류 is the whole set, never one. Says 일류 — the ㄴ bows to the ㄹ, exactly as in M64's 명령.

物質 thing-substance: the thing-物 of M35's 식물 ("植物 planted-thing") + the substance-質 of M45's 성질 ("性質 nature-substance") — what things are made of. The chemistry classroom's word (화학 물질 — 화학, chemistry, riding frozen) and the moralist's: 물질적 (material, through the -적 factory of M45) is the exact opposite of M45's 정신적 — 물질적인 도움 (M36's 도움) = material help, money. RADAR: the 물 is 物 (a thing), not M1's 물 (water) — 물질 has nothing to do with wet.

en: an object, a physical body (物體)
notes: 物體 thing-body: 物 again + the body-體 of M41's 체중 ("體重 body-heavy") — a thing considered as a body with mass and shape, the physics word. M9's 물건 is a thing you buy or own; 물체 is a thing that falls, floats, or reflects light: 물체가 움직여요 (M50's 움직이다) = the object is moving. The compound everyone knows rides frozen: 미확인 비행 물체 = unidentified flying object, the 비행 being the flight inside M12's 비행기 — Korean says UFO in five syllables of hanja when it wants to sound like the report.

核: the stone in the fruit — a first, and a word that stands alone. In the classroom it is the nucleus (세포의 핵 — 세포, the cell, riding frozen); in the headline it is nuclear, and it fronts compounds without a particle: 핵무기 (nuclear weapons — 무기 riding frozen), 핵 실험 (a nuclear test), 핵 문제 (M7's 문제) — the phrase this peninsula's news has run for thirty years. 핵심 (the crux, the core of the matter) is the next shelf's word; hear it as 핵 + 心 for now.

資源 asset-source: the asset-資 of M44's 자료 ("資料 asset-stuff") + 源, the spring a river rises from — a first, and NOT the 原 of M86's 원인 (that note: "原 the source, the origin (a FIRST)") — two source-characters, one for water, one for causes. 천연자원 (natural resources — 천연 riding frozen), 인적 자원 (human resources — the HR department's name for you, riding frozen), 자원이 풍부하다 — M89's 풍부하다 note ran it with the noun frozen ("자원이 풍부하다 (자원 — resources, riding frozen) = resource-rich") and today it is yours. RADAR: no kin with M9's 원 (₩) — a resource is what you spend the won to get.

大氣 big-air: the big-大 of M64's 대기업 + the energy-氣 of M36's 전기 ("電氣 electric-energy") — M22's 공기 is the air you breathe in a room; 대기 is the whole layer wrapped around M49's 지구. 대기 오염 (오염 — pollution, riding frozen) is the weather report's bad news; 대기 중에 = in the atmosphere. RADAR, two ways: the same spelling means WAITING (待機 — 대기실 the waiting room, 대기 번호 with M20's 번호 the ticket you pull; both riding frozen, and NIKL lists only the 大氣 row); and the 대기 inside M76's 꼭대기 is native syllables that mean nothing on their own.

氣候 air-season: 氣 again + the 候 that M90's 후보 decoded as "候 (to wait for, to watch for)" — the sky, watched over years. 기후 변화 (M32's 변화) = climate change, the phrase every editorial now carries; 온화한 기후 (온화하다 — mild, riding frozen). The sort against M7's 날씨 is the one geography teachers repeat: 날씨 is what the sky is doing today, 기후 is what it usually does — you dress for the 날씨 and move house for the 기후.

表面 outside-face: the outside-表 of M33's 표현 ("表現 surface-appear") + the face-面 of M43's 면접 ("面接 face-contact"). 물의 표면 = the water's surface, 지구의 표면 (M49's 지구), 표면이 매끄럽다 (매끄럽다 — smooth, riding frozen). The figurative use is the essayist's: 표면적으로는 (-적 from M45 plus 으로 plus 는) = on the surface, superficially — the phrase that promises a 사실은 (M24's 사실) in the next clause.

en: a river, a stream (the report's word) (河川)
notes: 河川 river-stream: 河, the big river — a first — + the 川 that M31's 인천 decoded as "천 (川 stream)". The word on the sign and in the flood report: 하천 정비 (정비 — maintenance, riding frozen), 하천이 넘치다 (넘치다 — to overflow, riding frozen). M22's 강 is the river you walk beside and name — 한강; 하천 is any watercourse a municipality is responsible for, including the concrete-lined one behind the apartment complex.

en: a valley; a mountain stream (溪谷)
notes: 溪谷 stream-valley: both firsts — 溪 the brook that runs down a mountain, 谷 the valley it cut. In English a valley is dry land; in Korean a 계곡 is where the water is, which is why the whole family goes to one in M11's 여름 — 계곡에 놀러 가다 (M19's 놀다) = go to the valley (to swim in the stream), 계곡 물이 차갑다 (M18's 차갑다). Sort: M11's 산 is the mountain, 계곡 is the cold crease in it, and 하천 above is what the stream becomes once it reaches town.

M1's 물 with the energy-氣 that runs 공기 (M22) and 전기 (M36) hung on its tail — NIKL writes the hybrid as 물-氣: water-vapour, the wet ON a thing rather than water itself. 물기를 닦다 (M8's 닦다, the wiping job) = to wipe the moisture off, the instruction on every recipe before oil meets pan; 물기가 없다 = dry; 물기가 남다 (M35's 남다) = still damp. Radar: 물 fills a glass; 물기 is what the glass leaves on the table.

肉體 flesh-body: 肉 flesh, a first, + the body-體 of M41's 체중. M45's 정신적 note split exhaustion in two — "정신적 vs 육체적 (bodily; a later shelf)" — and this is the later shelf: 육체적으로 힘들다 (M15's 힘들다) = physically hard, 육체 노동 (노동 — labour, riding frozen) = manual work. M14's 몸 is the body you wash and weigh; 육체 is the body as the opposite of M34's 정신 — the flesh that tires while the mind keeps going, or the other way round. RADAR: the 육 is 肉, not M2's 육 (six).

心臟 heart-organ: the heart-心 that M24's 진심 carried ("심 (heart)") + 臟, the internal organ, a first. This is the organ, not the feeling: 심장이 뛰다 (M28's 뛰다 — the heart runs) = the heart beats, 심장이 약하다 (M63's 약하다) = a weak heart, 심장 수술 (M53's 수술). The S1 slang deck welded it before you owned it — "심장 + 쿵 → **심쿵**" — paid. Three hearts, sorted: M19's 마음 is the one you feel with, M30's 가슴 the chest you feel it in, and 심장 the pump the doctor listens to.

呼吸 exhale-inhale: both firsts — 呼 to breathe out (to call), 吸 to breathe in (to suck) — one breath, both directions. 호흡하다 = to breathe (the textbook's), 호흡이 빠르다 (M12's 빠르다) = rapid breathing, 인공호흡 (artificial respiration, riding frozen). M41's 숨 is the native breath — "숨을 쉬다 = to breathe" — the one you hold and catch; 호흡 is the one the nurse counts. The idiom is the pleasant one: 호흡이 맞다 (M15's 맞다) = to be in sync, of a duet, a doubles team, two colleagues who finish each other's spreadsheets.

神經 spirit-thread: the spirit-神 of M34's 정신 ("精神 essence-spirit") + the 經 of M32's 경제 ("經濟 manage-and-aid") in its older sense, the warp-thread — the wiring the spirit runs on. Anatomically a nerve (신경 세포 — 세포 the cell, riding frozen); daily, the most-said phrase on this shelf: 신경 쓰다, with M10's 쓰다 in its use-job = to spend nerves on, to mind, to care about — 신경 쓰지 마세요 (gap deck) = don't worry about it, 신경 쓰이다 (M36's 쓰이다) = it bothers me, it is on my mind. 신경질 (a fit of nerves, riding frozen) is what happens when too much has been spent.

en: a sense; sensation; a feel for (感覺)
notes: 感覺 feel-perceive: the feel-感 of M42's 감정 ("感情 feel-affection") + 覺, to perceive, to wake to — a first. The IOU with two creditors: M45's 유머 note wrote 유머 감각 and confessed that "감각, the sense itself, waits on a later shelf"; M79's 패션 note ran "패션 감각 (감각 — a sense, riding frozen)" — both paid. Three jobs: the five senses (감각 기관 — 기관 from M90), a sensation (손에 감각이 없어요 = my hand is numb — M8's 손, M1's 없다), and a feel for something (유머 감각, 패션 감각, 언어 감각 — M26's 언어). M34's 느낌 is one feeling; 감각 is the faculty that has them.

en: a gaze, line of sight (視線)
notes: 視線 see-line: the 視 that M31's 시청 note filed as a homograph ("시청 (視聽) is also TV-watching") + the 線 that M76's 호선 called "a first for 線" — the line from an eye to a thing. Two notes have been waiting: M52's 머무르다 — "시선이 머무르다 (a gaze lingers)" — and M88's 머물다, "시선이 머물다 = a gaze lingers, the novel's". Now the noun: 시선을 끌다 (M51's 끌다 — "관심을 끌다 = pull attention") = to draw eyes, 시선을 피하다 (M36's 피하다) = to avoid someone's gaze, 시선을 느끼다 (M32's 느끼다) = to feel eyes on you, 남의 시선 (M74's 남) = what other people think — the pressure this culture names as a line of sight.

en: a glance, the eye's path; (homograph) a snowy road
notes: Native: M14's 눈 (eye) + M12's 길 (road / street / way) — the road an eye travels. NIKL's own hint on the row is ~을 피하다, and that is the frame: 눈길을 피하다 (M36's 피하다) = to avoid someone's eyes; 눈길을 끌다 (M51's 끌다) = to catch the eye; 눈길을 주다 (M9's 주다) = to spare a glance. 시선 above is the essay's word for the same line; 눈길 is the mouth's, and the warmer one. RADAR, mandatory: the other 눈 — M11's 눈, snow, whose note said "one syllable, sky and face" — makes the other 눈길, a snowy road: 눈길 운전 (M10's 운전하다, dismounted) in January is a road, not a look.

en: a fetus, an unborn child (胎兒)
notes: 胎兒 womb-child: both firsts — 胎 the womb, 兒 the child (the same 아 English hears in 아이, though M4's 아이 is native). The clinic's word: M47's 임신 (pregnancy) is the state, 태아 is who is in it — 태아의 심장 (this shelf's 심장) is what the ultrasound listens for. Korea's old habit of counting M4's 나이 from conception rather than birth (세는 나이 — the counted age, riding frozen) began with this word: the 태아 was already one.

出産 out-produce: the out-出 of M43's 출근 ("出勤 out-to-duty") + the 産 that M43's 부동산 filed as property ("the 産 is property") — here in its first sense, to bear. 출산하다 is the form's verb; M47's 낳다 is the mouth's. The compounds are the ones the news runs: 출산율 (the birth rate — 율 riding frozen), the number Korea leads the world downward in; 출산 휴가 (M11's 휴가) = maternity leave; 출산 준비 (M8's 준비하다, dismounted). Sort: M25's 태어나다 is the baby's verb, 낳다 and 출산 are the mother's.

en: one's children, sons and daughters (子女)
notes: 子女 son-daughter: the child-子 that M47's 손자 note pointed at ("The 자 is child-子") + the 女 of M32's 여성 ("女性 woman-nature"). The form's word — 자녀 교육 (M32's 교육), 자녀가 있으십니까 on the application. M47's 자식 is the same relationship in the mouth, and that note gave the reason to keep them apart: 자식 is a "Register double-agent" that flips into a scolding word; 자녀 never insults anyone. A survey asks about 자녀; a parent sighs about 자식.

Native: the house M22's 새 builds (that note: "새 새 — a new bird — is legal Korean and a tiny poem"). Its verb is fixed and rides frozen: 둥지를 틀다 = to build a nest, to settle somewhere — the verb the housing column borrows for newlyweds. 둥지를 떠나다 (M23's 떠나다) = to leave the nest, which Korean parents say about M47's 자식 exactly as English ones do; 빈 둥지 (M37's 비다) = the empty nest they are left with.

참 + M22's 새: the true bird, the one that is simply there. The prefix is the 참 that M82's 진달래 note filed on the flower — "country names call 진달래 참꽃 — M29's 참, the true flower" — and the sparrow gets it for the same reason: the commonest, the default, the one the word 새 means before you specify. Small and greedy, hence the proverb every Korean grandmother owns: 참새가 방앗간을 그냥 지나치랴 (gap deck) — can a sparrow pass the mill without stopping? — said of anyone who cannot walk past a bakery. NIKL's hint on the row is simply 동물 (M22).

Native: 꼬리를 흔들다 with M41's 흔들다 (that note ran "고개를 흔들다 = shake the head no") = to wag the tail — M22's 강아지 at the door. Two idioms carry it into the office: 꼬리에 꼬리를 물다 (M36's 물다, biting) = one thing leads to another, questions breeding questions; and 꼬리가 길면 밟힌다 = a long tail gets stepped on — do a thing often enough and you are caught — M66's 밟다 through the passive party of M36 (밟히다 riding frozen). 꼬리표 (a tag, a label that follows you, riding frozen) is the tail a reputation grows.

en: a gap, a crack; a spare moment
notes: Native: a crack between two things — 문 틈 (M6's 문) the gap under the door, 틈이 생기다 (M28's 생기다) a crack opens — and, by the same picture, a crack in the day. The M50 gap deck glossed it in passing — "틈 (a crack, a sliver of space)" — inside 발 디딜 틈이 없다; today the sliver is yours, and it has a verb: 틈이 나다 (M28's 나다 — the emerging job) = to find a moment, 틈이 나면 연락하세요 (M19's 연락하다) = call when you get a chance. Doubled it becomes an adverb, 틈틈이 = in spare moments, which is how this course expects you to study.

en: to be revealed, come to light
notes: Native, and the report's favourite intransitive: what was covered is now exposed. 사실이 드러나다 (M24's 사실) = the facts come to light; 문제가 드러났어요 (M7's 문제) = the problem surfaced; 조사 결과 드러났다 (M44's 조사, M32's 결과) is the headline's first line. RADAR against M32's 나타나다 ("갑자기 나타났어요 (appeared out of nowhere") — 나타나다 SHOWS UP, arriving from elsewhere; 드러나다 is EXPOSED, having been there all along under the cover. A ghost 나타나요; a scandal 드러나요. Its transitive twin 드러내다 (to reveal, lay bare) rides frozen.

en: to be revealed, be found out
notes: PAYS M87's 진실, whose note ran the phrase early — "진실이 밝혀지다 (the passive of M56's 밝히다, riding free) = the truth comes out" — and today it lands as a word. Build: M56's 밝히다 (make-bright, the news' bulb) + -아/어지다 from M35: 밝히 + 어지다 → 밝혀지다, the become-form. 원인이 밝혀졌어요 (M86's 원인) = the cause was established; 사실로 밝혀지다 (M24's 사실, M6's 으로) = turned out to be true; 아직 밝혀지지 않았다 (M14's 아직) = has not yet been determined — the line under every unsolved case. Sort against 드러나다 above: 드러나다 is exposed by circumstance, 밝혀지다 is established by someone's lamp — an investigation, a lab, a confession.

en: to grasp, get the picture of (把握)
notes: 把握 grasp-grip: 把 (to take hold of, a FIRST) + the grip-握 of M68's 악수 ("握手 grab-hand") — to understand is to get your hand around it. PAYS M86's 실정, which carried it frozen and named the date: "실정을 파악하다 (파악하다 — to grasp, riding frozen; it belongs to M93) = to get the picture". 상황을 파악하다 (M33's 상황) = to size up the situation; 원인을 파악하다 (M86's 원인) = to identify the cause; 내용을 파악하다 (M32's 내용) = to grasp the content, the reading-comprehension verb. Radar: M4's 알다 knows; M10's 이해하다 understands; 파악하다 has taken the measurements — it is the manager's verb, the investigator's, never the friend's.

en: to look over, examine; to read (a room)
notes: The root that M56's 살펴보다 was built on — that note defined the compound as "look with CARE, detail by detail" — and the bare verb does the same job one register up: 주위를 살피다 (M57's 주위) = to look around carefully, 상황을 살피다 (M33's 상황) = to survey the situation, 자료를 살피다 (M44's 자료) in a paper where the mouth would say 살펴보다. Its social job is the one M42's 눈치 note filed as 눈치를 보다: 눈치를 살피다 = to read the room, watching faces for the weather; 부모님 눈치를 살피다 is every teenager's evening. Print prefers 살피다; speech reaches for 살펴보다 — the -아/어 보다 from M16 is what makes it sound like a person.

en: to look into, find out; to recognize
notes: PAYS M33's 알아듣다, whose note promised this one — "Its eye-side twin 알아보다 = to recognize/look into" — the same weld, M4's 알다 + M1's 보다, aimed at the eyes. Two jobs. LOOK INTO: 가격을 알아보다 (M21's 가격) = to check on the price, 제가 알아볼게요 (with -(으)ㄹ게요 from M84) = I'll find out, 알아봐 주세요 = please look into it — the errand verb of every office. RECOGNIZE: 못 알아봤어요 = I didn't recognize you — the sentence that opens every reunion (M19's 오랜만 usually follows), and 사람들이 제 실력을 못 알아봐요 (M26's 실력) = people don't recognize my skill — the artist's complaint. Radar: the -아 보다 here is welded, not the try-machine from M16 — 알아보다 is one verb, 알아 봐요 is not something anyone says.

M72's 분석하다 dismounted — that note decoded it ("分析 divide-split") and already knew the noun would come: "The noun 분석 rides free — 데이터 분석 (데이터 riding frozen) on every job posting". The ride ends here. 분석 결과 (M32's 결과) = the analysis results, the report's second heading; 분석에 따르면 (에 따르면 from M32, the source frame M90 promoted) = according to the analysis; 자료 분석 (M44's 자료), 원인 분석 (M86's 원인), and 분석적 with the -적 stamp from M45 = analytical. To analyze (M72's 분석하다 note again) is to divide until it's bright — the noun is the pile of pieces, sorted.

M9's 주다 + -아/어지다 from M35: 주 + 어지다 → 주어지다, to be given — the become-form of the course's most useful verb, and the report's way of receiving without naming a giver. It lives mostly in the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24: 주어진 조건 (M39's 조건) = the given conditions, 주어진 시간 (M1's 시간) = the time allotted, 주어진 업무 (M57's 업무) = the duties assigned. Full verb too: 기회가 주어졌어요 (M33's 기회) = an opportunity was given — no one gave it, says the report. Radar: not the 지다 of M36's passive party (열리다, 잡히다 are that); this is the -아/어지다 of M35, the change-of-state machine, where 주다 turns into what arrives.

en: to put forward, present (a plan, evidence) (提示)
notes: 提示 hold-forth-show: the hold-forth-提 of M61's 제공하다 ("提供 hold-forth-supply") + the show-示 that M75's 표시하다 left frozen in "表示 surface-show" — to hold a thing up so the room can see it. PAYS M86's 방안, which wrote the collocation in advance: "방안을 제시하다 (제시하다 — to put forward, riding frozen; it belongs to M93) = to propose one". 근거를 제시하다 (M86's 근거) = to present grounds; 의견을 제시하다 (M24's 의견) = to put forward a view; 신분증을 제시하다 (신분증 — ID card, riding frozen) at every counter that wants to see it. Radar: M16's 발표하다 announces to an audience; 제시하다 lays a thing on the table for a decision — every 제시 expects an answer.

指摘 point-pick: 指 (the finger, and its pointing — a FIRST) + 摘 (to pick out, as fruit from a tree — a FIRST): to point at a thing and pick it out, and in Korean the thing picked is nearly always a fault. 문제점을 지적하다 (M63's 문제점) = to point out the problem; 잘못을 지적하다 (M63's 잘못) = to call out a mistake; 선생님이 지적하셨어요 (M4's 선생님 with the honorific -(으)시- from M4) = the teacher pointed it out — and the class went quiet. Sort against M75's 비판하다: 비판하다 argues a case, 지적하다 points a finger — one sentence, one flaw, no essay.

en: a pointing-out, a criticism (指摘); intellectual (知的)
notes: Two words, one spelling, and NIKL lists both. ONE — 指摘, the noun of the verb above: 지적을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to get called out, the way M75's 비판하다 note said 비판을 받다 is received; 지적 사항 (사항 — item, riding frozen) = the points flagged, the auditor's list; 좋은 지적이에요 = good point — the one polite thing to say when someone has found your error. TWO — 知的, the know-知 of M44's 지식 ("知識 know-recognize") + the -적 stamp from M45: intellectual, as a quality — 지적인 사람 (in the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24) = an intellectual person, 지적 호기심 (호기심 — curiosity, riding frozen) = intellectual curiosity, 지적 재산 (M43's 재산) = intellectual property. Radar: only the second one takes 인; a 지적인 지적 — an intellectual pointing-out — is possible and, in a seminar, common.

M56's 주장하다 dismounted — that note read it as "主張 master-stretch" with the master-主 of M27's 주인 (the same 主 M38's 주로 runs on) and left 張 frozen; today the stretch-張 gets a home: it is the tight-stretched 張 of M34's 긴장하다 ("緊張 tight-stretched"). A claim is a position stretched out and stood on. 주장을 하다 = to make a claim; 주장을 펴다 (펴다 — to spread, riding frozen) = to lay out an argument; 그 주장에 따르면 (에 따르면 from M32) = according to that claim — the reporter's way of not signing it. M56's 요구하다 note built the ladder — "말하다 says, 주장하다 insists, 강조하다 underlines, 요구하다 sends the bill" — and 주장 is rung two, as a thing you can hold. RADAR: 팀의 주장 (M16's 팀) is the team CAPTAIN — 主將, a different 장, riding frozen — and a good captain has plenty of the first kind.

M75's 비판하다 dismounted — that note decoded "批判 strike-judge", wrote "비판 rides free", and filed the collocation: 비판을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to come under criticism. Now the noun stands: 비판이 많다 = there is much criticism; 비판의 대상 (대상 — the target, riding frozen) = the object of criticism; 비판적 with the -적 stamp from M45 = critical, in the thinking sense — the same 비판적 사고 M75 mentioned. Sort against this module's 지적: a 지적 is one finger on one flaw, a 비판 is an argument with reasons — and both are received with 받다, because in Korean criticism is something delivered to you, like M53's 치료 and M90's 재판.

en: to acknowledge, admit; to recognize (認定)
notes: 認定 recognize-fix: the recognize-認 of M64's 확인 ("確 (certain) + 認 (recognize)") + the fix-定 of M33's 결정하다 ("決定 decide-fix") — to recognize a thing and set it down as so. 잘못을 인정하다 (M63's 잘못) = to admit a fault, the sentence the apology needs before 죄송합니다 can mean anything; 실력을 인정하다 (M26's 실력) = to acknowledge someone's ability; 인정할 수밖에 없어요 (밖에 from M39 on the can-machine from M10) = I have to admit it. The receiving side welds M9's 받다 on: 인정받다 = to be recognized, to get one's due — 실력을 인정받았어요, the line every underpaid expert is waiting to say. Speech has clipped it to 인정! (I admit it / fair enough), the slang concession you will hear in every group chat.

M64's 요청 ("要 (essential) + 請 (ask)") finally conjugates: the need-要 M56's 요구하다 uses + the ask-請 of M64's 신청 ("請 (ask to do)"). Three ways to ask, sorted by register: M16's 부탁하다 asks a favour (잘 부탁드립니다), 요청하다 files a request (자료를 요청하다 — M44's 자료; 도움을 요청하다 — M36's 도움), and M56's 요구하다 sends the bill. 협조를 요청합니다 (협조 — cooperation, riding frozen) is the signage of every construction site and public office. The request arrives by the favour-quote M33 taught: 자료를 보내 달라고 요청했어요 = asked them to send the materials.

en: to reflect (opinions, in a decision) (反映)
notes: 反映 turn-back-project: the turn-back-反 of M64's 위반 ("違 (go against) + 反 (turn back)") + the projecting 映 M48's 촬영 note glimpsed in 영화 ("映, projecting onto screens") — to bounce a thing back onto a surface. A mirror does it; in Korean, so does a policy: 의견을 반영하다 (M24's 의견) = to reflect opinions in a decision, the committee's promise; 현실을 반영하다 (현실 — reality, riding frozen) = to reflect reality; 요구를 반영한 계획 (M86's 요구, M8's 계획, the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24) = a plan that takes the demands into account. The become-form 반영되다 rides free — 반영됐어요 = it was reflected, no one did it, says the report. Radar: M5's 반 (half) and M15's 반 (class) are neither this 反 nor each other.

en: to handle, deal with; to treat (a topic)
notes: Native, three-handed. PAYS M51's 악기, whose note said "악기를 다루다 is the formal phrase" — to handle an instrument, the hands sense: 기계를 다루다 (M72's 기계) = to operate a machine, 컴퓨터를 잘 다루다 (M10's 컴퓨터) = to be good with computers. The desk sense: 문제를 다루다 (M7's 문제) = to deal with a problem, 이 논문은 환경 문제를 다룬다 (M44's 논문, M32's 환경) = this paper treats the environmental problem — the verb of every abstract's first line. And the people sense: 사람을 다루다 = to handle people, 아이를 다루다 (M4's 아이) — carefully. Radar: M56's 해결하다 solves; 다루다 only takes the thing in hand — an article can 다루다 a war without ending it.

M51's 끌다 (pull, drag) with 이 in front — an old prefix that turns pulling into leading: to pull from the front. Same ㄹ-stem manners as its parent (M51 wrote "ㄹ-verb: 끌어요"): 이끌어요, 이끌었어요, 이끄는 (the ㄹ drops before -는, as in M28's 날다 → 나는). 팀을 이끌다 (M16's 팀) = to lead a team; 회사를 이끌다 (M2's 회사); 승리로 이끌다 (승리 — victory, riding frozen; M6's 으로) = to lead to victory — the sports page's verb. RADAR: 끌다 pulls a suitcase and 관심을 끌다 pulls attention (the collocation M51's 끌다 filed); 이끌다 pulls PEOPLE, and always forward. Its passive 이끌리다 (to be led, drawn) rides frozen.

實踐 real-tread: the real-實 of M72's 실제 ("實際 real-between") and M34's 확실하다 + 踐 (to tread, to step on — a FIRST): to make a thing real by walking on it. The noun is the gap between a plan and a life: 계획은 좋은데 실천이 문제예요 (M8's 계획, -는데 from M53) = the plan is fine, doing it is the problem. 실천에 옮기다 (M50's 옮기다) = to put into practice — literally to MOVE a thing over into practice, the resolution's verb; 실천 방안 (M86's 방안) = an action plan. Radar: M72's 실제 is reality as measured; 실천 is reality as done — 實 audits, 踐 walks.

en: to put into practice, carry out (實踐)
notes: The noun above with 하다 on: 계획을 실천하다 (M8's 계획) = to carry out a plan; 약속을 실천하다 (M5's 약속) = to keep a promise by doing it, not by remembering it; 배운 것을 실천하다 (M2's 배우다 in the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24, -는 것 from M17) = to practise what you learned. The New Year's sentence: 올해는 꼭 실천할 거예요 (M25's 올해, M29's 꼭, -(으)ㄹ 거예요 from M8) = this year I'll actually do it. Sort against M10's 연습하다: 연습하다 practises a SKILL, repeating it; 실천하다 practises a PRINCIPLE, living it — you 연습하다 the piano and 실천하다 the diet.

en: to carry out, perform (a task) (遂行)
notes: 遂行 accomplish-go: 遂 (to accomplish, see through — a FIRST) + the going-行 that M28's 날다 note showed inside 비행기 ("飛行 — flying-going"): to go a task through to its end. 역할을 수행하다 (M57's 역할) = to perform a role; 업무를 수행하다 (M57's 업무) = to carry out duties; 임무를 수행하다 (임무 — a mission, riding frozen) = to carry out a mission — the soldier's and the spy's. PAYS M87's 평가, which parked the school's dread word: "수행평가 (riding frozen) = the school's performance assessment" — 수행 is this 遂行, the task as done, graded. Radar: M1's 하다 does; 수행하다 does what was ASSIGNED — nobody 수행하다s a hobby.

en: to display, bring out (an ability) (發揮)
notes: 發揮 launch-wield: the launch-發 of M35's 발전하다 ("發展 unfold-expand") + 揮 (to wave, to wield — a FIRST, the arm swinging a brush or a sword): to let a power out where it can be seen. One frame owns it: 실력을 발휘하다 (M26's 실력) = to show what you can do — the coach's wish before the match, the manager's before the pitch; 능력을 발휘하다 (M44's 능력), 제 실력을 발휘하지 못했어요 = I couldn't perform at my level, the honest exam post-mortem. 힘을 발휘하다 (M14's 힘) is what a policy or a medicine does when it works. Radar: M75's 표시하다 shows a feeling on the surface; 발휘하다 brings a stored power out — nothing is displayed that was not already inside.

對應 face-respond: the face-對 of M32's 대하다 ("對하다 to-face") + the respond-應 of M86's 반응 ("應 respond, answer (a FIRST)") — a response made facing the thing. 대응이 빠르다/늦다 (M12's 빠르다, M8's 늦다) = the response was quick / slow, the crisis review's first line; 대응 방안 (M86's 방안) = a response plan; 대응책 = a countermeasure, kin of M86's 대책 on the same plan-策. Sort the two: M86's 반응 is what comes back at you by reflex — a crowd's, a body's; 대응 is what you decide to send back. Radar: not the 응 of M71's 응 ("The casual yes"), though a fast 대응 often begins with one.

en: to respond to, deal with (對應)
notes: The noun above in motion, and it takes 에: 위기에 대응하다 (M86's 위기) = to respond to a crisis; 변화에 대응하다 (M32's 변화) = to respond to change, the strategy deck's verb; 빠르게 대응했어요 (M12's 빠르다 with the -게 adverbializer from M33) = responded fast. Where M10's 대답하다 answers a question and M71's 답하다 answers it in print, 대응하다 answers a SITUATION — no one asked, and something still had to be sent back. Also the maths and the diplomat's 'correspond to': A에 대응하는 B = the B that corresponds to A — the same facing, with nothing hostile in it.

en: to prepare for, guard against (對備)
notes: 對備 face-prepare: the face-對 of M32's 대하다 + the prepare-備 M83's 준비물 carried ("準備物") — to get ready FACING a thing. Takes 에: 시험에 대비하다 (M10's 시험) = to prepare for the exam; 겨울에 대비하다 (M11's 겨울); 지진에 대비해서 (지진 — earthquake, riding frozen) = in preparation for an earthquake — the drill's and the building code's verb. RADAR against M8's 준비하다: 준비하다 gets a thing ready (저녁을 준비하다), 대비하다 braces for a thing that might come — you 준비하다 the dinner and 대비하다 the storm. Second radar: 대비 is also 對比, contrast (명암 대비 — light-dark contrast, riding frozen), the designer's word; NIKL's row for this verb is 對備, the bracing one.

强化 force-becoming: the force-强 of M64's 강제 ("强 (force) + 制 (control)") + the becoming-化 that M32's 변화 explained ("(化, becoming)") — to make a thing become strong. 보안을 강화하다 (보안 — security, riding frozen) = to tighten security; 규정을 강화하다 (M90's 규정) = to tighten the regulations; 관리를 강화하다 (M57's 관리) = to strengthen oversight — the announcement after every accident. The become-form 강화되다 rides free: 검사가 강화됐어요 (M44's 검사) = screening has been stepped up. Radar: M22's 강 (the river) is 江; M63's 강하다 (strong) is this 强 as an adjective — 강화하다 is 강하다 industrialized.

改善 reform-good: 改 (to alter, reform — a FIRST) + the good-善 of M39's 최선 ("最善 most-good"): to change a thing toward the good. PAYS M81's 생활환경, which wrote the city-plan phrase with this word frozen — "생활환경 개선 (개선 — improvement, riding frozen)" — and today it stands alone. 개선이 필요하다 (M16's 필요하다) = needs improvement, the review's verdict; 개선 방안 (M86's 방안) = an improvement plan; 관계 개선 (M32's 관계) = an improvement in relations, the diplomatic page's. 개선하다 / 개선되다 ride free on the usual 하다/되다 split — 개선됐어요 = it has improved, no one did it. Radar: M53's 좋아지다 is getting better on its own; 개선 is getting better by design.

一致 one-reach: the one-一 of M45's 일반적 ("一般 one-kind") + 致 (to reach, to bring to — a FIRST): two things arriving at one point. Takes 와/과 (M30 — M2's 하고 in its written coat) or a plural subject: 의견이 일치하다 (M24's 의견) = opinions agree; 결과가 예상과 일치해요 (M32's 결과, M34's 예상) = the results match the prediction, the lab's sentence of relief; 말과 행동이 일치하지 않아요 (M4's 말, M57's 행동) = words and deeds do not match — the verdict on a politician. The noun 일치 rides free: 의견 일치 = consensus; 만장일치 (unanimity — riding frozen) is the committee's rarest word. Radar: the 一 is the 일 M2 counted with (one) — and this verb never counts anything.

克服 overcome-subdue: 克 (to conquer, to win over — a FIRST) + the 服 that M83's 운동복 wore as clothing ("服 clothing") — here in its other sense, to subdue, to make submit: the same character clothes you and bends the enemy's knee. 어려움을 극복하다 (M67's 어려움) = to overcome hardship; 위기를 극복하다 (M86's 위기) = to weather a crisis — the 1997 story every company history tells; 두려움을 극복하다 (두려움 — fear, riding frozen) = to get over a fear; 한계를 극복하다 (M39's 한계) = to break through a limit, the sports documentary's. Radar: M17's 이기다 wins against an opponent; 극복하다 wins against a condition — you 이기다 a team and 극복하다 an injury.

en: to refuse, reject (a demand, an order) (拒否)
notes: 拒否 refuse-no: the refuse-拒 of M33's 거절하다 ("拒絶 refuse") + the or-not-否 of M33's 안부 ("安否 peace-or-not"): to push back and say no. RADAR against M33's 거절하다, and the line is what is being refused: 거절하다 declines an OFFER or a favour (부탁을 거절하다, the example M33's 거절하다 gave), 거부하다 refuses a DEMAND or an order — 요구를 거부하다 (M86's 요구), 명령을 거부하다 (명령 — an order, riding frozen), 대답을 거부했어요 = declined to answer, the suspect's line. A 거절 can be gentle; a 거부 is a wall. The noun 거부 rides free — 거부권 (veto — the right-權 of M90's 권리) is the Assembly's, 거부감 = a feeling of resistance, on the -감 that M39's 자신감 bottles.

除外 remove-outside: 除 (to remove, to clear away — a FIRST) + the outside-外 of M39's 예외 ("例外 example-outside") — to put a thing outside the count. The verb is rarer than its frame: [noun]을/를 제외하고 = except for, leaving out — 저를 제외하고 다 왔어요 (M9's 다) = everyone came except me; 주말을 제외하고 (M2's 주말) = weekdays only, the timetable's phrase; 세금을 제외한 가격 (M43's 세금, the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24, M21's 가격) = the price before tax. Its become-form 제외되다 rides free — 명단에서 제외됐어요 (명단 — the list, riding frozen) = was dropped from the list, the squad announcement's cruellest verb. Radar: M39's 예외 is the exception that stands outside; 제외하다 is the hand that puts it there.

展望 unfold-gaze: the unfold-展 of M35's 발전하다 ("發展 unfold-expand") + the gaze-望 of M34's 희망 ("希望 rare-gaze") — to look out over what opens ahead. The report's sense is the forecast: 전망이 밝다/어둡다 (M13's 밝다, M13's 어둡다) = the outlook is bright / dark, the year-end economy page's verdict; 경제 전망 (M32's 경제); 전망에 따르면 = according to the forecast. The eye's sense is the actual view: 전망이 좋은 방 (M8's 방) = a room with a view, the hotel's upsell, and 전망대 — 전망 on the platform-臺 of M51's 무대 ("舞臺 dance-platform") — is the observation deck. Radar: M34's 예상 is what you personally expect; 전망 is what the horizon shows — an analyst gives a 전망, a friend gives an 예상.

en: to be expected, be forecast (豫想)
notes: M34's 예상 ("豫想 beforehand-think") through the flip M36's passive party named and M53's 걱정되다 quoted — "swap the 하다, get the happen-form" — the prediction that nobody makes. It closes the forecast: 비가 올 것으로 예상됩니다 = rain is expected — the future hook -(으)ㄹ from M8 on the 것 of M17, then 으로 (M6), then this verb in the 합니다체 from M4. That frame, -(으)ㄹ 것으로 예상되다, is the weather report's and the economics page's whole grammar: 물가가 오를 것으로 예상됩니다 (물가 — prices, riding frozen; M22's 오르다) = prices are expected to rise. 예상되는 결과 (in the badge -는 from M24, M32's 결과) = the expected result; 예상된 일이에요 = that was to be expected. Radar: 예상하다 (I expect — riding free on M34's 예상) has a person in it; 예상되다 has removed them, which is why print prefers it.

葛藤, both characters FIRSTS: 葛 the kudzu and 藤 the wisteria — two vines that climb the same tree and twist against each other. That is what a conflict is in Korean: not a blow but a tangle. It pays the IOU M86's 비롯되다 note wrote — "갈등 — conflict, riding frozen; it belongs to M95" — and the frame that note ran, 그 문제에서 비롯된 갈등, is now fully yours. 세대 갈등 (M47's 세대) = the generational conflict the 세대 차이 grows into; 갈등을 겪다 (M88's 겪다) = to go through a conflict; 갈등을 해결하다 (M56's 해결하다) = to resolve it. Says 갈뜽 — the ㄹ tenses the ㄷ.

競爭: 競 compete (a FIRST — two people running side by side) + the 爭 of M32's 전쟁 ("戰爭 war"): a war with running instead of weapons. 경쟁이 치열하다 (치열하다 — fierce, riding frozen) = the competition is fierce, the sentence on every university and every 취직 (M43); 경쟁 상대 (M57's 상대) = a rival; 경쟁하다 rides frozen, because print prefers the noun and a verb you own — 경쟁을 하다, 경쟁에서 이기다 (M17's 이기다). Where M51's 대회 is one competition with a date, 경쟁 is the condition of having rivals at all.

경쟁 + the 力 of M39's 노력 ("努力 exert-strength"): competing-strength — competitiveness, the ministry's favourite noun. 경쟁력이 있다/없다 = competitive / not; 경쟁력을 키우다 (M35's 키우다) = to build competitiveness, said of companies, cities, and, unkindly, of children; 국가 경쟁력 (M31's 국가) headlines the economy page. The ㄹ nasalizes after ㅇ the way M88's 겪다 note filed its batchim — say 경쟁녁, rom gyeongjaengnyeok.

協力: 協 join, unite (a FIRST — three strengths under one roof) + the same 力 of M39's 노력: joined strength — cooperation. 협력이 필요하다 (M16's 필요하다), 국제 협력 (M31's 국제) between countries, 협력하다 riding frozen for the verb. RADAR against 협조 (riding frozen), which is the compliance a form asks for — 협조 부탁드립니다 is a sign asking you to comply; 협력 is two parties working as one. Says 혐녁: the ㅂ becomes ㅁ and the ㄹ becomes ㄴ — the double shift M81's 국립 note filed for the ㄱ.

勝負: the 勝 of M51's 우승 ("優勝 excel-win") + the 負 of M86's 부담 ("負 to bear on the back" — to bear, and so to lose): win-and-lose as one word, the decision a match exists to produce. 승부를 내다 (M28's 내다, "The put-it-out verb") = to settle it; 승부가 나다 (M28's 나다) = it gets decided; 승부를 겨루다 (겨루다 — to vie, frozen) is the commentator's line; 승부차기 = the penalty shoot-out (차기 — the kick, frozen); 승부욕 (the 욕 of M45's 욕심) = the competitive streak, gap deck. RADAR: M17's 이기다 and 지다 are the verbs; 승부 is the noun that contains both — and its 부 is 負, not the section-部 of M32's 부분.

To argue it out — words, not fists. RADAR against M19's 싸우다: 싸우다 fights (and covers the fists), 다투다 argues (and never touches); 부부가 다투다 (M25's 부부) is a domestic squabble, 부부가 싸우다 may need a neighbour. Second job, the sports page: 순위를 다투다 (순위 — ranking, frozen) = to vie for the rankings. The -(으)ㅁ freezer from M67 makes the noun 다툼 — a quarrel — the way M67's 싸움 came from 싸우다. Conjugates plain: 다퉈요, 다퉜어요.

en: yielding, giving way; a concession (讓步)
notes: The noun inside M75's 양보하다 — that note decoded it, "讓步 yield-a-step", and ran the noun early: "양보 rides free: 양보 운전 (the 운전 inside M10's 운전하다) is painted on highway signs" — today it dismounts. 양보 운전 = yielding at the wheel; 자리 양보 (M12's 자리) = giving up a seat; 양보가 없다 = no give at all; 서로 양보하다 (M24's 서로) = to meet halfway — the word every negotiation in Korean ends with or breaks on. The whole module is built on this noun: concession is a step given.

接觸: the 接 of M43's 면접 ("面接 face-contact") + 觸 touch (a FIRST — a horn that touches): physical contact. 접촉 사고 (M36's 사고) = a fender-bender, the accident where two cars merely touched; 접촉을 피하다 (M36's 피하다) = to avoid contact, the clinic's phrase; 신체 접촉 (신체 — the body, frozen) = physical contact. Its adjective cousin 밀접 rides frozen — 밀접한 관계 (M32's 관계) = a close relationship. M91's 접근 is the approach; 접촉 is the arrival.

沈默, both FIRSTS: 沈 to sink + 默 to be silent — silence as something you sink into. Not the quiet of a room (M13's 조용하다) but the silence a person KEEPS: 침묵을 지키다 (M26's 지키다) = to keep silent, 침묵이 흐르다 (M35's 흐르다) = a silence falls, and the proverb the gap deck holds, 침묵은 금 (M60's 금) = silence is golden. 침묵하다 rides frozen. Says 침묵 with both ㅁs full — chimmuk.

Rough to the hand and rough in the manner: 거친 바람 (M11's 바람) = a rough wind, 거친 말 (M4's 말) = harsh words, 거친 손 (M8's 손) = work-worn hands, 거친 바다 (M11's 바다) = a rough sea. The mirror of M41's 부드럽다 — soft — and the pair sorts every surface and every voice. ㄹ-stem: the ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ and ㅅ — 거친 (the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24), 거칩니다, 거치세요 — exactly as M4's 살다 makes 삽니다 and 사는.

階層: the 階 of M88's 단계 ("段階 step-stairs") + 層 the layer — a FIRST by decode: M13's 층 (일 층, 이 층) is this character, and that note never spelled it. A stratum is a floor of society: 사회 계층 (M32's 사회), 소득 계층 (소득 — income, frozen) = an income bracket, 상류 계층 / 하류 계층 (frozen — upper / lower). The census word; the mouth says 층 alone (저 층은 — those people) with a curl in it. Radar: not the 계 of M9's 계산하다 — this 階 climbs.

地位: the 地 of M31's 지역 ("地 earth/land") + the 位 of M31's 위치 ("位置 place-put"): one's ground and place — status. 사회적 지위 (M32's 사회 through the -적 factory from M45) = social standing; 지위가 높다/낮다 (M7's 높다 and 낮다); 지위를 잃다 (M28's 잃다) = to lose one's position. Where M31's 위치 is where a thing sits on a map, 지위 is where a person sits in the order. RADAR: the 위 is 位, not M6's 위 (above), which is native — a 지위 is not above anything unless it is 높다.

身分: the 身 of M32's 당신 ("當身 that-body") + the 分 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion"): the portion of the body politic you were born into — one's station. It pays M83's 학생증 note, which ran the compound frozen and glossed it — "신분증 (the ID card — 신분 is status)" — and now the half that was frozen stands alone: 신분증 = the identity card, 신분을 확인하다 (M20's 확인하다) = to verify identity, 신분 사회 = a status society, the Joseon order of 양반 (frozen — the scholar-gentry) and everyone below. RADAR against 지위: 지위 is earned and can be lost; 신분 was assigned, and the word still carries the caste in it.

所屬: 所 place — the 소 of M27's 장소, which that note only sounded out ("소 (place — 안내소's 소)"), so the character is a FIRST by decode — + the 屬 of M61's 속하다 ("屬 belong-속"): the place one belongs to. 소속이 어디예요? = which organization are you with? — the first question at any conference; 소속 팀 (M16's 팀), 소속 회사 (M2's 회사); 소속감 (the -감 of M39's 자신감) = a sense of belonging. RADAR, and it is a trap: NOT M28's 속 (the inside) with M59's 소 (the cow) — no ox is inside anything here; 소속 is 屬 the belonging that 속하다 verbs.

權威: the 權 of M90's 권리 ("權利 authority-benefit") + the 威 of M90's 시위 ("示威 show-might"): authority-might. 권위가 있다 = to carry authority — a scholar, a journal, a court; 권위를 잃다 (M28's 잃다) = to lose it; 권위적 (the -적 factory from M45) = authoritarian — 권위적인 아버지 (M4's 아버지) is the drama's stern father; 권위주의 (the 주의 of M90's 민주주의) = authoritarianism, the history textbook's word. Sort it against M90's 권리: a 권리 is what you are OWED; 권위 is what you are OBEYED for.

獨立: 獨 alone — the character the M27 md filed under 독일 (獨逸, Korea's Deutschland by sound) — + the 立 of M81's 국립, which that note decoded as "立 stand": standing alone. 독립운동 (the 운동 inside M8's 운동하다) = the independence movement; 독립 기념일 (M25's 기념일) = Independence Day; the 독립신문 of 1896 that the spacing interlude credited with Korea's first spaces. And the everyday sense, gap deck: 독립하다 = to move out of one's parents' home — 서른 살에 독립했어요 (M30's 서른, M5's 살). Says 동닙: ㄱ before ㄹ turns to ㅇ and the ㄹ to ㄴ, the shift M81's 국립 note filed for 궁닙 — rom dongnip.

安定: the 安 of M33's 안부 ("安否 peace-or-not") + the 定 of M33's 결정하다 ("決定 decide-fix"): peace fixed in place — stability. 안정을 찾다 (M6's 찾다) = to find stability, 안정된 직장 (M43's 직장, the 되다-badge) = a stable job, the phrase every parent says; 안정적 (the -적 factory from M45) = stable, 경제 안정 (M32's 경제). RADAR against M81's 안전: 안전 is danger absent; 안정 is change absent. A bridge is 안전 (it will not fall); a life is 안정 (it will not lurch). The two 안s are the same 安.

爲主: the 爲 of M32's 위하다 ("爲하다 for-the-sake-of") + the 主 of M38's 주로 ("主로 main-ly"): taking [X] as the main thing. It never stands alone — [noun] 위주로 = centred on, oriented to: 학생 위주 수업 (M4's 학생, M10's 수업) = a student-centred class; 채소 위주로 먹어요 (M3's 채소) = I eat mostly vegetables; 성적 위주 (M35's 성적) = grades-first. Sort it against M38's 주로: 주로 is the adverb (mostly); 위주 is the noun that names what the mostly is ABOUT. RADAR: not M6's 위 (above) — nothing is on top of anything.

en: a kind of, a sort of (一種)
notes: 一種: M2's 일 (one) + the 種 of M57's 종류 ("種類 seed-sort"): one sort. Almost always with 의 in front of a noun — 일종의 + noun = a sort of: 일종의 게임 (M8's 게임) = a kind of game, 일종의 습관 (M35's 습관) = a habit of sorts, 일종의 시험 (M10's 시험) = a test of sorts. The essay's hedge, the way English says a sort of before a comparison it will not defend. Sort it against M57's 종류: 종류 counts kinds (무슨 종류?); 일종 puts one thing into one.

別途: the 別 of M57's 특별 (that note: "the 별 is separate-別") + the 途 of M52's 도중 ("途中 road-middle"): a separate road. 별도 요금 (M12's 요금) = an extra charge, the phrase in small print on every menu and hotel; 별도 공간 (M50's 공간) = a separate space; 별도로 = separately, in addition — the printed twin of M62's 따로: 따로 계산해 주세요 at the table, 별도로 준비하다 (M8's 준비하다) on the memo. RADAR: not M22's 별 (the star) + M2's 도 — no star is also anything; 別 is the set-apart of 특별.

en: opening up, opening (to the public) (開放)
notes: 開放: the 開 of M72's 개발하다 ("開發 open-launch") + the 放 of M32's 방송 ("放送 release-send"): opened and let go. 시장 개방 (M3's 시장) = opening the market — the trade page's word; 개방 시간 (M1's 시간) = opening hours on a park gate; 개방적 (the -적 factory from M45) = open-minded, of a person or a culture — 개방적인 사람. 개방하다 and 개방되다 ride frozen. Sort it against 공개, one entry down: 개방 opens a DOOR; 공개 opens a FILE.

公開: 公 public — the character M48's 공연 note read out of M6's 공원 ("공원's (M6) public-公") — + the same 開: opened to the public. 공개 사과 (the noun inside M33's 사과하다) = a public apology; 정보 공개 (M33's 정보) = disclosure of information; 공개하다 rides frozen — 사진을 공개하다 = to release photos; 비공개 (frozen — the 비 of M19's 비밀 is 秘, this one is 非 not) = closed-door, private. Radar: not M3's 사과 the apple, though a public apple would also be news.

參與: the 參 of M51's 참가하다 ("參加 join-add") + the 與 of M86's 여건 ("與 to give, to grant"): joining and giving — taking part. 시민 참여 (M50's 시민) = civic participation; 참여를 부탁드립니다 (M33's 부탁) is the poster's line. RADAR against 참가: 참가 enters an EVENT (a marathon, a contest — you add yourself to a list); 참여 takes part in a PROCESS (a vote, a project, a movement — you give something). 대회 참가, 사회 참여.

참여 + 하다, with 에: 프로젝트에 참여하다 (프로젝트 — riding frozen) = to take part in a project, 선거에 참여하다 (M90's 선거) = to take part in an election, 회의에 참여하다 (M10's 회의) = to join the meeting. The particle rule of M51's 참가하다 holds — "you participate INTO the event" — and so does the radar: 대회에 참가했어요 = I entered the competition; 토론에 참여했어요 (M44's 토론) = I took part in the debate. Every ministry poster ends in 참여하세요; every civics teacher says 참여가 중요해요.

支援: the 支 of M65's 지점 — that note: "支 (support, branch-off) + 店 (shop)" — + 援 to aid (a FIRST — a hand pulling): support, the institutional kind. 정부 지원 (M32's 정부) = government support; 지원금 (M60's 금 in its money job) = a grant; 지원을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to receive backing. RADAR, the one on every job form: 지원 also means APPLYING — 지원서 = an application form, 지원 자격 (M64's 자격) = eligibility — a different hanja, 志願 aspire-wish, by sound alone; context sorts them, and a 지원 사업 is a support programme while a 지원자 is an applicant. And not M9's 원 (₩): a grant may be in won, but the 원 is 援.

Both senses of the noun, verbed. Support: 정부가 기업을 지원하다 (M32's 정부, M90's 기업) = the government supports companies; 학생들을 지원하다 = to support students. Apply: 회사에 지원하다 (M2's 회사) = to apply to a company — the student's sense, and the one you will use first; 지원했어요? = did you apply? Sort them by particle: 을/를 지원하다 backs something; 에 지원하다 applies to it. Sort it against M9's 도와주다 — a person helps; an institution 지원하다.

投資: 投 to throw (a FIRST — a hand letting go) + the 資 of M44's 자료 ("資料 asset-stuff"): assets thrown, in the hope they come back bigger. 투자하다 rides frozen — 주식에 투자하다 (주식 — stocks, a C word riding frozen) = to invest in stocks; 부동산 투자 (부동산 — real estate, frozen) is the national sport; 투자자 (the person-者 of M43's 소비자) = an investor; 시간 투자 (M1's 시간) = an investment of time, the tutor's phrase. RADAR: this 자 is asset-資, the one M44's 자료 note kept apart from the self-自 of 자신.

M81's 보호 verbed — and that note left the receipt: "보호하다 is the Sino one, and print prefers it". 保 is the keep-safe of M43's 보험 ("保險"); 護 is guard, which M81 counted a first by decode. 환경을 보호하다 (M32's 환경) = to protect the environment — the sentence M32's 환경 note kept for M26's 지키다, now in its Sino coat; 아이를 보호하다 (M4's 아이); 개인 정보를 보호하다 (M57's 개인, M33's 정보) = to protect personal data, the checkbox on every sign-up. Calibration: 지켜요 is the mouth, 보호해요 is the law; 보호되다 (frozen) is the passive the notice board uses.

en: any (at all) — before a noun, with a negative
notes: M29's 아무 (any at all) wearing the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 and fossilized there, the way M29's 모든 note described its own frozen badge form. It stands before a noun and needs a negative behind: 아무런 문제가 없어요 (M7's 문제) = no problem whatsoever; 아무런 말도 안 했어요 (M4's 말, M3's 안) = didn't say a word; 아무런 이유 없이 (M24's 이유, M32's 없이) = for no reason at all. Sort the three: 아무 + noun (M29) says any; 아무런 says any AT ALL and emptier; M39's 아무리 is the adverb that announces -아/어도 (no matter how). Determiner by job, noun by house rule.

en: all sorts of, every kind of — before a noun
notes: M55's 온 (whole, all — before a noun) + 갖 (kinds — the old root of 갖가지, riding frozen): every kind. 온갖 음식 (M1's 음식) = all sorts of food; 온갖 문제 (M7's 문제) = every kind of trouble; 온갖 노력 (M39's 노력) = every effort; 온갖 소문 (M24's 소문) = rumours of every sort. It slots exactly like 온 — never alone, always in front — and the sort against M29's 모든 is variety versus count: 모든 사람 = every person; 온갖 사람 = people of every kind. Says 온갇 — the ㅈ batchim reads as ㄷ.

en: the other side; whereas, on the other hand (反面)
notes: 反面: the 反 of M64's 위반 ("違 (go against) + 反 (turn back)") + the 面 of M43's 면접 ("面接 face-contact"): the turned-back face — the other side of the coin. Two seats, both glue in Part 4: after a badge-clause, -(으)ㄴ/는 반면에 = whereas (값은 싼 반면에 = it is cheap, whereas…); at the head of a sentence, 반면 = on the other hand, the written cousin of M56's 한편. RADAR: this 반 is the flip-反 of M24's 반대 — the character M64's 위반 note filed as "turn-back-反" — not M5's 반 (half) nor M15's 반 (the class); and the 면 is a face, not the noodle of M3's 라면 — half a noodle is a different lunch.

en: to drape over, throw on; to span (across)
notes: Two jobs from one picture — a thing laid ACROSS something. On the body: 코트를 걸치다 (M21's 코트) = throw a coat on, over the shoulders and unbuttoned — M8's 입다 dresses you, 걸치다 only drapes; 어깨에 걸치다 (M14's 어깨) = sling over a shoulder. Across time and space the same verb frames a span: 일주일에 걸쳐 (the 일주일 M8's 주 note glossed) = over the course of a week, 두 나라에 걸쳐 (M23's 나라) = spanning two countries — -에 걸쳐 is the report's frame, the -아/어 coat frozen inside it. Kin of M20's 걸다, the hanging verb: what you hang is 걸다; what lies hung across is 걸치다.

en: to wrap around (the neck, the waist)
notes: To wind a thing AROUND: 목도리를 두르다 (M21's 목도리) = wrap the scarf round the neck, 앞치마를 두르다 (앞치마 — an apron, riding frozen), 허리에 두르다 (M14's 허리). M60's 매다 ties the knot (that note: "매다 knots at the front; 메다 hangs from the shoulder"); 두르다 is the wrapping before any knot. 르-family from M7: 둘러요, 둘렀어요 — and 둘러 is the coat 둘러싸다 wears, four entries down. RADAR, three -두르다 shapes: 두르다 wraps, M38's 서두르다 hurries, M42's 서투르다 fumbles — that note joined the last two ("rush and you fumble"); this one is the only wrap.

en: to put (a thing) against, touch to; (aux) -아/어 대다 keep on doing
notes: NIKL's hint on the row is 귀에 ~: 귀를 대다 (M14's 귀) = put an ear to it, 손을 대다 (M8's 손) = lay a hand on — to touch, and in the museum, not to; 자동차를 대다 (M50's 자동차) = pull the car up against the kerb. M39's 핑계 note met the put-forth job early and told you to recognize it: "핑계 대지 마세요 = don't make excuses (대다, to put forth — recognize it in this frame)" — paid: an excuse is a thing set against the question. Its second life is glue — -아/어 대다 in Part 5, where an action is done against you, over and over (떠들어 대다, 먹어 대다). RADAR: M55's 대 counts machines and scores; this 대 is native, and it touches.

en: to make (a thing) into, take as
notes: NIKL's hint is 친구로 ~: X를 Y로 삼다 = take X as Y, with M6's 로 doing the AS — 친구로 삼다 (M1's 친구) = make a friend of, 교훈으로 삼다 (교훈 — a lesson learned, riding frozen) = take it as a lesson, 문제 삼다 (M7's 문제) = make an issue of it, the committee's verb. It never stands alone; something is always being turned into something else, and the 로 is the hinge. RADAR, by ear: says 삼따, exactly as M40's 삶다 does ("Says 삼따") — 삶다 boils the egg, 삼다 adopts it as a symbol; and M2's 삼 (three) is a number, not a verb.

M37's 숨기다 is its twin, and the sort is what gets hidden from whom. 숨기다 (that note: "숨다 + 기: make-hidden") takes a thing out of SIGHT — the birthday present; 감추다 takes it out of KNOWLEDGE — 감정을 감추다 (M42's 감정, whose note already ran the 숨기다 version) = hide one's feelings, 사실을 감추다 (M24's 사실) = cover up a fact, 정체를 감추다 (정체 — one's true identity, riding frozen) is the superhero's verb. Both work on both; 감추다 is the graver word and the report's, and the sentence deck freezes it under -(으)ㄴ 채. RADAR: no dance in it — M17's 추다 only ever follows 춤.

두르다 in its 르-coat, 둘러 (around), + 싸다 — to wrap (riding frozen: the 싸다 that wraps M3's 김밥, and NOT M7's 싸다, cheap — a homograph, two verbs in one spelling): wrap around. 산이 마을을 둘러싸다 (M11's 산, M22's 마을) = mountains ring the village, 기자들이 둘러싸다 (M16's 기자) = reporters mob. Its done-to form 둘러싸이다, through the passive party of M36, is the one the page prefers: 나무에 둘러싸인 집 (M22's 나무, M1's 집) = a house surrounded by trees, in the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24. And the noun-frame the news runs daily: 그 문제를 둘러싼 논란 (논란 — controversy, riding frozen) = the controversy surrounding the issue.

덧- (extra, on top — a prefix riding frozen; the same 덧 as 덧신, an overshoe worn over a shoe) + M37's 붙이다 (M35's 붙다 through the causative party, make-stick): stick a thing onto what is already there. 한마디 덧붙이다 (M88's 한마디) = add a word — the meeting's last comment, the toast's last line; 설명을 덧붙이다 (M24's 설명하다 dismounted) = add an explanation; 덧붙여 말하면 (M4's 말하다) = to add to that — the essay's and-furthermore, the -아/어 coat as a connective. Sort: 붙이다 attaches; 덧붙이다 attaches to something already attached.

en: to hang from, cling to; to be absorbed in
notes: M60's 매다 (tie) + 달리다 — and this 달리다 is NOT M17's 달리다, to run: it is the hang-달다 inside 매달다 (to hang up, to suspend — riding frozen), through the passive party of M36, so that the thing tied-and-hung does the hanging itself. Bodies first: 나무에 매달리다 (M22's 나무) = hang from a tree, 엄마한테 매달리다 (M4's 엄마) = cling to mum, the toddler's verb. Then the mind: 일에 매달리다 (the 일 of M2's 일하다) = be absorbed in work, 시험에 매달리다 (M10's 시험) = cram for it. The particle is 에 — you hang FROM the thing — and the sentence deck hangs a friendship on it with -다 보니.

en: to let in; to spend (money, time, effort)
notes: NIKL files it as the causative of 들다 — M28's 들다 (that note: "entering was its first job all along") through the causative party of M37: make-enter. Let in: 손님을 들이다 (M9's 손님) = show the guest in. Spend: 돈을 들이다 (M9's 돈), 시간을 들이다 (M1's 시간), 정성을 들이다 (정성 — devoted care, riding frozen) = put one's heart into it — you let money and hours INTO a thing. The IOU: M56's 받아들이다 note decoded itself with this verb frozen — "M9's 받다 + 들이다 — 들다's enter-sense (M28: the 들 inside 들어가다) run through M37's party: let-IN" — and today the second half is a word; M68's 들여다보다 is the same let-in aimed by the eyes. RADAR: M9's 드리다 (to give, humble) is one vowel away and opens no doors.

en: to cook through; to master (a skill)
notes: Two NIKL rows, one verb, and M40's 익다 note built it in advance: "bolt on the causative 이 (M37's party) and 익히다 cooks it through on purpose". Row one, the kitchen: 고기를 익히다 (M3's 고기) = cook the meat through — 다 익었어요? is the question, 익히다 is what the tongs did. Row two, the classroom: 기술을 익히다 (M44's 기술) = master a skill, 한국어를 익히다 (M1's 한국어) — M91's 기능 note ran it frozen ("기능을 익히다 (익히다 — to master, riding frozen; M40's 익다 note met it as the cooking causative") and drew the picture: a skill is cooked through until it is done, which M42's 익숙하다 note had already said of you ("what you're used to has cooked all the way"). Sort: M2's 배우다 takes the class; 익히다 is what happens after the class, by repetition — the sentence deck puts it under -다 보면.

en: to gather in, reap; to achieve (a result)
notes: The harvest verb: 곡식을 거두다 (곡식 — grain, riding frozen) = bring in the grain, 빨래를 거두다 (M54's 빨래) = take in the washing. Then the headline's job, the same picture on a result: 성공을 거두다 (M44's 성공) = achieve success, 승리를 거두다 (승리 — a victory, riding frozen) = take the win, 좋은 결과를 거두다 (M32's 결과) — what a season sows a headline reaps, and Korean says the reaping with 거두다 where English says achieve. A quieter job, folding in: 눈물을 거두다 (M14's 눈물) = dry one's tears, 손을 거두다 (M8's 손) = withdraw one's hand. RADAR: it shares a syllable with M40's 두다 and nothing else — 두다 leaves a thing in place; 거두다 takes it in.

en: to pass over, hand over; to get past
notes: M36's 넘다 (that note: "the parent crosses, the child trips") through the causative party of M37: make-cross. Three things get sent over. Pages: 책장을 넘기다 (책장 — a page, riding frozen; not the counter 장 of M30) = turn the page. Things: 공을 넘기다 (M17's 공) = pass the ball, 서류를 넘기다 (M16's 서류) = hand the papers over. Time: 기한을 넘기다 (기한 — a deadline, riding frozen) = miss the deadline, and 위기를 넘기다 — M86's 위기 note ran the collocation and named the day: "위기를 넘기다 (넘기다 — to get past, riding frozen; it belongs to M94) = to weather a crisis" — paid. Sort against M61's 넘어가다: 넘어가다 goes over by itself (that note: "이번엔 넘어갈게요 = I'll let it slide this once"); 넘기다 sends something over — 그냥 넘기다 (M24's 그냥) = let it pass, the same mercy aimed at a remark.

The verb that takes only bad objects: 실수를 저지르다 (M63's 실수) = make a mistake, 잘못을 저지르다 (M63's 잘못) = do wrong, and the one the report uses — M90's 범죄 note: "범죄를 저지르다 (저지르다 — to commit, riding frozen) is the collocation the report uses; the mouth says 죄를 짓다". Today the report's verb is yours. Nobody 저지르다-s a good deed; the guilt is in the verb before the noun arrives. 르-family from M7: 저질러요, 저질렀어요 — and the -고 말다 of Part 5 fits it like a glove (저지르고 말았어요 = ended up committing it), because a wrong is always narrated as an accident; the sentence deck does exactly that with -기 일쑤다.

To strike a body: 아이를 때리다 (M4's 아이) — the verb the law now forbids parents; 문을 때리다 (M6's 문) = bang on the door; and the M86 gap deck ran it ahead of schedule — "사정없이 때리다 (때리다 — to hit, riding frozen; it belongs to M94)" — paid. Sort against M17's 치다 (that note: "If it's hit or plucked, it's 치다"): 치다 strikes a THING, with an instrument or a racket — a ball, a piano key; 때리다 beats a BODY, with the hand or worse, and the receiving end is M15's 맞다 in the job that note filed second (주사를 맞다) — 맞았어요 = I got hit. One poetic use: 비가 창문을 때리다 (M11's 비, M6's 창문) = rain beats the glass.

en: to hold (an event); to pay (a price); to go through
notes: Three jobs, one shape — a thing carried through to its end. Events: 시험을 치르다 (M10's 시험 — that note taught 시험을 보다; 치르다 is the registrar's verb for the same morning), 결혼식을 치르다 (M25's 결혼식), 장례를 치르다 (장례 — a funeral, riding frozen). Prices: 값을 치르다 (the 값 M21's 가격 note filed) = pay the price, and 대가를 치르다 (대가 — the cost of a thing, riding frozen) = pay for it, in the sense the drama means. Ordeals: 큰일을 치르다 (M67's 큰일) = get through a big affair. 르-family from M7: 치러요, 치렀어요. RADAR: M17's 치다 hits and plays; 치르다 endures and settles.

Down from upright — a person, a tree, a company: 과로로 쓰러지다 (과로 — overwork, riding frozen; M6's 로 gives the cause) = collapse from overwork, the office's darkest headline; 나무가 쓰러지다 (M22's 나무) after the typhoon; 회사가 쓰러지다 (M2's 회사) = the firm goes under. The sort with its two neighbours: M36's 넘어지다 (that note: "넘다 + 지다: to topple — people, bikes, and 김치 towers all 넘어져요") trips on the sidewalk and gets up; 쓰러지다 goes down and stays — 넘어지다 is the pavement, 쓰러지다 the hospital; and M88's 무너지다 (that note: "무너지다 takes a structure down") is for buildings and orders, not bodies. Its make-happen twin 쓰러뜨리다 rides frozen on the 뜨리다 tail M66's 떨어뜨리다 wears, and the sentence deck puts 쓰러지다 under -(으)ㄹ 뻔하다, where it belongs.

흩다 (to scatter a thing — riding frozen; the mouth barely uses it) + -아/어지다, the verb wing of the -아/어지다 machine from M35 that the M36 md called "the -지다 wing of the party": things come apart on their own. 사람들이 흩어지다 (M1's 사람) = the crowd disperses, 구름이 흩어지다 (M11's 구름) = the clouds break up, 흩어진 종이 (M15's 종이, in the badge) = scattered papers; and 가족이 흩어지다 (M4's 가족) = a family is scattered — the war's sentence, and the 이산가족 (separated families, riding frozen) it named. Its opposite is M25's 모이다: 모이다 gathers, 흩어지다 undoes the gathering — and neither needs a hand, which is what separates them from M17's 모으다.

en: to slip out, escape; to drain away
notes: M35's 빠지다 (that note: "The universal falling-verb") + M8's 나가다 (that note: "나 (out) + 가다 (go)"): fall out and away. People: 몰래 빠져나가다 (M62's 몰래) = sneak out, 회의에서 빠져나가다 (M10's 회의) = slip out of the meeting. Money: 돈이 빠져나가다 (M9's 돈) = money drains out — the sentence a bank statement says on the fifth of every month. Air: 공기가 빠져나가다 (M22's 공기) = the air escapes — a tyre, a balloon. Its mirror 빠져나오다 (M28's 나오다, riding frozen) is the same escape seen from outside. The 나가다 is the compass; the 빠지다 is the falling; an escape is a fall in a chosen direction.

Kin of M60's 펴다 (to unfold, spread open) — one vowel over, and instead of your hands doing it the thing spreads by itself, on the -지다 wing of the -아/어지다 machine from M35. 소문이 퍼지다 (M24's 소문 — that note: "travels faster than 뉴스") = a rumour spreads, 병이 퍼지다 (M14's 병) = a disease spreads, 냄새가 퍼지다 (M41's 냄새) = a smell fills the room, 널리 퍼지다 (M85's 널리) = be widespread — the headline's formula. Sort: 펴다 needs an agent and an object (책을 펴다); 퍼지다 has neither, which is why rumours take it — nobody ever admits to spreading one, and the sentence deck closes one with -고 말다.

To throw a voice with WORDS in it: 만세를 외치다 (만세 — hurrah, long live; riding frozen: the cry of 1919) = shout 만세, 구호를 외치다 (구호 — a slogan, riding frozen) = chant slogans, 이름을 외치다 (M1's 이름) = call out a name — the stadium's verb. Sort against M51's 소리치다 (that note: "부르다 (M19) calls a person; 소리치다 just launches the voice"): 소리치다 raises the voice — pain, anger, the back row; 외치다 proclaims — there is always a word in it, a slogan, a name, a demand. The report says 외치다 of protesters and fans; nobody 외치다-s at a spider. The sentence deck runs it under -아/어 대다, from outside a concert.

en: to stand up (to one's feet); to rise again
notes: M8's 일어나다 (whose note filed standing up and happening as its side jobs) + M14's 서다: rise AND stand. Where 일어나다 gets you out of bed, 일어서다 gets you onto your feet on purpose — 자리에서 일어서다 (M12's 자리) = stand up from one's seat, the classroom's verb when the teacher walks in. Then the drama's: 다시 일어서다 (M10's 다시) = get back on one's feet — the second half of the proverb M36's 넘어지다 note pre-installed, "일곱 번 넘어져도 여덟 번 일어난다 — fall seven, rise eight". Kin on the same chassis: 앞장서다 next door, M68's 앞서다, and M85's 앞서 — the -서다 line.

en: to take the lead, be at the head
notes: 앞장 (the head of a line — riding frozen; M6's 앞 with a 장 that is not the counter 장 from M30) + M14's 서다: stand at the front, on purpose. 앞장서서 일하다 (M2's 일하다) = lead the work, 시위에 앞장서다 (M90's 시위) = be at the head of the protest, 개혁에 앞장서다 (개혁 — reform, riding frozen) — the ministry's press release. The sort with M68's 앞서다 (that note: "stand at the front = be ahead"): 앞서다 is a POSITION — the runner who happens to be ahead; 앞장서다 is a DECISION — the person who steps to the front so the others follow. Nearly always in the -아/어서 coat: 앞장서서 = taking the lead, and then the verb everyone else copies.

en: to shine through, shine in; to be reflected, show
notes: Light arriving on a surface or through one: 햇빛이 비치다 (M49's 햇빛) = sunlight shines in, 달빛이 비치다 (M16's 달 + M49's 빛) = moonlight falls; then the mirror: 거울에 비치다 (M13's 거울) = be reflected in the mirror, 창문에 비친 얼굴 (M6's 창문, M8's 얼굴) in the badge = a face reflected in the window. M49's 빛 note set the sound — "the ㅊ resurfaces before a vowel — 빛이 = 비치" — and that is the etymology on the surface: 비치다 is 빛 doing something. RADAR: not M11's 비 — no rain, however wet the syllable sounds. Its make-happen twin is next door.

en: to shine (a light) on; to hold up to (a mirror); to judge against
notes: 비치다 with the 추 of the causative party from M37 — the same 추 that lowers 낮다 into 낮추다 — so that YOU aim the light: 손전등으로 비추다 (손전등 — a flashlight, riding frozen) = shine the torch on it, 거울에 얼굴을 비추다 (M13's 거울, M8's 얼굴) = hold one's face up to the mirror. The essay's job: 현실에 비추어 보면 (M92's 현실, M1's 보다 welded on) = seen in the light of reality — -에 비추어 = judged against, the report's frame for measuring a plan against a fact. The pair on one line: 빛이 비치다 (light arrives) · 빛을 비추다 (you send it) — the same pair as M38's 뜨다 and 띄우다, or M14's 눈 opening and being opened.

en: to catch the eye, stand out (눈에 ~)
notes: NIKL's hint is 눈에 ~, and that is nearly the whole entry: 눈에 띄다 (M14's 눈) = catch the eye, be noticeable — 눈에 띄는 변화 (M32's 변화) = a noticeable change, 눈에 띄게 (-게 from M33) = markedly, the report's adverb. It is M38's 뜨다 (that note: "Three lift-offs in one verb") wearing the passive party's 이 and clipped shut — 뜨이다 → 띄다: a thing lifted INTO the eye. The same clip on the causative (띄우다 → 띄어) gave M81's 글쓰기 note its line — "띄어쓰기, the spacing interlude, came off the same machine — 띄다 + 쓰기" — the space bar floats the words apart. One spelling, two engines: the eye and the space bar share it.

M49's 빛 note built it and used it: "Feed it to M28's 나다 machine and it shines: 빛나다 = light emerges = to shine, the verb inside half of K-pop's choruses". Today the chorus gets its card. 별이 빛나다 (M22's 별) = the stars shine, 눈이 빛나다 (M14's 눈) = eyes sparkle — the moment before an idea, 빛나는 순간 (M38's 순간, in the badge -는 from M24) = a shining moment, the yearbook's phrase. Says 빈나다 — the ㅊ shuts to a ㄷ and the ㄷ leans into the ㄴ, the same slide M8's 끝나다 makes. Sort against 비치다 two entries up: 비치다 is light LANDING on a thing; 빛나다 is the thing GIVING light.

en: to be loaded; to be carried, published; to carry weight
notes: NIKL files it as the passive of 싣다 — M61's 싣다 (that note: "pages carry articles the way trucks carry boxes") through the passive party of M36, and the ㄷ-irregular does what it always does before a vowel: 싣 + 리 → 실리. Cargo: 짐이 실리다 (M13's 짐) = the luggage is loaded. Print: 신문에 실리다 (M8's 신문) = appear in the paper, 기사가 실리다 (M48's 기사) = the article runs, 잡지에 실린 사진 (M48's 잡지, M17's 사진, in the badge) = the photo printed in the magazine. And weight: 목소리에 힘이 실리다 (M19's 목소리, M14's 힘) = the voice carries force — the editorial's verb for a claim with support behind it.

en: to tilt; to lend (an ear), devote (effort)
notes: 기울다 (to tilt, to lean — riding frozen; the ship and the scale do it alone) through the causative party of M37: make-lean. Literal: 고개를 기울이다 (M68's 고개) = tilt one's head — the puzzled dog and the listening friend; 몸을 기울이다 (M14's 몸) = lean in. Then the two frames the essay lives on: 귀를 기울이다 (M14's 귀) = lend an ear, listen closely — the gap deck has it; and 노력을 기울이다 (M39's 노력) = devote effort, 관심을 기울이다 (M24's 관심) = pay close attention — you tip yourself toward the thing. Sort: M2's 듣다 hears; 귀를 기울이다 leans the ear over, which is why the counsellor and the minister both ask for it.

en: to press firm, firm up; to mince
notes: To make firm by pressing: 땅을 다지다 (M22's 땅) = tamp the ground, 기초를 다지다 (M57's 기초) = lay the groundwork firm — the study plan's phrase and the builder's; and on the self: 마음을 다지다 (M19's 마음) = steel oneself, 결심을 다지다 (M34's 결심하다 dismounted — 결심, riding frozen) = harden a resolve. 결심하다 makes the decision; 다지다 is what you do to it the night before so it holds. The kitchen owns the second row: 마늘을 다지다 (M40's 마늘) = mince the garlic — the knife pressing until the thing is fine — and 다진 마늘, in the badge, is the jar every Korean fridge holds. One verb, a foundation and a paste.

en: to tie (a bond), form, conclude; to bear (fruit)
notes: Two notes have been holding it. M59's 열매: "Its verb, 맺다 (to form/bear), rides frozen for now" — 열매를 맺다 = bear fruit, the plant's and the effort's; and M88's 인연: "인연을 맺다 (맺다 — to tie, riding frozen) = to form a bond". Both paid. The picture is a knot: 관계를 맺다 (M32's 관계) = form a relationship, 계약을 맺다 (M43's 계약) = conclude a contract — the knot the paperwork ties, 결론을 맺다 (M86's 결론, whose 結 IS this knot in hanja) = wrap up, 말을 맺다 (M4's 말) = close one's remarks. Its done-to form 맺히다 (through the passive party of M36, riding frozen) is what dew and tears do: 눈물이 맺히다 (M14's 눈물) = tears well up. Says 맫따 — the ㅈ is a ㄷ at the end of a syllable.

en: to be sparing with; to cherish
notes: M75's 절약하다 note drew the line: "The native 아끼다 (to be sparing — riding frozen) is what a grandmother says; 절약하다 is what the light switch says". Now the grandmother's verb is yours. Money and hours: 돈을 아끼다 (M9's 돈), 시간을 아끼다 (M1's 시간), 아껴 쓰다 (M10's 쓰다 in its use-job) = use sparingly — the phrase on the water-saving sticker. And the thing English cannot do with the same word — to cherish: 아끼는 후배 (M58's 후배, in the badge -는) = a junior one is fond of, 아끼는 물건 (M9's 물건) = a treasured possession — to be sparing WITH a person is to hold them dear. RADAR: M21's 끼다 wears rings and gloves; 아끼다 is not 아 + 끼다, whatever the shape says. Its cousin 아깝다 (what a waste — riding frozen) is the sigh when something was not spared.

en: to be together with (lives only as 더불어)
notes: A verb that survives in one form: 더불어 = together with, along with — the -아/어 coat frozen into an adverb the way M85's 앞서 froze off M68's 앞서다 (that note called it a fossil; M85 made the fossil a word). 이웃과 더불어 살다 (M13's 이웃, 과 from M30, M4's 살다) = live alongside one's neighbours, 자연과 더불어 (M22's 자연) = in harmony with nature — the essay's phrase; standing at the head of a clause, 더불어 = furthermore, the formal M7's 그리고. Sort: M9's 같이 and M29's 함께 say together in the mouth and on the page; 더불어 says it from a podium and implies a whole life lived that way. The party name on every ballot — 더불어민주당 (riding frozen; M90's 민주주의 + the 당 of M90's 정당) — is this word, chosen for exactly that implication.

en: to do this, go on like this; (이러다가) at this rate
notes: M33's 이렇게 + M1's 하다, contracted: 이렇게 하다 → 이러다, to do like this, to go on like this. It lives almost entirely inside Part 3's -다가: 이러다가 늦겠어요 = at this rate we'll be late (with the -겠- of M49 sniffing the future), 이러다 큰일 나요 (M67's 큰일 — the gap deck) = keep this up and there'll be trouble — the sentence every Korean parent has said to a child standing on a chair. Also the shrug: 이러면 안 되는데 (-(으)면 안 되다 from M20, -는데 from M53) = I shouldn't be doing this. RADAR: M24's 이런 (the badge) and M33's 이렇게 (the adverb) are its siblings off 이렇다; 이러다 is the verb that lets you DO it — and its twin 그러다 is next.

en: to do that, go on like that; (그러다가) and then
notes: M33's 그렇게 + 하다, contracted — the verb of the 그렇다 machine M29 built (that note: "The connective factory's engine"): 그렇다 is to BE that way, 그러다 is to DO that way. Its most-said forms: 그러지 마세요 (-지 마세요 from M14) = don't do that — the sentence that stops a hand; 그러다가 어느 날 (M27's 어느, M11's 날) = and then one day — the hinge of every story told aloud; 그러다 보니 (Part 4) = and doing that, I found; 그러다 큰일 나요 = keep that up and see. RADAR: M29's 그러니까, 그러면, 그러나 came off the same machine (that note: 그렇다 + -(으)면, 그렇다 + -(으)니까) and only connect sentences; 그러다 still conjugates — 그랬어요? = did you? — one past form the two verbs share. 이러다 points at what I am doing; 그러다 at what you or the story did.

en: (dependent noun) as is, in the state of; (counter) buildings; (adverb) not yet
notes: Three NIKL rows wear this spelling and the ledger counts them as one, so all three are yours. The dependent noun — NIKL hints it as 옷을 입은 ~로 — is Part 2's glue: 옷을 입은 채로 잤어요 (M8's 입다, M7's 옷, M1's 자다) = slept with my clothes on; it takes the past badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 in front and 로 behind, and names the state a thing was LEFT in while something else happened. The counter — the hint the ledger row carries, 집 한 ~ — counts buildings: 집 한 채 (M1's 집, the 한 that M5 clips 하나 to before a counter) = one house, 아파트 두 채 (M13's 아파트). The adverb rides frozen and means not yet: 말이 채 끝나기도 전에 = before the words were even finished. RADAR: the 채 of M18's 야채 (that note: "채 (greens)") is 菜 and a vegetable; the state-채 and the house-채 are native, and neither grows.

産業 produce-work: the 産 of M43's 부동산 ("不動産 not-moving-property" — that note banked the character as property: "the 産 is property, banked next door in 재산") in its other job, to produce, + the work-業 of M43's 사업 ("事業 affairs-work"). Industry, as a sector: 관광 산업 (M23's 관광) = the tourism industry, 자동차 산업 (M50's 자동차), 산업 혁명 (혁명 — revolution, riding frozen) = the industrial revolution, the chapter every 역사 (M15) textbook opens the modern age with. The pair rule of this shelf starts here: 산업 has no 하다, but every noun that follows it does. RADAR: M43's 재산 note already ruled "no mountain here" — M11's 산 (山) only sounds like this 産.

工業 craft-work: the 工 of M43's 공장 ("工場 work-grounds") + the same work-業 — industry with a factory in it. 공업 도시 (M22's 도시) = an industrial city (울산, 포항 — riding frozen); 공업 지역 (M31's 지역) = the industrial zone on the edge of every map. Calibrate against M59's 농업, whose note drew the line ("농사 is what a grandfather does; 농업 is what the ministry manages"): 농업 grows it, 공업 makes it, and 산업 above is the drawer both sit in. RADAR: M43's 공장 note warned that "The 공-syllable stays crowded" — this 공 is craft-工, not sky-空 (M12's 공항) or public-公 (M6's 공원).

生産 birth-produce: the life-生 M11's 날 note filed inside 生日 + the produce-産 of 산업 — to produce is to give birth at scale. 생산량 (量 — the measure-量 of M63's 양, riding frozen as a suffix) = output; 대량 생산 (대량 — mass, riding frozen) = mass production; 생산자 = the producer, with the person-者 M43's 소비자 note ran ("기자 M16 records, 환자 suffers, 소비자 spends") — 생산자 makes, and the two words are the economy page's two ends. This is the 하다-noun the M91 md described ("Korean names structure with 하다/되다 twins"): the verb is next door, and its 되다 twin rides free on the headline.
