생산 + M1's 하다: 공장에서 자동차를 생산해요 (M43's 공장, M50's 자동차) = the factory produces cars; 쌀을 생산하는 지역 (M59's 쌀, M31's 지역, the badge -는 from M24) = a rice-producing region. Flip it and the report speaks: 생산되다 (riding free — M70's 마련되다 note: "되다 doesn't check pedigree, only the 하다 it replaces") — 한국에서 생산된 제품 (M43's 제품) = a product made in Korea. Sort the makers: M3's 만들다 makes anything, M54's 짓다 composes a whole ("To 짓다 is to compose something whole out of parts"), 생산하다 produces at scale — the factory floor's verb, never the kitchen's.

勞動 toil-move: the 勞 of M53's 피로 ("疲勞 worn-labor") + the 動 of M42's 감동 ("感動 feel-move") — labour, as the newspaper counts it. PAYS M58's 노동자, whose note carried the root frozen ("labor-勞 (riding frozen — NOT 노력's exert-努, which M39's 노력 note filed)") and named the holiday: "May 1 is 노동절 (Labor Day — frozen)"; M92's 육체 wrote the second receipt, "육체 노동 (노동 — labour, riding frozen) = manual work". Today the bare noun lands. 노동 시간 (M1's 시간) = working hours; 노동 시장 (M3's 시장) = the labour market; 노동조합 (frozen), clipped to 노조, is the union in every strike headline. M64's 근로자 note sorted the two labour-words ("勤-勞 vs 動-勞; 근로자 is the formal register"): 근로 is the ministry's word, 노동 the union's.

農民 farm-people: the 農 of M59's 농사 ("農事 farm-affairs") + the 民 of M32's 국민 ("國民 country-people"). Farmers as a class — the word that protests, gets subsidies, and ages: 농민들 (M27's 들) = the farmers; 농민 단체 (단체 — an organization, riding frozen). Calibrate: 농부 (a farmer — the one man in the field, riding frozen) is the storybook's word; 농민 is the newspaper's plural, and it lives where M59's 농촌 is. The same 民 builds 시민 (a citizen, frozen) and 주민 (M90) — people, sorted by what they belong to.

農産物 farm-produce-thing: 農 + this shelf's produce-産 + the 物 of M35's 식물 ("植物 planted-thing") — what the farm produces, as goods. 농산물 시장 (M3's 시장) = the produce market; 수입 농산물 (M43's 수입, in its ship-in reading) = imported produce, the label Korean shoppers check first; 농산물 가격 (M21's 가격) is the economy page's weather. The mould is reusable: 수산물 (seafood — riding frozen) swaps in the water-水 M17's 수영 found, and 축산물 (livestock products, frozen) the 축 of a barn. The 物 is the thing-物 of M9's 물건, which M48's 인물 note read as "물건's (M9) thing-物".

食糧 eat-grain: the eat-食 that M35's 식물 note kept apart from the plant ("this 식 (植 plant) is NOT 음식/식당's eat-식 (食)") + 糧 grain, a FIRST — and a decodable one: 糧 is 米 (rice) with the measure-量 of M63's 양 beside it, rice measured. Food as SUPPLY: 식량 문제 (M7's 문제) = the food problem, 식량 부족 (M78's 부족) = a food shortage, 식량 위기 (M86's 위기) = a food crisis. Sort against M1's 음식: 음식 is the food on the plate; 식량 is the ministry's count of plates. Said 싱냥 — ㄱ before ㄴ nasalizes, and the ㄹ follows it.

en: a business, a firm (the operator) (業體)
notes: 業體 work-body: the work-業 of 산업 + the 體 of M41's 체중 ("體重 body-heavy") — a business as a body that does the work. 통신 업체 (M48's 통신 — that note called the 통신사 "your phone carrier") = a telecom operator; 건설 업체 = a construction firm; 배달 업체 (M18's 배달) = the delivery company. Sort the three firm-words: M2's 회사 is the office you go to, M90's 기업 is the firm as an institution, 업체 is the VENDOR — the one named in a contract, a bid, or a complaint. When the news says 관련 업체 (M56's 관련), it means the companies involved, without naming one.

en: small and medium-sized enterprises, SMEs (中小企業)
notes: 中小企業 middle-small-enterprise: S2's 중 (the middle-中) + 小 small — M58's 소년 note drew the line ("少 counts FEW, 小 measures SMALL"), and this is the measuring one — + M90's 기업. PAYS M90's 기업, which wrote the word frozen and knew its rank: "중소기업 (small and medium firms — riding frozen) is the other half of every economic headline". The first half is M64's 대기업, and the two together are the country's two-tier job market — the gap deck runs the sort. 중소기업에 다녀요 (M16's 다니다) = I work at an SME — said with a small shrug that the 대기업 answer does not carry.

建設 build-set-up: the 建 of M50's 건축 ("建築 build-erect" — the same note retro-decoded M22's 건물) + the 設 of M50's 시설 ("施設 lay-out-and-set-up"). Construction, as the industry: 건설 회사 (M2's 회사), 건설 업체, 건설 현장 (현장 — the site, riding frozen; it belongs to M98) = the construction site behind every green fence in 서울. Sort: M50's 건축 is the discipline — the drawing; 건설 is the doing — the crane. Its 하다 is next door, and the country's whole 1970s was written in this noun's 되다 form.

건설 + 하다: 새 공항을 건설하다 (M13's 새, M12's 공항) = to build a new airport; 아파트를 건설하다 (M13's 아파트). The 되다 twin rides free and is what the sign says: 새 도로가 건설되고 있어요 (도로 — a road, riding frozen) = a new road is under construction. Sort against M54's 짓다, the native maker: 짓다 builds a house, a bowl of rice, a name; 건설하다 builds a highway, a dam, a city — the object is always bigger than one family, and the subject is a company or a state.

所得 that-which-is-gained: 所 — the place-소 of M27's 장소, read as a character for the first time; in this position 所 means 'that which' — + 得 gain, a FIRST. Income, as the tax office counts it: 소득세 (M43's 세금 — 稅 in front) = income tax; 국민 소득 (M32's 국민) = national income; 고소득/저소득 (high- and low-income, riding frozen) sort the population. Sort against M43's 수입, whose note read the money one as "收入 gather-in: income, what your work collects": 수입 is what comes in the door, 소득 is what you are taxed on — the same money one form later. RADAR: not M59's 소, the ox, which earns no income.

需要 need-want: 需 need, a FIRST, + the 要 of M56's 요구하다 ("要求 need-seek: the need-要 hiding inside M16's 필요하다"). Demand, the economist's: 수요가 많다/적다 (M7's 많다, 적다), 수요가 늘다 (M35's 늘다), and the pair 수요와 공급 (M30's 와) that the gap deck runs. MANDATORY RADAR: M5's 수요일 is Wednesday, and its 수 is water — M17's 수영 note said so ("수 (water — the 수 in 수요일's water-day!)"); 수요 the demand has no water in it and no day. 수요일에 수요가 늘어요 is a sentence, and a bad pun.

供給 offer-give: the 供 of M61's 제공하다 ("提供 hold-forth-supply") + the pay-給 that M84's 급 note read out of M16's 월급 ("is pay-給, a character shown here for the first time"). PAYS M78's 신혼부부, which carried the word inside the housing lottery: "신혼부부 특별공급 — the housing lottery's special allotment (특별공급 riding frozen, M57's 특별 in front)". Supply: 공급이 부족하다 (M39's 부족하다), 전기 공급 (M36's 전기), 공급하다 and 공급되다 riding free as the 하다/되다 pair — 물이 공급돼요 (M1's 물). 수요와 공급 = supply and demand, in the Korean order: demand first.

物價 thing-price: the 物 of 농산물 + the price-價 of M87's 평가 ("評價 judge-price"). Prices as a LEVEL — all the tags averaged. PAYS M93's 예상되다, whose note wrote the economy page's whole sentence with this word frozen: "물가가 오를 것으로 예상됩니다 (물가 — prices, riding frozen; M22's 오르다) = prices are expected to rise". 물가가 올랐어요 = prices have gone up, the grumble (gap deck); 물가가 비싸요 (M7's 비싸다) = it's expensive here, the tourist's verdict on 서울. Sort: M21's 가격 is ONE tag; 물가 is all of them. RADAR: not M1's 물 + M1's 가 — the price is 物價; the native 물가 (물 + 가, the waterside) is a homograph riding frozen, and NIKL's C-row is the price.

豫算 beforehand-count: the 豫 of M34's 예상 ("豫想 beforehand-think") + the 算 of M43's 계산기 ("計算器 count-machine") — a count made before the spending. PAYS M76's 년도, which filed it on a document: "2025년도 예산 (예산 — budget, riding frozen)". 예산이 부족하다 (M39's 부족하다) = the budget is short — the sentence every project ends on; 예산을 세우다 (M12's 세우다 in the make-stand job M37's 주차장 note explained; M8's 계획 takes the same verb) = to draw up a budget; 예산안 (the budget bill, riding frozen) is what 국회 (M90) fights over every December.

財政 wealth-govern: the 財 of M43's 재산 ("財産 wealth-holdings") + the 政 of M32's 정치 ("政治 govern-manage") — the governing of money. Public finance: 국가 재정 (M31's 국가), 재정 위기 (M86's 위기 — that note: "경제 위기 (M32's 경제) = the economic crisis") = a fiscal crisis, 재정 상태 (M34's 상태) = the financial position, a company's as well as a state's. RADAR: M43's 재산 note already sorted the two 재s — "one 재 builds dinner, the other builds portfolios" — and 재정 is the portfolio one, not M40's 재료's timber-材.

株式 stump-form: 株 the tree-stump, a FIRST — a share was a stake, and a stake was once a stump — + the 式 of M55's 식 ("式 the way-hanja"). Shares: 주식을 사다 (M2's 사다) = to buy stock, 주식 시장 (M3's 시장) = the stock market, 주식 투자 (M95's 투자 — whose note already wrote the pair from the other side, "주식에 투자하다 (주식 — stocks, a C word riding frozen) = to invest in stocks"; today the C word lands and PAYS that note); 주식회사 = Co., Ltd — the (주) in front of every company name. RADAR: there is a second 주식, 主食, the staple food — the main-主 of M38's 주로 ("主로 main-ly") + 食 — riding frozen: 쌀이 주식이에요 (M59's 쌀) = rice is the staple. NIKL's C-row is 株式 only, so the ledger counts the shares; the note keeps both so that 주식이 올랐어요 stays about money.

證券 proof-ticket: the 證 of M83's 학생증 ("學生證: M4's 학생 + 證 proof") + 券 a ticket, a FIRST — the 권 of 입장권 and 상품권 (admission ticket, gift voucher — both riding frozen; not M5's 권, the book-counter). A paper that proves you own a share of something: 증권 회사 (M2's 회사) = a brokerage, 증권 시장 (M3's 시장) = the securities market, 증권가 = the financial district — 여의도 (riding frozen), with the street-街 of 대학가 (frozen) on the end. Sort: 주식 is what you own; 증권 is the paper — and the industry — that says so.

消費 vanish-spend: M43's 소비자 dismounted — that note decoded it ("消 makes things vanish, 費 is 비용's spend") and then wrote the person; today the act stands alone. 소비가 늘다/줄다 (M35's 늘다, 줄다) = consumption rises/falls, the sentence the economy page lives on; 소비하다 rides free (에너지를 소비하다 — M72's 에너지); 과소비 (overspending, riding frozen) is the 소비 your 통장 (M43) warns you about. The 하다-noun rule again: 소비자 spends, 소비 is the spending, and 소비되다 is what the headline says happened to the electricity.

商標 commerce-mark: the 商 of M43's 상품 ("商品 commerce-goods") + the 標 that M75's 표시하다 note filed as the third 표 ("標 signpost (the label)"). A trademark — the mark on the goods: 상표 등록 (M64's 등록) = trademark registration, 유명 상표 (M17's 유명하다 dismounted) = a famous brand — though the ad says 브랜드 (the loanword, riding frozen) where the law says 상표. RADAR: not M12's 표, the ticket, and not M40's 상, the table — the 상 is the same commerce-商 that seated the 상-shelf's fifth member in M43's 상품 note, so no new tenant today.

成長 become-long: the 成 of M35's 성공하다 ("成功 achieve-merit") + the 長 of M39's 장점 ("長點 long-point") — to grow is to become long. PAYS M88's 이룩하다, whose note wrote it frozen in the textbook sentence: "눈부신 성장을 이룩하다 (눈부시다 — dazzling, and 성장 — growth, both riding frozen) = to achieve dazzling growth". 경제 성장 (M32's 경제) = economic growth; 성장률 (the rate — 率 riding frozen) is the number the page leads with. RADAR: not M23's 성, the castle — the M91 md sorted this 成 once already, at 구성 ("구성's 성 is the 成 of M35's 성공하다, not M23's 성, the castle").

en: to grow (an economy, a company, a child)
notes: 성장 + 하다: 경제가 빠르게 성장했어요 (M32's 경제, M12's 빠르다 through the -게 adverbializer from M33) = the economy grew fast — the sentence behind M35's 발전하다 note, which said 한국이 빨리 발전했어요 was "the sentence behind every skyline photo". Sort against M35's 자라다 ("the biography verb"): 자라다 grows UP — a child, a plant; 성장하다 grows on a CHART — an economy, a company, a market — though a paediatrician will say 아이가 성장하다 too. No 되다 twin, because it is already the thing happening to itself.

en: pushing forward, promotion (of a plan) (推進)
notes: 推進 push-advance: 推 push, a FIRST, + the 進 of M61's 진행되다 ("進行 advance-go"). The pushing-forward of a plan: 사업 추진 (M43's 사업), 추진력 (the 力 of M44's 능력 — drive, thrust; the word a job posting wants), 추진 중 (S2's 중) = in progress, against resistance. RADAR: M60's 진하다 ("津 the strength dial, turned up") shares the syllable and nothing else — a plan gets 추진, a coffee gets 진하게.

en: to push forward, press ahead with (a plan)
notes: 추진 + 하다: 정부가 그 계획을 추진하고 있어요 (M32's 정부, M8's 계획) = the government is pressing ahead with the plan; 사업을 추진하다 (M43's 사업) = to drive a project. The 되다 twin, 추진되다, rides free and is the headline's: 계획이 추진되고 있다. Sort against M64's 진행하다 ("進 (move forward) + 行 (do): moving a thing forward by doing"): 진행하다 moves a thing ALONG — a meeting, a procedure; 추진하다 pushes it AGAINST something — a budget, an opposition, a deadline. The 推 is the shove.

進行 advance-go, dismounted at last: M61's 진행되다 froze the parent ("進行 advance-go (the parent 진행하다 = to conduct, frozen here)") and then M64 landed it ("進 (move forward) + 行 (do): moving a thing forward by doing"); today the noun both verbs stand on. 진행 상황 (M33's 상황) = the state of progress — the question every manager asks; 진행 중 (S2's 중) = under way, the sign the M61 진행되다 note listed ("meetings, ceremonies, and roadworks are all 진행 중"); 진행자 = the host, the MC — the person-者 who moves a show along. Sort: 진행 is the going, 추진 above is the pushing.

en: to operate, run (a business, a site, a program)
notes: 運營 carry-run: 運 — M36's 운 ("運: luck") and, read as a verb, the carry-運 of M88's 운명 ("運命 carry-life") — + the 營 of M43's 경영 ("經營 manage-and-run"). To keep a thing running: 회사를 운영하다 (M2's 회사), 식당을 운영하다 (M2's 식당), 사이트를 운영하다 (M20's 사이트), 프로그램을 운영하다 (M32's 프로그램). Sort against 경영하다 (riding free on M43's 경영): 경영 MANAGES a business — strategy, profit; 운영 keeps ANYTHING running — a shop, a website, a shelter, a school bus. 운영되다 is the 되다 side, and 운영 the noun rides free (운영 시간 = opening hours, on every door). RADAR: M76's 영하 ("零下 zero-under") shares 영 and no character.

購入 buy-enter: 購 buy, a FIRST, + the in-入 that M43's 수입 read ("輸入 ship-IN (入, the in-door of 입구 M12)"). To purchase — the receipt's verb where M2's 사다 is the mouth's: 구입하신 상품 (M43's 상품, the honorific -(으)시- from M4) = the item you purchased, on every 영수증 (M9); 구입 날짜 (M25's 날짜) = date of purchase; 온라인으로 구입했어요 (온라인 — riding frozen) = I bought it online. Its mirror is M43's 판매하다 — 판매 sells, 구입 buys, and both belong to the store, not to the person. The noun 구입 rides free (구입 문의 — 문의, enquiry, frozen).

M72's 개발하다 ("開發 open-launch") through the flip M70's 마련되다 note described ("되다 doesn't check pedigree, only the 하다 it replaces"): to be developed, developer unnamed. 신제품이 개발됐어요 (M43's 제품 note: "신제품 = the new product every launch event exists for") = a new product has been developed; 새로 개발된 기술 (M44's 기술, the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24) = newly developed technology; 그 지역이 개발되고 있어요 (M31's 지역) = the area is being developed — the 재개발 that M72's 개발하다 note collected receipts for. The nation-sized job: 개발도상국 (developing country, riding frozen) is the pair for the next word.

先進國 ahead-advance-country: the 先 of M56's 우선 ("于先 at-the-front") + the 進 of 추진 + the country-國 of M31's 국가 — the country that advanced first. 선진국에 비해 (에 비해 from M86) = compared to developed countries, the frame every Korean editorial measures itself with; 선진국 진입 (진입 — entry, riding frozen) = joining the developed world, the goal the country announced it had reached in the 2020s and still argues about. The pair: 개발도상국 (developing country, frozen) and the older, now-avoided 후진국 (frozen) — the 後 of M58's 후배 doing an unkind job.

傾向 lean-facing: 傾 lean, a FIRST, + the 向 of M31's 방향 ("방 (方 direction) + 향 (向 facing)") — a leaning toward. The frame is the word: -는 경향이 있다 (the badge -는 from M24, M1's 있다) = tends to — 젊은 사람들은 늦게 자는 경향이 있어요 (M24's 젊다, M8's 늦다, M1's 자다) = young people tend to go to bed late. Sort against M55's 편, whose note ran "-는 편이에요 = 'tends to be on that side'": 편 is the mouth's tends-to (일찍 자는 편이에요, about yourself); 경향 is the report's, about a population. RADAR: another 경 for the pile M32's 경제 note counted — none of them collide.

調味料 tune-flavour-stuff: the 調 of M44's 조사 ("調査 tune-examine") + the 味 of M32's 의미 ("意味 intent-flavor") + the 料 of M40's 재료 ("材料 timber-stuff") — the stuff that tunes the flavour. The manufactured kind: 화학 조미료 (화학 — chemistry, riding frozen) = MSG, the 미원 on every 1970s shelf (frozen); 조미료를 넣다 (M28's 넣다) = to add seasoning; 조미료를 안 쓴 음식 (M10's 쓰다, M1's 음식) = food without additives, the health-café's boast. Sort against M40's 양념 ("The all-purpose flavor squad"): 양념 is the paste you mix, 조미료 is the bottle you buy — one is a recipe, the other an ingredient list.

en: to appear, make an entrance (on stage, on the scene) (登場)
notes: 登場 climb-stage: the 登 of M64's 등록 ("登 (climb up) + 錄 (record)") + the 場 of M37's 주차장 ("駐車場 park-car-place") — to climb onto the grounds. PAYS M48's 인물, which wrote the cast list frozen ("등장인물 = the characters"): the people who come on stage. 무대에 등장하다 (M51's 무대) = to enter the stage; 새 제품이 시장에 등장했어요 (M43's 제품, M3's 시장) = a new product has appeared on the market — the economy page's stage. Sort against M32's 나타나다 ("갑자기 나타났어요 (appeared out of nowhere"): 나타나다 SHOWS UP, 등장하다 makes an ENTRANCE — a ghost 나타나요, a hero 등장해요. The noun 등장 rides free: 스마트폰의 등장 (M20's 스마트폰) = the arrival of the smartphone.

演劇: the perform-演 of M48's 연기 ("演技 perform-skill: perform-演 + the craft-技 inside M44's 기술.") + 劇, the drama character — a FIRST, and the next entry owns it bare. The play as an event: 연극을 보다 (M1's 보다) at the 극장 M27 decoded as "극 (drama) + 장 (place — 주차장/광장's 장). The older, broader word"; 연극 무대 (M51's 무대) = the theatre stage; 연극 배우 (M48's 배우) = a stage actor, said with a little more respect than 영화배우. Rank 543 — the highest-ranked word in this module, because 연극 is also the accusation: 연극하지 마 = stop acting, drop the performance. Radar: M17's 드라마 is the television series; 연극 has a curtain.

en: drama; a play (劇) — and the drama-suffix
notes: 劇, bare: the category (극을 쓰다, M10's 쓰다 — to write drama) and, far more often, the SUFFIX that files every kind of it — 희극 (comedy — 희, riding frozen), 비극 (tragedy, three entries down), 사극 (a period drama — the 史 that is the history in M15's 역사), 연극 above. RADAR, and two earlier 극s make it mandatory: M26's 태극기 is 極, the pole — that note's "태극 (the red-blue yin-yang) + 기 (flag)" — and M45's 적극적 is the same 極 ("積極 piled-to-the-pole"). Pole-極 stacks and flags; drama-劇 is the one with a curtain. The gap deck's 막장 드라마 is the -극 rail run off the end.

en: a play (the text), drama as literature (戱曲)
notes: 戱曲: 戱 (to play, to perform) + 曲 (a tune, a bend) — both characters FIRSTS. The play as a TEXT: what M48's 작가 writes and a 연극 stages — 희곡을 읽다 (M2's 읽다), 희곡 작가 = a playwright, 셰익스피어의 희곡 (the name riding frozen). Sort the shelf: 희곡 is on the page, 연극 is on the stage, 극 is the suffix that files both. The 곡 is also the song-counter — 한 곡 (one song, riding frozen) is what the 노래방 (M17) charges by — and this 희 is NOT the 희 of M34's 희망: hope is 希, play is 戱.

悲劇: 悲 (sad, grieving — a FIRST) + today's drama-劇. The stage sense first — 그리스 비극 (the name riding frozen), 비극으로 끝나다 (M8's 끝나다) = to end in tragedy — and then the newspaper's: 비극적인 사고 (the -적 stamp from M45 + M36's 사고) = a tragic accident; 가족의 비극 = a family's tragedy. Its mirror 희극 (comedy) rides frozen, but you can already read it: the 희 of 희곡 + this 극. RADAR: this 비 is grief-悲, not M11's 비 (rain) and not the compare-比 of M86's 비하다 — three 비s now, and only one of them falls from the sky.

監督: 監 (to oversee) + 督 (to supervise) — both FIRSTS, and both mean watching from above. One word runs the film set and the football pitch: 영화감독 (M2's 영화) = the film director; 축구 감독 (M17's 축구) = the manager, the one sacked after three losses; 봉준호 감독 (the name riding frozen) = Director Bong, the title hung after the name the way M4's 씨 is. The verb 감독하다 (to supervise — 시험 감독 is proctoring an exam) rides frozen; the noun is where the word lives. Radar: M42's 감정 and M39's 자신감 are feeling-感; this 감 is 監, a watching.

M48's 연기 ("演技 perform-skill") + 者, the person-suffix M27's 환자 note introduced — "The -자 is a person-suffix (기자, 학자 — reporter, scholar); 환자 is the suffering-person." — so: the acting-person. It is the FORMAL twin of M48's 배우: the credits, the awards ceremony and the union say 연기자; the fan and the gossip column say 배우. 연기자 출신 (출신, below) = a former actor. Radar inside the word: M48's 연기 note warned that 연기 is also smoke (煙氣) — but nobody is a smoke-person; the -자 pins the sense.

en: an appearance (on stage, screen, a show) (出演)
notes: M51's 출연하다 dismounted — that note decoded it as "to step OUT and perform, i.e., to appear on. 방송에 출연하다 (M32's 방송), 드라마에 출연하다; the credits call the cast 출연진." The noun stands alone on the poster and the invoice: 특별 출연 (M57's 특별) = a special appearance, the cameo; 출연자 (with today's -자) = a guest, a cast member — the talk show's word; 출연료 (the fee — riding frozen) is what the tabloid guesses at. 出 is the out-door of M12's 출구 and M43's 출근; 演 is the perform-演 that runs 연기, 연극, 공연 and now 출연 — four words, one syllable, one theatre.

en: production; making (a film, a show, a product) (製作)
notes: 製作: 製 of M43's 제품 ("製品 made-goods: 品 stacks three boxes into 'goods'; 製 is the making.") + 作 of M48's 작가 ("作家 make-house"): making, as an industry. It PAYS M57's 자체, which carried the phrase frozen — "자체 제작 = made in-house (제작 rides frozen: 製作, manufacture) — how streaming credits brag." — and today the credit reads itself: 영화 제작 (M2's 영화), 드라마 제작 (M17's 드라마), 제작사 = a production company (the company-사 of M2's 회사), 제작진 = the crew (the same 진 as the 출연진 in M51's 출연하다 note). The verb 제작하다 rides frozen; print uses the noun. Radar: M33's 제목's 제 is 題, a topic; this 제 is 製, making — and the 제 of 제자 (below) is 弟, a third.

en: material, subject matter (of a work); (also) whereabouts (素材 / 所在)
notes: 素材: 素 of M38's 평소 ("平素 flat-ordinary: the baseline") + 材 of M40's 재료 ("材料 timber-stuff" — "the 재 is raw material"): the plain stuff a story is cut from. 영화의 소재 = the film's subject matter; 소재가 새롭다 (M35's 새롭다) = a fresh premise, the review's first compliment; 소재가 부족하다 (M39's 부족하다) = the writer is out of material. RADAR, because the newsroom uses the homograph daily: 소재 is ALSO whereabouts (所在 — place-所 + 있다's Sino twin 在) — 소재 파악 (M93's 파악하다) = locating someone, the police brief's phrase. NIKL lists only the 素材 row; own that one, recognize the other.

媒體: 媒 (a go-between, a matchmaker — a FIRST) + 體 of M41's 체중 ("體重 body-heavy"): the body that goes between — a medium. PAYS M79's 미디어, which sorted the shelf and left this word on it: "the Sino synonym 매체 (媒體, the medium — riding frozen) is what the dictionary says"; that md's Calibration ruled the register, "Print and officialdom lean Sino (계산대, 상자, 매체, 언론); shop signs, apps, and speech lean the loan (카운터, 박스, 미디어, 홈페이지)." So: 대중 매체 (M48's 대중, "大衆 great-crowd") = the mass media; 언론 매체 = news outlets; 매체를 통해 (M32's 통하다) = through the medium of. 미디어 is what a syllabus says; 매체 is what the ministry says.

報道: 報 of M33's 정보 ("情報 feeling-report: information.") + 道 of M38's 도로 ("道路 way-road: the official road"): the report-way — how news travels. 언론 보도 (M48's 언론) = press coverage; 보도에 따르면 (에 따르면 from M90) = according to reports, the sentence every second headline hides behind; 보도 자료 (M44's 자료) = a press release. RADAR, mandatory: M23's 횡단보도 has a 보도 in it that is 步道, the walkway — that note glossed the whole word "'crossing-walk-way.'" — and 보도 alone also means the pavement. Same sound, same spelling: one you read, one you walk on; 언론 in front settles it.

보도 + 하다: what a 기자 (M16) does to a 사건 (M36) — 언론이 보도했어요 = the press reported it; 사실을 보도하다 (M24's 사실) = to report the facts; 크게 보도되다 (the passive party from M36) = to be widely covered. It takes the quoting -다고 하다 from M32: 신문은 그 감독이 새 영화를 만든다고 보도했어요 (M8's 신문, M3's 만들다) — reports that the director is making a new film. Sort the three telling-verbs: M24's 설명하다 explains to you, M16's 발표하다 announces to everyone, 보도하다 reports what happened to those who were not there — only the last needs a newsroom.

en: a topic of talk; the talk of the town (話題)
notes: 話題: the speech-話 that M32's 평화 note filed ("speech 話 (전화)") + the topic-題 of M33's 제목 ("題目 topic-eye: a title."): the topic people are TALKING about. 화제가 되다 (M10's 되다) = to become the talk of the town — the verb it lives in; 화제의 인물 (M48's 인물) = the person everyone is discussing, the magazine's cover line; 화제를 바꾸다 (M9's 바꾸다) = to change the subject, the dinner table's escape. Radar against M48's 주제 ("主題 master-topic"): a 주제 rules a piece of writing; a 화제 is whatever has the room's attention this week.

en: a record; a written record; a (sports) record (記錄)
notes: M44's 기록하다 dismounted — that note decoded "記錄 record-engrave" and already booked the noun: "The noun 기록 rides free and moonlights in sports: 세계 기록 = world record (M23's 세계) — same word whether you're keeping minutes or breaking them." The ride ends here. 기록을 남기다 (M37's 남기다) = to leave a record; 기록을 깨다 — M36's 깨다 note ran it early, "기록을 깨다 — records too" — = to break a record; 역사 기록 (M15's 역사) = the historical record; 신기록 (the new record — riding frozen) is what the commentator shouts. The 록 keeps its ㄹ mid-word and drops it word-initially, the spelling law M48's 녹음 note filed.

en: the late period (of an era); (also) a review, an afterword (後期 / 後記)
notes: 後期: 後 of M34's 후회하다 ("後悔 after-ache") + 期 of M34's 기대 (期待): the after-period. PAYS M88's 초기, which set the pair and left this half frozen — "Its mirror is 후기 (the late period — riding frozen), and 중기 sits between." — so 조선 후기 (M26's 조선) = late Joseon, 후기 작품 (M48's 작품) = the late works. That is the NIKL row (後期). RADAR, and the everyday sense is the OTHER hanja: 후기 as 後記 — after-writing — is the REVIEW under every product and hotel: 사용 후기 (S2's 사용) = user reviews, 후기를 남기다 (M37's 남기다) = to leave a review, 후기가 좋다 = well reviewed. Historians mean the period; shoppers mean the stars.

用語: the use-用 of M43's 비용 ("費用 spend-use") + the language-語 of M42's 어색하다 ("語塞 words-blocked"): a word in use — by a field. 전문 용어 (M57's 전문) = technical terms, the jargon the doctor forgets to translate; 법률 용어 (M90's 법률) = legal terminology; 경제 용어 (M32's 경제) = the economics vocabulary the business page assumes you have. Sort against M10's 단어: any word is a 단어; a 용어 belongs to a discipline and means one thing there. This module's glue index is written in 용어 — 종결어미, 연결어미 — and you have never needed one of them to use the endings.

神話: M69's 신 ("god, deity" — "神: a god — or God") + the speech-話 of 화제: god-talk — a myth. 단군 신화 (단군, riding frozen — the bear's son who founded the first Korean kingdom) = the founding myth every schoolchild recites; 그리스 신화 (riding frozen) = Greek mythology, the bookshelf version; 신화적 (the -적 stamp from M45) = mythic. And the newspaper's use, which is most of them: 불패 신화 (undefeated — riding frozen) = the myth of invincibility a team or a company builds and then loses; 신화를 깨다 (M36's 깨다) = to shatter a myth. The 신 that is excitement (신이 나다, that same M69 note) has no hanja at all.

哲學: 哲 (wise, discerning — a FIRST) + the 學 M15's 수학 note told you to watch ("The -학 suffix names every field — watch for it."): the study of wisdom. PAYS M31's 동양, which ran the phrase before the word existed — "동양 철학 (Eastern philosophy)" — and now the other half stands: 서양 철학 (M31's 서양) = Western philosophy, 철학과 (the department — the -과 riding frozen) = the philosophy department, 철학자 (today's -자) = a philosopher. The everyday sense is bigger than the discipline: 인생 철학 (M25's 인생) = one's philosophy of life, 경영 철학 (M43's 경영) = a CEO's, 나만의 철학 = my own way of doing things — Koreans give the word to anyone with a principle and the patience to explain it.

M23's 세계 (the atlas world) + 觀, the see-觀 M35's 습관 note pointed at while sorting its own 관 ("nor 관광's see-觀"): a way of seeing the world — a worldview. 작가의 세계관 (M48's 작가) = the author's worldview; 세계관이 다르다 (M24's 다르다) = we see the world differently, the polite end of an argument. And the sense the young own outright: a franchise's UNIVERSE — 마블 세계관 (the name riding frozen), 같은 세계관 (M24's 같다 in the badge from M24) = set in the same universe — where every hero, idol group and webtoon now comes with one. Three 관s remain three: gate-關 (관계), see-觀 (here), accustomed-慣 (습관).

The German Ideologie through the converter — 이데올로기, five syllables and no hanja in any of them. PAYS M87's 이념, which named the date: "The loan 이데올로기 (a C-word saved for Module 96, riding frozen) is its foreign twin, and the press uses both." So sort the twins: 이념 is the idea a system is ordered by, in Sino dress; 이데올로기 is the same idea when the writer wants it to sound imported and suspect — 이데올로기 대립 (대립 riding frozen) = the ideological standoff, 이데올로기 교육 (M32's 교육) = indoctrination when the writer disapproves. RADAR: nothing in it is a taught part — unlike 신화 and 철학, this word cannot be decoded, only recognized, the way the M79 loan shelf taught you to. Say 이데올로기 with the ㄹㄹ held: i-de-ol-lo-gi.

美, bare: the beauty you have been carrying since M27's 미국 — that note: "미 (beautiful — chosen for the sound of 'America') + 국 (country, M23's 외국's 국). The flattery is accidental" — and since M44's 미술 ("美術 beauty-skill"). Alone it is the aesthetician's noun: 미의 기준 (M39's 기준) = the standard of beauty, which every century redraws; 한국의 미 = Korean beauty, the museum's title card; 미인 (with the person-人 of M23's 외국인) = a beauty, a beautiful woman; 미용실 (the hair salon — riding frozen) = beauty-use-room. RADAR, twice, because the syllable is crowded: M33's 미소 drew the line itself — "this 미 is 微 (tiny), NOT 미국's 美 (beautiful, M27)" — and M25's 미래 is 未, "미 (not-yet)". Beautiful, tiny, not-yet: three 미s, and only this one hangs in a gallery.

en: cultural heritage; a cultural treasure (文化財)
notes: M26's 문화 ("The 문 here is writing, not M6's door") + the wealth-財 of M43's 재산. That note wrote the receipt — "문화재 (M26's 문화 + this 財) = a cultural treasure" — and today the word is yours: 문화재 보호 (M81's 보호) = heritage protection, 문화재청 (the Heritage Administration — the 청 M31's 시청 decoded as "청 (廳 government hall)") = the agency that stamps it, 국보 (a national treasure — riding frozen) = the top grade, numbered, with 숭례문 (the gate — riding frozen) as 국보 1호. 무형 문화재 (intangible — riding frozen) is where the 판소리 singers live. Radar: the 재 is 財 wealth, as in 재산 — not the timber-材 of M40's 재료 that 소재 borrowed above.

en: the Three Kingdoms (Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla) (三國)
notes: 三國: M2's 삼 + the country-國 of M32's 국민 ("國民 country-people"). Three countries — and in Korean the phrase is a proper noun: the Three Kingdoms, 고구려·백제·신라 (all three riding frozen), the seven centuries before 통일 (M31) under 신라. 삼국 시대 (M26's 시대) = the Three Kingdoms period, the era the 사극 love second only to 조선; 삼국사기 and 삼국유사 (the two chronicles — riding frozen) are where 단군 신화 was written down. RADAR: this 국 is 國, the country of 한국, 미국 and 국민 — not M3's 국, the soup that comes with rice. 삼국 is never three soups, though the classroom joke is older than you.

en: the Middle Ages, medieval times (中世)
notes: 中世: S2's 중 (the middle-中 of 중국, hung after nouns as the busy sign) + the generation-世 of M38's 세기 ("世紀 generation-record"): the middle age of the world. 중세 유럽 (M31's 유럽) = medieval Europe — castles, plague, monks; 중세 시대 (M26's 시대); 중세 국어 (M44's 국어) = Middle Korean, the language 한글 was invented to write down. It sits on a timeline you can now read end to end: 고대 (ancient — riding frozen) · 중세 · 근대 (early modern — riding frozen) · 현대 (M46). Radar: M23's 세계's 세 is this same 世; M41's 체중's 중 is heavy-重, not the middle-中 here.

學 + 者: the learning-person. The suffix's oldest example finally standing alone — M27's 환자 note named it in passing ("The -자 is a person-suffix (기자, 학자 — reporter, scholar)"), and M72's 과학자 note booked the payoff outright: "학자 (scholar — riding frozen) is the suffix bare; 과학자 is the one with a lab coat." Paid. The -자 payroll, in order of hire: 기자 (M16) records, 환자 (M27) suffers, 소비자 (M43) spends, 과학자 (M72) measures, 초보자 (M78) begins, 후보자 (from M90's 후보 note) runs, and today 학자 studies, 연기자 acts, 필자 writes, 출연자 appears. 역사학자 (M15's 역사) = a historian; 학자들의 주장 (M93's 주장) = the scholars' claim, the report's citation line. Radar against 지식인, next: a 학자 has a field; a 지식인 has a public.

M44's 지식 + the person-人 of M23's 외국인. That note decoded the compound early — "지식인 = an intellectual (외국인's person-인, M23, on suffix duty)" — and today it is a headword. The 지식인 is the 학자 who speaks outside the seminar room: 지식인의 책임 (M39's 책임) = the intellectual's responsibility, the essay title of every decade; 지식인 사회 (M32's 사회) = the intelligentsia, as a class. Two person-suffixes now sit side by side on this shelf: -자 (者) marks a role or trade (학자, 기자, 소비자), -인 (人) marks a kind of person (지식인, 외국인, 정치인 — M32's 정치 note built that one). Both hire; the 者 shelf is longer.

en: the writer (of this piece); the author, as 'I' (筆者)
notes: 筆者: the writing-tool-筆 of M44's 필통 ("筆筒 brush-tube") + 者: the brush-person — the writer. But not a profession: 필자 is how a columnist says I. 필자는 그렇게 생각하지 않는다 = this writer does not think so — the newspaper's third-person modesty, which is also its authority. Sort the writing shelf M48 built: 작가 ("作家 make-house") is the author as a career, 저자 (M48) is the author of record on a title page, 독자 (M48) is who reads it, and 필자 is the author pointing at himself from inside the text. When an article says 필자, the writer has stepped behind his own byline.

Native, no hanja: the teacher you OWE. M4's 선생님 is the address — what you call any teacher, and any stranger you respect; 스승 is the relationship — what a person is to you once they have shaped you. Nobody says 스승님, 안녕하세요 to a face; everybody writes 저의 스승 in a dedication. 스승의 날 (M11's 날) = Teachers' Day, the fifteenth of May, when carnations go on lapels; 스승과 제자 = master and disciple, the phrase the next entry completes; 평생의 스승 (M46's 평생) = a lifelong mentor. The proverb the gap deck files: 스승의 은혜는 하늘 같아서 — a teacher's grace is like the sky.

弟子: the younger-brother-弟 of M47's 형제 ("兄弟 older-brother-younger-brother") + the child-子 M47's 손자 decoded ("The 자 is child-子, hiding in plain sight inside 남자 and 여자 (M4)"): a younger-brother-child — the one who follows a master. 스승과 제자 = master and disciple; 제자를 키우다 (M35's 키우다) = to raise pupils, what a 스승 does with a life; 예수의 열두 제자 (예수 riding frozen) = the twelve disciples. Radar, one clause: M88's 머물다 ran "제자리에 머물다 (제자리 — one's original place, riding frozen) = to stay put, to stagnate" — that 제자리 is 제 (one's own) + M12's 자리, and no disciple is in it. And this 자 is 子, not the person-者 of 학자: a child, not a role.

en: origin, background (where one is from) (出身)
notes: 出身: the out-出 of M43's 출근 ("出勤 out-to-duty") + the body-身 of M32's 당신 ("當身 that-body"): where the body came out of — one's origin. The résumé's word, hung after any noun: 서울 출신 (M12's 서울) = from Seoul; 부산 출신 (M12's 부산); 서울대 출신 (riding frozen) = a Seoul National graduate, the line that opens doors; 배우 출신 정치인 (M48's 배우, the 정치인 M32's 정치 note built) = a former actor turned politician; 연기자 출신 = ex-actor. Sort against M27's 고향: 고향 is the hometown you miss; 출신 is the origin on a form. The particle is none — 출신 sits bare after its noun, then takes 이다: 저는 대구 출신이에요.

en: skill of the hands; craft, knack (native)
notes: Native: what the hands know. 음식 솜씨 (M1's 음식) = cooking skill, the compliment that makes a Korean grandmother pretend to be offended; 요리 솜씨 (the 요리 inside M3's 요리하다) the same; 말솜씨 (M4's 말) = a way with words — the one skill here the hands do not do; 솜씨가 좋다 (M1's 좋다) = to be handy, deft; 솜씨를 발휘하다 (M93's 발휘하다) = to show one's skill. RADAR: the 씨 is not M4's 씨 — M83's 글씨 filed the same suffix, "M32's 글 + 씨, a native suffix — RADAR: not M4's 씨, the name suffix" — 글씨 is the hand's letters, 솜씨 is the hand's craft. Against M26's 실력: 실력 is measured ability, the exam's word; 솜씨 is the touch, the kitchen's.

en: an old-style tearoom, coffee house (茶房)
notes: 茶房: M2's 차 in its OTHER reading — 茶 reads 차 in 차례 (M46's 차례 note: "차례 (茶禮), tea-차 (M2)") and 다 in 다방, 다도 and 다과 (the tea ceremony, the refreshments — both riding frozen) — + the room-房 of M8's 방 (the 房 M32's 방송 note sorted: "A THIRD 방 (M8's room 房, M31's direction 方, now release 放)"). The tea-room: where Korea drank coffee from the 1950s to the 1990s — vinyl seats, a 디제이 (riding frozen) spinning records, a 마담 (riding frozen) who remembered your order. M2's 카페 replaced it, decade by decade — and now 다방 is nostalgia, or a very small town, or the gap deck's 다방 커피. The register pair this module was built on, in one storefront: Sino 다방 / loan 카페, the way 스승 / 선생님 and 극 / 드라마 split the same referent by era and mouth.

en: position, standpoint (立場); entry, admission (入場)
notes: 立場 stand-place: the 立 of M81's 국립 (that note: "立 stand — a FIRST") + the 場 of M37's 주차장 ("駐車場 park-car-place"): the place you stand on = your position, your standpoint. 정부의 입장 (M32's 정부) = the government's position; 입장을 밝히다 (M56's 밝히다) = to state one's position; 제 입장에서는 = from where I stand. PAYS M90's 공식, which ran "공식 입장 (입장 — a stated position, riding frozen)" — the position is now yours. RADAR, mandatory: the same spelling is ALSO entry, admission — 入場, the in-入 of M43's 수입 and M12's 입구 + the same 場: 입장료 (the fee-료 of M20's 무료) = admission, and M47's 신부 note's "신랑 신부 입장!" is THAT 입장 — the couple walking IN, not taking a stance. NIKL lists only 立場; the wedding's 入場 rides on the call you already know.

現場 appear-place: the 現 of M33's 표현 ("表現 surface-appear") + 場: the place where a thing appeared = the scene, the site. 사고 현장 (M36's 사고) = the accident scene, 공사 현장 (S2's 공사) = the construction site, 현장 학습 (M44's 학습) = a field trip — learning at the place itself. 현장에서 = on site, in the field, the reporter's location line. The 場 rail, read twice: 입장 is where YOU stand, 현장 is where IT happened.

中央 middle-centre: S2's 중 ("중국's middle-中") + 央, centre — a FIRST: the exact middle of a nation, a page, a stage. 중앙 정부 (M32's 정부) = the central government; 중앙선 (선 — a line, riding frozen) = the centre line on the road; 광장 중앙에 (M23's 광장) = in the middle of the square. Sort against M50's 중심 — that note's "the center, located exactly where anatomy would put it": 중앙 is geometric, the midpoint you could measure; 중심 is what matters — 관심의 중심 is never 관심의 중앙.

en: the interior; the inside (of an organization) (內部)
notes: 內部 inside-section: the 內 of M31's 국내 (that note: "내 (內 inside)") + the 部 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion"): the inside section = the interior, and the inside of an organization. 건물 내부 (M22's 건물) = the interior of the building; 내부 사정 (M86's 사정) = internal circumstances; 내부 고발 (고발 — an accusation, riding frozen) = whistle-blowing, the report from inside. The 部 rail opens here and runs through the next five words: 部 cuts a whole into sections, and the first syllable says which section.

en: the exterior; the outside, outsiders (外部)
notes: 外部 outside-section: the 外 of M55's 외 and M39's 예외 ("例外 example-outside") + 部: the exterior, and outsiders as a body. 외부인 (frozen) = an outsider; 외부 공격 (this module's 공격) = an attack from outside; 외부에 알리다 (M37's 알리다) = to make it known outside. Sort the three pairs: 안/밖 (M6) are the mouth's inside and outside, 안쪽/바깥 (M65) are sides and places, 내부/외부 are the report's — 회사 내부에서는 the staff say, 외부에서는 the press says.

en: the southern part, the south (of a country) (南部)
notes: 南部 south-section: the 南 of M27's 남쪽 + 部: the southern section. M32's 남성 note filed the 남s — "man 男 (남자), south 南 (남쪽, 남산)" — and 남부 is the south one. 남부 지방 (M50's 지방) = the southern provinces, the forecast's phrase; the rail runs 북부, 동부, 서부 (frozen — the north, east and west parts) and 중부 (frozen) for the middle, each a compass syllable of M27 on 部. Sort: 남쪽 is the direction you point, 남부 is the region on the weather map.

en: a zone, a block, a designated area (區域)
notes: 區域 district-domain: 區, the district-區 M49's 지구 note flagged ("a homograph 지구 (地區) is a zoned DISTRICT") + the 域 of M31's 지역 (that note: "역 (域 domain)"): a zone, a block, an area somebody drew a line around. 금연 구역 (M53's 금연) = the no-smoking area, 주차 구역 (M50's 주차) = the parking zone, 위험 구역 (M12's 위험하다 dismounted) = the danger zone — the sign's word. Seoul's own districts wear this 區 (강남구, 종로구 — riding frozen). RADAR: not M2's 구 (nine). Sort: 지역 is a region, 구역 is a block with a boundary drawn by an official.

en: a belt, a zone (of land) (地帶)
notes: 地帶 land-belt: the 地 of M31's 지역 + 帶, the belt — the 帶 inside M77's 무더위 note's 열대야 ("熱帶夜 — the tropical night that never cools"): a belt of land, a zone the terrain itself makes. PAYS M60's 회색, which ran "회색 지대 (zone, riding frozen) = the gray zone, where the rules blur" — the zone lands. 산악 지대 (산악 — mountains, riding frozen) = mountainous terrain, 안전 지대 (M81's 안전) = a safe zone, 비무장 지대 (비무장 — unarmed, riding frozen) = the DMZ across the middle of the peninsula. Sort: a 구역 is drawn by someone; a 지대 is the land's own belt.

en: a boundary, a border (境界); vigilance (警戒)
notes: 境界 boundary-boundary: the 境 of M32's 경우 ("境遇 boundary-meeting") + the 界 of M39's 한계 ("限界 limit-boundary"): the line where one thing ends and the next begins. 경계선 (선 — a line, riding frozen) = the boundary line; 경계를 넘다 (M36's 넘다) = to cross the line — on a map or in manners; 두 나라의 경계 (M23's 나라) = the border between two countries. RADAR, one clause: 경계 is also vigilance — 警戒, 경계하다 = to be on guard, to be wary (riding frozen) — the guard on the border does 경계 at the 경계. NIKL lists only 境界; the guard's word rides frozen.

西歐 west-Europe: the compass-西 of M27's 서쪽 and M31's 서양 + 歐, Europe — a FIRST, the hanja that spells M31's 유럽. 서구 문화 (M26's 문화) = Western culture, 서구 사회 (M32's 사회) = Western society, 서구식 (the 식 of M55's 식) = Western-style. Sort against 서양, which M31 glossed as "Europe and the Americas as one cultural bloc": 서양 is the cultural West, 서구 the European one — an American is 서양 사람, rarely 서구. RADAR: not M2's 구 (nine), and not the district-區 of 구역 — though 서구 is ALSO the West District of several cities (인천 서구, 대전 서구 — 西區, riding frozen), which is that 구.

en: the persons concerned; officials, staff (關係者)
notes: 關係者: M32's 관계 ("關係 connect-tie") + 者, the person-suffix of M43's 소비자: the persons tied to a matter — the officials, the staff, the people involved. PAYS M55's 외, which read the sign for you — "관계자 외 출입 금지 (staff only; 관계자 = 'persons concerned', riding frozen)" — the word behind half of Korea's doors is now yours, and the gap deck files the sign. 관계자에 따르면 = according to officials — M32's 따르다 in its news frame (that note: "[source]에 따르면 = according to") — the newspaper's anonymous source; 정부 관계자 (M32's 정부) = a government official.

指導者 point-lead-person: the 指 of M93's 지적하다 ("指摘 point-pick") + the 導 of M91's 도입 ("導入 lead-in") + 者: the one who points the way and leads = a leader. 정치 지도자 (M32's 정치), 종교 지도자 (M69's 종교), 세계의 지도자들 (M23's 세계). RADAR, mandatory: M12's 지도 (the map) is 地圖, land-picture, on the land-地 of M31's 지역 — a different 지도; 지도하다 (to guide, to coach — riding frozen) is THIS one, so a 지도 교사 (this module's 교사) is the supervising teacher, not the geography one.

en: an executive; the leadership (of a party, a company) (幹部)
notes: 幹部 trunk-section: 幹, the trunk of a tree — a FIRST + 部: the trunk-section = the executives, the leadership of a party, a company, an army. 간부 회의 (M10's 회의) = an executives' meeting; 고위 간부 (고위 — high-ranking, riding frozen) = senior officials; 당 간부 (M90's 정당 clipped) = party leadership. Sort: M58's 부장 is one rung on the title ladder that note built; 간부 is the whole upper floor, seen from below. The 部 rail: 내부 and 외부 cut space, 간부 cuts an organization.

en: a military unit; the base (部隊)
notes: 部隊 section-ranks: 部 + the 隊 of M58's 군대 ("軍隊 army-ranks: 軍 + unit-隊"): a section of the ranks = a military unit, and the base it lives on. PAYS M80's 소시지, which explained "부대찌개 (frozen — the army-base stew built from post-war American rations)" — the 부대 is that base. 부대에 들어가다 = to join the unit; 특수 부대 (특수 — special, riding frozen) = special forces. RADAR: the 부 is the same 部 that M76's 부 counts copies with, now cutting an army into sections; the 대 is 隊, not the counter-臺 of M55's 대.

en: military affairs; military (as a determiner) (軍事); a soldier, archaic (軍士)
notes: NIKL SENSE COLLAPSE — two rows, both yours. 軍事: the 軍 of M58's 군 ("軍 the military") + the 事 of M36's 사고 (事故): military affairs, and the determiner in front of everything the military does — 군사 훈련 (this module's 훈련), 군사 시설 (M50's 시설), 군사 기술 (M44's 기술). And 軍士: the same 軍 + 士, the licensed-士 that M78's 운전기사 note sorted against teacher-師 ("licensed-士 (박사, 기사, and M16's 변호사 — 辯護士") — a soldier, the historical drama's word where M27's 군인 is the modern one. The sentence sorts them: 군사 before a noun is affairs; 군사 with 이/가 is a man.

武器 martial-tool: 武, martial — a FIRST + the 器 of M51's 악기 (that note: "The 기 is tool-器") and M83's 도자기: the martial tool = a weapon. PAYS M92's 핵, which ran "핵무기 (nuclear weapons — 무기 riding frozen)" — landed. 무기를 들다 (M28's 들다) = to take up arms; 무기 거래 (거래 — trade, riding frozen) = the arms trade; 무술 (frozen) = the martial arts, where M26's 태권도 lives. RADAR: not M40's 무 (the radish) + 기 — a fourth 무: radish (M40), the nothing-無 of M20's 무료, the water of M77's 무더위, and now martial-武.

攻擊 attack-strike: the 攻 of M44's 전공 ("專攻 sole-attack") + the 擊 of M42's 충격 ("衝擊 collide-strike"): attack — in war, in football, in a comment section. 공격을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to come under attack; 공격하다 rides frozen; 공격적 (the -적 of M45) = aggressive. Its opposite, 방어 (defence — riding frozen), is the commentator's other half. And 전공, read back through this word: a major is an attack on one field, which is exactly how M44 glossed it.

訓鍊 instruct-temper: 訓, to instruct, to drill + 鍊, to temper metal — both FIRSTs: training that hardens. PAYS M78's 강도, which ran "강도 높은 훈련 = high-intensity training (훈련 riding frozen)". 훈련을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be trained; 군사 훈련 = military exercises; 훈련소 (frozen) = the boot camp every conscript enters. Sort against M10's 연습하다: 연습 is the piano — practice; 훈련 is the barracks and the pitch — drill. Says 훌련: the ㄴ gives way to the ㄹ, so rom hullyeon.

指示 point-show: 指 + the 示 of M75's 표시하다 ("表示 surface-show"): to point and show = an instruction, a directive. 지시를 따르다 (M32's 따르다) = to follow instructions; 지시를 내리다 (M6's 내리다, sending an order DOWN the ladder) = to issue one; 지시하다 rides frozen. Sort: M3's 시키다 orders food; 지시하다 orders people, from a desk; M64's 명령 is the barked version. The 指 rail: 지적하다 points at a fault, 지도자 points the way, 지시 points at the job.

所有 place-have: 所, the place-所 of M27's 장소 + the 有 of M81's 유명 ("有名 have-name"): what is had in one's place = ownership. 개인 소유 (M57's 개인) = private property, 국가 소유 (M31's 국가) = state-owned; 소유자 (with the 者 of 관계자) = the owner; 소유하다 rides frozen. Sort: M43's 재산 is WHAT you own, 소유 is the owning; 소유 is also the word for the possessive in grammar — 소유격.

en: a case, an instance, an example that happened (事例)
notes: 事例 matter-example: 事 + the 例 of M39's 예외 ("例外 example-outside"): a case that happened. 성공 사례 (M35's 성공하다 dismounted) = a success story; 사례 연구 (M32's 연구) = a case study; 피해 사례 (M86's 피해) = cases of harm, the consumer report's word. Sort against M33's 예 (that note: "예 = example — 예를 들면"): an 예 is GIVEN to explain, a 사례 HAPPENED and is reported. Not M32's 사회 or M2's 사 — the 사 is the matter-事 of M36's 사고 and 사건.

en: a law (of nature, of science) (法則)
notes: 法則 law-rule: the 法 of M39's 법 + the 則 of M39's 규칙 ("規則 rule-standard"): a law nobody voted on. 자연의 법칙 (M22's 자연) = the laws of nature; 중력의 법칙 (중력 — gravity, riding frozen); 법칙을 발견하다 (M56's 발견하다) = to discover a law. Three laws, sorted: 법 is the statute, 규칙 is the house rule, 법칙 is the one that would hold if every human left the room.

en: wrongdoing, corruption, foul play (不正); negation, denial (否定)
notes: 不正 not-correct: the 不 of M39's 부족하다 ("不足 not-enough-foot" — the 不 that M86's 불구하다 note said "reads 불 before most consonants and 부 before ㄷ and ㅈ") + the 正 of M44's 정답 ("正答 correct-answer"): not-correct = wrongdoing, corruption, foul play. 부정 선거 (M90's 선거) = a rigged election; 입시 부정 (this module's 입시) = admissions fraud; 부정행위 = cheating on an exam. RADAR, mandatory: the same spelling is ALSO negation — 否定, the 否 of M33's 안부 ("安否 peace-or-not"): 부정하다 = to deny, and 부정적 = negative, the word M45's 긍정적 note held for you — "mirror 부정적 (negative — recognize it now, a later shelf owns it)". This shelf owns it, and it is the 否 one. NIKL's C-row is 不正; 否定 rides on 부정적.

en: illegal, unlawful (不法); the Buddhist dharma (佛法)
notes: NIKL SENSE COLLAPSE — two rows. 不法 not-law: 不 + the 法 of M39's 법 — against the law: 불법 주차 (M50's 주차) = illegal parking, 불법 행위 (this module's 행위) = an unlawful act, 불법 체류 (체류 — a stay, riding frozen) = overstaying a visa. And 佛法: the Buddha-佛 of M69's 불교 ("佛敎 Buddha-teaching") + 法 in the way-sense M39's 법 note called "the way" — the Dharma, the Buddha's law, the temple's word. The parking ticket and the sutra share a spelling. Sort against 부정: 불법 breaks a written law, 부정 breaks fairness — and the news hands out both in one headline.

en: detention, arrest under warrant; constraint (拘束)
notes: 拘束 hold-bind: PAYS M86's 불구하다, whose note left it here — "拘 hold, restrain (a FIRST; 구속, detention, is a C word riding frozen on it)" — + 束, the bind-束 M61's 속하다 note filed ("약속's (M5) 속 is bind-束"): held and bound = detention, the arrest a judge signs. 구속 영장 (영장 — a warrant, riding frozen); 구속되다 (frozen) = to be taken into custody — the news ladder runs 체포 (arrest — frozen) → 구속 → M90's 재판. A second, gentler job: constraint — 시간의 구속 (M1's 시간) = the tyranny of the clock. 불구하고, read again: NOT held by it.

證據 proof-basis: the 證 of M83's 학생증 (that note: "證 proof") + the 據 of M86's 근거 ("根據 root-rely"): the proof a case rests on = evidence. 증거가 있다/없다 on the 있다-chassis; 증거를 찾다 (M6's 찾다) = to look for evidence; 증거 부족 (M39's 부족하다 dismounted) = insufficient evidence, the two words that end a case. Sort against M86's 근거: 근거 is grounds for an argument — the margin of an essay; 증거 is proof in a court — the table in front of a judge.

刑事 punishment-matter: 刑, punishment — a FIRST + the 事 of M36's 사건: the punishment-matter — criminal, as in 형사 사건 (M36's 사건) = a criminal case, against 민사 (civil — riding frozen); and, by the job, the detective who works it: 형사가 범인을 잡았어요 (범인 — the culprit, riding frozen; M28's 잡다) = the detective caught the culprit. 형사님 is how the drama addresses him. RADAR: not M4's 형 (older brother) + M2's 사 (four) — nobody's brother, nobody's number.

行爲 go-do: 行, the going-行 of the 飛行 in M28's 날다 note ("飛行 — flying-going") + the 爲 of M32's 위하다 ("爲하다"): a thing done = an act. 범죄 행위 (M90's 범죄) = a criminal act, 불법 행위 = an unlawful act, 부정행위 = cheating; 행위 예술 (M44's 예술) = performance art. Sort against M57's 행동: 행동 is behaviour you can watch; 행위 is the act the law, or the critic, has a name for.

手段 hand-step: the 手 of M37's 세수 ("洗手 wash-HANDS") + 段, the step-段 M55's 단 note filed ("M13's 계단 climbs a different 단 — step-段"): a step the hand takes = a means. 교통 수단 (M12's 교통) = a means of transport; 수단과 방법을 가리지 않다 (가리다 in its choosing sense — riding frozen) = to stop at nothing, the gap deck's phrase. Sort against M32's 방법 ("方法 direction-law: a method is a direction with rules"): 방법 is HOW, 수단 is WITH WHAT — a method is a route, a means is a tool in the hand. RADAR: not the number-수 of 수학 (M15) — this 수 is the hand.

敎師 teach-master: the 敎 of M32's 교육 ("敎育 teach-raise") + 師, the teacher-師 that M58's 사모님 left frozen ("teacher-師 rides frozen") and M78's 운전기사 note sorted against licensed-士: a teacher, the profession — the payroll word. 초등학교 교사 (M15's 초등학교) = a primary-school teacher; 교사 자격증 (자격증 — a licence, frozen) = a teaching certificate. Sort: M4's 선생님 is what you CALL them, 교사 is what the form calls them, M27's 교수 is the university's; and 스승 (the master you bow to — riding frozen) is the one 스승의 날 in May honours.

校長 school-chief: 校, the school-building 校 that M32's 교육 note kept apart ("NOT 학교's (校, the school building)") + 長, the chief-長 of M58's 부장 ("部長 section-chief"): the head of the school = the principal. Always 교장 선생님 in the school's own mouth — bare 교장 is for the newspaper; 교장실 (the 실 of M15's 교실) = the office nobody wants to be sent to. The 長 ladder: 부장 runs a section, M9's 사장님 a company, 교장 a school.

入試 enter-test: 入 + 試, the exam-試 M31's 시청 note counted ("시험's 試") — 입학 시험 (M44's 입학, M10's 시험) clipped to two syllables. 대학 입시 (M15's 대학교 clipped) = university admissions; 입시 지옥 (지옥 — hell, riding frozen) = exam hell, the gap deck's concept; 입시 부정 = admissions fraud. Its summit is the November 수능 (frozen), the day the country's planes reroute — M32's 교육 note called it "The national obsession M15 toured". Sort: 시험 is any test; 입시 is the one that decides the door.

姿勢 figure-force: 姿, a figure, a form — a FIRST + the 勢 of M53's 증세 ("症勢 illness-momentum"): the set of the body = posture, and the set of the mind = attitude. PAYS two notes at once — M63's 바르다 ran "바른 자세 (posture — riding frozen)", and M73's 자세히 flagged "자세 (posture — 姿勢, untaught) is a different word wearing the same two syllables" — taught now. 자세가 좋다 = good posture, or a good attitude; 배우는 자세 (M2's 배우다 in the badge of M24) = a learner's stance. Sort against M33's 태도: 태도 is the attitude others see, 자세 is the stance you hold. RADAR: 자세히 is 仔細, in detail — sitting 자세히 helps nobody's 자세.

en: a side, a face (面); a township (面, 읍/면/동); cotton (綿)
notes: Three NIKL rows under one syllable, and the first is the face-面 you have owned in compounds since M20 — M20's 화면 read it as "면 (surface)", M43's 면접 as "面接 face-contact". Rank 643, the side: 양쪽 면 (M65's 양쪽) = both sides, 종이의 한 면 (M15's 종이) = one side of the paper, 동전의 양면 (M43's 동전 — 양면, frozen as a compound) = both faces of a coin, and a person's too: 그 사람의 다른 면 (M24's 다르다) = another side of him. Row two, rank 4058: the township — 읍/면/동, the rural rung below the county (읍 and 군 riding frozen), where a country address says 면 and a city address says 동 (the neighbourhood 동 of M22's 동네). Row three, rank 5347: 綿 cotton — 면 티셔츠 (M21's 티셔츠) = a cotton T-shirt, 면 백 퍼센트 (M30's 퍼센트) on the label. RADAR: the noodle-면 of M3's 라면 and M30's 냉면 is a fourth, 麵 — the M30 냉면 note read it as "면 (noodles — 라면's 면)" — and NIKL leaves that row to its compounds.

線 — the 線 M76's 호선 decoded as "號線 number-line" and marked "a first for 線"; today the character stands alone, and two frozen riders thaw at once: M36's 넘다 ran "선을 넘다 (over the LINE — the boundary idiom Korea loves: 선 넘었어 = you went too far)", and M72's 연결하다 filed "선을 연결하다 (선 — a cord or line, riding frozen)". So 선 is a drawn line, a boundary, and a cable — 선을 긋다 (긋다 — to draw a stroke, riding frozen) = to draw a line, on paper and between people; 선이 없는 이어폰 (the Konglish 이어폰, frozen) = wireless earphones; 노선 (a route — the word M76's 호선 note left frozen) = a bus or subway route. RADAR, the other 선s you own: M4's 선생님 is before-先, M17's 선수 is choose-選, M9's 선물 is 膳, M26's 조선 is 鮮 — one syllable, and only this row can be crossed.

The loan — English goal through the converter, its long vowel flattened to ㅗ. 골을 넣다 (M28's 넣다 — that note: "Sugar into coffee, coins into machines, 넣다 feeds them all") = to score, and the ball is one more thing 넣다 feeds; 골을 먹다 (M1's 먹다) = to concede one — the goalkeeper EATS the goal; 한 골 차이로 졌어요 (M57's 차이, M17's 지다) = lost by a goal; 골키퍼, 골대, 골인 (the keeper, the posts, and the Konglish goal-in for crossing any line — all riding frozen). Native numbers count it: 두 골, 세 골, the 축구 (M17) commentator's whole vocabulary. RADAR: the native 골 of M22's 골목 (that note measured charm "in 골목s per block") and M22's 시골 is a valley, no relation; M79's 골프 is the same English go- converted, and nobody scores a 골 at 골프.

en: a shape; a sorry state, a sight (colloquial)
notes: Native, and NIKL's hint is 모양새 — the look of a thing (M34's 모양 with a native tail). But in the mouth 꼴 is never neutral: 이게 무슨 꼴이야 (M19's 반말) = what a state this is; 꼴 보기 싫다 (M1's 보다 through -기 from M13, M3's 싫다) = I can't stand the sight of him; 그 꼴로 나가려고? (-(으)려고 from M50, M8's 나가다) = you're going out looking like THAT? It pays the IOU M76's 일등 filed — "꼴찌 (dead last — riding frozen) is the floor" — because 꼴찌 is this 꼴 plus a tail: the sorry-shape at the end of the line, the word every race ends with for someone. The mocking suffix -꼴 stamps a state onto a noun: 거지꼴 (frozen — looking like a beggar). RADAR: not 골 above — the tense ㄲ is the whole difference between a goal and a disgrace.

Two rows. 氣 rank 1607 — the energy-氣 that has been running inside M36's 전기 ("電氣 electric-energy"), M26's 분위기, M17's 인기 and M41's 향기 — finally alone, and alone it means a person's spirit: 기가 세다 (M41's 세다) = strong-willed, 기가 죽다 (M14's 죽다) = to be cowed, the spirit dying, 기가 살다 (M4's 살다) = to perk up, 기가 막히다 (M12's 막히다 — the energy blocked) = dumbfounding, gap deck; 기를 쓰다 (M10's 쓰다) = to strain every nerve. Row two, 旗 rank 5730 — the flag of M83's 국기 ("國旗") and M26's 태극기 ("태극 (the red-blue yin-yang) + 기 (flag)"): 기를 들다 (M28's 들다) = to raise a flag, 기를 흔들다 (M41's 흔들다) = to wave one. RADAR: M83's 국기 note drew the file — "machine-機 (전화기), tool-器 (악기), energy-氣 (M41's 향기), and now flag-旗 — four hanja, one syllable, and the compound tells you which" — and M44's 기술 (技) and M72's 기계 (機) are the two rows NIKL does not give the bare syllable.

en: pyeong — floor-area unit, 3.3 m² (坪); a review, a comment (評)
notes: Two rows. 坪 rank 1450, a dependent noun (house pos noun, like M84's 호): the floor-area unit — 3.3 square metres, the floor two grown men can lie on — and though the law switched to square metres in 2007, every Korean still sizes a home in it: 삼십 평 아파트 (M13's 아파트) = a thirty-pyeong flat, 몇 평이에요? (M5's 몇) = how big is it, the first question at any 부동산 (M43). Sino numbers in front, because it is a unit — the M76 md's rule, "Sino in front of every unit". Row two, 評 rank 5427 — the judging-評 M87's 평가 decoded as "評價 judge-price: 評 (a FIRST — to weigh a thing in words": 평이 좋다 = good reviews, 평이 나쁘다 (M29's 나쁘다) = panned, 평이 갈리다 (갈리다 — to split, riding frozen) = reviews are divided, the film page's verdict. RADAR: M16's 평일 ("평 (ordinary) + 일 (day)"), M32's 평화 ("平和 flat-harmony") and M89's 평균 carry flat-平 — a third 평 the list files under its compounds.

en: a case, a matter, an item (件) — counts cases
notes: 件 — the item-件 of M36's 사건 ("事件: the incident") and M39's 조건 ("條件 clause-item"), bare: a dependent noun that counts matters. 사고 한 건 (M36's 사고) = one accident, 이번 건 = this matter, the one on the desk; 건수 (a case count — riding frozen) is the police station's tally, 건당 (per case — frozen) the freelancer's rate. The office says 그 건은 어떻게 됐어요? (M24's 어떻다, M10's 되다) = what happened with that one — 건 is the neutral word for a thing that needs doing, where M7's 문제 says it has gone wrong. Native or Sino numbers count it (한 건, 이십 건), the report preferring Sino. RADAR: M11's 건조하다 is dry-乾, M50's 건축 is build-建, M14's 건강 is sound-健 — three 건s, none of them a case.

en: article, clause of a law (條); a group, a team (組)
notes: Three rows. 條 rank 1726, the dependent noun that numbers a law's articles: 제일 조 = Article 1 — the ordinal 제 in front, as in M84's 호 (제일 호), Sino numbers, and below it the paragraph and the item (항, riding frozen; M84's 호), so a statute reads 제일 조 제이 항 제삼 호. M39's 조건 ("條件 clause-item") was this 條 all along. Then 組 — the assemble-組 of M90's 조직 ("組織 assemble-weave") — in two rows: the dependent noun (rank 6303) that numbers groups, 일 조, 이 조, the way every Korean classroom (M15's 반) is split for a project, and the noun (rank 6680), a team: 우리 조 = our group, 조별 과제 (M44's 과제 — 조별, by group, frozen) = the group assignment, 조를 짜다 = to form groups — and that 짜다 is not the salty 짜다 of M3 but its homograph, to weave or organize, riding frozen. RADAR: M11's 건조하다 carries 燥, M69's 조상 carries 祖, M56's 조사하다 carries 調 — a syllable with more tenants than any shelf.

現 — the appear-現 of M35's 현재 ("現在 appear-exist"), M92's 현실 and M92's 현상, clipped to a determiner: 현 정부 (M32's 정부) = the current government, 현 대통령 (M32's 대통령) = the sitting president, 현 단계 (M88's 단계) = the current stage, and 현 시점 = at this point — M88's 시점 note ran "현재 시점 (M35's 현재) = as of now", and print, counting characters, shortens it to this. It is the newsroom's word: the mouth says M2's 지금 or 현재, the headline says 現. RADAR: M13's 현관 is dark-玄, the gate; M9's 현금 IS this 現 — cash is money that appears in the hand.

en: the same (同) — before a noun; building no. (棟) — counts apartment blocks
notes: Two rows NIKL lists, and a third it does not. 同 rank 1879, the same-同 of M38's 동시 ("同時 same-hour"), M19's 동갑 and M69's 동창, as a determiner: 동 대학 (M15's 대학교, clipped) = the same university, 동 시간대 (시간대 — a time slot, riding frozen) = the same slot, 동 회사 (M2's 회사) — the form's word, where the mouth says M24's 같다 in the badge, 같은. 棟 rank 4197, the dependent noun for buildings: 백일 동 = building 101, and with M84's 호 the full address every 아파트 (M13) dweller recites — 백일 동 삼백일 호, gap deck. Row three, unlisted: 洞, the neighbourhood — the 동 of M22's 동네 and the 동 on every Seoul address (역삼동, 서교동 — frozen); NIKL leaves it in its compounds, but you will read it on every door. RADAR: M27's 동쪽 is east-東, M22's 동물 is move-動 — the 動 of today's 동작.

en: this year's (before a noun); this year
notes: M25's 올해 decoded itself — "올 + M11's 해" — and today the 올 dismounts, in two rows: the determiner (rank 1951), 올 여름 (M11's 여름) = this summer, 올 겨울 (M11's 겨울), 올 시즌 (the Konglish season, frozen) — the sports page's; and the noun (rank 4449), 올 들어 (M28's 들다 — entering the year) = since the year began, 올 초 and 올 말 (frozen — the start and the end). Native, no hanja: it is the year the mouth wears, and 금년 (今年, riding frozen) is its Sino twin on documents. Radar against M25's 내년 and 작년 (the M25 pair): those are full nouns; 올 alone before a noun does what 올해 does with one syllable fewer. RADAR: not M20's 올리다 nor M28's 올라가다 — those 올 are a verb's stem, and they climb.

某 — two NIKL rows, the determiner (rank 5613) and the pronoun (rank 2095), one job: to withhold a name. 모 대학 (M15's 대학교, clipped) = a certain university, 모 기업 (M90's 기업) = a certain firm, 모 씨 = a certain person; and after a surname — 김 모 씨 (M4's 씨), 이 모 씨 — a Mr Kim, the news anchor's anonymizer for suspects and witnesses whose names the law protects, and the reason every Korean crime story has the same three cast members. 서울 모처 (frozen) = an undisclosed place in Seoul. The written and broadcast register only; the mouth says M24's 어떤 or M10's 누구. RADAR: M4's 부모님 carries mother-母, M9's 모자 is 帽, M34's 모양 is 模, and M17's 모으다 is native — none of them anonymous.

M88's 잇다 in its -아/어 coat — the ㅅ gone before the vowel, exactly as M88's 이어지다 note built it: "잇다 (above) + -아/어지다 — the ㅅ gone before the vowel (이어 + 지다)" — and fossilized into an adverb the way M85's 앞서 was (that note: "M6's 앞 + M14's 서다 in its -아/어 coat"). Following on, next: 이어 말했다 (M4's 말하다) = went on to say, 이어 발표했다 (M16's 발표하다) = then announced — the newsreader's and the minutes-taker's word, linking two events with no gap; 이어서 (riding frozen) is the fuller spoken form — 이어서 뉴스입니다 (M24's 뉴스) = and now, the news. Where M7's 그리고 merely adds, 이어 says the next thing followed straight on. NIKL files it as an adverb, house pos noun. RADAR: the 이어 inside M35's 다이어트 is English die- through the converter — no verb in it.

特性 special-nature: the special-特 of M32's 특히 and M45's 특징 + the nature-性 of M32's 여성 ("女性 woman-nature") and M19's 성격. It pays the IOU M45's 특징 filed — "Sibling worth filing: 특성 (special-NATURE) — science says 특성 about materials where people-watching says 특징." — and that is the whole sort: 물의 특성 (M1's 물) = the properties of water, 지역 특성 (M31's 지역) = regional characteristics, 특성을 파악하다 (M93's 파악하다) = to grasp the properties — the lab report's and the planning document's word. 특징 picks a thing out of a lineup; 특성 is what it is made of.

個性 individual-nature: the unit-個 M45's 개인적 decoded as "個人 individual (unit-個 + the person-人 of 외국인, M23) + 적" + the same 性: what makes one unit unlike the others. 개성이 강하다 (M63's 강하다) = has a strong personality, said of a face, a voice, a font; 개성이 있다/없다 = distinctive / generic, the fashion page's only two verdicts; 개성 있는 옷 (M7's 옷, M1's 있다 in the badge). Sort against M19's 성격: 성격 is what you are LIKE — kind, stubborn; 개성 is what makes you unlike anyone else. And the city 개성 (開城, across the border — frozen) is a homograph on the map.

獨特 alone-special: the alone-獨 M95's 독립 read as "獨 alone — the character the M27 md filed under 독일" + the special-特 of 특성 above: special in a way nothing shares. Unique, distinctive — and, said of food, the polite word for strange: 독특한 맛 (M18's 맛) = a distinctive taste, the review's phrase where M24's 이상하다 would be rude; 독특한 개성 = a one-of-a-kind personality; 독특한 방식 (M91's 방식) = an unusual way of doing it. Conjugates 독특해요, 독특한, and says 독트캐요 — the ㄱ+ㅎ merge M32's 특히 note filed ("ㄱ+ㅎ merge — 축하's rule from M25"). RADAR: M24's 특별하다 is special (chosen out of the ordinary); 독특하다 is unlike anything else — a birthday is 특별하다, the cake shaped like a shoe is 독특하다.

本格的 root-frame: the origin-本 of M57's 기본 ("base-基 + 일본's (M27) origin-本") + the frame-格 of M44's 합격 ("合格 fit-the-frame") + the -적 stamp of M45: fitting the original frame — full-scale, the real thing at last. Almost always the adverb: 본격적으로 시작하다 (M8's 시작하다) = to begin in earnest — the verb every project's second week gets, when the meetings stop and the work starts; 장마가 본격적으로 시작됐어요 (M11's 장마) = the monsoon has properly begun, the July forecast; 본격적인 여름 (M11's 여름) = summer proper. The M45 md's hardware rule holds — -적이다 to predicate, -적인 before a noun, -적으로 to adverb — and this word lives nine tenths of its life in the third. Tagged noun, as M45 and M91 filed every -적 word.

效果的 — M57's 효과 ("效果: effect-效 + 결과's (M32) fruit-果") through the -적 factory of M45, and it pays the IOU M57's 효과 wrote: "M45's stamp makes 효과적 = effective, 광고's (M32) favorite adjective." — the stamp lands. 효과적인 방법 (M32's 방법) = an effective method, 효과적으로 = effectively; 시간을 효과적으로 쓰다 (M1's 시간, M10's 쓰다) = to use time well, the planner's promise. RADAR against 효율적 (efficient — 효율, riding frozen): 효과적 WORKS, 효율적 works cheaply — a diet can be one without being the other, and the advertising page prefers the first because nobody checks.

相對的 — M57's 상대 ("相對 mutual-facing") stamped: relative — true only when set against a facing thing. 상대적으로 = relatively, the essay's favourite hedge: 상대적으로 싸다 (M7's 싸다) = relatively cheap, 상대적으로 적다 (M7's 적다) = relatively few; 상대적 빈곤 (빈곤 — poverty, riding frozen) = relative poverty, the sociologist's. Its opposite, 절대적 (absolute — riding frozen), is M39's 절대 through the same stamp: 절대적 기준 (M39's 기준) = an absolute standard. The pair 상대적/절대적 is how Korean print sorts every measurement — and the pair rides on today's 상대적 alone.

直接的 — M56's 직접 ("直接 straight-touch: no middleman between you and the thing") stamped: direct. 직접적인 원인 (M86's 원인) = the direct cause, the investigation's verdict; 직접적인 영향 (M86's 영향) = a direct effect; 직접적으로 말하다 (M4's 말하다) = to say it straight, without the layer Korean conversation usually keeps. Its shadow stamps too — M56's 직접 filed it, "Its shadow twin 간접 (indirect — riding frozen: the between-間 of M40's 간식)" — so 간접적 (riding frozen) = indirect, 간접적인 영향 = an indirect effect, 간접 흡연 (frozen) = second-hand smoke. Sort: 직접 is the adverb (직접 만들었어요 — M3's 만들다); 직접적 is the -적 noun you hang on another noun with -인.

客觀的 guest-view: the guest-客 of M48's 관객 ("觀客 view-guest") + the see-觀 M35's 습관 note sorted as "관광's see-觀" + 적 — the view from a guest's seat, someone with no stake in the house: objective. Its opposite is the master's view, 주관적 (主觀的, riding frozen), on the owner-主 of M38's 주로 ("owner/main-主") — subjective; the pair 객관적/주관적 is every debate's first sort. 객관적으로 보면 (M1's 보다 with -(으)면 from M20) = objectively speaking; 객관적인 사실 (M24's 사실) = an objective fact; and the exam hall's pair, 객관식 vs 주관식 (both frozen) — the multiple-choice question (a guest picks) vs the written answer (the owner speaks) — is how every Korean test is divided.

體驗 body-test: the body-體 of M41's 체중 ("體重 body-heavy") and M44's 체육 + the test-驗 of M33's 경험 ("經驗 pass-through-test"): experience taken through the body — hands-on. 체험 학습 (M44's 학습) = a field trip, the school's; 문화 체험 (M26's 문화) = a cultural experience, the tourist office's; 체험단 (frozen) = the trial-user panel every cosmetics brand recruits; 체험하다 rides free. The sort against 경험: 경험 is what you have HAD — it accumulates, and the interview asks for it; 체험 is what you SIGN UP for — it lasts an afternoon and comes with an apron. 김치 만들기 체험 (M3's 김치, M3's 만들다 through -기 from M13) is the one every visitor to Korea gets offered.

實驗 real-test: the real-實 of M34's 확실하다 ("確實 firm-real") + the same 驗: to test a thing against the real — an experiment. It pays M90's 기구 IOU — that note: "실험 기구 (실험 — an experiment, riding frozen) lab apparatus" — and M92's 핵 ran "핵 실험 (a nuclear test)"; both riders land. 실험실 = the laboratory (the room-室 of M15's 교실, frozen as a compound), 실험을 하다 = to run an experiment, 동물 실험 (M22's 동물) = animal testing, 실험 결과 (M32's 결과) = the results; 실험하다 rides free. RADAR: M10's 시험 is the exam — one vowel apart, same 驗: a 시험 tests you, a 실험 tests the world.

化學 becoming-study: the becoming-化 of M32's 변화 ("變化 change-becoming") + the study-學 of M1's 학교 and M15's 과학: the science of things becoming other things — chemistry. Three notes wrote it frozen and it pays all three: M86's 작용 ("화학 작용 (화학 — chemistry, riding frozen) the lab's"), M86's 반응 ("화학 반응 (화학 — chemistry, riding frozen) is the lab's"), and M92's 물질 ("화학 물질 — 화학, chemistry, riding frozen"); M97's 조미료 even used it for MSG, 화학 조미료. So: 화학 반응 = a chemical reaction, 화학 물질 = a chemical, 화학 시간 (M1's 시간) = chemistry class, 화학자 (frozen — the person-者) = a chemist. RADAR: this 화 is 化, not the talk-話 of M20's 전화 nor the fire-火 M32's 평화 note counted in "the 화 triple".

汚染 filth-dye: 汚 dirt + 染 to dye, both FIRSTS — pollution is dirt that has soaked in and will not wash out. It pays M92's 대기 IOU — that note: "대기 오염 (오염 — pollution, riding frozen) is the weather report's bad news" — and the shelf fills: 환경 오염 (M32's 환경) = environmental pollution, 수질 오염 (수질 — water quality, frozen), 토양 오염 (토양 — soil, frozen); 오염 물질 (M92's 물질) = a pollutant; 오염되다 (riding free — the 되다 flip) = to be contaminated, 오염된 물 (M1's 물) in the badge = polluted water. The noun the newspaper prints where M22's 공기 and M1's 물 would say 더럽다 (M13).

體操 body-drill: the body-體 of 체험 above + 操 to handle, to drill, a FIRST: the body put through its drills. 국민 체조 (M32's 국민) = the national calisthenics — the radio routine, twelve moves to a march, that every Korean over forty can still do on command, played in schoolyards and army camps since 1977; 체조 선수 (M17's 선수) = a gymnast; 맨손 체조 (M55's 맨 on M8's 손, frozen as a compound) = free-hand exercises, what the office does at three o'clock; 스트레칭 (Konglish, frozen) is what the young call the same thing. RADAR: the 운동 inside M8's 운동하다 is exercise in general; 체조 is exercise with a count.

動作 move-make: the move-動 of M42's 감동 ("感動 feel-move") and M8's 운동하다 + the make-作 of M48's 작가 ("作家 make-house"): a movement, a motion — one unit of doing. 동작이 빠르다 (M12's 빠르다) = quick on one's feet, 동작이 느리다 (M12's 느리다) = slow-moving; 이 동작을 따라 하세요 (M32's 따르다, M1's 하다) = copy this move — the dance teacher's and the physiotherapist's sentence; 동작 하나하나 (M5's 하나, doubled) = every single movement. RADAR: M38's 동시 and today's 동 carry same-同; the 동 of 동작 moves, like M22's 동물.

en: a part (of the body); a cut (of meat) (部位)
notes: 部位 section-place: the section-部 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion") + the place-位 of M31's 위치 ("位置 place-put"): a part with a location — on a body, or on a carcass. The doctor's word: 아픈 부위 (M14's 아프다 in the badge) = the part that hurts, 수술 부위 (M53's 수술) = the surgical site, 통증 부위 = where the pain is (below); and the butcher's: 고기 부위 (M3's 고기) = the cut, 어느 부위로 드릴까요? (M27's 어느, M9's 드리다) = which cut would you like — the question at every 정육점 (frozen), and M18's 삼겹살 is the answer. Sort against M32's 부분: 부분 is a part of anything — a song, a plan; 부위 is a part with an address on a body.

痛症 pain-symptom: the pain-痛 of M53's 두통 ("頭痛 head-pain") + the symptom-症 of M53's 증상 ("症狀 illness-shape"): pain as it appears on a chart. 통증이 심하다 (M39's 심하다) = the pain is severe, 통증을 느끼다 (M32's 느끼다) = to feel pain, 통증이 사라지다 (M35's 사라지다) = the pain goes away; 만성 통증 (만성 — chronic, frozen); and the pharmacy's 진통제 (frozen — the painkiller) carries the same 痛 with a stopping-鎭 in front. Sort against M14's 아프다: 아프다 is what you say, 통증 is what the chart writes — 여기가 아파요 to the nurse, 통증 부위 on the form.

營養 run-nourish: the run-營 of M43's 경영 ("經營 manage-and-run") + 養 to nourish, to raise, a FIRST: the managed feeding of a body — nutrition. 영양이 풍부하다 (M89's 풍부하다) = rich in nutrients, the label's boast; 영양가 (frozen — the value-價 of M87's 평가) = nutritional value; 영양제 (frozen) = supplements, the bottles on every Korean parent's kitchen counter; 영양사 (frozen) = the dietitian every school lunch program employs. RADAR: M63's 양 is 量, amount — 영양의 양 puts the two 양s side by side, nourishment and its quantity — and the 양 of M21's 양말 is Western-洋.

祭祀 offering-sacrifice: 祭 and 祀, both FIRSTS, both meaning the rite. It pays M69's 조상 IOU — that note: "The evening version of the rite, 제사 (the memorial — riding frozen), keeps them fed year-round." — and the sort against M46's 차례 is the whole lesson: 차례 (that note: "the ancestral table set on 명절 mornings") is the holiday-morning version, 제사 is the death-anniversary one, held at night on the day the ancestor died (기일 — frozen). 제사를 지내다 (M23's 지내다 — the verb M46's 차례 note put "on ritual duty") = to hold the rite; 제사상 (M40's 상 — frozen as a compound) = the offering table with its fruit in odd numbers; 제사 음식 (M1's 음식) = the ritual food, which is why so many Korean daughters-in-law dread 명절 (M25). Fewer houses keep it every year; the word does not know that yet.

智慧 wise-clear: 智 knowing that lasts and 慧 the clear mind, both FIRSTS — Korean doubles the character, as it doubles for weight. 지혜롭다 (through the -롭다 factory of M45 — that md: "same paint in a different can") = wise, 지혜로운 사람 (M1's 사람); 조상의 지혜 (M69's 조상) = the wisdom of the ancestors, the phrase on every folk-village brochure; 생활의 지혜 (M29's 생활) = household wisdom, the tips-and-tricks segment's title. Sort against M44's 지식 ("知識 know-recognize: knowledge as inventory"): 지식 is what you know; 지혜 is what you do with it — and the two 지s differ, 知 to know and 智 to know well.

衣服 garment-clothing: 衣 the garment, a FIRST, + 服 — the clothing-복 M83's 운동복 called "the suffix's character shown for the first time", and M21's 교복 and 한복 wear. The category word for what M7's 옷 names in the mouth: 의복 is on the museum placard, the textbook page, the customs form — 전통 의복 (M26's 전통) = traditional dress, 의복 문화 (M26's 문화) = clothing culture. 의식주 (gap deck) = food, clothing and shelter — 衣 + the food-食 of M1's 음식 + the live-住 of M81's 주택 ("住 live — a FIRST") — the three needs, and Korean puts clothes first. RADAR: M4's 의사 is heal-醫, M34's 의심 is doubt-疑, and 의 the possessive particle is native — four 의s.

恐怖 fear-dread: 恐 and 怖, both FIRSTS, both meaning fear — the doubled character again, and here the doubling is the meaning: terror. It pays M53's 치과 IOU — that note: "the whole country shares one 치과 공포" — dental terror, the word now yours. 공포 영화 (M2's 영화) = a horror film, 공포에 떨다 (M41's 떨다) = to tremble with fear, 공포심 (frozen — the heart-心 of 심정 below) = a sense of dread, 고소 공포증 (frozen — with the 症 of 통증 above) = fear of heights. Sort against M24's 무섭다 ("Scary AND scared"): 무섭다 is the adjective the body says; 공포 is the noun the newspaper and the film poster print — and M42's 겁 is the everyday timidity between them.

en: one's feelings (in a situation), state of heart (心情)
notes: 心情 heart-feeling: the heart-心 of M34's 의심 ("疑心 doubt-heart") and M24's 관심 + the feeling-情 of M26's 정 and M42's 감정 ("感情 feel-affection"): the heart's state at this moment. 심정을 이해하다 (M10's 이해하다) = to understand how someone feels, 솔직한 심정 (M24's 솔직하다) = one's honest feelings, 심정이 복잡하다 (M22's 복잡하다) = mixed feelings, 부모의 심정 (M4's 부모님, clipped) = a parent's heart — and the reporter's question to the winner and the bereaved alike: 지금 심정이 어떠세요? (M2's 지금, M24's 어떻다). Sort the three: M19's 마음 is the heart itself; M42's 감정 is emotion as a category; 심정 is what the heart holds right now, in this situation.

連絡 link-tie: the link-連 of M72's 연결하다 ("連結 link-tie") + 絡, the tie the same note left unspelled. M19's 연락하다 dismounted — that note ran "연락해! — text me!" and "연락이 없어요 — radio silence — is how worry starts." — and the noun has been riding ever since: M83's 연락처 ("連絡處") wrote the split as "the M75 move", M70's 끊어지다 filed "연락이 끊어지다 (연락 — the noun inside M19's 연락하다) = to lose touch". Today it stands: 연락이 오다 (M1's 오다) = word arrives, 연락을 드리다 (M9's 드리다) = I'll be in touch, the desk's line; 연락 없이 (M32's 없이) = without notice. The newspaper's use is the one this shelf files: 정부와 연락을 취하다 (M32's 정부; M61's 취하다 in its formal take job — "取 take, in full formal dress") = to be in contact with the government.

en: a formal interview; a press conference (會見)
notes: 會見 meet-see: the meet-會 of M32's 사회 ("社會 gather-meet") + the see-見 of M56's 발견하다 ("發見 shoot-forth-see"). A formal meeting granted to be seen at — and in practice the word lives in one place: 기자 회견 (M16's 기자) = a press conference, the gap deck's entry. 기자 회견을 열다 (M13's 열다) = to hold one; 기자 회견에서 밝히다 (M56's 밝히다) = to state at a press conference. Sort it against M33's 인터뷰 — that note: "This is the press kind — what M16's 기자 does after the 뉴스." An 인터뷰 is one reporter asking; a 회견 is all of them at once, and the one answering called them.

聲明 voice-bright: 聲, the voice — a first — + the bright-明 of M34's 분명하다 ("分明 divided-bright"): to make one's voice clear, in writing. A statement issued, never spoken: 성명을 발표하다 (M16's 발표하다) = to issue a statement, 공식 성명 (M90's 공식) = an official statement, 성명서 (the document-書 of M2's 도서관, riding frozen) = the paper it is printed on. RADAR: 성명 is also your full name, 姓名 — the surname-姓 of M33's 성함 ("姓銜 surname-title") + 名 — the word on the FORM (성명: ____) where the mouth says M1's 이름. NIKL lists only the 聲明 row, but the form will show you the other; the particle sorts them — a 성명 you 발표하다 is a statement, a 성명 you 쓰다 (M10) is your name.

社說 company-talk: the 社 of M32's 사회 in its other job — the company, the one M32 found by flipping 사회 into 회사 — + the talk-說 of M48's 소설 ("小說 small-talk"). The newspaper company speaking in its own voice: the editorial, unsigned. 사설을 읽다 (M2's 읽다); 신문 사설 (M8's 신문); 오늘의 사설 is the column on the inside page that argues where the rest of the paper reports. Sort against M48's 기사 ("記事 record-affair") — a 기사 records what happened, a 사설 says what the paper thinks of it — and against M48's 언론, the whole apparatus that prints both.

弘報 broad-report: 弘, to broaden — a first — + the report-報 of M33's 정보 ("情報 feeling-report"). Telling the world about yourself: 홍보 영상 (M20's 영상) = a promotional video, 홍보 자료 (M44's 자료) = press materials, 홍보하다 (riding frozen — the 하다 twin) = to publicize; 홍보팀 (M16's 팀) is the department. Sort it against M32's 광고 ("廣告 wide-tell") — a 광고 is paid space, a 홍보 is the company telling you itself, for free and at length; the press release is 홍보, the banner beside it is 광고. Both 弘 and 廣 mean wide, which is the whole point of both words.

非難 not-hard: the not-非 that M90's 공식 note left frozen ("비공식 (unofficial — the not-非 riding frozen) is the leak") + 難, hard — a first: to call a thing wrong, and hard to bear. Blame as the headline counts it: 비난을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to come under fire, 비난이 쏟아지다 (M70's 쏟아지다 — the verb that note gave to rain, applause and tears) = blame rained down, 비난의 대상 (대상 riding frozen, as M93's 비판 note filed it). Sort against M93's 비판 — that note: "a 지적 is one finger on one flaw, a 비판 is an argument with reasons" — 비판 argues, 비난 attacks; the editorial writes 비판 about itself and 비난 about its enemies. 비난하다 (frozen) is the verb; the noun is what the page prints.

論爭 argue-fight: the argument-論 of M44's 논문 ("論文 argument-writing") + the fight-爭 of M32's 전쟁 ("戰爭 war").
