A war fought in arguments: 논쟁이 벌어지다 (M61's 벌어지다 — "The happen-verb of headlines") = a controversy breaks out, 논쟁을 벌이다 (M56's 벌이다) = to wage one, 뜨거운 논쟁 (M18's 뜨겁다) = a heated dispute, 논쟁거리 (거리 — the stuff-suffix, riding frozen) = a bone of contention. Sort against M44's 토론 ("討論 strike-argue"): a 토론 has rules, a moderator and a clock; a 논쟁 has none of those and goes on for years. Same 論, and the ㄹ→ㄴ that M44 explained for 논문 holds here too: 論爭 → 논쟁.

支持 prop-hold: the 支 that M65's 지점 read as "支 (support, branch-off)" + the hold-持 of M88's 유지하다 ("維持 tie-hold"): to hold a thing up from beneath. Support as a poll counts it: 지지를 받다 (M9's 받다), 지지를 얻다 (M35's 얻다) = to win support, 지지율 (율 — the rate that M90's 범죄 note left frozen) = the approval rating, the number under every politician's name; 지지하다 (frozen) is the verb. PAYS M81's 적극 — that note filed "적극 지지 (지지 — support, riding frozen)"; today the rider lands. RADAR, two sound-twins: the 지지 of 만지지 마세요 (M41's 만지다 — "every museum's favorite sentence") is -지 + 지, two grammar pieces and no hanja; and 지지 said to a toddler means dirty, hands off — a nursery word that has never held anything up.

警告 warn-tell: 警, to warn — a first, the character the police wear in 경찰 (M16) — + the tell-告 of M32's 광고 ("廣告 wide-tell"). A warning as a document or a card: 경고를 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be warned, 경고를 주다 (M9's 주다), 경고문 (the writing-文 of M33's 문장) = the warning notice on the wall, 경고 없이 (M32's 없이) = without warning. The football pitch says it plainest: 옐로카드 = 경고, the first card, and two 경고 make a sending-off. 경고하다 (frozen) is the verb; the noun is the one you receive.

威脅 might-threaten: the might-威 of M90's 시위 ("示威 show-might") + 脅, to press on someone's ribs — a first. A threat as the report names it: 위협을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be threatened, 위협이 되다 (M10's 되다) = to pose a threat, 생명의 위협 (M92's 생명 — "生命 life-mandate") = a threat to life, the line under a stalking story; 위협적 with the -적 of M45 = threatening; 위협하다 (frozen) is the verb. Sort it against M90's 시위: a 시위 shows might on purpose and in public; a 위협 is what the other side calls it.

差別 differ-separate: the differ-差 of M57's 차이 ("差異 differ-differ") + the separate-別 M57's 특별 decoded ("the 별 is separate-別: special = set apart"). A difference acted on: 차별을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be discriminated against, 차별하다 (frozen) = to discriminate, 성차별 (the nature-性 of M78's 성별 — "性別 nature-separate") = sexism, 인종 차별 (인종 — race, riding frozen) = racism, 차별 없이 (M32's 없이) = without discrimination, the clause every hiring page carries. Sort against 차이: a 차이 is a difference that exists; a 차별 is a difference someone was made to pay for. Same 差, different crime.

區分 district-divide: the 區 that M49's 지구 note radared ("a homograph 지구 (地區) is a zoned DISTRICT") + the divide-分 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion"). Sorting into zones: 구분이 있다/없다 = there is / is no distinction, 남녀 구분 (M32's 남성 and 여성, clipped) = separation by sex, 구분이 안 되다 (M10's 되다) = you can't tell them apart — the sentence about twins. Its verb is next door. Sort against M56's 나누다 ("Divide AND share — Korean refuses to split the two."): 나누다 splits a cake; 구분 sorts a category, and nobody eats it.

en: to distinguish, to tell apart; to classify (區分)
notes: 구분 + 하다: to sort into kinds. 둘을 구분하다 (M5's 둘) = to tell the two apart, 사실과 의견을 구분하다 (M24's 사실, M24's 의견) = to separate fact from opinion — the media-literacy sentence, 쓰레기를 구분해서 버리다 (M13's 쓰레기, M13's 버리다) = to sort the trash, the civic act every Korean building enforces. 구분되다 (the 되다-row) = to be classified; 구분이 되다 says the same with the noun. Where M24's 다르다 says two things ARE different, 구분하다 says you can SEE that they are.

憤怒 fury-anger: both characters are firsts, and both mean anger — the hanja habit M57's 차이 showed you, two of the same stapled for force. The editorial's anger, not the kitchen's: 분노를 느끼다 (M32's 느끼다), 국민의 분노 (M32's 국민) = public outrage, 분노가 폭발하다 (폭발하다 — to explode, riding frozen) = anger explodes; 분노하다 (frozen) is the verb. Sort against M19's 화나다 — that note: "anger emerges, weather-style" — 화 is what you feel across a table; 분노 is what a headline says a nation feels. Rom bunno: ㄴ + ㄴ, said as written.

義務 right-task: the 義 of M44's 강의 ("講義 explain-the-meaning") — the character of what is right — + the task-務 of M43's 근무 ("勤務 duty-task"). What is right to do, made a task: 의무가 있다 = to have a duty, 의무를 다하다 (M9's 다 + 하다) = to fulfil one's obligations, 의무 교육 (M32's 교육) = compulsory schooling, 의무적으로 (-적 from M45 + 으로) = compulsorily. PAYS M90's 권리 — that note: "Its twin is 의무 (duty — riding frozen): 권리와 의무, the pair on every civics test" — today the twin arrives, and the test can be taken. Korean men learn the word early: 국방의 의무 (국방 — national defence, riding frozen) is why M58's 군대 is not optional.

勝利 win-gain: the win-勝 of M51's 우승 ("優勝 excel-win") + the gain-利 of M43's 이익 ("利益 edge-plus-increase"). The noun for having won: 승리를 거두다 — PAYS M94's 거두다, which filed "승리를 거두다 (승리 — a victory, riding frozen) = take the win"; 승리로 이끌다 — PAYS M93's 이끌다, which filed "승리로 이끌다 (승리 — victory, riding frozen; M6's 으로) = to lead to victory — the sports page's verb". Two riders, one landing. Sort the shelf: M17's 이기다 is the verb the mouth uses, 승리 the noun the page prints, M51's 우승 the title at the end of a tournament ("you 이기다 six times and 우승 once"), M95's 승부 the decision that contains both outcomes. Rom seungni: ㄹ after ㅇ goes to ㄴ — 승니, as 대통령 is 대통녕.

左右 left-right: both firsts — the Sino pair under the native M6's 왼쪽 and M6's 오른쪽. Bare, it is the two sides at once: 좌우를 살피다 (M93's 살피다 — that note's "주위를 살피다 (M57's 주위) = to look around carefully") = to look both ways, the crossing rule; 좌우로 (M6's 으로) = side to side; and in politics 좌 and 우 are the left and the right, so 좌우 is the whole spectrum. Then the verb, one clause: 좌우하다 (frozen) = to sway, to determine — 결과를 좌우하다 (M32's 결과) = to decide the outcome — because whatever stands at your left AND right has you surrounded. Radar: this 우 is 右, not the excel-優 of M51's 우승.

en: a trace, a mark left behind (痕跡)
notes: 痕跡 scar-footprint: both firsts — 痕 the mark on skin, 跡 the print on ground. What stays after the thing has gone: 흔적을 남기다 (M37's 남기다 — that note: "What remains, someone left: the pair tells you who.") = to leave a trace, 흔적이 남다 (M35's 남다) = a trace remains, 흔적도 없이 (M2's 도, M32's 없이) = without a trace — the detective's line and the breakup's. 범인의 흔적 belongs to the law drawer below. RADAR, mandatory: this 적 is 跡, a footprint, NOT the -적 stamp of M45 — 흔적 is not 'trace-ish', and 흔 is not a root you can peel the suffix off.

en: the political class, political circles (政治權)
notes: 政治權 politics-power: M32's 정치 ("政治 govern-manage") + the authority-權 of M90's 권리 ("authority-權 of M64's 권하다"). The people who hold political power, counted as one body: 정치권의 반응 (M86's 반응) = the reaction from political circles, 정치권 전체 (M57's 전체) = the whole political class — the headline's way of blaming everyone at once. RADAR, a triple 권: here 權 (power); in 수도권, two entries down, 圈 (a ring); and M5's 권 is the book-counter, 책 세 권 — M64's 권하다 note drew the first line ("this 권 is 權 (power), NOT M5's 권 (the book-counter)"), and today's shelf adds the third.

M32's 정치 + the person-人: PAYS M32's 정치 note, which built the word in passing — "정치인 = politician (M31's person-인 doing suffix work)" — and M96's 지식인 note, which filed the suffix's job ("-인 (人) marks a kind of person (지식인, 외국인, 정치인 — M32's 정치 note built that one)"). Today it gets its own card. 정치인이 되다 (M10's 되다), 배우 출신 정치인 — the phrase M96's 출신 note ran — a former actor turned politician, and the M45 md's line worth keeping: "적이 많은 정치인, a politician rich in both" — enemies and the -적 stamp. Sort against M90's 의원: an 의원 holds a seat; a 정치인 is anyone in the trade, seat or not.

總理 all-manage: the 總 of M58's 총장 ("總長 all-chief" — that note left the character "gathers-everything — riding frozen") + the manage-理 of M34's 이해 ("理解"). The one who manages everything: Korea's prime minister, second to M32's 대통령. PAYS M78's 수상 — that note: "Korea's own head of cabinet is the 총리 (riding frozen), under M32's 대통령, so 수상 in Korean news is almost always someone else's" — and s_m78_pm_visit repeated the debt ("Korea has a 총리 (frozen) under M32's 대통령"). Today it is paid: 국무총리 (국무 — state affairs, riding frozen) is the full title, 총리 후보 (M90's 후보) the nominee. Rom chongni: ㄹ after ㅇ turns ㄴ, as in 승리 above.

en: the capital region (Seoul, Incheon, Gyeonggi) (首都圈)
notes: 首都圈 capital-ring: M31's 수도 ("首都 head-city: where a country keeps its head") + 圈, a ring, a circle — a first. The ring around the head: M12's 서울, M31's 인천 and 경기도 together, where half the country lives. PAYS M50's 전철 — that note filed "수도권 전철, the capital-region network; 수도 M31" — and the news prints the word daily: 수도권 집값 (M1's 집 + 값), 수도권 인구 (M64's 인구), 수도권 집중 (M44's 집중) = concentration in the capital region, the problem every government promises to fix. RADAR: this 권 is 圈, the ring — not the 權 of 정치권 above, not M5's 권, the book-counter. Three 권, three characters, one sound.

en: democratic; democracy as a root (民主)
notes: 民主 people-master: the people-民 of M32's 국민 + the master-主 of M27's 주인. PAYS M90's 민주주의 — that note read the root in advance, "민주 (the people as masters) + 주의 (a doctrine): the people rule, as a creed" — and M90's 민주화 built on it ("민주 + the becoming-化 of M32's 변화"). Today the bare root stands, and it works as a prefix: 민주 국가 (M31's 국가) = a democratic state, 민주 사회 (M32's 사회), 민주 시민 (M50's 시민) = a democratic citizen — and in party names, where 민주당 (the 당 of M90's 정당) has been on Korean ballots for seventy years. RADAR: not M8's 주, the week — 민주 has no Mondays in it.

所謂 that-which-is-said: the 所 of M52's 숙소 ("宿所 stay-place") in its grammar job — that which — + 謂, to say — a first. An adverb that puts scare quotes on the next noun: 소위 전문가 (M58's 전문가) = the so-called experts, 소위 명문대 (명문대 — a prestige university, riding frozen) = the 'top' schools — the columnist's eyebrow, in print. Its native twin 이른바 (riding frozen) does the same job in warmer prose. Sort it against M32's 특히, the other one-word adverb the editorial leans on: 특히 points a spotlight, 소위 holds up a pair of tongs. Gap deck.

en: total, all (總, determiner); a gun (銃)
notes: Two 총, one sound — and NIKL lists both, so the radar is mandatory. First, 總: the gathers-everything character of M58's 총장 ("總長 all-chief"), used bare as a determiner before a count: 총 인원 (M58's 인원 — "people as a NUMBER") = the total headcount, 총 열 명 (M5's 열, M5's 명) = ten in all, 총 백만 원 (M9's 백, M9's 만, M9's 원) = a total of a million won — the last line of every invoice and every casualty report. Second, 銃 — a first: the gun. 총을 쏘다 (M66's 쏘다 — "The laser-gun verb") = to fire a gun, 총소리 (M19's 소리) = a gunshot, 총에 맞다 (M15's 맞다 in the receiving job that note gave 주사를 맞다) = to be shot. The particle sorts them: 총 before a number is 總; 총 with 을 or 에 is 銃. The economy page uses the first; the crime page, the second.

數十 several-tens: the number-數 M63's 수많다 read as "The number-數 of M15's 수학" + M2's 십. PAYS M77's 수년 — that note filed the rail in advance: "수십 년 = decades, 수백 명, 수천 개 (수십/수백/수천 — several tens, hundreds, thousands — riding frozen)" — and today the first rung lands; 수백 and 수천 keep riding. Always before a counter: 수십 명 (M5's 명) = dozens of people, 수십 년 (M25's 년) = decades, 수십 차례 (M46's 차례 in its turn sense) = dozens of times. M77 also gave the sound: "수십 년 is said 수심 년, the ㅂ sliding before ㄴ". Where the mouth says M76's 몇십 ("some-tens = dozens of"), the page says 수십.

en: a large quantity; mass, bulk (大量)
notes: 大量 big-amount: M1's 크다 in its character, 大, + the measure-量 of M63's 양 ("量 amount"). PAYS M97's 생산, one module ago — that note filed "대량 생산 (대량 — mass, riding frozen) = mass production"; today the rider lands. 대량으로 (M6's 으로) = in bulk, 대량 구매 (구매 — purchase, riding frozen; M97's 구입하다 is its verb) = bulk buying, 대량 해고 (해고 — layoffs, riding frozen) = mass layoffs — the word a factory town dreads. Its opposite 소량 (a small amount) rides frozen and costs more per unit.

特殊 special-different: the special-特 of M32's 특히 + 殊, different — the character M78's 수상 note met in "수상하다 (殊常, riding frozen) = suspicious". Special as a CLASS, not a compliment: 특수 효과 (M57's 효과) = special effects, 특수 학교 (M1's 학교) = a special-needs school, 특수 부대 (M98's 부대) = special forces — PAYS that note, which filed "특수 부대 (특수 — special, riding frozen)" one module ago, 특수한 경우 (M32's 경우) = a special case. Sort against M57's 특별: 특별 is special to someone — a 특별 메뉴, a 특별한 사람; 특수 is a category the ministry files you under. Nobody says 특수한 사람 as a compliment.

en: to be identical, the same (同一)
notes: 同一 same-one: the same-同 of M38's 동시 ("同時 same-hour") + the one-一 of M2's 일. Identical, in print: 동일한 조건 (M39's 조건) = the same conditions, the contract's phrase; 동일 인물 (M48's 인물) = the same person, the detective's; 동일하게 (-게 from M33) = identically. Sort against M24's 같다: 같다 is the mouth's same — 같은 옷 — and can also mean like; 동일하다 means only identical and only on a page. 동일시하다 (to equate — riding frozen) is the noun grown a verb.

持續的 hold-continue-ish: the hold-持 of M88's 유지하다 ("維持 tie-hold") + 續, to continue — a first, the character M28's 계속 (繼續) carries but never spelled out — + the -적 stamp of M45. Sustained, as a plan or a problem is: 지속적인 노력 (M39's 노력) = sustained effort, 지속적으로 (M6's 으로) = continuously, 지속적인 관심 (M24's 관심). The parents ride frozen: 지속하다 = to keep up, 지속되다 = to persist, 지속 가능한 (M39's 가능하다) = sustainable — the word on every corporate report since 2015. Sort against 계속: 계속 is what you say when the rain won't stop; 지속적 is what the report says about the rain.

處罰 handle-punish: the handle-處 of M36's 상처 ("傷處 wound-place") in its verb sense — to deal with — + 罰, to punish — a first. Punishment as the law hands it out: 처벌을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be punished, 강력한 처벌 (M89's 강력하다) = severe punishment, the phrase every outraged headline demands; 처벌하다 (frozen) is the state's verb, 처벌되다 the report's. Sort against bare 벌 (riding frozen), the plain penalty a teacher or a parent gives — 벌을 서다, standing in the corner; 처벌 needs a court. Radar: this 처 is 處, the place-and-handle character, not the wife-妻 of 처가 (the in-laws — riding frozen).

殺人 kill-person: 殺, to kill — a first — + the person-人 of 정치인 above. What M37's 죽이다 becomes when the report writes it up: 살인 사건 (M36's 사건 — "사고 is bad luck; 사건 has a suspect.") = a murder case, 살인범 (the 범 of 범인 below) = the murderer, 살인 미수 (미수 — an attempt, riding frozen) = attempted murder. RADAR, a sound trap: s_m53_momsal_guess ran 몸살인 것 같아요, and the M53 md listed the noun row of -ㄴ데 as "(몸살인데)" — that 살인 is 몸살 + the copula's 인, and nobody was killed. Rom sarin: ㄹ between vowels is r.

犯人 commit-person: the commit-犯 of M90's 범죄 ("犯罪 commit-wrong") + the person-人. The one who did it: 범인을 잡다 (M28's 잡다) = to catch the culprit, 범인이 잡히다 (M36's 잡히다) = the culprit is caught — the passive party's sentence, 범인은 이 안에 있다 (M6's 안) = the culprit is in this room, every detective's line. Sort against the 범죄자 M90's 범죄 note listed ("범죄자 the criminal (the person-者 of M27's 환자)"): a 범죄자 is anyone with a record; a 범인 is the one who did THIS. Radar, as M90 warned: 범 alone is the folk-tale tiger, who never stood trial.

損害 lose-harm: 損, to lose, to diminish — a first — + the harm-害 of M86's 피해 ("被害 suffer-harm"). Loss on a ledger: 손해를 보다 (M1's 보다 in its suffer job) = to take a loss, 손해를 입다 (M8's 입다, the wear-verb worn as a wound, as M86 read it) = to suffer damage, 손해가 크다 (M1's 크다) = the losses are heavy. PAYS M43's 이익 — that note: "Its shadow, 손해 (the loss), waits on a later shelf; may your ledgers never need it early." Fifty-seven modules later the shadow arrives, and with it the gap deck's 손해 보는 장사 — the opposite of M43's 남는 장사. RADAR: not M8's 손 (the hand) + M11's 해 (the sun) — no hand, no sun, only the red column.

Software through the converter: s→ㅅ with the ㅡ-cushion, f→ㅍ, and the -ware landing as 웨어 — six syllables where English has two. The industry's word: 소프트웨어 회사 (M2's 회사), 소프트웨어를 설치하다 (설치 — installation, riding frozen). The M79 md's rule holds — "every loanword in Korean lives next to a Korean word it did NOT replace" — except that here the neighbour is ANOTHER loan: M32's 프로그램 is one program, 소프트웨어 is the category the programs belong to, and M10's 컴퓨터 is the box both run in. Sort them by count: 프로그램 하나, 소프트웨어 전체. The clip law M32 named ("Koreans clip it too (준말 law): a TV show is often just 프로") does not touch this one; the office says all six syllables.

System: s→ㅅ, the ㅡ-cushion, and -tem as 템. The word for any machinery of parts — 교육 시스템 (M32's 교육) = the education system, 예약 시스템 (M52's 예약) = the booking system — and the office's verdict on a bad morning: 시스템이 다운됐어요 (다운 — down, riding frozen) = the system is down. The Korean word it did NOT replace is 체계 (體系 — riding frozen), which is what the textbook writes where the office says 시스템: 교육 체계 in the ministry's report, 교육 시스템 in the newspaper's. The loan took the machine; the Sino word kept the theory.

Code, through the converter — and three jobs share the spelling. First the computer's 코드: 코드를 짜다 (짜다 — the weave-and-organize homograph of M3's 짜다 that M99's 조 note left riding frozen) = to write code, the programmer's phrase. Second the rulebook's: 드레스 코드 (드레스 — dress, riding frozen) = the dress code on a wedding invitation. Third, and it is a different English word in the same Korean coat: the power CORD — 코드를 뽑다 (M61's 뽑다, the pull-out verb that already pulled "cash from the machine") = to pull the plug, 코드를 꽂다 (꽂다 — to plug in, riding frozen). Code and cord fall together because the converter has no r before a consonant. Sort the cord against M99's 선, whose note thawed "선을 연결하다 (선 — a cord or line, riding frozen)": 선 is any cable or line; 코드 is the one with a plug on the end. RADAR: not M14's 코 with a 드 attached — the nose has nothing to do with it.

Text: t→ㅌ, the cluster -xt broken open by two ㅡ-cushions — four syllables for one. The TEXT of a document, on a screen or a page: 텍스트 파일 (M79's 파일) = a text file, 텍스트를 복사하다 (복사 — copy, riding frozen) = copy the text, 이미지와 텍스트 (이미지 riding frozen) = image and text, the web designer's two materials. The Korean word it did NOT replace is 본문 (本文 — the body text, riding frozen), the editor's word. THE TRAP, and every learner walks into it: the text MESSAGE is M20's 문자 — 문자 보냈어요, never 텍스트 보냈어요. 텍스트 is what a page holds; 문자 is what a phone sends.

Circle through the converter: c→ㅅ before i-sounds, -rcle as 클. A club at university — the 1990s word: 대학 서클 (M15's 대학교), 서클 활동 (M57's 활동), 같은 서클 선배 (M58's 선배). It PAYS a sort M69's 동아리 note left open: that note called the campus club "a rare native word on this hanja shelf", and the loan is the word the same club had a generation earlier. Students say 동아리 now; 서클 dates the speaker to their parents' campus, the way 다방 dates a coffee (M96's 다방). The geometric circle is a different word: 원 (圓 — riding frozen, a homograph of M9's 원, the money). One loan, one native, one Sino — three circles, and the loan is the one going out of use.

車輛: the cart-車 of M37's 주차장 ("駐車場 park-car-place") and M50's 자동차 + 輛, the vehicle-counter character — a FIRST. Vehicles, as the traffic report counts them: 차량 통제 (M90's 통제 — that note's "교통 통제 (M12's 교통 — a road closed for a parade)" is the same event from the cars' side) = vehicle control, 차량 정체 (정체 — congestion, riding frozen), 차량 한 대 (M55's 대, the counter) = one vehicle. Register, and M50's 자동차 note already drew it — "Register: 차 is what you SAY; 자동차 is what forms and news say" — 차량 is one rung higher still: the police report's word. M2's 차 is what you drive to work; 차량 is what the radio says is backed up on the bridge.

運轉士: 운전 — the carry-運 and turn-轉 that M50's 운전자 note split open ("carry-運, turn-轉") — + 士, the licensed-士 of M44's 박사 ("博士 broad-scholar"). It PAYS M78's 운전기사, which filed this word in one clause — "운전사 (the older form) rides frozen" — and today the older form lands: 버스 운전사, 택시 운전사 (M6's 버스 and 택시) in the older newspaper and the older mouth, where the current form is 운전기사 and the face-to-face form is 기사님. The 士 is the point: M78's 운전기사 note sorted the two job-사s — "licensed-士 (박사, 기사, and M16's 변호사 — 辯護士" — against teacher-師 (M4's 요리사, M14's 간호사, and M4's 의사, which is 醫師), and 운전사 sits on the licence side: a person certified to turn the wheel. Sort the three: M50's 운전자 is anyone driving, on paper; 운전사 and 운전기사 are the job; 기사님 is the man in the mirror.

船長: 船 the ship-character — M92's 우주 note carried it frozen in "우주선 = spaceship (船 the ship-character, riding frozen)" — + 長, the chief-長 of M39's 장점 ("長點 long-point") in its chief job. The captain of a ship; and the 長 ladder M98's 교장 note laid out — "The 長 ladder: 부장 runs a section, M9's 사장님 a company, 교장 a school" — gains a rung at sea, with M58's 총장 above the campus and M58's 회장 above the company. 선장님 to his face (the -님 ladder M16 built, as always); 배의 선장 (M3's 배, the boat sense that note flagged on day three); 선장이 되다 (M10's 되다) = to become a captain. RADAR: the 선 is 船, not the line-線 that M99's 선 landed bare, nor the before-先 of M4's 선생님 and M97's 선진국.

Native, and built from two Ring 1 words: M3's 배 in its boat sense + linking-ㅅ + M1's 사람 — the same wedge M82's 바닷물 note filed ("M11's 바다 + linking-ㅅ + M1's 물"), now between a boat and a person. Says 뱃싸람: the ㅅ tenses the ㅅ behind it. A man of the sea — the folk word, the fishing village's, the folk song's; the payroll word is 선원 (船員 — crew member, riding frozen, with the 船 of 선장 above and the member-員 of M16's 직원). Sort the deck: 선장 commands, 선원 is on the roster, 뱃사람 is what the shore calls them all. RADAR: the 배 here is the boat, not the belly of 배고프다 and not the pear — M3 warned you it would be context that decides.

一行: M2's 일 (one) + 行, the going-行 that M28's 날다 note read inside 비행기 ("飛行 — flying-going") — one going, one line of people moving together. Your party: 일행이 있어요? (M1's 있다) = are you with a group? — the restaurant host's first question, and the gap deck runs it; 일행이 몇 명이에요? (M5's 몇 and 명) = how many in your party?; 일행과 함께 (M29's 함께) = with one's companions. RADAR: not M2's 일 (work) with a 행 attached, and not a line of text — that 一行 is read 한 줄 in Korean. The word lives at the restaurant door, the tour bus and the hotel desk: wherever someone has to count who belongs to whom.

女人: the woman-女 of M32's 여성 ("女性 woman-nature") + the person-人 of M32's 인간. A woman, in the novel's register — the third rung of a ladder M32 already drew two rungs of: "Forms, news, and signage say 여성; conversation says 여자" — and the poem says 여인. 여인의 향기 (M41's 향기) = Scent of a Woman, the film title; 한 여인이 (한 — the counter contraction M5 taught) = a woman, as a novel's first line has it; 아름다운 여인 (M22's 아름답다 in the badge). You will read it and hear it in songs; you will almost never say it, and if you do, you are quoting. RADAR: the 여 is 女, the one M32's 여성 carries — not the 여 of M11's 여행 (旅), which is a journey.

en: a maiden, an unmarried young woman (dated); (prefix) maiden-, first
notes: 處女: the place-處 of M36's 상처 ("傷處 wound-place") and M86's 처지 ("處地 place-ground") + 女 — a woman still in her place, at home; the old word for an unmarried young woman, and it wears its century. REGISTER, and M58's 아가씨 note wrote the rule for this whole shelf — "Understand it everywhere, deploy it almost never": in a folk tale (처녀와 총각 — the maiden and the bachelor, 총각 riding frozen) it is neutral; said of a living woman it is dated at best. Where it still works in daily Korean is as a prefix meaning FIRST: 처녀작 (with the 作 of M48's 작가) = a debut work, 처녀 비행 (비행 — a flight, riding frozen) = a maiden flight — the same metaphor English makes with 'maiden'. RADAR: the 처 is 處, the place — M86's 처지 shares the character but not the word — and it is not 妻, the wife-처 of 처가 (riding frozen), which is a different character wearing the same sound.

en: the top place, first rank (首席)
notes: 首席: the head-首 of M31's 수도 ("首都 head-city") and M78's 수상 + the seat-席 of M64's 참석하다 ("參 (mix in) + 席 (seat)") and M83's 좌석: the head seat — first place among those seated. 수석 합격 (M44's 합격, "合格 fit-the-frame") = passing in first place, the newspaper's phrase for the exam's top scorer; 수석 졸업 (M44's 졸업) = graduating top of the class; 수석 연구원 (연구원 — researcher, riding frozen) = senior researcher, the seat with no exam behind it. Sort against M30's 첫째: 첫째 is first in a list or a family; 수석 is first in a ranking, and only the ranking uses it. Next seat down is 차석 (riding frozen).

品質: the goods-品 of M43's 제품 ("製品 made-goods") + the substance-質 of M81's 질. It PAYS M81's 질, which sorted the pair in advance — "품질 (frozen) is the label's word; 질 is the mouth's" — and today the label's word lands: 품질이 좋다 (M1's 좋다) = the quality is good, 품질 관리 (M57's 관리) = quality control, the department on the factory floor, 고품질 (고 — the high-高 of M81's 고속, in front) on the box. Say 질이 좋아요 about a coat you are holding; write 품질이 우수합니다 (우수 — excellence, riding frozen) on the coat's tag. Same 質, one register apart — the M43 md's 제품/상품 split, applied to the adjective.

en: item (on a list of goods) (品目)
notes: 品目: the goods-品 of 품질 above and M43's 상품 + the eye-目 of M33's 제목 ("題目 topic-eye") — the eye that points at each item on a list. An item, as inventory counts it: 수입 품목 (M43's 수입) = import items, 판매 품목 (M43's 판매하다, the noun inside) = items for sale, 품목별로 (-별 — by each, riding frozen; M6's 으로) = item by item, the line on every customs form. Sort: M43's 상품 is a thing on a shelf; 품목 is the same thing as a ROW on a list. RADAR: not M14's 목 — the neck — though M33's 제목 note already told you so: "This 목 is Sino 目 (eye/item), NOT your native neck".

en: line of business, industry sector (業種)
notes: 業種: the work-業 of M43's 사업 ("事業 affairs-work") + the seed-種 of M57's 종류 ("種類 seed-sort") and M81's 종 — the sort of work. A line of business, as the tax office files it: 업종 변경 (변경 — a change, riding frozen) = a change of business type, 같은 업종 (M24's 같다) = the same trade, 업종별 (-별 riding frozen) = by sector. Sort the three works: M43's 사업 is a business you run, M97's 산업 is the sector as the economist sees it, 업종 is the sector as the form asks for it — 업종: 음식점 (M1's 음식). RADAR: not M97's 업체 — the 체 is a body, the vendor; the 종 is a kind.

裝備: the dress-裝 of M80's 포장 (that note: "裝 (to dress, to fit out — frozen; NOT the 粧 of M6's 화장실)") + the ready-備 of M83's 준비물 ("準備物") — to be dressed and ready: equipment. 등산 장비 (M17's 등산) = hiking gear, the aisle that note said was "Full gear mandatory"; 촬영 장비 (촬영 — filming, riding frozen); 장비를 갖추다 (M88's 갖추다, whose note ran "시설을 갖추다 (M50's 시설) = to be fitted out with facilities") = to be equipped. Sort: M72's 기계 is one machine; 장비 is everything the job needs laid out together. And the 비 pays in advance: 준비, 장비, 대비 (riding frozen) — the same 備, readiness, each time.

en: planning (of a project); a plan as a job (企劃)
notes: 企劃: the stand-up-企 of M90's 기업 ("企 (stand up to; to plan)") and M64's 대기업 + the stroke-劃 of M75's 계획하다 ("計劃 count-scheme" — that note left the second character "劃 (frozen — a stroke drawn out)") — standing up a scheme. Planning, as a department does it: 기획팀 (M16's 팀) = the planning team, 상품 기획 (M43's 상품) = product planning, 기획 회의 (M10's 회의). The verb 기획하다 rides frozen. Sort against M8's 계획 — same 劃, different job: 계획 is the plan you have (주말 계획); 기획 is planning as WORK, the thing a 기획자 (the person-者 of M50's 운전자) is paid to do.

檢討: the check-檢 of M44's 검사 ("檢査 check-examine") + the strike-討 of M44's 토론 ("討論 strike-argue") — to check and to strike at: a review. What a proposal gets before a yes: 검토 중 (S2's 중, "The busy-sign machine") = under review — the email's non-answer, which the gap deck files; 검토를 거치다 (M88's 거치다) = to go through review; 재검토 (재 — again, riding frozen) = a re-examination. The verb 검토하다 rides frozen. Sort the two 檢s: M44's 검사 checks a THING against a standard (homework, eyes); 검토 examines a PROPOSAL for whether to accept it. RADAR: not the prosecutor 검사 (檢事) that M44 flagged — though the prosecutor does plenty of 검토.

貸出: 貸 to lend — a FIRST — + the out-出 of M43's 출근 ("出勤 out-to-duty"): money lent out. The bank's word: 대출을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to take out a loan, 주택 대출 (주택 — housing, riding frozen) = a mortgage, 학자금 대출 (학자금 riding frozen) = a student loan, 대출 이자 (이자 — interest, riding frozen). Sort against M69's 빌리다 — that note's line "빌다 asks heaven, 빌리다 asks the bank": 빌리다 is the verb you do; 대출 is the noun the bank does, and the form never says 빌리다. M6's 은행 is where both happen. RADAR: the 대 is 貸, lend — not the big-大 of M64's 대기업 nor the counter 대 of M55.

en: a sum, an amount of money (額數)
notes: 額數: 額 an amount — a FIRST — + the number-數 of M63's 수많다 ("The number-數 of M15's 수학"): the figure of a sum. A sum of money, as a figure: 액수가 크다 (M1's 크다) = a large sum, 액수가 적다 (M7's 적다) = a small one, 대출 액수 (today's 대출) = the size of the loan. Its twin is 금액 (金額 — riding frozen), the same 額 with the gold-金 of M43's 세금 in front: 금액 is the amount written on the receipt; 액수 is the amount talked about. RADAR: not M63's 양, which measures anything — 액수 measures only money.

生産力: M97's 생산 ("生産 birth-produce") + the strength-力 of M39's 노력 ("努力 exert-strength") and M44's 능력 — the power to produce. Says 생산녁: the ㄹ nasalizes after the ㄴ, as it does in M44's 능력. The economist's noun and the history textbook's: 생산력이 높다 (M7's 높다) = high productive capacity, 생산력 향상 (향상 — improvement, riding frozen) = a rise in productivity. Sort the two 力 words the page pairs: M95's 경쟁력 is the power to win against others; 생산력 is the power to make. And the -량 M97's 생산 note left frozen ("생산량 (量 — the measure-量 of M63's 양, riding frozen as a suffix) = output") is the count; 생산력 is the capacity behind the count.

國際化: M31's 국제 ("국 + 제 (際 between)") + the becoming-化 of M32's 변화 — becoming international. The 1990s slogan: 국제화 시대 (M26's 시대) = the age of internationalization, 대학의 국제화 (M15's 대학교) = the university going global. History replaced it, and M32's 변화 note already filed the replacement in passing — "The suffix industrializes: 세계화 globalization, 노령화 aging" — so 세계화 (riding frozen) is the word after 1995 and 국제화 the word before. Sort them by the character: 국제 is BETWEEN countries, so 국제화 keeps the borders; 세계 is the whole world, so 세계화 dissolves them. Say 국제화 and you have dated yourself, as with 서클.

聯合: the link-聯 of M56's 관련 ("關聯 gate-link" — that note left the second character "link-聯 (frozen)") + the fit-合 of M44's 합격 ("合格 fit-the-frame") — linked and fitted together. A union of bodies: 국제 연합 (M31's 국제) = the United Nations — 유엔 (riding frozen) in the mouth, 국제 연합 in Sino; 연합 뉴스 (M24's 뉴스) = Yonhap, the national wire service, on the byline of half the articles you will read; 연합군 (with the army-軍 of M27's 군인) = the allied forces. Sort: M23's 단체 is one organization; 연합 is several agreeing to act as one. RADAR: not M48's 연기 — the 연 here is 聯, a link, not 演, a performance.

en: direction, staging (of a play, a show) (演出)
notes: 演出: the perform-演 of M48's 연기 ("演技 perform-skill") + the out-出 of M96's 출연 — bringing the performance out: directing, staging. The act, not the person: 연출을 맡다 (M37's 맡다, in its take-on job) = to take on the directing, 무대 연출 (M51's 무대) = stage direction, and in the credits 연출: followed by a name. Sort against M96's 감독: 감독 is the PERSON, the film director, and the football manager; 연출 is what the person does — and in television and theatre the person is called 연출자 (the person-者 of M50's 운전자) or, on set, 피디 (PD, riding frozen). The verb 연출하다 rides frozen — and it has grown a second job: 연출된 사진 = a staged photo, where the performing was faked.

古典: 古 old — a FIRST — + 典 a canon, a standard text — a FIRST: the old canon. A classic: 고전 음악 (M2's 음악) = classical music, 고전 문학 (M44's 문학) = classical literature, 고전을 읽다 (M2's 읽다). Through the -적 factory of M45: 고전적 = classical, classic in style. Sort against the old-words you own: M24's 옛날 is the old DAYS, M46's 옛 is old in front of a noun (that note: "새 breaks things in; 옛 breaks your heart"), and 고전 is old and still READ — the age plus the canon. RADAR: the 고 is 古, old — not the high-高 of M81's 고속 — and the 전 is 典, not the before-前 of M13's 전에 or the electric-電 of M36's 전기; both characters are firsts, so learn the pair as one word.

醫學: the doctor-醫 — M86's 의존하다 note pointed at it while ruling it out ("the 의 is 依, not the doctor-醫 of M4's 의사") — + the study-學 of M44's 입학 ("入學 enter-study") and M15's 수학. Medicine, as a science: 의학 드라마 (M17's 드라마) = the medical drama, 의학을 공부하다 (M1's 공부하다), 한의학 (한 — Korean, riding frozen as the prefix of 한식 and 한복) = traditional Korean medicine, with its own 한의사. So M4's 의사 is 醫師 — the doctor is a teacher-師 of this 醫, which settles the 사 that M78's 운전기사 note left on the 師 side. Sort: M6's 병원 is where medicine is practised; 의학 is what is studied to practise it.

創造: 創 to create, to begin — a FIRST — + the make-造 of M91's 구조 ("構造 construct-make"): to begin and make. Creation, from nothing: 천지창조 (천지 — heaven and earth, riding frozen) = the Creation, the first chapter; 창조적 (through the -적 factory of M45) = creative; 창조 경제 (M32's 경제) was a government slogan of the 2010s. Sort against M3's 만들다: 만들다 makes from materials; 창조 makes what was not there — which is why M69's 신 gets 창조 and a carpenter gets 만들다. RADAR: not the window-窓 of M6's 창문 — a different 창, and M65's 창고 is a third.

en: a technique (in art, in writing) (技法)
notes: 技法: the craft-技 of M44's 기술 ("技術 craft-skill") + the law-法 of M32's 방법 ("方法 direction-law"): the law of a craft — a technique. 표현 기법 (M33's 표현) = a technique of expression, the literature teacher's phrase; 촬영 기법 (촬영 riding frozen) = a filming technique; 새로운 기법 (M35's 새롭다). Sort the three: M44's 기술 is skill and technology, undivided; M32's 방법 is any way of doing; 기법 is a NAMED way inside an art — the thing a critic can point at. RADAR: this 기 is 技 — the row M99's 기 note said NIKL never gives bare ("M44's 기술 (技) and M72's 기계 (機) are the two rows NIKL does not give the bare syllable") — not the energy-氣 of M99's 기 and M7's 기분, and not the record-記 of M96's 기록.

字板: the character-字 of M76's 숫자 ("數字 number-character") and M20's 문자 + 板, the board — the 판 of M15's 칠판 and M23's 간판, read as a character at last: a board of characters — the keyboard. 자판을 치다 (M17's 치다, the hit-verb) = to type, 한글 자판 = the Korean keyboard layout, 자판 배열 (배열 — arrangement, riding frozen). RADAR, and it PAYS M72's 자동, which built the trap in passing — "자동 판매기 → clipped to 자판기 (the vending machine, riding frozen)": M80's 자판기 is 自販機, self-sell-machine, a different word that clips to the same three letters — 자판 is the keyboard, 자판기 the coffee machine, and the 기 is the only visible difference. The shop's word is 키보드 (riding frozen); 자판 is the word the typing-class and the settings menu use.

腦: the brain — a FIRST, and a rare one-syllable Sino word standing alone. 뇌과학 (M15's 과학) = neuroscience, the pop-science shelf; 뇌를 쓰다 (M10's 쓰다) = to use your brain; 뇌 손상 (손상 — damage, riding frozen). Sort against M8's 머리, which that note said is "Head and the hair on it": 머리가 좋아요 is the mouth's smart, and the brain inside the head is 뇌 only when a doctor or a scientist is talking. RADAR: 뇌 shares nothing with M39's 노력 or M97's 노동 — the vowel is ㅚ, and the word is its own.

筋肉: 筋 sinew — a FIRST — + the flesh-肉 of M92's 육체 ("肉體 flesh-body"): sinew and flesh. Muscle: 근육이 생기다 (M28's 생기다, the sprouting verb) = to build muscle, the gym's report; 근육통 (with the pain-痛 of M53's 두통, "頭痛 head-pain", and of M99's 통증) = muscle ache, the day after; 근육 운동 (운동 — the noun inside M8's 운동하다) = strength training. RADAR: the 근 is 筋, not the duty-勤 of M43's 출근 and not the near-近 of M32's 최근 — a third 근, and this one is in your arm.

人格: the person-人 of M32's 인간 + the frame-格 of M44's 합격 ("合格 fit-the-frame") and M19's 성격 — the frame of a person. It PAYS M91's 형성, which carried it frozen in its first phrase: "인격 형성 (인격 — character, personhood, riding frozen) = character formation" — and today the word lands: 인격을 존중하다 (존중 — respect, riding frozen) = to respect someone's dignity, 인격 모독 (모독 — insult, riding frozen) = an attack on one's dignity, the courtroom's phrase, 인격이 훌륭하다 (훌륭하다 — riding frozen). Sort the two 格 words: M19's 성격 is personality — how you come across; 인격 is character as WORTH, what you owe respect to. A bad 성격 is annoying; a bad 인격 is a moral verdict.

本性: the origin-本 of M57's 기본 ("base-基 + 일본's (M27) origin-本") + the nature-性 of M32's 여성 and M45's 성질 — the root nature. What you are underneath: 본성을 드러내다 = to reveal one's true nature — the transitive twin M93's 드러나다 note left waiting ("Its transitive twin 드러내다 (to reveal, lay bare) rides frozen") gets its noun today; 인간의 본성 (M32's 인간) = human nature, the philosopher's; 본성은 변하지 않는다 (M26's 변하다) = nature does not change, the proverb's verdict. Sort the ladder: M19's 성격 is how you act, M45's 성질 is the raw material and the fuse, 본성 is what you ARE — the one you cannot train away.

NIKL's hint is 살짝 닿다 — a light touch: kin of M61's 닿다 (contact made), but 스치다 is contact that does not stay — a shoulder in a corridor, a breeze on a cheek, a thought crossing the mind (생각이 스치다, on the 생각 of M10's 생각하다). Two gap decks already ran it frozen and both thaw today: the M43 gap 월급이 통장을 스쳐 간다 called it "to graze, brush past — the verb K-dramas use for near-touch moments, worth keeping", and the M88 proverb 옷깃만 스쳐도 인연 let it ride as "스치다 (to brush past — riding frozen)". 스쳐 지나가다 (M38's 지나가다) = to brush past and be gone — the drama's first-meeting verb, and the office worker's payday.

NIKL's hint is 물건을 ~ (M9's 물건): the verb of M36's 도둑 — that note: "The thief — who ENTERS" — and 훔치다 is what the thief does once inside: 지갑을 훔치다 (M21's 지갑), 마음을 훔치다 (M19's 마음) = to steal a heart, the drama poster's line. An older sense shares the spelling: 땀을 훔치다 (M41's 땀) = to wipe away sweat — frozen as one clause, the farmer's gesture with the back of the hand. RADAR: not M17's 치다 with a 훔 in front — 치다 strikes and plays; 훔치다 is one native verb, and it takes.

허리를 굽히다 (M14's 허리) = to bend at the waist — the deep bow and the weeding posture; 무릎을 굽히다 (M14's 무릎) = to bend the knee; 뜻을 굽히다 (M10's 뜻) = to bend one's will = to back down — 뜻을 굽히지 않았어요 (-지 않다 from M28) is the biography's stubborn sentence. RADAR, a homograph trap: M18's 굽다 is the grill — 삼겹살을 구워요 — but a second 굽다, riding frozen, means to be bent (허리가 굽다 = a bent back), and 굽히다 is THAT one through the causative party of M37: you make it bend. The grill's 굽다 has no 히 form; if you read 굽히다, nobody is cooking.

못을 박다 = to hammer in a nail — and 못, the nail, is a homograph of M3's 못 (can't), riding frozen: 못을 못 박아요 is a legal sentence. 벽에 박다 (M13's 벽) = to drive it into the wall; 머리를 박다 (M8's 머리) = to bang one's head — on a low door, or on a desk in despair. The do-verb of a pair; its happen-form is next, through the passive party of M36. Says 박따.

en: to be driven in; to be stuck fast
notes: 박다 through the passive party of M36 — 히, like 잡히다: the nail is IN. PAYS two notes at once: M91's 틀 filed the gap deck's 틀에 박히다 with the verb "to be driven in, stuck, riding frozen", and that gap read it as "the passive of 박다, to hammer in" — today it lands. 가시가 손에 박혔어요 (가시 — a thorn, frozen; M8's 손) = a thorn is stuck in my hand; 머리에 박히다 = to be lodged in the mind — 귀에 박히도록 들었어요 (M14's 귀) = heard it until it was nailed into my ears. 틀에 박힌 생활 (M29's 생활) = a life in a rut, the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 doing the M91 work.

en: to put a hand or finger on; to lean on
notes: PAYS the M84 gap 번지수가 틀리다, which ran "짚다 — to put a finger on, riding frozen": the hand set down, for support or for pointing. 손을 짚다 (M8's 손) = to put a hand down to steady yourself; 지팡이를 짚다 (지팡이 — a walking stick, frozen) = to lean on a cane; 이마를 짚다 (M41's 이마) = to feel a forehead for fever; 짚어 보다 (the try-machine from M16) = to point one out — 문제를 짚어 봅시다 (M7's 문제). RADAR: M66's 집다 picks a thing UP between the fingers; 짚다 sets the hand DOWN — same sound 집따 and 짚따, opposite direction.

NIKL's hint is 드리다: M9's 드리다 gives upward to a person; 바치다 gives upward to something larger — a god, a country, a cause. 목숨을 바치다 (M92's 목숨) = to give one's life; 평생을 바치다 (M46's 평생) = to devote a lifetime; 이 책을 부모님께 바칩니다 (M1's 책, M4's 부모님, 께 from M27) = the dedication page's verb, in the -ㅂ니다 register. RADAR: M87's 바 + M17's 치다 is a false weld — there is no 'thing which' and no striking in 바치다; it is one native verb, and it kneels.

The thesis verb: M9's 주다 + M9's 받다, welded through verb--고 from M10 into ONE word — give-and-receive = to exchange. 선물을 주고받다 (M9's 선물) = to exchange gifts; 말을 주고받다 (M4's 말) = to exchange words; 문자를 주고받다 (M20's 문자) = to text back and forth; 눈빛을 주고받다 (M41's 눈빛) = to exchange glances. Written closed and said in one breath: the welding IS the meaning — two verbs you have owned since M9, one action they make together.

M28's 바로 + M28's 잡다: to grab a thing back to straight = to correct. 잘못을 바로잡다 (M63's 잘못) = to right a wrong; 자세를 바로잡다 (M98's 자세) = to fix one's posture; 오류를 바로잡다 (오류 — an error, frozen) = to correct an error — the newspaper's corrections column. Sort against M13's 고치다: 고치다 repairs what broke; 바로잡다 straightens what leaned.

en: to be spread out, to carpet; to be run over
notes: 깔다 — the spread-on-the-floor verb M83's 신문지 note ran frozen: "깔다 — to spread on the floor, riding frozen" — through the passive party of M36: what was spread is now lying there. 길에 낙엽이 깔렸어요 (M12's 길, M49's 낙엽) = fallen leaves carpet the road; 안개가 깔리다 (M49's 안개) = fog lies low; and the dark row: 차에 깔리다 = to be run over, pinned under — the 차 clipped from M50's 자동차, not M2's 차 the tea. 깔다 itself stays frozen: the floor needs the mat, but the newspaper needs the happen-form.

en: to be submerged; to be locked
notes: NIKL's hint is 물에 ~ (M1's 물): two verbs share the spelling, and both are passives. One is 잠그다 (to lock — frozen) through the passive party of M36: 문이 잠겼어요 (M6's 문) = the door is locked. The other is sink-잠기다: 물에 잠기다 = to be submerged — 마을이 물에 잠겼어요 (M22's 마을) is the flood headline — and from it 생각에 잠기다 (the 생각 of M10's 생각하다) = to be lost in thought, 슬픔에 잠기다 (M42's 슬픔) = sunk in grief. RADAR: M28's 잠 (sleep) is not inside it — a locked door and a sunk village are both wide awake.

en: to open up, clear (a road, the chest, the tongue)
notes: The passive shape of 트다 (to open, to break through — frozen): what was blocked comes open. 길이 트이다 (M12's 길) = a road opens up; 속이 트이다 (M28's 속) = the insides open = to feel relieved, unburdened; 말문이 트이다 (말문 — the gate of speech, frozen) = to find one's tongue, the gap deck's phrase — and the language learner's own sentence: 한국어가 트였어요 (M1's 한국어) = my Korean has opened up, the day the words stop jamming. 트여요, 트였어요 — the 이 folds into the vowel.

M4's 살다 + M35's 남다 welded on -아: to live and be left = to survive — the one still living when the count is taken. 사고에서 살아남다 (M36's 사고) = to survive the accident; 살아남은 사람 (M1's 사람, the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24) = a survivor; 경쟁에서 살아남다 (M95's 경쟁) = to survive the competition — the business page borrows the battlefield. M88's 살아오다 lived up to now; 살아남다 lived when others did not.

M41's 숨 (that note: "숨을 쉬다 = to breathe") + M17's 지다 the lose-verb (that note: "Losing and sunsets share a verb") — the breath is lost = to die. The newsroom's euphemism: where the mouth says M14's 죽다, the caption says 숨지다 — 현장에서 숨졌어요 (M98's 현장) = died at the scene; 병원으로 옮기던 중 숨졌어요 (M6's 병원, M50's 옮기다, -던 from M88) = died while being moved to hospital. M92's 목숨 said "life is the breath in the throat"; 숨지다 is that breath leaving. Sort: 죽다 is any death; 숨지다 is a person's, reported.

en: to collapse into a sitting position, slump down
notes: M9's 앉다 with 주저- (to slump, frozen — the give-way prefix): to sit down NOT on purpose — the knees fold. 바닥에 주저앉다 (M13's 바닥) = to sink to the floor; 그 자리에 주저앉았어요 (M29's 그, M12's 자리) = collapsed on the spot, the bad-news sentence; 울면서 주저앉았어요 (-(으)면서 from M38, M7's 울다). RADAR: not M1's 저 or M8's 주 — 주저 is one native chunk. Says 주저안따, the ㅈ buried exactly as in 앉다.

en: to follow one after another, come in succession
notes: M88's 잇다 ("To join end to end — a rope, a road, a lineage") + M32's 따르다 (follow): joined-and-following = one after another. The news's verb for a run of events: 사고가 잇따르다 (M36's 사고) = accidents come one after another; 비판이 잇따랐어요 (M93's 비판) = criticism followed criticism; and the -아 form as an adverb, 잇따라 = in succession — 잇따라 발생했어요 (M56's 발생하다). The 르-family table of M7: 잇따라요, 잇따랐어요. Says 읻따르다 — the ㅅ of 잇 closes like M1's 있다.

en: to follow behind; to come with (a consequence)
notes: M6's 뒤 + M32's 따르다: to follow from behind. Bodies first — 뒤따라 가다 (M1's 가다) = to follow along behind, 뒤따라 오세요 (M1's 오다) = come along behind me; then consequences: 책임이 뒤따르다 (M39's 책임 — that note: "책임을 지다 = to bear responsibility") = responsibility follows — 권리에는 책임이 뒤따라요 (M90's 권리) is the civics lesson; 위험이 뒤따르다 (the 위험 of M12's 위험하다) = risk comes with it. Sort: 잇따르다 is many things in a row; 뒤따르다 is one thing walking behind another.

M28's 내다 ("The put-it-out verb") + M1's 보다: to put the gaze out = to look out. 창밖을 내다보다 (M65's 창밖) = to look out the window — the train's and the sickbed's verb; 미래를 내다보다 (M25's 미래) = to see into the future = to foresee; 앞을 내다보는 사람 (M6's 앞, M1's 사람, the badge -는 from M24) = a person with foresight. Sort the gaze ships: M68's 들여다보다 peers IN, M49's 바라보다 gazes AT, 내다보다 looks OUT — from inside a room or inside the present.

M19's 부르다 (불러-, the 르-family table of M7) + M56's 일으키다 (that note: "문제를 일으키다 = cause trouble"): to call up and raise = to stir up. 관심을 불러일으키다 (M24's 관심) = to arouse interest; 논쟁을 불러일으키다 (논쟁 — a controversy, frozen) = to spark controversy — the review's verb; 감정을 불러일으키다 (M42's 감정) = to stir feelings. Five syllables, every one already yours; the longest weld on the shelf and the most printed.

en: to stand out, be conspicuous, be marked
notes: To stick out from the surface — an adjective on the -지다 wing from M35. 두드러진 특징 (M45's 특징, in the badge) = a marked feature; 두드러지게 (-게 from M33) = markedly — 두드러지게 늘었어요 (M35's 늘다) = rose markedly, the chart's adverb. Three stand-outs, sorted: M89's 뛰어나다 ("leaps out = stands out") is praise; M94's 띄다 ("a thing lifted INTO the eye") is noticing; 두드러지다 is prominence, praised or not — a flaw can 두드러지다. RADAR: M66's 두드리다 knocks on a door; the two share two syllables of sound and nothing else.

What OUGHT to be: 마땅한 이유 (M24's 이유, in the badge) = a proper reason — 마땅한 이유 없이 (M32's 없이) = without due cause, the ruling's phrase; 칭찬을 받아 마땅해요 (M33's 칭찬) = deserves the praise; 마땅히 (frozen) = rightly, duly. In the mouth it is mostly negative-first: 마땅한 말이 없어요 (M4's 말) = there is no right word for it. Sort: M73's 적당하다 (suitable, moderate) and M87's 적절하다 (apt) fit the situation; 마땅하다 fits what is OWED. RADAR: M22's 땅 is a coincidence — nothing is on the ground.

擇 — the pick-擇 of M33's 선택하다 ("選擇 select-pick"), standing alone with 하다: to choose, formally. 길을 택하다 (M12's 길) = to choose a path — 다른 길을 택했어요 (M29's 다른) = took a different road; 방법을 택하다 (M32's 방법) = to opt for a method. Three pickers: M34's 고르다 (that note: "The native pick") is the shop; 선택하다 is the form; 택하다 is the essay — one character, one syllable, the whole decision.

斟酌 — pour and measure: two FIRSTS, the pouring-斟 and the measuring-酌 of wine, together = weighing a thing up by eye = to guess, to surmise. 짐작이 가다 (M1's 가다) = one can guess — 짐작이 가요 = I can imagine; 대충 짐작했어요 (today's 대충) = I roughly guessed; 짐작조차 못 했어요 (조차 from M89) = couldn't even guess. Sort: 것 같다 from M34 is a guess shown; 짐작하다 is the guess named. RADAR: not M13's 짐 (luggage) — nobody is carrying anything.

除去 — the 除 of M93's 제외하다 ("除外 remove-outside") + the 去 of M35's 과거 ("過去 passed-gone"): remove-and-send-away = to eliminate. 냄새를 제거하다 (M41's 냄새) = to remove the odour, the detergent's verb; 위험을 제거하다 (the 위험 of M12's 위험하다) = to remove the risk, the report's. The native is M74's 없애다 ("make-not-exist = get rid of") — same act, the mouth's; 제거하다 is the label's and the manual's.

寄與 — 寄 to send, to entrust (a FIRST) + the 與 of M86's 여건 ("與 to give, to grant (a FIRST)"): sent-and-given = to contribute. 사회에 기여하다 (M32's 사회) = to contribute to society, the scholarship essay's closing verb; 발전에 기여하다 (M57's 발전) = to contribute to development; 크게 기여했어요 = contributed greatly. Sort against M28's 돕다: 돕다 helps a person, hands on; 기여하다 adds to a whole — and gets a plaque.

en: to be applied, to apply (a rule)
notes: 適用 — M64's 적용하다 ("適 (fit) + 用 (use)") through the 되다-flip M70's 마련되다 described: "되다 doesn't check pedigree, only the 하다 it replaces". 법이 적용되다 (M39's 법) = the law applies; 모든 학생에게 적용돼요 (M29's 모든, M4's 학생) = applies to all students; 새 규정이 적용됩니다 (M13's 새, M90's 규정) = the new rule takes effect, in the notice's -ㅂ니다. The 하다 side is the official applying it; the 되다 side is the notice on the wall.

展開 — PAYS M91's 전개, which filed "전개하다/전개되다 ride frozen; the noun is the one you will read": today the 되다 side lands, because it is the one the review writes. 이야기가 전개되다 (M24's 이야기) = the story unfolds; 사건이 빠르게 전개됐어요 (M36's 사건, -게 from M33) = events moved fast; 생각과 다르게 전개되다 (the 생각 of M10's 생각하다) = to develop otherwise than expected. 전개하다 stays frozen — a plot unrolls; nobody unrolls it.

否定 — the 否 of M33's 안부 ("安否 peace-or-not") + the 定 of M33's 결정하다: to fix a not = to deny. The verb of M98's 부정 in its 否定 row — that note already said "부정하다 = to deny" — and NOT its 不正 row: 부정하다 never means to commit fraud. 사실을 부정하다 (M24's 사실) = to deny the facts; 혐의를 부정하다 (혐의 — the allegation, frozen) = to deny the charge, the courthouse steps. RADAR: M33's 정하다 sets a thing; 부정하다 un-sets it — and M45's 긍정적 is its mirror, with 긍정하다 (frozen) = to affirm.

en: to instruct, direct, order (from a desk)
notes: 指示 — the 指 of M93's 지적하다 ("指 (the finger, and its pointing — a FIRST)") + the 示 of M75's 표시하다 ("示 (show — frozen)"): the verb of M98's 지시, which filed it "지시하다 rides frozen" and drew the line already: "지시하다 orders people, from a desk". 부장이 지시했어요 (M58's 부장) = the department head gave the order; 지시한 대로 (대로 from M54) = as instructed. Sort: M3's 시키다 orders food; 지시하다 orders staff; M64's 명령 barks.

公開 — PAYS M95's 공개, which ran "공개하다 rides frozen": 사진을 공개하다 (M17's 사진) = to release the photos; 결과를 공개하다 (M32's 결과) = to publish the results; 정보를 공개하다 (M33's 정보) = to disclose information. 공개되다 rides free on the flip: 명단이 공개됐어요 (명단 — the list, frozen) = the list was made public. The verb of the press release — and of the apology that becomes one.

分布 — the 分 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion") + 布 to spread, cloth laid out (a FIRST): spread in portions = to be distributed across space. 전국에 분포하다 (M31's 전국) = to be found nationwide — the geography textbook's verb; 남부에 주로 분포해요 (M98's 남부, M38's 주로) = mainly distributed in the south; 인구 분포 (M64's 인구) = population distribution, the noun riding free. Note the grammar: 하다 in form, a state in meaning — 분포하다 and 분포되어 있다 draw the same map.

The inside corner — where the dust and the shy child go. 방 구석 (M8's 방) = the corner of the room; 구석에 앉다 (M9's 앉다) = to sit in the corner; 마음 한구석 (M19's 마음) = a corner of the heart, where the small worry lives; 구석구석 = every nook and cranny — the gap deck files it, the cleaner's and the tourist's word alike. RADAR: not M2's 구 (nine) and no 석 of any kind — native, one piece.

The wet field. M59's 밭 filed it: "Its wet partner 논 (the rice paddy — riding frozen)" — the frozen partner lands. 논밭 = fields, farmland, the pair as one word; 논에 물을 대다 (M1's 물, M94's 대다) = to flood the paddy; 논농사 (M59's 농사) = rice farming. RADAR: M44's 논문 noted "The 논 is argument-論" — that 논 is Sino and argues; this one is native and grows M59's 쌀.

en: a flock, a swarm, a crowd
notes: NIKL's hint is 양 ~: 양 떼 = a flock of sheep — the sheep-양 that M63's 양 note flagged ("the NIKL C-list adds sheep-羊"), still frozen; M63's 양 itself is the amount. 새 떼 (M22's 새) = a flock of birds; 떼를 지어 (M54's 짓다) = in a flock, in a gang — 떼를 지어 다니다 (M16's 다니다) = to roam in packs, said of teenagers and pigeons alike. RADAR: M61's 떼다 detaches, and the 라떼 of S1's 꼰대 note ("punned as '라떼는'") is a coffee — neither is a herd.

M15's 가르치다 through the -(으)ㅁ freezer of M67 — a vowel stem, so bare ㅁ: the act of teaching, frozen into a thing you can keep. 스승의 가르침 (M96's 스승) = a master's teaching; 부모님의 가르침 (M4's 부모님) = what your parents taught you; 가르침을 따르다 (M32's 따르다) = to follow a teaching. Its mirror, 배움 (frozen — M2's 배우다 through the same freezer), is the learner's side: 배움에는 끝이 없어요 (M28's 끝) = there is no end to learning.

en: upside down, backwards, the wrong way round
notes: Native adverb (pos noun by house rule): the wrong way round on any axis. 거꾸로 입었어요 (M8's 입다) = wore it inside out, or back to front; 거꾸로 가다 (M1's 가다) = to go backwards — 시계가 거꾸로 가요 (M5's 시계) = the clock runs backwards; 거꾸로 읽다 (M2's 읽다) = to read backwards; 거꾸로 서다 (M14's 서다) = to stand on one's head. RADAR: the 로 of M6 is a fossil inside it — 거꾸 + 로 — but the word is one piece now; never add another 로.

The mouth's approximation (adverb, pos noun by house rule): 대충 알아요 (M4's 알다) = I roughly know; 대충 했어요 = I did it roughly — a half job; 대충 얼마예요? (M9's 얼마) = roughly how much? Doubled, 대충대충 = slapdash — the gap deck files the boss's complaint. Twin of M85's 대체로, whose note said "대체로 is the survey's": 대체로 is the page's on-the-whole; 대충 is the mouth's more-or-less. RADAR: not M55's 대 — no counter, no versus; native, and lazy by design.

en: the front, the face (of a thing); head-on (正面)
notes: 正面 correct-face: the 正 of M44's 정답 ("正答 correct-answer") + the 面 of M43's 면접 ("面接 face-contact") — the side a thing is meant to be seen from. 건물 정면 (M22's 건물) = the front of the building; 정면에서 보면 (M1's 보다 with -(으)면 from M20) = seen from the front; and the adverb the news uses, 정면으로 = head-on — 문제를 정면으로 다루다 (M7's 문제, M93's 다루다) = to face the problem squarely, 정면 충돌 (충돌 — a collision, riding frozen; its 衝 is the collide-衝 of M42's 충격, "衝擊 collide-strike") = a head-on crash. Sort against M6's 앞: 앞 is where you stand; 정면 is which face the thing shows you. RADAR: the 정 here is correctness-正, the fourth 정 M44's 정답 note counted — not the jeong-情 of M26 and not the 精 of 정성 below.

en: the middle phase, the midpoint (中盤)
notes: 中盤 middle-board: S2's 중 ("중국's middle-中") + the board-盤 of M46's 초반 ("初盤 opening-board") — and that note already set the table: "the Go board, where games phase 초반/중반/후반 as the stones fill". Today the middle stone lands. 삼십 대 중반 (the 代 age bracket M55's 대 note reached — "30대 = the thirties") = mid-thirties; 경기 중반 (M17's 경기) = midway through the match; 영화 중반에 (M2's 영화) = halfway into the film. RADAR: M46's 후반 warned that its 반 is the half-半 of M5, "where 초반's 반 was the board-盤" — 중반 sits on the board, not on the half, and 반 alone (M5) is still thirty minutes.

直前 straight-before: the 直 of M56's 직접 ("直接 straight-touch") + the 前 M31's 전국 note counted as "전에's before-전 (前)" — the moment before, no gap. It pays the mirror M88's 직후 note hung on the wall: "Its mirror 직전 (right before — riding frozen) does the same job on M13's 전에 side: 시험 직전 = just before the exam." Rides a noun, or a past badge -(으)ㄴ from M24, and then takes 에: 출발 직전에 (M52's 출발) = just before departure; 시험 직전에 = right before the exam; 잠들기 직전 (M74's 잠들다 through the -기 nominalizer from M13) = the moment before sleep. Sort: M13's 전에 is any time before; 직전 is the seconds before — the pair the newsroom uses for the clock around an event, and now you hold both ends.

最終 most-end: the 最 of M32's 최근 ("最近 most-near") + the 終 of M38's 종일 ("終日 end-of-day") — the most-final, the last of the line. A determiner in practice: 최종 결정 (M57's 결정) = the final decision, 최종 합격 (M44's 합격) = passing the last round — the phone call after the third interview, 최종 목표 (M26's 목표) = the ultimate goal. Through the -적 factory of M45 and 으로: 최종적으로 = finally, in the end — the report's 결국 (M32). Sort against M15's 마지막: 마지막 is the last one in the mouth (마지막 버스); 최종 is the last one on the form. RADAR: the 종 is end-終, not the bell-鐘 of M31's 종로 — the same sort M38's 종일 note made.

大陸 big-land: the big-大 M50's 대도시 called "the big-大 fronting 대학교 (M15) and 대중 (M48)" + 陸, land as against sea — a FIRST. 아시아 대륙 (M31's 아시아) = the Asian continent, 유럽 대륙 (M31's 유럽); 대륙 횡단 (횡단 — a crossing, riding frozen) = a transcontinental journey. The map's sort: M22's 섬 is land the sea surrounds; 대륙 is land the sea cannot. Korea calls its own peninsula 반도 (半島 — half-island, riding frozen), the piece that hangs off the 대륙, and the phrase 대륙의 기질 (기질 — temperament, frozen) is what Koreans say about Chinese scale. Said 대륙 with the ㄹ sounded, not the ㄴ of M64's 등록.

en: the central region, the middle part (中部)
notes: 中部 middle-section: S2's 중 + the 部 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion") — the middle section of a country, a continent, a body. It pays the M98 남부 note, which set the compass on 部 and left this one waiting: "the rail runs 북부, 동부, 서부 (frozen — the north, east and west parts) and 중부 (frozen) for the middle". 중부 지방 (M50's 지방) = the central provinces — the forecaster's phrase, said before 남부 지방 every evening; 중부 유럽 (M31's 유럽) = Central Europe; 중부 고속도로 (M50's 고속도로) is the motorway that runs down the country's spine. RADAR: M84's 공중 is 空中 with the 중 in second seat; here the 중 leads and means the middle of a map, not the middle of the air.

en: both countries, the two nations (兩國)
notes: 兩國 both-countries: the both-兩 M63's 양 note filed as a radar row — "the NIKL C-list adds sheep-羊 and both-兩" — + the 國 of M32's 국민 ("國民 country-people"). The diplomatic page's word: 양국 관계 (M32's 관계) = relations between the two countries, 양국 정부 (M32's 정부) = the two governments, 양국 간의 협력 (M55's 간, 협력 — cooperation, riding frozen) = cooperation between the two. It never names them — the article has already said 한국과 일본, and 양국 is how it declines to say it twice. RADAR, the 양 file: M63's 양 is measure-量, the 양 of M21's 양말 and M40's 양파 is Western-洋, and today's is 兩, the pair — the 양 of 양쪽 (M65) and 양면, which is why 양국 means exactly two and never several.

同胞 same-womb: the same-同 of M38's 동시 + the 胞 of M52's 교포 ("僑胞 sojourner-sibling: 僑 (living abroad) + 胞 (from the same womb)") — people born of the same mother, which is how Korean names a nation. 해외 동포 (M31's 해외) = Koreans overseas, 재외동포 (frozen — the official form of the same), 북한 동포 (M31's 북한) = our compatriots in the North — the phrase every presidential address uses for the people across the line. Sort against M52's 교포: 교포 is the Korean who LIVES abroad (재미교포); 동포 is any fellow Korean seen as family, wherever they are — a 교포 is always a 동포, but the 동포 in 평양 is no 교포. The warmest word Korean politics owns, and the one it reaches for when the border is the subject.

en: an entrance, an appearance (on the scene) (登場)
notes: 登場 climb-stage — M97's 등장하다 dismounted, exactly as that note said it would: "The noun 등장 rides free: 스마트폰의 등장 (M20's 스마트폰) = the arrival of the smartphone." The 登 of M64's 등록 and the 場 of M37's 주차장 stand as a noun now, and the noun keeps the stage: 새 인물의 등장 (M48's 인물) = the arrival of a new figure — and M48's 인물 note already held the compound, "등장인물 = the characters", the people who make an entrance. 첫 등장 (M46's 첫) = a debut appearance; 등장과 함께 (M29's 함께) = with the arrival of; 등장 장면 (장면 — a scene, riding frozen) = the entrance scene. Sort, as M97 did: M32's 나타나다 shows up, 등장 makes an entrance — a product 등장, a rumour merely 나타나요.

en: the substance, the true nature, the real entity (實體)
notes: 實體 real-body: the real-實 of M34's 확실하다 ("確實 firm-real") + the body-體 of M41's 체중 ("體重 body-heavy") — what a thing actually is, under its name. 실체가 없다 (M1's 없다) = has no substance — the verdict on a rumour, a company, a promise; 실체를 드러내다 = to reveal its true nature, with the transitive twin M93's 드러나다 note left frozen ("Its transitive twin 드러내다 (to reveal, lay bare) rides frozen"); 실체를 파악하다 (M93's 파악하다) = to get at what it really is. The essay's sort: M24's 사실 is a fact you can state; 실체 is the thing behind the facts — the investigation looks for the 실체, and reports 사실. RADAR: not M72's 실제 (實際 — real-between, the actual case): 실제로 is an adverb about how things went; 실체 is a noun about what a thing is.

en: application (of a rule, a method) (適用)
notes: 適用 fit-use — M64's 적용하다 dismounted, that note's decode intact: "適 (fit) + 用 (use): making a rule fit the case and putting it to work." The noun is the rule-book's own word: 적용 범위 (M89's 범위) = the scope of application — which cases the rule reaches; 적용 대상 (대상 — the target, riding frozen) = who it applies to; 새 규정의 적용 (M90's 규정) = the application of the new regulation; and the 되다-side, 적용되다 (riding frozen on the flip M70's 마련되다 note described) = to apply, to be in force — 내년부터 적용됩니다 (M25's 내년) is how every price change is announced. The 適 is the one M73's 적당하다 and M87's 적절하다 both decoded as fit; the 用 is the use-用 of M56's 이용하다. RADAR: not M45's 적, the -적 suffix — 적용 is a word, -적 is a tail.

比率 compare-rate: the compare-比 of M86's 비하다 + 率, the rate — the character M97's 성장 note left on the shelf, "성장률 (the rate — 率 riding frozen)", and today it lands as a word of its own. 비율이 높다/낮다 (M7's 높다, M7's 낮다) = the ratio is high/low; 남녀 비율 (남녀 — M4's 남자 and 여자 clipped into one, riding frozen) = the gender ratio; 일정한 비율로 (M89's 일정하다) = in a fixed proportion. Sort against M30's 퍼센트: 퍼센트 is the UNIT the number wears; 비율 is the THING measured — 비율이 삼십 퍼센트예요 uses both, and the second is the answer to the first. RADAR: 율 after a vowel or ㄴ, 률 elsewhere — 비율 but 성장률, 합격률 (M44's 합격) — the same ㄴ/ㄹ seesaw as 백분율.

變動 change-move: the 變 of M32's 변화 ("變化 change-becoming") + the 動 of M42's 감동 ("感動 feel-move") — change that moves a number. 가격 변동 (M21's 가격) = price fluctuation; 환율 변동 (환율 — the exchange rate, riding frozen) = currency swings; 변동이 심하다 (M39's 심하다) = fluctuates wildly; 변동이 없다 = unchanged — the flat line. The sort M32's 변화 makes possible: 변화 is change as a becoming — a person changes, a city changes; 변동 is change on a chart — a price, a rate, a temperature goes up and down and lands somewhere else. 변동 없음 (M1's 없다 nouned, as in the 해당 사항 없음 of today's 해당) is the two-word line on every form that asks whether anything is different since last time.

追加 chase-add: 追, to chase after — a FIRST — + the add-加 of M51's 참가하다 ("參加 join-add"): something added by running after what was already sent. 추가 요금 (M12's 요금) = the surcharge, the word the bill uses when it grows; 추가 주문 (주문 — the order, dismounted from M3's 주문하다) = a further order — 추가요! is what you call across the 삼겹살 (M18) table; 추가로 = additionally, in addition; 추가하다 (riding frozen, 하다 on the noun) = to add — 친구 추가 (M1's 친구) is the button on every messaging app. Sort against M74's 더하다: 더하다 adds salt and does arithmetic ("2 더하기 3 = two plus three"); 추가 adds a line to a list or a bill. RADAR: not the fall-秋 of 추석 (M25) nor the cold-추 of M11's 춥다 — the 追 here is on the move.

支出 pay-out: the 支 of M65's 지점 ("支 (support, branch-off)" — here in its pay-out sense, money branching off) + the 出 of M43's 출근 ("出勤 out-to-duty"), the out-door of M12's 출구 — what goes out. Its column-mate is M43's 수입 in the second of the two senses that note taught ("收入 gather-in: income, what your work collects"): 수입과 지출 = income and expenditure, the two columns of every household book (가계부 — riding frozen). 지출을 줄이다 (M37's 줄이다) = to cut spending — the January sentence; 지출이 늘다 (M35's 늘다) = spending is up; 추가 지출 (today's 추가) = extra outlay. The mouth says 돈을 쓰다 (M9's 돈, M10's 쓰다); the ledger says 지출 — and the ledger is where you find out what the mouth did.

en: securing, obtaining (a supply, a place) (確保)
notes: 確保 firm-guard: the firm-確 of M34's 확실하다 + the guard-保 of M43's 보험 ("保險 guard-the-cliff-edge") — to make a thing firmly yours before anyone else can. 자리를 확보하다 (M12's 자리; 확보하다 rides frozen, 하다 on the noun) = to secure a seat — the library at exam week, the beach at seven; 예산 확보 (M97's 예산) = securing the budget, the sentence every department chases; 인력 확보 (인력 — manpower, riding frozen) = securing staff; 증거를 확보하다 (증거 — evidence, riding frozen) = to obtain the evidence, the detective's verb. Sort against M43's 구하다 in its first job (to look for, to get): 구하다 goes looking; 확보 has already got it and is holding on. RADAR: the 보 is 保, not the see-보 of M1's 보다 — 확보 is not a certain look, it is a firm hold.

制約 control-bind: the control-制 of M64's 제한 ("制 (control) + 限 (limit)") + the bind-約 of M43's 계약 ("契約 bind-promise") — a limit that ties you. 제약이 많다 (M7's 많다) = there are many constraints; 시간의 제약 (M1's 시간) = time constraints; 제약을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be constrained; 제약이 따르다 (M32's 따르다) = constraints come with it — the sentence under every offer. Sort against M64's 제한: 제한 is the ceiling set from outside (속도 제한); 제약 is the rope that ties the hands — a budget 제한s, a family 제약s. RADAR, mandatory: NOT M10's 약 (medicine), and NOT the 제약 of 제약 회사 (製藥 — pharmaceuticals, make-medicine, riding frozen) — the drug company is 製藥, your limits are 制約, and NIKL lists only the constraint (제약01, rank 3088).

en: overdoing it, unreasonableness (無理); a crowd, a group (native)
notes: Two NIKL rows, one spelling. Row one, 無理 rank 2896: the empty-無 of M39's 무조건 ("無 (no) + 조건: zero-conditions") + the 理 of M34's 이해 (理解) — no-reason, pushed past what makes sense. 무리하지 마세요 (-지 마세요 from M14) = don't overdo it — the doctor's, the mother's, the trainer's line, gap deck; 무리한 요구 (M86's 요구) = an unreasonable demand; 무리예요 = that's asking too much; 무리가 가다 (M1's 가다) = to put a strain on (허리에 무리가 가요 — M14's 허리). Row two, rank 3468, native and unrelated: a crowd, a group — 사람들 무리 (M1's 사람) = a crowd of people, 무리를 이루다 (M35's 이루다) = to form a group, 한 무리의 학생들 = a group of students. RADAR: M39's 아무리 ("아무리 바빠도") is 아무 + 리 and shares nothing but the sound — 아무리 무리해도 (with -아/어도 from M39) = however much you overdo it, and both words are in it.

極히 pole-ly: the pole-極 of M45's 적극적 ("積極 piled-to-the-pole: effort stacked as high as it goes") + the adverb-히 M32's 특히 decoded ("the adverb-히 of 천천히/열심히 (M10)") — to the pole, to the utmost. 극히 드물다 (M89's 드물다) = extremely rare; 극히 일부 (M57's 일부) = a tiny minority — 극히 일부의 학생 = a very few students, the phrase every official denial reaches for; 극히 제한적 (M64's 제한 through the -적 factory of M45) = extremely limited. The register ladder: M11's 아주 is the mouth's very, M38's 훨씬 is the comparison's, and 극히 is the report's — it almost never sits on a happy adjective (극히 좋다 is odd; 극히 어렵다 is the sentence). House pos noun, the adverb rule. Said 그키, the ㄱ+ㅎ merge M32's 특히 note filed as "축하's rule from M25".

窮極的 exhaust-pole-ish: 窮, to run out, to reach the end — a FIRST — + the pole-極 of 극히 above + the -적 stamp of M45: the point past which there is nothing. It lives almost entirely as an adverb, 궁극적으로 = ultimately, in the last analysis — the essay's closing move, one rung past 최종적으로; and in the badge, 궁극적인 목표 (M26's 목표) = the ultimate goal, 궁극적인 원인 (M86's 원인) = the root cause. The M45 md's hardware rule holds — -적이다, -적인, -적으로 — and this word barely uses the first. RADAR: not M23's 궁 (palace) — 경복궁 has no 窮 in it; the palace is 宮, the exhaustion is 窮, and only one of them has a gift shop.

不可避 not-can-avoid: the not-不 of M39's 부족하다 ("不足 not-enough-foot") + the can-可 of M39's 가능하다 ("可能 can-able") + the dodge-避 of M36's 피하다 ("避하다: to dodge") — cannot be dodged. The report's regretful adjective: 불가피한 선택 (M64's 선택) = an unavoidable choice, 가격 인상이 불가피하다 (M21's 가격, 인상 — a raise, riding frozen) = a price rise is unavoidable — the sentence every company issues before it raises them; 불가피하게 (the -게 adverbializer from M33) = unavoidably. The prefix reading: 不 is 불 before most consonants and 부 before ㄷ and ㅈ — 불가피, 불가능하다 (M39), but 부족, 부정 — the same rule M39's 부족하다 was quietly obeying. Sort: 어쩔 수 없어요 (riding frozen) is the mouth's no-choice; 불가피하다 is the memo's. Three taught halves, no new character — the shelf's cleanest weld.

自尊心 self-honour-heart: the self-自 of M32's 자기 ("自己 self") + 尊, to honour — a FIRST, the 尊 of 존경 (respect, riding frozen) — + the heart-心 of M34's 의심 ("疑心 doubt-heart"): the heart that honours itself. 자존심이 상하다 = one's pride is wounded — M36's 상하다 in the job that note filed second ("feelings do too: 기분이 상했어요 = my feelings soured"), gap deck; 자존심을 지키다 (M26's 지키다) = to keep one's pride; 자존심이 세다 (M41's 세다) = proud, stiff-necked; 자존심을 버리다 (M13's 버리다) = to swallow one's pride. Sort: M26's 자신 is confidence, the belief you can; 자존심 is the pride that can be hurt — 자신감 goes up and down, 자존심 gets 상하다-ed. The K-drama's engine, and the reason nobody in it says sorry first.

愛情 love-feeling: the love-愛 of M78's 애인 ("愛人 love-person") + the 情 of M26's 정 — affection with a name on it. 애정 표현 (M33's 표현) = a show of affection, the thing Korean couples are said to be bad at in public and good at in text; 애정이 식다 (M40's 식다 — that note: "사랑이 식다 = love cools") = affection cools; 애정을 쏟다 (쏟다 — to pour, riding frozen) = to lavish affection on; 애정 어린 (frozen badge) = affectionate. Sort: M7's 사랑하다 nouned, 사랑, is the whole thing; M26's 정 is the attachment that accumulates; 애정 is the warm regard you can show or withhold — a parent has 애정 for a child and 정 for the neighbour. RADAR, the one M78's 애인 note already ran: NOT M47's 애 (the kid) + 정 — 애정 is not child-jeong; the 애 is a full hanja syllable, 愛.

精誠 essence-sincerity: the essence-精 of M34's 정신 ("精神 essence-spirit") + 誠, sincerity — a FIRST, the whole heart in it. It pays M94's 들이다, which spent it before you had it: "정성을 들이다 (정성 — devoted care, riding frozen) = put one's heart into it". The cook's word: 정성껏 (-껏 — to the full extent of, riding frozen) = with all one's heart — 정성껏 만든 음식 (M3's 만들다, M1's 음식) = food made with love, the phrase on every home-style restaurant's wall; 정성이 담긴 선물 (M61's 담기다, M9's 선물) = a gift with real care in it; 정성이 부족하다 (M39's 부족하다) = it wanted more care. Sort: M39's 노력 is effort measured in hours; 정성 is effort measured in heart — the 제사 table (M99) is set with 정성, never with 노력. RADAR: a FIFTH 정 for the file M34's 정신 note kept — affection 情, politics 政, fixing 定, correctness 正, and this essence-精, the same one as 정신.

刺戟 prick-halberd: 刺, to prick, and 戟, a spear — both FIRSTS — a poke with a point. Three registers: the doctor's — 자극적인 음식 (M1's 음식, through the -적 factory of M45) = strong, spicy, irritating food, the thing every stomach patient (위 — the stomach, riding frozen) is told to give up; the teacher's — 자극을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to be spurred on, 친구에게 자극을 받았어요 = my friend's success lit a fire under me; and the page's — 자극하다 (riding frozen) = to provoke, to stimulate — 경제를 자극하다 (M32's 경제). The mouth's version is M3's 맵다 — the taste; 자극적 is the nurse's word for it, and for the news you should not read before bed. RADAR: not M71's 자 (the attention-gatherer) and not the self-自 of 자존심 above — 刺 is a needle, and 자극 is what the needle does.

抗議 resist-discuss: 抗, to resist, to push back — a FIRST — + the discuss-議 M58's 국회의원 decoded ("discuss-議, the syllable that has sat silently inside 회의 (M10 — 會議, gather-and-discuss)"): a discussion made in resistance. 항의 전화 (M20's 전화) = a complaint call — 항의 전화가 쏟아졌어요 (쏟아지다 — to pour in, riding frozen) is the line after every broadcasting mistake; 항의하다 (riding frozen) = to protest — 심판에게 항의하다 (심판 — the referee, frozen); 항의 시위 (M90's 시위) = a protest demonstration; 항의 편지 (M27's 편지). Sort: M24's 반대 is being against; 항의 is saying so, loudly, to the one responsible — you can 반대 in silence, never 항의. RADAR: the 항 is 抗, not the harbour-港 of M12's 공항 nor the 航 of 항공 — resist, not sail.

德 virtue, standing alone — the character M31's 덕수궁 unpacked ("덕 (德 virtue) + 수 (壽 longevity) + 궁 (palace") and M69's 덕분 built on ("德分 virtue-portion: 덕수궁's virtue-德 (M31) + 부분's portion-分 (M32) — your share of someone else's goodness"). Alone it is the Confucian word: 덕을 쌓다 (M61's 쌓다) = to build up virtue — the good deeds a person banks; 덕이 높다 (M7's 높다) = of great virtue; 덕이 있는 사람 = a person of character; and the everyday fossil, 덕을 보다 (M1's 보다) = to benefit from someone's goodness, 친구 덕을 많이 봤어요 = I owe my friend a lot — M69's 덕분 without the 분. Sort: 덕분 is the credit you hand out (덕분에요); 덕 is the stock it draws on. RADAR: S1's 덕후 is not virtuous — that note: "Japanese 오타쿠 → 오덕후 → 덕후: a loanword localized twice" — its 덕 is a Japanese syllable that happened to land on a Korean one.

香 incense, bare — the root M41's 향기 decoded as "香氣 fragrance-energy" and traced to its first hiding place: "the 향 is incense-香 — the root that was burning inside M36's 모기향 coil all along". Alone it means the stick and the smell: 향을 피우다 (M14's 피우다 — that note's "Literally 'to make bloom'", the same verb Korean lends to cigarettes) = to burn incense — the first act at M99's 제사, three sticks and a bow; 향이 좋다 (M1's 좋다) = smells lovely — the coffee, the tea, the candle; 커피 향 (M1's 커피), 꽃향 (M7's 꽃 — frozen as one word). M83's 향수 ("香水 fragrance-water") is this 향 in water. Sort: M41's 냄새 is any smell and usually a bad one; 향기 is the good one; 향 is the good one as a THING — you buy 향, you smell 향기. RADAR: the 향 of M27's 고향 is home-鄕 (M83's 향수 note: "the home-鄕 of M27's 고향"), and the 향 of M31's 방향 is facing-向 — three 향s, and only this one burns.

騷音 clamour-sound: the word the M54 gap deck spelled out before it was yours — "소음 (騷音, noise — untaught, riding frozen: clamor-騷 plus the sound-音 inside M26's 발음)" — 騷 a FIRST, 音 the same sound-音 as M48's 음악가 (音樂家). Noise as a grievance: 층간 소음 (M13's 층 + M55's 간) = the noise between floors, Korea's apartment war — M54's 위층 note called it exactly that, "The gap deck names the war: 층간 소음"; 소음이 심하다 (M39's 심하다) = the noise is bad; 소음 공해 (공해 — pollution, riding frozen; M99's 오염 is its cousin) = noise pollution; 소음 때문에 잠을 못 자요 (M29's 때문, M28's 잠) = can't sleep for the noise. Sort: M19's 소리 is any sound — 새 소리, 빗소리; 소음 is sound that has been ruled against. RADAR: the 소 is 騷, not the small-小 of M59's 소 nor the cow of M18's 소고기 — a small sound is 작은 소리, never 소음.

en: a living thing, an organism; biology (生物)
notes: 生物 life-thing: the life-生 M25's 인생 read as "생 (life — 생일's 생)" + the thing-物 of M35's 식물 ("植物 planted-thing") — anything alive. 생물학 (學 — the study-學 of M15's 과학) = biology, the school subject, clipped to 생물 on the timetable (생물 시간 = biology class); 해양 생물 (해양 — the ocean, riding frozen) = marine life; 미생물 (frozen — the tiny-微 in front) = microorganisms; 외계 생물 (frozen) = alien life. The shelf it completes: M35's 식물 is the planted thing, M22's 동물 is the moving thing, and 생물 is the living thing that covers both. Sort against M92's 생명: 생명 is the life IN a body; 생물 is the body that has it — a sparrow is a 생물 and has 생명. RADAR: not M9's 물건 (a thing, the goods) — 物 is the same, but a 생물 breathes and a 물건 has a price.

en: the source, the origin, the root (根源)
notes: 根源 root-spring: the root-根 of M86's 근거 ("根據 root-rely: 根 root (a FIRST — the Sino twin of M49's 뿌리") + the spring-源 of M92's 자원 ("資源 asset-source: the asset-資 of M44's 자료 ("資料 asset-stuff") + 源, the spring a river rises from") — where a thing starts, root and spring together. 문제의 근원 (M7's 문제) = the root of the problem — the phrase the report reaches for when 원인 (M86) is not deep enough; 갈등의 근원 (갈등 — conflict, riding frozen) = the source of the conflict; 근원을 찾다 (M6's 찾다) = to trace something to its source; 근원적인 (through the -적 factory of M45) = fundamental. Sort: M86's 원인 is the cause you can name in a sentence; 근원 is the cause under the causes. RADAR, and M92's 자원 note drew both lines: this 원 is 源 the spring — "NOT the 原 of M86's 원인" — and it has "no kin with M9's 원 (₩)".

en: the actual state (of affairs), the real conditions (實態)
notes: 實態 real-state: the real-實 of 실체 above and M34's 확실하다 + the 態 of M33's 태도 ("態度 posture-degree") — the posture things are actually in. The survey's noun: 실태 조사 (M44's 조사) = a fact-finding survey — 청소년 흡연 실태 조사 (청소년 and 흡연 riding frozen) is the headline every spring; 실태를 파악하다 (M93's 파악하다) = to get a grip on the real situation; 실태가 드러나다 (M93's 드러나다) = the true state comes to light. Sort against M86's 실정, its nearest neighbour: that note called 실정 "the report's word, with no person in it, only the facts on the ground" — and the difference is who is talking: 실정 PLEADS (우리 실정에 맞지 않아요 — it does not fit our circumstances), 실태 is SURVEYED (실태를 조사하다). A ministry has an 실정; a problem has an 실태. RADAR: the 태 is 態, not the 太 of M49's 태양.

en: the said, the one in question; corresponding (該當)
notes: 該當 that-fit — M86's 해당하다 dismounted, and that note already showed the bare word at work: "Bare 해당 is a determiner: 해당 지역 (M31's 지역) = the region in question, 해당 사항 없음 (사항 — item, riding frozen; M1's 없다 nouned) = not applicable, N/A". So 해당 sits in front of a noun and points at the one already under discussion — the form's THE: 해당 기간 (M38's 기간) = the period in question, 해당 제품 (M43's 제품) = the product concerned, 해당 학생 = the student in question. It replaces M29's 그 in print — the notice cannot say 그 학생, so it says 해당 학생. Sort against M99's 동 and M99's 현: 동 says the same one, 현 says the current one, 해당 says the one we are talking about — three determiners the form stamps and the mouth never says. RADAR: not M11's 해 (the sun) + 당 — this 해 is 該, the said; the 당 is the fit-當 of M34's 당연하다.

en: to replace, to substitute for, to stand in for (代身)
notes: M39's 대신 ("代身 substitute-body: instead") with 하다 welded on — the noun that was doing instead-work as an adverb becomes a verb that does the standing-in. Transitive, with 을/를: 기계가 사람을 대신해요 (M72's 기계, M1's 사람) = machines replace people — the automation sentence; 사진이 말을 대신해요 (M17's 사진, M4's 말) = the photo speaks for itself; and in its -아/어(서) coat, 을/를 대신해서 = on behalf of — 사장님을 대신해서 인사드립니다 (M9's 사장님, M19's 인사하다 nouned) = I greet you on the boss's behalf, the deputy's opening line. Sort: M9's 바꾸다 swaps A for B and both still exist; 대신하다 puts B where A was and A is gone; M39's 대신 alone (커피 대신 차) is the adverb both grew from. The 되다-twin 대신되다 barely exists — you cannot be replaced-by in Korean, someone replaces you.

en: to snap off, break (a stem); to turn (a corner); to defeat
notes: To break a thing across its grain: 꽃을 꺾다 (M7's 꽃) = snap a flower off at the stem, the act every park sign forbids. Then the steering wheel: 왼쪽으로 꺾다 (M6's 왼쪽 — that note: "왼 (left) + 쪽 (side/direction)") = hang a left, the driver's verb. Then the sports page: 상대를 꺾다 (M57's 상대 — its note ran "경기 상대 (M17) = the opponent") = to beat the opponent — but a record is not 꺾다, it is 깨다: M96's 기록 note filed "기록을 깨다 — records too" on M36's 깨다. 꺾다 is the hand doing the snapping; the thing that snaps on its own is 부러지다 (to break, riding frozen) — 다리가 부러졌어요, the leg broke.

en: to pierce, bore through; to open (a way)
notes: To make a hole go all the way through: 구멍을 뚫다 (M60's 구멍) = drill a hole, 벽을 뚫다 (M13's 벽) = break through a wall, 터널을 뚫다 (M50's 터널) = bore a tunnel. Then the way: 길을 뚫다 (M12's 길) = open a road — or a way out of a problem. The passive is 뚫리다 (to be pierced, to clear — riding frozen), and the body owns it: 코가 뚫리다 (M14's 코) = the nose clears — the cold's first good morning. Says 뚤타: the ㅀ batchim reads as ㄹ, and the ㅎ hardens the ㄷ, the same route M3's 싫다 takes to 실타.

To dig: 땅을 파다 (M22's 땅) = dig the ground, 구멍을 파다 (M60's 구멍) = dig a hole — the hand's answer to 뚫다 above, which pierces THROUGH; 파다 goes DOWN. 무덤을 파다 (this shelf's 무덤) = dig a grave, and the idiom 자기 무덤을 파다 (M32's 자기) = to dig one's own grave — the same figure English uses. RADAR, three ways: not M40's 파 ("파를 썰다 is knife skill number one" — the scallion), not the 파 of M49's 파도 (that note already ruled "this 파 has nothing to do with M40's 파"), and not the 파 sound M15's 졸업하다 note wrote in "Said 조러파다" — a ㅎ-merge, no digging in it.

en: to spread (on the floor), to lay down (a mat, a blanket)
notes: To lay a thing flat under something — the floor-dwelling verb.
