It PAYS M83's 신문지, which ran the collocation frozen: "신문지를 깔다 (깔다 — to spread on the floor, riding frozen)" — and it pays M102's 깔리다, whose note said outright "깔다 itself stays frozen": 깔리다 is this verb through the passive party of M36, and today the active end lands. 이불을 깔다 (M13's 이불) = lay out the bedding — the 온돌 verb, done every night and undone every morning; 방석을 깔고 앉다 with 방석 (a floor cushion) riding frozen and M9's 앉다 = sit on a cushion. The pair to hold: 이불을 깔다 (you spread it) / 이불이 깔려 있다 (it lies spread) — the party's two ends on one blanket.

en: to wrap around, envelop; to shield (someone)
notes: M41's 감다 in its third job — that note: "실을 감다 — wind the thread" — + a wrap-싸다 you have met only inside M94's 둘러싸다, whose md ruled "the 싸다 inside 둘러싸다 wraps; M7's 싸다 is cheap": wind-and-wrap. 아이를 감싸다 (M4's 아이) = wrap a child in one's arms or a blanket; 상처를 감싸다 (M36's 상처) = bind a wound. Then the moral row: 감싸 주다 (M9's 주다) = to cover for someone, to shield them from blame — the parent's verb, and the bad manager's. 둘러싸다 (M94) surrounds from outside; 감싸다 holds from inside the wrap.

en: to hold in one's arms, to brood; to harbour (a feeling, a dream)
notes: NIKL hints 가슴에 ~ (M30's 가슴): to hold against the chest — 아기를 품다 (M25's 아기), and the hen's version, 알을 품다 (M59's 알) = to brood, sit on the eggs. The noun under it is 품, two entries down — the bosom the holding happens in. Then the inner row, the one print uses: 꿈을 품다 (M8's 꿈 — "the sleeping kind and the life-goal kind", and this is the second) = to harbour a dream, 의문을 품다 (M87's 의문) = to hold a doubt — its note ran 의문이 생기다 for the doubt arising; 품다 is what you do with it afterwards. 마음에 품다 (M19's 마음) = to keep in one's heart, for good or ill: a grudge is 품다 too.

The active end of a pair the M36 md printed in its 기-row — "쫓다 → 쫓기다" — and glossed in Part 2 as "쫓기다 (be chased — 시간에 쫓기다, chased by time)": today the chaser gets its own entry. Two directions in one verb: 도둑을 쫓다 (M36's 도둑) = chase the thief (toward), 파리를 쫓다 (M31's 파리 — whose note filed "파리 is also the housefly") = shoo the fly (away). 유행을 쫓다 (M21's 유행) = chase trends, the fashion page's mild reproach; 쫓아가다 (M1's 가다) = to run after. The party rule from the M36 md, run backwards: 쫓기다 flips the object into the subject suit; 쫓다 puts it back.

en: to be buried; to get (dirt) on, to be smeared with
notes: NIKL collapses two rows here, and the note covers both. 땅에 묻히다 (M22's 땅) = to be buried — the passive party of M36 on 묻다 (to bury — riding frozen), the homograph M28's 묻다 note flagged in passing: "A homograph 묻다 buries things — context, as ever, decides." 역사에 묻히다 (M15's 역사) = buried in history, 소문에 묻히다 (M24's 소문) = drowned out by rumour. Second row: 옷에 흙이 묻다 (M7's 옷, M49's 흙) = dirt gets ON the clothes, and 옷에 흙을 묻히다 = to get dirt on them — the same 히 as the causative party of M37, doing the make-happen job on the stick-묻다. Says 무치다: ㄷ + 히 → 치, the rule M73's 굳이 note filed for 구지.

en: to dry (something); to stop (a fight), to dissuade
notes: Two NIKL rows, one spelling. 빨래를 말리다 (M54's 빨래) = hang the laundry to dry — M36's 마르다 — three jobs on one 르-verb, the laundry, the thin person and the dry throat — through the causative party of M37, its 리-row: 마르다 dries on its own, 말리다 makes it dry; 머리를 말리다 (M8's 머리) = blow-dry the hair. Then the other row: 싸움을 말리다 (M67's 싸움) = break up a fight, and 친구를 말리다 (M1's 친구) = talk a friend out of it — the verb of the bystander who steps in. 말려도 소용없어요 (-아/어도 from M39, M63's 소용없다) = there's no stopping them. RADAR: not M4's 말 grown a tail — the laundry and the fight share a shape by accident.

되- (again, back — a native prefix riding frozen) + M6's 찾다 ("One verb covers both the searching and the finding"): to find again, to get back what was lost. 건강을 되찾다 (M14's 건강) = recover one's health, 자신감을 되찾다 (M39's 자신감 — whose note ran "자신감이 떨어졌어요 (M36's faller, at its saddest)"; this is the climb back) = regain confidence, 잃어버린 시간을 되찾다 (M20's 잃어버리다 in the badge, M1's 시간) = win back lost time — the memoir's phrase. RADAR: this 되 is a prefix, not M10's 되다 the verb — 되돌아가다 (to go back, riding frozen) wears the same prefix.

en: to count, reckon; to fathom (a feeling)
notes: The literary count: 별을 헤아리다 (M22's 별) = count the stars, where the mouth would use count-세다 — the one M41's 세다 note logged as "a separate verb in the same clothes" and left frozen. Its most-said form is a negative: 헤아릴 수 없는 (-(으)ㄹ 수 없다 from M10 in the badge) = countless, beyond reckoning. Then the heart: 마음을 헤아리다 (M19's 마음) = to read someone's heart, to fathom what they feel — the verb of the good listener and the eulogy. Rides the 리-shape without being a party product: there is no 헤아다 underneath.

다짐 (a resolution, a pledge — the noun, riding frozen) + 하다: to make a firm resolve. Kin of M94's 다지다 (to press firm) — that note ran "마음을 다지다 (M19's 마음) = steel oneself", and 다짐 is what the pressing produces: a resolve made hard. 새해 다짐 (M25's 새해) = the New Year's resolution, written every January beside M26's 목표; 다시는 안 하겠다고 다짐했어요 (M10's 다시, -겠- from M49, -다고 하다 from M32) = I vowed never again. Sort: M34's 결심하다 decides; 다짐하다 promises yourself you will hold to it — and the -기로 하다 from M48 is the everyday version of both.

en: to sink; to subside, calm down
notes: 가라 (down, under — riding frozen) + M9's 앉다: to sit down into the water. 배가 가라앉다 (M3's 배, whose note lets context pick between the stomach, the pear and the boat — the sea picks here) = the boat sinks. Then the inner weather: 마음이 가라앉다 (M19's 마음) = the heart settles, calms; 흥분이 가라앉다 (흥분 — excitement, riding frozen) = the excitement dies down; 목소리가 가라앉다 (M19's 목소리) = the voice drops low. Sort against M35's 빠지다, "The universal falling-verb": 빠지다 falls INTO the water; 가라앉다 goes to the bottom and stays. Its causative, 가라앉히다 (riding frozen), is what a deep breath does to the 마음.

en: to rise up, soar; to gush, well up
notes: To rise sharply from below: 해가 솟다 (M11's 해) = the sun leaps up — the New Year's dawn crowd's verb; 건물이 솟다 (M22's 건물) = a tower rises; 눈물이 솟다 (M14's 눈물 — "눈 + 물: eye-water") = tears well up; 물이 솟다 (M1's 물) = water gushes. The fuller form 솟아오르다 (riding frozen) adds M22's 오르다, and the price page's 치솟다 (to skyrocket, riding frozen) is the same verb with a kick. Sort: 오르다 climbs by steps — "Mountains, stairs, and prices — all things that 오르다"; 솟다 shoots, all at once, from underneath.

en: to harden, set; to be firm (of resolve)
notes: It PAYS M73's 굳이, which decoded itself on a verb it did not own — "굳다 (to harden — untaught, riding frozen) + -이: hardened-ly = insistently" — and the verb lands today. 시멘트가 굳다 (시멘트 — cement, riding frozen) = the cement sets, 떡이 굳다 (M18's 떡) = the rice cake goes hard, 몸이 굳다 (M14's 몸) = the body stiffens — with cold, or with stage fright. In the badge it is an adjective of will: 굳은 결심 (결심 — resolve, riding frozen) = a firm resolve, 굳은 표정 (M34's 표정) = a set face. NIKL files it as an adjective; sort it against M60's 딱딱하다, which is the STATE and "nearly always a complaint" — 굳다 is the hardening as it happens, and can be praise.

굳다 above + -아/어지다 from M35 — the change-of-state machine, run on the shelf's own adjective, and the third member of the table this module opened with: 굳다 is hard, 굳어지다 is turning hard. 표정이 굳어지다 (M34's 표정) = the face stiffens — the bad news arriving in a face before a word is said; 습관이 굳어지다 (M35's 습관) = a habit sets, hardens past changing; 분위기가 굳어지다 (M26's 분위기) = the room freezes. Where 굳다 states, 굳어지다 narrates — it is the one you see happen.

en: to go hungry, starve; to skip (a meal)
notes: Two mds ran it frozen and the ride ends here: the M91 md's "굶다시피 했어요 (굶다 — to starve, riding frozen)" and the M95 md's "굶을망정 (굶다 — to go hungry, riding frozen)". 굶어 죽다 (M14's 죽다 — whose note warned "casual Korean 'dies' of hunger, heat, and homework hourly") = starve to death, said mostly as 굶어 죽겠어요 = I'm starving; 아침을 굶다 (M2's 아침, the breakfast sense) = skip breakfast — the student's daily 굶다. Sort against M3's 배고프다, which its note reads out as the stomach being hungry: 배고프다 is the feeling; 굶다 is the fact of no food. Says 굼따: the ㄻ batchim keeps only the ㅁ, exactly as 삶다 does — its causative 굶기다 (to let someone go hungry, riding frozen) is the M37 party's.

en: to go bankrupt, be ruined; to fail utterly
notes: 亡 + 하다 — the vanish-亡 M66's 도망가다 decoded, "도망 is 逃 (flee) + 亡 (vanish)", now the whole verb: to vanish as an enterprise. 회사가 망하다 (M2's 회사) = the company goes under, 가게가 망하다 (M1's 가게) = the shop folds, 나라가 망하다 (M23's 나라) = the country falls — the history textbook's verb for a dynasty. Then the exam-hall groan: 망했다 = I'm doomed, it's ruined (gap deck) — said of a test, a dish, a haircut. Sort against M35's 실패하다, "失敗 lose-the-attempt": 실패하다 fails at one attempt; 망하다 is the whole thing gone.

en: to come into contact with, encounter (news, a culture); to border
notes: 接 + 하다 — the contact-接 of M43's 면접 ("面接 face-contact"), of M91's 접근 and M95's 접촉 (that note sorted them: "M91's 접근 is the approach; 접촉 is the arrival."), alone at last as a verb. 소식을 접하다 (M20's 소식) = to receive news — the condolence's opener, 소식을 접하고 (verb--고 from M10); 문화를 접하다 (M26's 문화) = to encounter a culture, 외국어를 접하다 (M15's 외국어) = to be exposed to a foreign language. Then the map: 바다에 접하다 (M11's 바다) = to border the sea — three sides of the peninsula. The particle is 을/를 for the news and 에 for the border.

en: to turn one's face away; to ignore, look away from
notes: 外面 + 하다: M55's 외 ("外 the outside-root, finally solo") + the face-面 of M43's 면접 — to turn the face outward, away. 현실을 외면하다 (M92's 현실) = to look away from reality — the exact opposite of the frozen verb that note carried, "현실을 직시하다 (직시하다 — to look straight at, riding frozen) = face reality"; 문제를 외면하다 (M7's 문제) = to ignore the problem, 친구를 외면하다 (M1's 친구) = to turn one's back on a friend. The editorial's verb: a government 외면하다-s its citizens, and the editorial notes the direction of the face. Sort: M75's 무시하다 looks down on; 외면하다 looks away.

加 + 하다 — the add-加 of M51's 참가하다 ("參加 join-add") standing alone: to add force to a thing. It PAYS M86's 압력, which ran the frame frozen — "압력을 가하다 (가하다 — to apply, riding frozen)" — and the newspaper's verb lands: 압력을 가하다 = to apply pressure, 힘을 가하다 (M14's 힘) = to apply force (the physics textbook), 열을 가하다 (M14's 열 in its heat job) = to apply heat (the chemistry one), 공격을 가하다 (M98's 공격) = to launch an attack. Print only — the mouth says 힘을 주다 with M9's 주다. RADAR: not M1's 가, the subject particle, grown a verb.

en: to reach, attain (a goal, a level, an agreement)
notes: 到達 + 하다: the reach-到 of M89's 도저히 ("到底 reach-bottom") + the arrive-達 of M56's 발달하다 ("發達 launch-arrive") — to reach-arrive. 목표에 도달하다 (M26's 목표) = to reach the goal, 결론에 도달하다 (M86's 결론) = to arrive at a conclusion, 한계에 도달하다 (M39's 한계) = to hit the limit — and in the report, 최고치에 도달하다 (최고치 — the peak value, riding frozen). Sort against M8's 도착하다, "Arrive AT a place takes 에": 도착하다 arrives at a place on a map; 도달하다 arrives at a level on a graph — same 到, same 에, different axis.

保障 + 하다: the keep-保 of M43's 보험 (that note: "保 is keeping-safe") + 障, a wall, a barrier — a FIRST, and one you meet again three entries down in 천장. To keep safe behind a wall: 안전을 보장하다 (M81's 안전) = to guarantee safety, 자유를 보장하다 (M23's 자유) = to guarantee freedom — the constitution's verb, 품질을 보장하다 (M101's 품질) = to guarantee quality — the label's. The noun 보장 rides frozen: 사회 보장 = social security. Sort: M5's 약속 is a promise made with a mouth; 보장하다 guarantees with a document.

M34's 예상 ("豫想 beforehand-think") + 하다, and it PAYS M93's 예상되다, whose radar line named it — "예상하다 (I expect — riding free on M34's 예상)" — and sorted the pair: 예상하다 has a person in it, 예상되다 has removed them. 결과를 예상하다 (M32's 결과) = to predict the result, 예상했던 대로 (the -던 badge from M88, 대로 from M54) = just as expected, 예상보다 (M22's 보다-particle) = than expected — 예상보다 어려웠어요. Sort against M42's 기대하다: 기대하다 hopes for it; 예상하다 only thinks it will come, good or bad.

en: to produce, make (a film, a show, a product)
notes: M96's 제작 ("製作") + 하다, and that note booked this entry — "The verb 제작하다 rides frozen; print uses the noun." — so today the verb stands. 영화를 제작하다 (M2's 영화) = to produce a film, 드라마를 제작하다 (M17's 드라마) = to make a series, 제품을 제작하다 (M43's 제품 — the 製 is the same character) = to manufacture a product. Sort against M3's 만들다: the mouth 만들다-s a cake; a studio 제작하다-s a season, and the credits say 제작 where the kitchen says nothing.

M57's 기초 ("기초 is the footing that carries what comes next") + 하다: to stand on a footing. Always with 에: 사실에 기초하다 (M24's 사실) = to be based on fact, 사실에 기초한 영화 (in the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24) = a film based on a true story — the same film M86's 바탕 note built as "사실을 바탕으로 한 영화 (M24's 사실, M2's 영화) = a film based on a true story", with one frame swapped for the other. Sort: 을/를 바탕으로 한 is the essay's; 에 기초한 is the law's and the paper's — 경험에 기초한 판단 (M33's 경험, M34's 판단).

M93's 개선 ("改善 reform-good") + 하다 — that note ran the pair free, "개선하다 / 개선되다 ride free", and today the active half is filed: 관계를 개선하다 (M32's 관계) = to improve relations, 환경을 개선하다 (M32's 환경) = to improve the environment, 성적을 개선하다 (M35's 성적) = to bring one's grades up — the report card's verb. 개선되다 keeps riding free: 개선됐어요, it got better, nobody named. Sort against M13's 고치다: 고치다 fixes one broken thing; 개선하다 makes a working thing better by plan.

en: the bosom, one's arms (as an embrace); the cut, fit (of a garment)
notes: NIKL hints 옷이 ~이 크다: the space a garment leaves around the body — 옷의 품이 크다 (M7's 옷, M1's 크다) = loose-fitting, 품이 맞다 (M15's 맞다) = fits across the chest. The same word is the chest as a place to be held: 품에 안다 (M28's 안다) = hold to one's chest, 엄마 품 (M4's 엄마) = a mother's arms, 고향의 품 (M27's 고향) = the embrace of home — and 품다, above, is this noun made a verb. RADAR: not the goods-品 M23's 기념품 decoded as "품 (goods" and M101's 품질/품목 built on — that 품 is Sino and ends words; this one is native and stands alone.

NIKL hints ~을 뱉다: 침을 뱉다 (뱉다 — to spit out, riding frozen) = to spit, and 침이 고이다 (고이다 — the pooling verb M82's 빗물 note ran frozen: "빗물이 고이다 (고이다 — to pool, riding frozen)") = the mouth waters — the food-show sentence (gap deck). Then the clinic: 침을 맞다 (M15's 맞다 — "the receiving end of M14's 주사를 맞다") = to get acupuncture, the 한의원's 침 (鍼). RADAR, three sound-twins: M2's 아침 — "Also means breakfast" — has no spit in it; the 침 of M6's 침대 is sleep-寢, as M13's 침실 filed it, "침 (sleep — the one in 침대)"; and M95's 침묵 is sink-沈.

en: a joint, a node (of bamboo, a finger); a bar (of music); a word
notes: The joint where a thing bends or is counted off — and it PAYS M88's 한마디, which built on it frozen: "마디 (a joint of bamboo, a bar of music, a single word — riding frozen)". 손가락 마디 (M28's 손가락) = a finger joint, 뼈마디 (M41's 뼈) = the joints, what aches in old age; 대나무 마디 (대나무 — bamboo, riding frozen) = the node; 한 마디 (M5's 하나 in counter shape) = one bar of music, and — written solid — one word, 말 한마디 (M4's 말). One noun for every place a long thing is divided.

The seat. It PAYS M82's 원숭이, whose chain-rhyme carried it frozen — "엉덩이 = bottom, riding frozen" — 원숭이 엉덩이는 빨개, and the red bottom is now a word. 엉덩이를 붙이다 (M37's 붙이다) = to sit down and stay put — 엉덩이 붙일 시간도 없어요 (M1's 시간) = no time to sit; 엉덩이가 무겁다 (M21's 무겁다) = slow to get moving — and, of a student, able to sit long. 엉덩이를 맞다 (M15's 맞다) is the old schoolroom. The polite doctor's word is 둔부 (riding frozen); the nursery's is 궁둥이 (riding frozen).

en: jeogori — the short jacket of the hanbok
notes: The upper half of M21's 한복: 치마 저고리 (M21's 치마 — that note: "Also the bottom half of a 한복") = the women's set, 바지 저고리 (M21's 바지) = the men's. Short, tied at the chest with a long ribbon (고름 — riding frozen), and the part of a 한복 that dates a photograph: the length of the 저고리 changed by the decade. Not M7's 옷 in general — 옷 is any clothing; 저고리 is this jacket only. RADAR: not M1's 저 + a 고리 (a ring, riding frozen) — one native word, no seam.

The grave, and it PAYS M39's 핑계, which ran the proverb with the noun frozen — "핑계 없는 무덤이 없다 — no grave lacks an excuse" — today every word of it is yours (gap deck). 무덤을 파다 (this shelf's 파다) = dig a grave; 조상의 무덤 (M69's 조상) = the ancestral grave — the one 추석 (M25) visits, the visit being 성묘 (riding frozen); 무덤까지 가져가다 (M6's 까지, M52's 가져가다) = take a secret to the grave. Sort against M53's 죽음: 죽음 is the event; 무덤 is the address. The mound on a Korean hillside is 묘 (riding frozen); 무덤 is the native word for the same place.

en: a wave, a ripple; a tide (of people, of change)
notes: M1's 물 + 결 (grain, texture, the direction a surface runs — riding frozen): the grain of the water — a ripple, a wave. 물결이 일다 (일다 — to rise, stir, riding frozen) = ripples form, 물결이 치다 (M17's 치다) = waves lap; then the crowd: 사람들의 물결 (M1's 사람) = a sea of people, 변화의 물결 (M32's 변화) = a wave of change — the headline's row. Sort against M49's 파도, "波濤 wave-billow": 파도 crashes — you 파도를 타다; 물결 ripples — you watch it. The 결 also runs through 머릿결 (the grain of hair, riding frozen).

en: the meal table; a meal as served
notes: M1's 밥 + M40's 상 (床), and it PAYS that note, which listed the family frozen — "밥상, 술상, 생일상" — the first of the three lands. 밥상을 차리다 (M40's 차리다 — its note: "상을 차리다 = lay the table, feast-grade") = set the table, serve the meal; 밥상에 앉다 (M9's 앉다) = sit down to eat; 밥상을 치우다 (M54's 치우다) = clear it. Then the meal itself: 소박한 밥상 (소박하다 — plain, riding frozen) = a simple spread, and 밥상머리 교육 (M32's 교육; 머리 as the head of the table) = manners learned at the table — the phrase every grandmother owns. M40's 상 is any low table; 밥상 is the one with dinner on it.

天障: the heaven-天 M49's 천둥 traced ("天動 — 'heaven moves'") + the wall-障 of 보장하다, above — the barrier toward heaven. The room's three planes, now all yours: M13's 바닥 ("The surface you sit on — and in Korea, often sleep on."), the 천장 over it, and M54's 지붕 outside on top. 천장이 높다 (M7's 높다) = a high ceiling, 천장에 닿다 (M61's 닿다) = to touch the ceiling, 천장을 뚫다 (this shelf's 뚫다) = to punch through it — and 유리 천장 (M36's 유리) = the glass ceiling, the same figure as English. RADAR: not M9's 천 (thousand) + M30's 장 — one 天障, and the 장 is a barrier, not a sheet.

en: not yet, not even (with a negative)
notes: The adverb that only ever travels with a negative: 미처 생각하지 못했어요 (M10's 생각하다, the long negation -지 못하다 from M28) = it never even occurred to me; 미처 준비하지 못했어요 (M8's 준비하다) = I didn't get it ready in time. It measures the thing you did not reach before the moment closed, which is why 못하다 is almost its only partner. Its spoken twin is M14's 아직 — that note's rule, "With a negative it reads 'not yet'" — but 아직 leaves the clock running and 미처 says the clock has stopped.

en: at a glance; vaguely, in passing
notes: The corner-of-the-eye adverb: 얼핏 보다 (M1's 보다) = to catch a glimpse, 얼핏 듣다 (M2's 듣다) = to half-hear — and 얼핏 들었어요 is how a rumour enters a conversation with nobody owning it. 얼핏 보면 (the -(으)면 from M20) = at first glance, the essay's hinge before a but. The near-twin 언뜻 (frozen) does the same job with a different first syllable; both are standard and no Korean sorts them. Radar: 얼핏 is not fast, it is partial — the eye or the ear got only an edge of the thing.

A determiner, not an adverb — it stands in front of a noun and paints it with surprise: 웬 사람 (M1's 사람) = some person, out of nowhere; 웬 돈이에요? (M9's 돈) = where did THIS money come from? It PAYS M34's 왠지, whose note named the trap before the word existed for you — "웬 (what kind of)" — and stands under M67's 웬일: "웬일이에요? = what brings YOU here?!". RADAR, the spelling test every Korean fails once: 왠지 is the adverb (somehow, for some reason) and 웬 is the determiner — if a noun follows, it is always 웬.

en: as many as, a full (before a big number)
notes: 無慮 — the 無 of M39's 무조건 ("無 (no) + 조건: zero-conditions") plus the 慮 of M61's 고려하다 ("考慮 examine-ponder"): without pondering, i.e. more than you would stop to count. It sits in front of a number and declares it large: 무려 천 명 (M9's 천, M5's 명) = a full thousand people; 무려 열 시간 (M5's 열, M1's 시간). The headline's amplifier — speech hangs the (이)나 from M43 behind the amount, the page puts 무려 in front of it, and the loudest sentences do both at once.

M55's 줄 — the line, from a note that counted its jobs ("Rope, row, know-how: one syllable, three careers.") — welded to M10's 곧: in a straight line from then until now. 줄곧 기다렸어요 (M8's 기다리다) = I waited the entire time; 줄곧 같은 자리 (M12's 자리). Its spoken twin is M28's 계속, and the difference is direction: 계속 keeps going forward from here, 줄곧 looks back across a stretch that never broke.

M4's 말 + M32's 없이 ("없다 + -이: without"), written solid: wordlessly. 말없이 앉아 있었어요 (M9's 앉다) = he just sat there saying nothing; 말없이 듣기만 했어요 (M2's 듣다, the -기 nominalizer from M13 under 만 from M30). Its twin is M33's 조용히, and they are not interchangeable: 조용히 is about noise, 말없이 is about speech — you can leave a room 조용히 by accident, but leaving it 말없이 always means something.

en: early on, at an early date
notes: M8's 일찍 ("일찍 일어나요 — get up early") plus the adverb-factory -이 that also built M32's 없이: early in a life or a history, never early this morning. 일찍이 없던 일 (the -던 from M88) = a thing unprecedented — literally, a thing that never was before; 일찍이 시작했어요 (M8's 시작하다) of a career, not a meeting. Swap them and the register breaks: 일찍 왔어요 = you're here early today; 일찍이 왔어요 sounds like you arrived in the Joseon period.

하기는 (frozen) squeezed into one word — the -기는 하다 from M92 shrunk until it can stand alone as a whole turn: 하긴 그래요 (M29's 그렇다) = you know, you've got a point; 하긴, 비쌌어요 (M7's 비싸다). That md already showed the clipping at work — "좋긴 한데 = it's good, but" — and 하긴 is what is left when the concession swallows the sentence. Sort it from M85's 다만: 하긴 concedes what the other person just said; 다만 qualifies what you are about to say yourself.

The small number's adverb, and it always sneers a little: 고작 천 원 (M9's 천) = a measly thousand won; 고작 이 정도예요? (M29's 이, M32's 정도) = this is all? Its twin is M62's 겨우, whose note ran both jobs — "겨우 십 분 = a mere ten minutes, 겨우 그거? = THAT's all?" — and here is the split: 겨우 can still honour the effort that barely made it, 고작 honours nothing. Set it against 무려 on this same shelf: identical slot, identical numbers, opposite verdict.

M29's 그 + -토록 (frozen): to that degree — and the degree is always high, always looking back. 그토록 원하던 일 (M34's 원하다, the -던 from M88) = the thing you wanted that badly; 그토록 기다렸는데 (M8's 기다리다, the -는데 from M53). Its spoken twin is M33's 그렇게, which the M89 md sorted for its own purposes — "그렇게 (M33) points at manner; 그만큼 points at amount" — and the division is that 그렇게 does manner and degree both, while 그토록 does only degree, only on the page, and usually in a sentence about to be disappointed.

各其 — the 各 of M55's 각 ("the written-notice determiner") plus 其, that (a FIRST): each one its own. 각기 다른 방향으로 갔어요 (M24's 다르다, M31's 방향, M1's 가다) = each went a different way; 각기 다른 명칭 (today's 명칭). The shelf is now four deep: 각 stamps the front of a noun in a notice, M56's 각각 ("各各 each-each") hands out one apiece, M73's 각자 ("各自 each-self") gives each person their own, and 각기 — the written one — spreads a property across a list of things.

en: to the maximum, as much as possible (最大限)
notes: 最大限 — and it PAYS M63's 최대, which spelled the word out and left one hanja owing: "최대한 = to the fullest possible (a limit-限 rides frozen)". That 限 is the one in M39's 한계 ("限界 limit-boundary"), and M63's 최소한 closed it a line later — "closing the 限 that 최대한 left frozen one line ago" — so what lands today is the word itself, not its gloss. 최대한 빨리 (M12's 빨리) is, in that note's words, "the deadline's national adverb"; 최대한 노력할게요 (M26's 노력하다, the -(으)ㄹ게요 from M84). NIKL files it as a noun and 최대한의 노력 proves it, but nine times in ten it stands in front of a verb like any adverb.

設置 — M91's 설치하다 dismounted, and that note both used the verb ("앱을 설치하다 (M20's 앱) = to install an app") and promised this entry: "The noun 설치 rides free and NIKL lists it too: 설치 중 (S2's 중) = installing." M101's 소프트웨어 borrowed it frozen on the way past — "소프트웨어를 설치하다 (설치 — installation, riding frozen)" — and today it is yours outright: 에어컨 설치 (M11's 에어컨), 설치 기사 (M48's 기사) = the technician who comes to the door, 설치 비용. The button on your phone has said this word to you a hundred times.

en: to be installed, be set up
notes: The flip, and the machine's first run: swap 하다 for 되다 and the installer vanishes. 카메라가 설치되다 (M20's 카메라) = a camera goes in; 프로그램이 설치됐어요 (M32's 프로그램). M70's 마련되다 issued the licence in one line — "되다 doesn't check pedigree, only the 하다 it replaces" — and eight words in this module are that licence being used. 설치했어요 names the person holding the drill; 설치됐어요 names nobody, which is precisely why the notice on the wall prefers it.

M16's 발표하다 flipped. That note gave the 하다 side and its terror — "발표 = the presentation. Feared equally in 교실 and 회의실." — while the 되다 side belongs to the news: 결과가 발표되다 (M32's 결과) = the results are announced; 아직 발표되지 않았어요 (M14's 아직, the long negation -지 않다 from M28). One side has a person standing at a podium; the other has a website updating at midnight, which is where Korean exam results actually appear.

M20's 확인하다 flipped — that note ended on the noun ("확인 alone stamps documents and dialog boxes"), and this is the stamp landing by itself. 사실로 확인되다 (M24's 사실) = confirmed to be true, the newsroom's verb; 아직 확인되지 않았어요 (M14's 아직, the long negation -지 않다 from M28) = not confirmed yet — the press office's entire job in five syllables. Note the 로: what a thing is confirmed AS rides on 로, the same particle the 되다 of M10 has taken since Ring 1.

en: to be established; to hold (a contract, an argument)
notes: 成立 — the 成 of M35's 성공하다 ("成功 achieve-merit") plus the 立 of M81's 국립 ("立 stand — a FIRST"): to come to stand as a finished thing. 계약이 성립되다 (M43's 계약) = the contract is concluded; 그 말은 성립되지 않아요 (M4's 말) = that argument doesn't hold. 성립하다 rides frozen and means much the same, which makes this one of the rare pairs where both sides face one way — nobody establishes a contract on purpose, it simply stands or it doesn't. Say 궁닙- : the ㄹ bows to the ㄴ exactly as M81's 국립 filed it, rom seongnipdoeda.

en: to be concentrated, be focused on
notes: M44's 집중 ("集中 gather-middle") through the flip: 관심이 집중되다 (M24's 관심) = attention converges on it — the press's phrase, and the reason 관심 집중 rides across so many headlines; 한 지역에 집중돼 있어요 (M31's 지역). Sort the two sides with care, because this pair is a genuine fork: 집중하다 is a person choosing to focus, 집중되다 is everything piling onto one point with nobody deciding it. The library's 집중이 안 돼요 that M44 filed is the 되다 side already — the focus will not assemble itself.

M56's 해결하다 ("解決 untie-decide") flipped — and Korean has been rehearsing this contrast natively since M36's 풀리다, the knot that loosens on its own. 문제가 해결됐어요 (M7's 문제) = the problem is sorted, said when you don't know or don't care who sorted it; 아직 해결되지 않은 문제 (the past badge -(으)ㄴ from M24 under the long negation -지 않다 from M28). 해결했어요 hands out the credit; 해결됐어요 withholds it, which is why the announcement always chooses the flip.

M97's 생산하다 wrote the IOU in four words — "Flip it and the report speaks" — and today the entry lands. 한국에서 생산되다 = made in Korea, the label's line; 이 지역에서 생산되는 쌀 (M31's 지역, M59's 쌀, the badge -는 from M24). The 하다 side names a company and the 되다 side names a country, which is the whole reason the trade page runs on flips: the sentence is about the goods, and nobody wants to say whose factory.

原稿 — the 原 of M86's 원인 ("原因 source-cause") plus 稿, a draft (a FIRST): the text as first written. 원고를 쓰다 (M10's 쓰다) = to write the copy; 원고 마감 (마감 — a deadline, riding frozen) is what every writer misses. RADAR, and NIKL lists this sense: the courtroom's 원고 is 原告, the plaintiff — 원고와 피고 (frozen: plaintiff and defendant) — two syllables shared, and only the second hanja separating the writer from the litigant.

文書 — the 文 of M33's 문장 ("文章 writing-piece") plus the 書 of M43's 보고서 ("報告書 report-document"): writing as an object that can be filed. 문서 작업 (M91's 작업) = paperwork, an entire office day; 문서를 확인하다 (M20's 확인하다). Sort it from M16's 서류: 서류 is the pile you hand across a counter — forms, copies, a photo stapled on — and 문서 is the file itself, in the cabinet or on the server. A 서류 becomes a 문서 the moment nobody has to carry it.

計座 — the 計 of M43's 계산기 ("計算器 count-machine") plus the 座 that M83's 좌석 filed as new ("座 seat (a first)"): the seat where the counting sits. 계좌 번호 (M20's 번호) = the account number Koreans text each other after dinner; 계좌를 만들다 (M3's 만들다). Sort from M43's 통장 ("通帳 through-ledger"): the 통장 is the little printed book, the 계좌 is the number inside it — you can lose a 통장 and never lose a 계좌, and the transfer app only ever asks for the second.

en: a store, a sales floor (賣場)
notes: 賣場 — the 賣 of M43's 판매 ("販賣 sell-sell") plus the place-場 that M43's 통장 listed for the radar ("the place-場 of 시장/직장") and M37's 주차장 paved ("駐車場 park-car-place"). 매장 직원 (M16's 직원) = the floor staff; 매장에서 팔아요 (M28's 팔다). Sort from M1's 가게: a 가게 has an owner and you can point at it; a 매장 has a manager and a head office. RADAR: 매장 is also 埋葬, burial (frozen) — NIKL lists the 賣場 sense, and the funeral word has never once appeared on a mall directory.

名稱 — the name-名 that M75's 절약하다 traced on its way past ("M25's 명절 (名節, the named ones)") plus the 稱 of M33's 칭찬 ("稱讚 praise"): the official calling-name of a thing. 공식 명칭 (M90's 공식) = the official designation; 명칭이 바뀌었어요 (M35's 바뀌다). Sort from M1's 이름: people, pets and babies have 이름; institutions, products, streets and diseases have 명칭 — and the day an 이름 becomes a 명칭 is the day somebody puts it on a sign.

商業 — the 商 of M43's 상품 ("商品 commerce-goods") plus the 業 of M43's 사업 ("事業 affairs-work"): trade as a whole sector. 상업 지역 (M31's 지역) = a commercial district; 상업적 (the -적 factory from M45) = commercial, most often said of a film that sold out. Set it above the pair M43 already sorted — that note's verdict, "사업 is the boardroom; 장사 is the counter" — because 상업 is neither: not your enterprise and not your stall, but the activity itself, in the word an economics chapter uses.

實習 — the 實 of M34's 확실하다 ("確實 firm-real") plus the 習 that M35's 습관 ("習慣 practice-accustomed") and M44's 학습 ("學習 study-practice") have both been carrying: learning with your hands on the real thing. 교육 실습 (M32's 교육) = teaching practice, the month a student teacher spends in front of an actual class; 실습 시간 (M1's 시간). Sort from 연습 (practice — riding frozen, the noun under 연습하다 from M10): 연습 is repetition in a safe room, 실습 is the same skill performed where it counts and where it is graded.

自律 — the 自 of M32's 자기 ("自己 self") plus the 律 of M90's 법률 ("法律 law-rule"): the rule you run on yourself. 자율 학습 (M44's 학습) = self-directed study, which in a Korean high school means the compulsory evening study hall the gap deck files under its nickname; 자율적으로 (the -적 factory from M45). Sort from M23's 자유 ("자유 여행 — independent travel, no flag-following."): 자유 is nobody holding you, 자율 is you holding yourself — and the school chose the second word deliberately.

en: improvement, a rise in level (向上)
notes: 向上 — the facing-向 of M31's 방향 ("방 (方 direction) + 향 (向 facing)", the one M103's 향 sorted from its homographs: "the 향 of M31's 방향 is facing-向") plus the 上 of M32's 이상 ("以上 from-here-up"): to face upward. It PAYS M101's 생산력, which carried it frozen — "생산력 향상 (향상 — improvement, riding frozen) = a rise in productivity". 실력 향상 (M26's 실력) = improvement in ability, every language app's promise. Sort from M93's 개선 ("改善 reform-good"): 개선 repairs what was wrong, 향상 raises what was already working.

休息 — the 休 of M11's 휴가 ("여름 휴가 — the sacred summer week.") plus the 息 of M38's 순식간 ("瞬息間 blink-breath-between"): to stop, and to breathe. It PAYS M61's 취하다, which parked the phrase whole — "휴식을 취하다 (休息 = rest, frozen)" — and today the noun is yours: 휴식 시간 (M1's 시간) = the break; 휴식이 필요해요 (M16's 필요하다). Sort the three registers: M8's 쉬다 is what your body does, M11's 휴가 is what HR approves, and 휴식 is what a doctor prescribes — which is why it keeps the formal 취하다 as its verb.

診斷 — 診, to examine medically (a FIRST), plus the 斷 of M34's 판단 ("判斷 judge-cut"): the doctor looks, then cuts the question. 진단을 받다 (M9's 받다) = to get a diagnosis; 진단서 (the 書 of M43's 보고서 again — a medical certificate, riding frozen) is the paper your school or your employer asks for. Radar against M44's 검사 ("檢査 check-examine"): the 검사 is the test they run, the 진단 is the name they give the result — you are 검사 first and 진단 after.

疾病 — 疾, sickness (a FIRST), doubled with the 病 of M14's 병, the syllable that note took apart ("병 (illness) + 원 (house) = 병원"). 질병관리청 = the KDCA, the agency a whole country learned to name during the pandemic. Sort the two: your 병 is the one you have — 감기에 걸렸어요 (M14's 감기, M12's 걸리다) — and 질병 is the one a ministry counts. Nobody says 질병에 걸렸어요 about a cold, because 질병 lives in the statistics, not at the sickbed.

體力 — the 體 of M53's 신체 ("身體 the body, formal register") plus the 力 of M39's 노력 ("努力 exert-strength"): the body's strength as a reserve you spend down. 체력이 좋다 (M1's 좋다) / 체력이 약하다 (M63's 약하다); 체력 검사 (M44's 검사) = the fitness test, first cousin of the 신체검사 that note remembers. Radar: 체력 is neither muscle nor health — it is how long you last, which is why a Korean says 체력이 떨어졌어요 after a week of overtime and means exactly that.

人體 — the person-人 that M86's 원인 pointed at for its own radar ("the person-人 of M23's 외국인") plus the 體 of M53's 신체: the body as an object of study. 인체에 해롭다 (해롭다 — to be harmful, riding frozen) = harmful to the human body, the warning label's whole phrase; 인체 구조 (M91's 구조). The shelf closes here, three bodies in three registers: M14's 몸 is yours and it aches, M53's 신체 is "M14's 몸 in a suit" and gets measured on a form, and 인체 is the one in the textbook diagram — the only one of the three that is nobody's in particular.

待合室 — the 待 of M34's 기대 ("期待 appointed-time-await") plus the 合 of M44's 합격 ("合格 fit-the-frame") plus the 室 of M54's 욕실 ("浴室 bathe-room"): the room where those who wait are gathered. 역 대합실, 병원 대합실 (M6's 병원) — benches, a television nobody chose, and a number board. RADAR: this 대 is 待, await — not the machine-counter 대 of M55 — and 대합 is not a word you can assemble from parts you own; the three hanja only mean anything as one room. The newer sign says 대기실 (frozen); 대합실 is what the old station painted above the door.

人, the person itself — the character you have been reading as a SUFFIX since M23's 외국인 ("외국 + 인 (person)") and M27's 주인 ("주 (master) + 인 (person — 외국인's 인)"), and which M96's 지식인 finally filed: "-인 (人) marks a kind of person (지식인, 외국인, 정치인 — M32's 정치 note built that one)". Bare 인 is the printed register's word for one human unit — 일 인 이상 and the restaurant's 이 인분 (인분 — a portion per head, riding frozen) — where the mouth says M1's 사람 or M5's 명. SOUND RADAR, three cards: M17's 인기 carries this same 人, exactly as M32's 인간 said ("This person-인 (人) also fronts 인기 (M17, people-energy = popularity)"), and so does the 인 of M19's 인사하다 (人事, person-affairs); but M86's 원인 is the cause-因, and M31's 인천 is 仁 — three characters, one sound.

en: the owner, the holder (of title) (所有者)
notes: 所有者 own-person: M98's 소유 + the person-者 that M27's 환자 introduced ("The -자 is a person-suffix (기자, 학자 — reporter, scholar)"). PAYS M98's 소유, which built the word and left it standing — "소유자 (with the 者 of 관계자) = the owner" — so the 者 rail that carries M98's 관계자 and 지도자 and M43's 소비자 gets its plainest passenger. 건물 소유자 (M22's 건물), 소유자가 바뀌다 (M35's 바뀌다) = to change hands. Sort against M27's 주인: the 주인 stands behind the counter; the 소유자 is the name on the paper.

en: a victim, the injured party (被害者)
notes: 被害者 suffer-harm-person: M86's 피해 on the same 者. PAYS that note, which printed the job and the payroll in one clause — "피해자 = the victim" — the one 者 position nobody applies for. 사고 피해자 (M36's 사고), 피해자 가족 (M4's 가족) = the victim's family, the bulletin's phrase; 피해자를 돕다 (M28's 돕다). Its mirror rides frozen: 가해자 (the one who did the harm) — 피해자와 가해자 is how every court report sorts a room, and the difference is one character.

en: parents of a student, the school's parents (學父母)
notes: 學父母 study-father-mother: the study-學 of M15's 학원 ("학 (study) + 원 (the institute-원 of 병원)") + 父, the father-父 of M47's 신부 in its OTHER vocation ("a priest is ALSO 신부 (神父, god-father)") + 母, the mother-母 M47's 고모 read ("the 모 is mother-母, 부모님's (M4) second syllable"). PAYS M78's 담임, which ran the word frozen — "the 학부모 (parents of students — riding frozen) phone the 담임" — and now the school's own noun lands: parents IN THEIR CAPACITY as parents of a pupil. 학부모 회의 (M10's 회의), 학부모 총회 (총회 — a general meeting, riding frozen). Sort: M4's 부모님 is how you address them; 학부모 is how the office files them.

en: the head of an institution, the director (院長)
notes: 院長 institution-chief: the 院 of M37's 유치원 ("園/院, walled place") + the chief-長 of M39's 장점 ("長點 long-point"). Whoever runs a building whose name ends in -원: 병원 원장 (M6's 병원), 학원 원장 (M15's 학원), 유치원 원장 — and the address is 원장님, built exactly as M9's 사장님 is. PAYS M90's 위원장, which welded the same character onto a committee — "the 長 that closes 사장, 부장 and 장관 now closes a committee" — and 원장 is that 長 on a walled place instead. Sort the chiefs by what they head: a company (사장님), a section (부장님), a committee (위원장), an 원 (원장님).

農夫 farm-man: the 農 of M59's 농사 ("農事 farm-affairs") + 夫, the husband-夫 that M78's 형부 called a first ("夫, husband — a FIRST: no shipped note has read this character"). PAYS M97's 농민, which held this word open and told you the register in advance — "농부 (a farmer — the one man in the field, riding frozen) is the storybook's word" — landed. 부지런한 농부 (M15's 부지런하다) is the fable's opening; 농부 아저씨 (M27's 아저씨) is the picture book's address. The pair sorts by number: 농민 is the class that protests, 농부 is the man in the field.

en: one's wife (blunt, affectionate — a husband's word)
notes: Native, and the only word on this shelf with no hanja behind it: a man's own wife, said among men and, when the marriage is old enough, to her face. History with a warning in it — 마누라 began as 마노라, a court title for a person of rank, and slid all the way down the register, the same drift M27's 아줌마 took. The ladder is now complete: M27's 아내 is the neutral one ("Your own wife. Someone ELSE's wife gets the honorific 부인"), M27's 부인 is the other man's ("The honorific wife: 사장님 부인"), 와이프 (frozen) is what younger husbands actually say, and 마누라 is the bottom rung — 우리 마누라 (M4's 우리), warm in one mouth and rude in the next. LOAD-BEARING WARNING: never about someone else's wife, never upward (M58's 사모님 is that word), and never by a woman about herself.

同行 same-going: the same-同 of M38's 동시 ("同時 same-hour") + the 行 that M28's 날다 read inside 비행기 ("飛行 — flying-going"). Both the act of going along and the person who does it: 동행이 있어요? (M1's 있다), 동행을 구하다 (M43's 구하다) = to look for someone to go with, 동행하다 rides frozen as the verb. Sort against M101's 일행, which owns the restaurant door — that note: "일행이 있어요? (M1's 있다) = are you with a group?" — 일행 is the GROUP you arrived with, counted at the desk; 동행 is one person going the same way, and the word a notice or a hiking sign uses. The 行 file fills: M11's 여행, M6's 은행, M101's 일행, and today's 동행.

en: grassland, a prairie, the steppe (草原)
notes: 草原 grass-plain: 草, grass — a FIRST, and the Sino twin of M22's 풀 — + the 原 of M86's 원인 ("原因 source-cause"), the plain, the field a thing starts on. 넓은 초원 (M13's 넓다), 초원을 달리다 (M17's 달리다), 몽골 초원 (몽골 — Mongolia, riding frozen). RADAR, mandatory: this is NOT M25's 초 (the candle — "This one melts.") and NOT M9's 원 (won); an 초원 has no price and nothing to blow out. The 原 here is the plain, not the 園/院 of M37's 유치원 and today's 원장.

en: Gangnam; south of the river (Seoul) (江南)
notes: 江南 river-south: M22's 강 in its hanja coat — the river-江 that M63's 강하다 pinned ("M22's 강 is the river-江: the 한강 is long, not strong") — + the 南 of M27's 남쪽, the one M32's 남성 filed third ("man 男 (남자), south 南 (남쪽, 남산)"). South of the river: Seoul's south bank, and for thirty years a byword for money, offices and tutoring. PAYS two street notes at once — M31's 종로 stamped the road names ("That -로 stamps street names nationwide: 세종대로, 강남대로…") and M54's 대로 read the ending ("the -대로 ending 강남대로 is 大路, a boulevard"). 강남역 (M6's 역), 강남구 (the 區 of M98's 구역, frozen), and 강남 스타일 rides frozen — the song that taught the word to the rest of the planet.

en: the northern part, the north (of a country) (北部)
notes: 北部 north-section: the north-北 that M51's 북 flagged ("the 북 of 북쪽 (M27) and 북한 (M31) is north-北") + the 部 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion"). PAYS M98's 남부, which laid the whole rail and left this car frozen — "the rail runs 북부, 동부, 서부 (frozen — the north, east and west parts) and 중부 (frozen) for the middle" — M103's 중부 collected the middle, and the north lands here. 북부 지방 (M50's 지방) = the northern provinces, the forecast's phrase; 이탈리아 북부 (frozen). Sort exactly as that note did: "남쪽 is the direction you point, 남부 is the region on the weather map" — and 북쪽/북부 split the same way.

한- + M28's 가운데 ("The middle of anything"). This 한- is the native intensifying prefix — the very, the deepest part of — not the native 한 (one) that M5 contracts in front of counters and not the 韓 of 한국: it also builds 한밤중, 한여름 and 한겨울 (all riding frozen), the dead of the night, the height of the summer, the depth of the winter. 방 한가운데 (M8's 방), 길 한가운데 (M12's 길) = the middle of the road, where you should not stand; 도시 한가운데 (M22's 도시). Sort: 가운데 is the middle; 한가운데 is the middle with the argument already over.

en: BC, before the common era (紀元前)
notes: 紀元前 record-origin-before: 紀, a reckoning — the 紀 of M38's 세기 ("世紀 generation-record") — + the 元 of M57's 원래 ("元來: origin-元") + the before-前 that M31's 전국 filed second of three ("전화's electric-전 (電), 전에's before-전 (前), now all-전"). Before the reckoning's origin: BC. 기원전 삼 세기 = the third century BC — Sino numbers in front, always; 기원후 (AD) and 서기 (the common era) ride frozen behind it. A reading word before it is ever a speaking one: you will meet it under a museum case, in the caption, next to a pot.

en: the final period, the last stage (末期)
notes: 末期 end-period: the end-末 of M46's 연말 ("年末 year-end") + the 期 of M34's 기대 ("期待 appointed-time-await"). The last stretch of any span: 조선 말기 (M26's 조선) = late Joseon, 말기 환자 (M27's 환자) = a terminal patient, 말기 암 (M53's 암) = terminal cancer — the phrase the word is heaviest in, and the reason it is said softly. It closes a ladder you half own: M88's 초기 opened it and set the mirror ("Its mirror is 후기 (the late period — riding frozen), and 중기 sits between."), M96's 후기 collected that mirror, and 말기 is the rung after it — the difference being that nothing follows a 말기.

M29's 이 ("The bare pointer inside 이거/이런/이쪽, finally naked") welded onto M16's 달 ("The native month") and written closed, with no space. The whole lesson is register: M16's 이번 달 is what the mouth says ("이번 주, 이번 달, 이번 회의"), 이달 is what the page prints — 이달의 책 = book of the month, 이달 안에 (M6's 안) = within this month, 이달 초 and 이달 말 (frozen) for its ends. The spacing is the tell: 이번 달 takes a space; 이달 never does. Its neighbours ride the same weld — 지난달 (the 지난- prefix M25's 지난주 promised would work the whole calendar) and 다음 달, which keeps its space.

애 (the very start — a native root that now survives only here and in 애당초, riding frozen) + the 初 of M46's 최초 ("最初 most-first"), the beginning-character M25's 초 note already had on the radar. Almost always in its adverb: 애초에 = in the first place, to begin with — the opening move of an argument that intends to win. 애초에 계획이 잘못됐어요 (M8's 계획, M63's 잘못되다) = the plan was wrong from the start; 애초부터 = from the very outset. RADAR, loud: not M47's 애 (the kid — "아이 (M4) worn smooth by speech"); there are no children in 애초. The gap deck runs the adverb.

en: [number] countries — the counter for nations (個國)
notes: 個國 unit-country: M5's 개 ("The general-purpose counter") in its hanja 個 + the country-國 of M31's 국가 ("국 (country) + 가 (家 house — 가족's 가, M4)"). A BOUND counter — it never stands alone and never follows a native number: 십 개국 = ten countries, 백 개국 이상 (M32's 이상) = more than a hundred nations, 참가국 and 회원국 (frozen) for the ones taking part and the ones signed up. NIKL files it as a dependent noun, which is the grammar in one word. RADAR: a homograph 개국 (開國) is the FOUNDING of a state and a third opens a broadcasting station — neither is on the list; the counter is the one the Olympics headline wants.

M101's 창조 ("創 to create, to begin — a FIRST") through the -적 factory of M45. PAYS that note, which stamped the word in passing and promised nothing more — "창조적 (through the -적 factory of M45) = creative" — and today it gets its own card. The factory's hardware rule runs it in all three settings: 창조적이에요 to predicate, 창조적인 생각 (M10's 생각하다, the noun inside) with the badge from M24, 창조적으로 일하다 (M2's 일하다) as an adverb. Sort against M3's 만들다 the way M101 did: 만들다 makes from materials, 창조 makes what was not there — so a factory is not 창조적 and a first draft can be.

M39's 절대 — 絶對, the 絶 of M33's 거절하다 ("拒絶 refuse") + the 對 of M32's 대하다 ("對하다 to-face") — stamped: true with nothing set against it. PAYS M99's 상대적, which held the pair open for exactly this module — "Its opposite, 절대적 (absolute — riding frozen), is M39's 절대 through the same stamp: 절대적 기준 (M39's 기준) = an absolute standard" — and the pair lands whole. 절대적인 권력 (권력 — power, riding frozen), 절대적으로 부족하다 (M39's 부족하다). Note the split from its root: bare 절대 demands a negative behind it ("절대(로) + a negative = never ever"), while 절대적 takes none at all.

合理 fit-reason: the 合 of M44's 합격 ("合格 fit-the-frame") + the 理 of M34's 이해 ("理解: the noun of M10's 이해하다"), stamped. What fits reason — and, in a shop window, what fits your wallet: 합리적인 가격 (M21's 가격) = a reasonable price, the line on every Korean product page; 합리적인 선택 (M64's 선택), 합리적으로 생각하다 (M10's 생각하다). Calibrate the shelf: 합리적 is reason-shaped, M45's 긍정적 is attitude-shaped, and today's 절대적 admits no comparison at all. The same 理 sits inside M103's 무리 and M34's 이해 — the character for whether a thing makes sense.

必須 must-must: the 必 of M86's 필요성 — M16's 필요하다 wearing its hanja — plus 須, must, a FIRST. Both characters mean have-to, which is why the stamped word comes out meaning non-negotiable: 필수적인 조건 (M39's 조건), 건강에 필수적이에요 (M14's 건강). Its bare form is a determiner that refuses the 적: 필수 과목 (M44's 과목 — "科目 branch-item") = a required subject, against 선택 과목 (M64's 선택) = an elective — the pair every Korean timetable is built out of, and 필수 조건 and 필수 항목 (frozen) run the same way on forms.

全般 all-kinds: the all-全 of M31's 전국 ("전 (全 all) + 국: all-country") + the 般 of M45's 일반적 ("一般 one-kind"), stamped — taken across every kind of case = overall. It lives in its adverb: 전반적으로 = on the whole — 전반적으로 만족해요 (M39's 만족하다), 전반적인 분위기 (M26's 분위기). Twin, one register apart: M85's 대체로 ("大體로 by-the-big-body") is the survey's on-the-whole and cannot wear the badge from M24; 전반적 is the report's, and 전반적인 wears it happily. On the same shelf sit M45's 일반적 (as a rule) and M45's 전체적 — 전반적 sweeps the cases, 전체적 sweeps the thing.

M98's 부정 in its 否定 row, stamped: inclined to say no to what is. It PAYS two notes at once. M45's 긍정적 held it open from Band 5 — "mirror 부정적 (negative — recognize it now, a later shelf owns it)" — and M98's 부정 named the character and the debt — "부정하다 = to deny, and 부정적 = negative, the word M45's 긍정적 note held for you". Landed, on the 否 that denies and NOT the 不正 that cheats. 부정적인 반응 (M86's 반응), 부정적인 영향 (M86's 영향), 부정적으로 보다 (M1's 보다). 긍정적/부정적 is interview Korean's first axis, and the answer is always the first one.

M32's 사회 ("社會 gather-meet") + 主義, the -ism M90's 민주주의 decoded end to end. PAYS that note, which built today's word inside its own and left it standing — "The same -주의 builds 자본주의 (capitalism) and 사회주의 (M32's 사회 + -ism), both riding frozen" — and the creed lands. 사회주의 국가 (M31's 국가), and 자본주의 (frozen) is the word it is always printed against. The -주의 rail is productive without limit: 개인주의, 민족주의, 완벽주의 (all frozen) — any noun plus 主義 becomes the doctrine of that noun. RADAR, straight from M90: "S2's 주의 is 注意, caution" — a 사회주의자 is not being careful about anything.

en: a securities firm, a brokerage (證券社)
notes: M97's 증권 ("證券 proof-ticket") + the company-社, which is M32's 사회 read the other way — the job M100's 사설 named ("the 社 of M32's 사회 in its other job — the company"). PAYS M97's 증권, which spelled the firm out long — "증권 회사 (M2's 회사) = a brokerage" — and 증권사 is that phrase clipped for the headline, the way Korean clips every company name. 증권사 직원 (M16's 직원), 증권사 발표 (M44's 발표). The -사 company rail now runs four cars: M2's 회사, M52's 여행사, M81's 신문사 ("the newspaper as a company"), and today's 증권사.

M32's 환경 ("環境 ring-boundary") + M99's 오염 ("汚染 filth-dye"), and not one new character between them. PAYS M99's 오염, which set the phrase down with a space — "환경 오염 (M32's 환경) = environmental pollution" — where NIKL files the headword closed: 환경오염, one word. 환경오염 문제 (M7's 문제), 환경오염을 줄이다 (M37's 줄이다) = to cut pollution, the pledge every campaign makes. This is the long tail's whole thesis in one entry: you already owned both halves, so the word cost you nothing.

M22's 자연 + M32's 환경 — two taught words, closed up, no new hanja: the environment as nature made it, against the built one (인공 환경, frozen). 자연환경 보호 (M81's 보호, whose note filed the register — "환경 보호 — M32's 환경 note kept it with M26's 지키다, the native verb"), 자연환경을 지키다 (M26's 지키다), 자연환경 파괴 (파괴 — destruction, riding frozen). Read it beside today's 환경오염 and the shelf's grammar shows: Korean stacks two nouns and closes the space, and the first noun always says which kind.

M87's 가치 ("價値 price-worth") + the see-觀 that M35's 습관 sorted out of the pile ("the 관 (慣) is neither 관심/관계's gate-關 nor 관광's see-觀 — a third 관"): how you SEE what is worth what. It PAYS two debts. M87's 가치 held the word and named its natural habitat — "가치관 (the see-觀 again — a C-word riding frozen) = one's values, the interview question" — and M91's 형성하다 used it as its own worked example — "자신의 가치관을 형성하다 (M26's 자신, 가치관 — values, riding frozen) = to shape one's own values". 가치관이 뭐예요? is asked at interviews and on second dates; 가치관 차이 (M57's 차이) is the reason given for half of Korea's breakups. Its shelf-mate is M96's 세계관 — the same 觀, aimed at the world instead.

en: student number; one's university entry year (學番)
notes: 學番 study-number: the same study-學 as today's 학부모 and 학용품 ("학 (study) + 원 (the institute-원 of 병원)", M15's 학원) + the 番 of M12's 번 ("Sino numbers + 번: 삼 번 출구"), the 這番 M77's 저번 decoded. Two jobs, and the second is the one that matters: the ID number on your student card, and the YEAR YOU ENTERED, which Korean campus life sorts everyone by. 십칠 학번 = the class of 2017, in Sino numbers; 학번이 어떻게 되세요? asks a stranger's rank without asking their age. It is M58's 선배 and 후배 made countable — that note: "age is irrelevant, ENTRY DATE is everything" — and the 학번 IS the entry date. The gap deck files the caste.

學用品 study-use-goods: the study-學 again + the use-用 of M43's 비용 ("費用 spend-use") + the goods-品 of M43's 제품 ("製品 made-goods"). Things made to be used at school: M15's 공책, M15's 연필, M15's 지우개, M54's 가위, and M44's 필통 — "the humble case the whole module fits in" — are all 학용품. 학용품 가게 is the shop beside every elementary school and 학용품을 챙기다 (M40's 챙기다) is the night-before ritual. The 品 rail is now four deep: M43's 제품, M43's 상품, M48's 작품, and today's 학용품. Says 하굥품 — the ㄱ liaises across into 용.

好奇心 like-strange-heart: 好, to like — a FIRST — + 奇, strange — a FIRST — + the heart-心 of M34's 의심 ("疑心 doubt-heart"). A heart that likes strange things. PAYS M93's 지적 in its 知的 row, which ran the compound frozen inside its own example — "지적 호기심 (호기심 — curiosity, riding frozen) = intellectual curiosity" — and the noun lands. It rides the possession chassis M45 audited the whole of character on: 호기심이 많아요 = is a curious person, 호기심에 물어봤어요 (M15's 물어보다) = I asked out of curiosity. Sort against M24's 궁금하다 ("궁금해요 — I wonder"): 궁금하다 is the itch right now; 호기심 is the standing appetite that keeps producing it.

en: and so on and so forth, etcetera (等等)
notes: S2's 등 doubled, exactly as that note promised it would be — "Doubled — 등등 — it trails off aloud" — and NIKL files the doubling as a headword of its own, a dependent noun like its single. 공책, 연필, 지우개 등등 = notebooks, pencils and so on and so forth. Sort the pair by medium: 등 closes a written list and stops dead (every receipt, syllabus and ingredients label); 등등 closes a spoken one and keeps trailing, with a shrug in it. Doubling is a Korean machine you have now seen three times — M102's 구석 and 대충 double into 구석구석 and 대충대충 — and here it means: I could go on, and I am not going to.

M6's 뒤 + M8's 늦다: late from behind = belated — late not for the appointment but for the point. M88's 깨닫다 already ran the weld and labelled it in passing — "뒤늦게 깨달았어요 (M6's 뒤 + M8's 늦다, welded) = I realized too late" — so today the adjective only has to dismount. It lives in its adverb coat from the -게 adverbializer of M33: 뒤늦게 후회하다 (M34's 후회하다) = to regret it too late, 뒤늦게 도착했어요 (M8's 도착하다). M8's 늦다 measures a clock; 뒤늦다 measures a moment that has already closed.

en: to rummage through; to lag behind
notes: The same M6's 뒤, but nothing here adds up — 뒤지다 turns a thing over from behind: to rummage. NIKL files it 가방을 ~, so start there: 가방을 뒤지다 (M6's 가방) = to go through a bag, 서랍을 뒤지다 (M54's 서랍). Its second job is the other end of that same 뒤 — to lag behind: 실력이 뒤지다 (M26's 실력), and the sports page's compliment, 뒤지지 않다 (the long negation from M28) = second to none. RADAR: the 지다 in it is NOT M17's 지다 (to lose) and not the -아/어지다 wing from M35 — one native verb, and nothing in it loses.

M18's 맛 + M1's 보다: put a taste in the eye = to taste. Food first — 국을 맛보다 (M3's 국), 먼저 맛보세요 (M8's 먼저) — and then the whole abstract shelf, because Korean lets the tongue stand for experience: 자유를 맛보다 (M23's 자유) = to taste freedom, 성공을 맛보다 (M44's 성공), 실패를 맛보다 (M44's 실패). It is NOT the try-machine -아/어 보다 from M16 bolted onto 맛: 맛보다 is one word, written solid, and it takes an object where the try-machine takes a verb.

M14's 힘 + M10's 쓰다: to spend strength = to work at, to strive. It takes 에 on the thing you are working at — 교육에 힘쓰다 (M32's 교육), 발전에 힘쓰다 (M57's 발전) — which is why it is the verb every company and every ministry uses about itself. Sort it against M88's 애쓰다, whose note closed on the line that separates them: "Where M26's 노력하다 makes an effort, 애쓰다 makes it visibly and at a cost." 애쓰다 strains and the strain shows; 힘쓰다 simply applies the strength.

M28's 뛰다 + M36's 넘다: to cross it, with a jump in it. The M68 md welded 뛰다 onto 들다, 나가다, 오다 and 다니다, and M89's 뛰어나다 counted itself "the fifth weld, and the only one that came out an adjective" — this is the sixth. Literal on a low wall (담을 뛰어넘다 — 담, a garden wall, riding frozen); figurative nearly everywhere else: 한계를 뛰어넘다 (M39's 한계, whose note already ran "한계를 넘다 = push past the limit") = to transcend the limit. M36's 넘다 crosses; 뛰어넘다 crosses with a running start, and print keeps it for whatever was supposed to be impossible.

M66's 집다 (that note: "The fingers-in pick verb") + M28's 넣다, welded on -어: pick it up and put it in. 주머니에 집어넣다 (M21's 주머니) = to shove it in a pocket, 가방에 집어넣다 (M6's 가방), 서랍에 집어넣다 (M54's 서랍). Against plain 넣다 it adds a hand and a little impatience — 넣다 places a thing where it goes, 집어넣다 stuffs it — and 감옥에 집어넣다 (감옥 — a prison, riding frozen) puts a person away.

M37's 돌다 + M16's 다니다 (that note: "가다 is one trip; 다니다 is a routine with your name on it"): to go round and round as a routine = to wander about. 이곳저곳 돌아다니다 (M82's 이곳저곳, whose note already ran "이곳저곳을 다니다 (M16's 다니다)") = to knock around here and there; 하루 종일 돌아다녔어요 (M38's 종일) = I was out all day. M23's 돌아오다 and 돌아가다 are 돌다 in travel shoes with a destination on them; 돌아다니다 is the same 돌다 with none.

en: to get out of, escape (this way)
notes: M35's 빠지다 (that note: "The universal falling-verb") + M28's 나오다: fall out of a thing, and come this way. M94's 빠져나가다 wrote the receipt in its own note — "Its mirror 빠져나오다 (M28's 나오다, riding frozen) is the same escape seen from outside" — and today it dismounts. 건물에서 빠져나오다 (M22's 건물) = to get out of the building; 어려움에서 빠져나오다 (M67's 어려움) = to come out of a hard stretch. The pair is a compass, not two verbs: 빠져나가다 leaves from where the speaker stands, 빠져나오다 arrives where the speaker stands.

en: to pull off, manage to do
notes: M1's 하다 + M28's 내다 in the put-forth job its note demonstrates with 시간을 내다: do the thing, and put the doing out where it shows = to pull it off. 결국 해냈어요 (M32's 결국) = in the end, they did it — the sports headline's whole verb, and the sentence a Korean parent saves for the hard win. 잘 해냈어요 is praise for a finished difficult thing, where 잘했어요 will do for anything at all; the 내다 is what makes it an achievement rather than an act.

en: to greet, receive; to usher in
notes: 맞이 (a welcoming — riding frozen) + M1's 하다: to receive what is coming toward you. The 맞 is a greet-맞다, a different verb that happens to be spelled like M15's 맞다 (to be right — and the receiving end of 주사를 맞다), so do not try to add this one up. People: 손님을 맞이하다 (M9's 손님) = to receive a guest, 문 앞에서 맞이하다 (M6's 문, M6's 앞). Time, and this is the commoner job: 새해를 맞이하다 (M25's 새해) = to usher in the new year — the sentence every December broadcast runs.

en: to be no different from, as good as
notes: M24's 다르다 through the -(으)ㅁ freezer of M67 (다름 — a difference, riding frozen) + M1's 없다: there is no difference. It takes 와/과, and in practice it means as good as: 가족과 다름없어요 (M4's 가족) = they are family in all but name; 새 옷과 다름없어요 (M13's 새, M7's 옷) = as good as new. Its adverb 다름없이 does the same job about time — 평소와 다름없이 (M38's 평소) = just as always.

M60's 폭 (that note: "幅 width") + M13's 넓다: wide in the width = broad. It nearly always arrives wearing the badge -(으)ㄴ from M24: 폭넓은 지식 (M44's 지식) = broad knowledge, 폭넓은 경험 (M33's 경험), 폭넓게 읽다 (M2's 읽다). Physical width stays with M13's 넓다 — a room is 넓다, never 폭넓다 — because 폭넓다 measures RANGE: what a mind, a policy or a reading list covers.

en: to fly (something); to blow away; to squander
notes: M28's 날다 through the causative party of M37 — NIKL files it as '날다'의 사동사, the made-to-fly one. Hands and wind: 연을 날리다 (연 — a kite, riding frozen), 종이가 바람에 날리다 (M15's 종이, M11's 바람) = paper blowing about. Then money, which is the sense the headlines want: 돈을 날리다 (M9's 돈) = to blow the lot, lose it in one go. RADAR: not M11's 날 (a day) with something on the end — this is 날다 with the party's 리 bolted on.

To take part of a load off: 부담을 덜다 (M86's 부담) = to ease a burden, 짐을 덜다 (M13's 짐) = to lighten the load, 걱정을 덜다 (M29's 걱정). It is the verb under M73's 덜, the adverb that note called the rung M9's 더 "never had: LESS" — one root, two jobs: 덜 modifies, 덜다 takes an object and removes some of it. At the table it also portions out: 앞접시에 덜어 드세요 (앞접시 — a side plate, riding frozen) = help yourself onto a small plate.

en: to soak into, seep; to be steeped in
notes: To soak in and stay: NIKL files it 땀이 ~, so 땀이 배다 (M41's 땀) = sweat soaks through, and 냄새가 배다 (M41's 냄새) = the smell gets into everything, which is what a Korean says about a coat after 삼겹살. The figurative row is the same picture: 몸에 밴 습관 (M14's 몸, M35's 습관) = a habit soaked into the body. Its dated second row is 아이가 배다 (M4's 아이) = to be pregnant; nobody under fifty says it. RADAR: nothing to do with M3's 배 — the stomach, the boat and the pear are nouns, and this is a verb.

To leak: NIKL files it 비가 ~ — 비가 새다 (M11's 비) = the roof lets the rain in — and the news runs the abstract one, 정보가 새다 (M33's 정보) = information leaks. RADAR, and it is the sharpest on the shelf: M38's 밤새다 is built on a DIFFERENT verb of the same shape, glossed there as "새다 (to dawn)" — the night dawns, nothing leaks. Two verbs, one spelling, and neither of them is M13's 새 (new) or M22's 새 (the bird).

To hand back what you owe: 돈을 갚다 (M9's 돈) = to repay money, 빚을 갚다 (빚 — a debt, riding frozen; the homophone M83's 빗 sorted out as "빚 (debt — riding frozen)"), 은혜를 갚다 (은혜 — a kindness received, riding frozen). M88's 한마디 ran the proverb with this verb inside it — "말 한마디로 천 냥 빚을 갚는다 (riding frozen) says one can pay off a debt of a thousand coins" — and today the verb lands. It is M69's 빌리다 run backwards: 빌리다 asks the bank, 갚다 answers it.

en: to insert, slot in, fit in
notes: M21's 끼다 (that note: "The snug-fit verb") through the causative party of M37, wearing the 우 that module recruited: to make a thing sit snugly in. The pair is the module's clearest: 반지를 끼다 (M21's 반지) is you putting the ring on your own hand; 반지를 끼워 주다 (with the do-for-me machine from M9) is you slipping it onto somebody else's. Also 책 사이에 끼우다 (M1's 책, M6's 사이) = to slip between the pages, and the traffic verb 끼어들다 (riding frozen) = to cut in.

To go over a thing and take off what should not be there — improvement by subtraction. 머리를 다듬다 (M8's 머리) = a trim, not a cut; 채소를 다듬다 (M3's 채소) = to prep vegetables before they go near a pan; 글을 다듬다 (M32's 글) = to polish a draft. The noun 손질 (a going-over — riding frozen) is the same job filed as a noun. It is why a Korean hairdresser asks 다듬어 드릴까요? (M9's 드리다) before anything shorter is discussed.

To move without finding: 길을 헤매다 (M12's 길) = to be lost and still walking, 한참 헤맸어요 (M38's 한참). It does the mind as readily as the feet: 답을 못 찾고 헤매다 (M15's 답, M6's 찾다) = to flounder. RADAR: the 매 is not M60's 매다 (to tie) — 헤매다 is one verb and ties nothing, but the ear will offer you the knot anyway.

en: to stick in, insert upright; to plug in
notes: To push a thing in so that it stands: 꽃을 꽂다 (M7's 꽃) = to arrange flowers — and the spelling trap is inside the example, 꽃 (the flower, ㅊ) into 꽂 (the verb, ㅈ), both said 꼳. M101's 코드 left the plug on credit — "코드를 꽂다 (꽂다 — to plug in, riding frozen)" — and today the verb lands. Also 책을 꽂다 (M1's 책) = to shelve a book upright, and 이어폰을 꽂다 (이어폰 — earphones, riding frozen).

Fear in the register that admits it. ㅂ-irregular by the table M7 hung: 두려워요, 두려운. Against M24's 무섭다, which does scary AND scared in one breath: 무섭다 is the dark corridor and the horror film; 두렵다 is the fear you name on the page — 실패가 두렵다 (M44's 실패), 미래가 두려워요 (M25's 미래). Its noun 두려움 (riding frozen) comes off the -(으)ㅁ freezer of M67, the same machine that softened the ㅂ in M67's 어려움.

M74's 멋 + -지다: style, made visible. That note wrote the IOU out in full — "Its adjective twin 멋지다 (splendid — riding frozen) does what 멋있다 does with more voltage: 멋져요!" — so the only new thing today is the entry itself. Against M21's 멋있다: 멋있다 says cool, about an outfit or a person; 멋지다 says magnificent, and will take a building, a view, or a save in the last minute. 멋진 사람 (M1's 사람), and 멋지게 해냈어요 with today's 해내다.

Bright in the way that opens something: a room with every lamp on, and a face. 환한 미소 (M33's 미소) = a radiant smile, 환하게 웃다 (M7's 웃다, the -게 adverbializer from M33) = to beam. Sort it from M13's 밝다, which measures light — 방이 밝아요 (M8's 방) — where 환하다 is light with an effect on what it lands on, which is why the face takes it and the light meter does not. RADAR: M88's 전환 carries the syllable and none of the meaning — that note's 전환하다 is 轉換, to switch over.

貴 noble — a FIRST, and the character behind every 귀- you will meet from here. Precious because rare: 귀한 손님 (M9's 손님) = an honoured guest, 귀한 시간 (M1's 시간) = your valuable time, 요즘 귀해요 (M26's 요즘) = it is hard to come by these days. Frozen on an envelope, 귀하 is the formal after-the-name address, Korean's Esq. RADAR: not M14's 귀 (the ear) with 하다 on it, and M74's 귀엽다 is native Korean with no 貴 in it at all.

en: to feel wronged, hard done by
notes: 抑鬱: 抑 to press down (a FIRST) + the 鬱 of M34's 우울하다 ("憂鬱 worry-dense") — pressed down and stopped up, but pointed outward. It is not gloom, it is injustice felt in the chest: 억울해요! = that is not fair, I did not do it — the playground's cry and the courtroom's, and the one word a Korean drama cannot do without. 억울한 일을 당하다 (M86's 당하다) = to be wronged. RADAR: not M76's 억 (億, a hundred million) — this 억 presses.

堂堂: the 堂 of M65's 강당 ("堂 (hall)") doubled — hall-hall, a person built like a building, with nothing to hide. 당당하게 걷다 (M6's 걷다, the -게 adverbializer from M33) = to walk in with your head up; 당당한 태도 (M33's 태도). RADAR, and it is a sound trap worth a minute: M86's 당하다 is 當, having something bad land on you — 당당하다 and 당하다 share their letters and sit at opposite ends of the same story.

健全, and both halves have been decoded elsewhere: M99's 건 sorted the three 건s ("M14's 건강 is sound-健"), and M31's 전국 owns the other ("전 (全 all) + 국: all-country"). Whole and healthy, said of arrangements rather than bodies: 건전한 생활 (M29's 생활) = a wholesome life, 건전한 비판 (M93's 비판) = criticism meant to help. M14's 건강 is a body's health; 건전하다 is the health of a habit, a hobby, or a society.

The pretend-auxiliary: the badge -(으)ㄴ/-는 from M24 + 척하다. 아는 척하다 (M4's 알다) = to pretend to know; 모르는 척하다 (M4's 모르다) = to play dumb, the national one; 자는 척했어요 (M1's 자다). M74's 귀엽다 already ran the bare noun — "귀여운 척 (척 — pretending, frozen) is the performance" — and today the auxiliary lands under it; its twin 체하다 (riding frozen) is the same word in a book. Sort both against M87's 듯하다: 듯하다 SEEMS, judged from outside; 척하다 PRETENDS, decided from inside.

en: by itself, of its own accord
notes: With nobody pushing: 문이 저절로 열렸어요 (M6's 문, M36's 열리다) = the door opened on its own; 저절로 눈물이 났어요 (M14's 눈물, M28's 나다). Against M56's 스스로, whose note drew the line at agency ("스스로 is alone in AGENCY (nobody made you — 스스로 결정했어요, M33)"): 스스로 needs somebody who chose, 저절로 needs nobody at all. 저절로 낫다 (M14's 낫다) — it heals by itself — is what a Korean doctor says about most of what walks in.

Again and again, and on purpose: 거듭 사과하다 (M33's 사과하다) = to apologize repeatedly, 거듭 확인하다 (M20's 확인하다) = to check and check again, 거듭된 실수 (M63's 실수). Against M38's 자꾸, which that note called "The can't-stop adverb" carrying "a shrug of helplessness": 자꾸 is repetition you cannot stop, 거듭 is repetition you chose. It is print-flavored too — a statement 거듭 밝히다 (M56's 밝히다) belongs to the press release, where 자꾸 belongs to the kitchen.

The storyteller's adverb: time passes inside a story, and then the next thing happens. 이윽고 문이 열렸어요 (M6's 문, M36's 열리다) = presently the door opened — the fairy tale and the novel own this word, and conversation does not. Against M10's 곧, which that note called "The most-texted word in Korea": 곧 looks forward from now (곧 도착해요), 이윽고 looks back from later. Say it out loud to a friend and you will sound like you are reading to them.

en: after a long while, for once
notes: For the first time in a long while, and therefore worth something: 모처럼 쉬는 날 (M8's 쉬다, M11's 날) = a rare day off, 모처럼 만났어요 (M2's 만나다). It carries a gratitude the clock does not, which is why 모처럼 왔는데 (-는데 from M53) is the reproach when the rare visit goes wrong. Against M19's 오랜만, the greeting-noun: 오랜만 measures the gap, 모처럼 colours the occasion. RADAR: the 처럼 sitting inside it is not M41's 처럼 — the like-particle is a coincidence of spelling.

Tight, and all the way: 꽉 잡다 (M28's 잡다) = hold on tight — the handrail on M6's 지하철, and a parent's hand — 꽉 안다 (M28's 안다) = to hug hard. It also does fullness: 꽉 차다 (차다 — to be full, riding frozen; the verb M62's 가득 already glossed as "가득 차다 (to be full)") = packed solid. Against M62's 가득: 가득 is the level the contents reached, 꽉 is the pressure they are under — a glass is 가득, a subway car at eight in the morning is 꽉.

A copy made with the body, and it lives on M28's 내다: 흉내를 내다 = to imitate, to do an impression. 동물 흉내 (M22's 동물) is what every Korean child gets asked for; 흉내 내지 마 (-지 마세요 from M14, in its casual coat) = quit copying me. The word is neither praise nor insult by itself — the tone decides — and 흉내만 내다 (only-만 from M30) is the put-down: all imitation, no substance.

Matter with no shape of its own: 고기 한 덩어리 (M3's 고기) = a hunk of meat, 흙덩어리 (M49's 흙) = a clod of earth, 얼음덩어리 (M40's 얼음). Against M60's 조각, which is a PIECE — something broken off a whole and still showing the break: a cake arrives in 조각, a mass of dough is a 덩어리. Feelings take it too: 걱정 덩어리 (M29's 걱정) = a great ball of worry, said of a person as often as of a mood.

機器 machine-vessel: the machine-機 that M33's 기회 named ("機會 machine-meeting") + the 器 of M43's 계산기 ("計算器 count-machine") — a made thing with a plug. 전자 기기 (M72's 전자) = electronic devices; 의료 기기 (의료 — medical, riding frozen) = medical equipment. Sort against M72's 기계, whose note drew the line at the know-how — "기술 is the know-how, 기계 is the iron that runs on it" — and 기기 is the third rung: 기계 has a motor, 기기 has a plug. RADAR: this doubles the 기 file M83's 국기 opened, "four hanja, one syllable, and the compound tells you which" — 機 in the first syllable, 器 in the second, and 氣 and 旗 elsewhere.

羅針盤 net-needle-board: 羅, a net spread out — a first — + 針, the needle sense of M104's 침, + the board-盤 of M46's 초반 ("初盤 opening-board") — a needle on a ruled dial. 나침반이 북쪽을 가리켜요 (M27's 북쪽, M66's 가리키다) = the compass points north, and the figurative job is the same: 인생의 나침반 = the thing that tells you which way. RADAR, all three syllables, because lookup --comp flags each: not M1's 나 (me), not M5's 반 (half) or M15's 반 (the homeroom), and the 침 is the needle, not the spit. Note the two boards on today's shelf: 나침반 takes 盤, the round dial M46's 초반 phases a game on; 판 at the end takes 板, a flat plank.

統計 unite-count: the unite-統 that M31's 통일 isolated — "통 (統 unite — NOT 교통's pass-through 통 (通, M12): two Sino 통s, same sound, different hanja)" — + the count-計 of M43's 계산기. Counting everything into one number: 통계에 따르면 (에 따르면 from M90) = according to the statistics, the first line of every report; 통계 자료 (M44's 자료) = statistical data; 통계청 (the national statistics office — riding frozen) is who publishes them. The 계 is the same one M43's 계산기 counts with, so the compound is two owned halves and no new hanja at all.

M72's 관찰하다 dismounted. That note decoded it as "觀察 view-inspect" and promised the noun in the same breath — "The noun 관찰 rides free" — so today it rides free on the list. Its standing example came with it: "관찰 일기 (M48's 일기) is the bean-sprout diary every Korean schoolchild keeps". 관찰력 (the power of observation — riding frozen) straps on the same 력 that 상상력 takes two entries down; 세밀한 관찰 (세밀하다 — minute, riding frozen) is the lab report's phrase. The see-觀 is M87's 관점 and M23's 관광 wearing their third hat.

PAYS M67's 상상, which booked this exact word: "상상력 straps on the 력 M44's 능력 filed (M14's 힘 in a suit) and becomes imagination-as-capacity, the job-posting word" — and here it is. 想像力 = M67's 상상 + the strength-力 of M39's 노력 ("努力 exert-strength"): imagination counted as a faculty rather than an act. 상상력이 풍부해요 (풍부하다 — rich, abundant, riding frozen) is the school report's praise; 상상력을 키우다 (M35's 키우다) is what every children's book claims to do. Said 상상녁 — the ㄹ nasalizes after ㅇ.

頭腦 head-brain: the head-頭 that M31's 백두산 read out as "두 (頭 head)" + M101's 뇌, which that note called "the brain — a FIRST, and a rare one-syllable Sino word standing alone". The organ is 뇌; 두뇌 is the organ used as a compliment. 두뇌가 뛰어나요 (M89's 뛰어나다) = brilliant; 두뇌 회전이 빨라요 (회전 — rotation, riding frozen; M12's 빠르다) = quick on the uptake; 두뇌 유출 = brain drain. RADAR: the 두 is a head, not the counter-contraction 두 from M5 (두 개, 두 시) — and where a doctor says 뇌, a job posting says 두뇌.

物理學 thing-principle-study: the thing-物 of M35's 식물 ("植物 planted-thing") + the principle-理 of M34's 이해 (理解) + the study-學 of M44's 입학 ("入學 enter-study") — the study of the principles of things. 물리 (riding frozen) is the subject on the school timetable, and 물리학자 is the physicist; 물리 법칙 (법칙 — a law of nature, riding frozen). RADAR: not M1's 물 (water) — this 물 is 物, the thing-物 that M83's 준비물 also carries. Said 물리학 with the ㄹㄹ of 신라, not two separate ㄹs.

音聲 sound-voice: the sound-音 of M48's 음악가 ("音樂家: 음악 (M2) + 家") + the 聲 that M100's 성명 landed — "聲, the voice — a first". This is the machine's word for a voice: 음성 인식 = voice recognition, on M87's 인식하다, whose note filed the noun in advance ("얼굴 인식 (M8's 얼굴; 인식 the noun riding frozen) = face recognition"); 음성 메시지 (M20's 메시지) = voicemail; 음성 파일. Sort against M19's 목소리, built as "M14's 목 (throat) + 소리 (sound): throat-sound" — 목소리 is whose voice it is, 음성 is the signal the device processes.

裝飾 dress-adorn: the dress-裝 that M80's 포장 isolated — "裝 (to dress, to fit out — frozen; NOT the 粧 of M6's 화장실)" — + 飾, to adorn, a first. What you put on a thing to dress it: 크리스마스 장식 (M25's 크리스마스), 장식이 화려해요 (화려하다 — ornate, riding frozen), 장식품; 장식하다 rides frozen. RADAR: three 식s and none of them each other — this is 飾, M55's 식 is "式 the way-hanja", and the eat-식 is the 食 M35's 식물 warned you off ("this 식 (植 plant) is NOT 음식/식당's eat-식 (食)").

PAYS M92's 하천, which carried it frozen in its first phrase — "하천 정비 (정비 — maintenance, riding frozen)" — and today it lands. 整備 order-prepare: the order-整 of M54's 정리 ("整理 order-arrange") + the prepare-備 of M83's 준비물 (準備物) — to put a thing back in order and ready to run. 자동차 정비 (M50's 자동차, "自動車 self-moving-cart") = car servicing, and 정비소 is the garage; 도로 정비 (M38's 도로), 시설 정비 (M50's 시설) fill the budget line. Sort: M54's 정리 tidies what is already there, 정비 repairs what has worn out.

豫防 beforehand-defend: the beforehand-豫 of M34's 예상 ("豫想 beforehand-think") + 防, to defend — a first here, and back in front in 방지 further down the shelf. Blocking a thing before it arrives: 예방 주사 (M14's 주사) = a vaccination, the thing that note called "The thing every Korean kid fears at the 병원"; 사고 예방 (M36's 사고); 예방하다 rides frozen. RADAR: this 예 is 豫, not M33's 예 (yes; an example), and this 방 is 防, not M8's 방 (a room) — the syllables are borrowed, the hanja are not.

完成 complete-achieve: the complete-完 of M39's 완벽하다 ("完璧 complete-jade") + the achieve-成 of M35's 성공하다 ("成功 achieve-merit") — a thing carried all the way to done. 작품을 완성하다 (M48's 작품) = to finish the work; 완성도가 높다 = highly finished; 완성하다 and 완성되다 ride frozen off the 되다-row M70 shelved, and both are one module away from being yours outright. Sort the 완 family, which M39's 완벽하다 already ranked — "S1's 완전 was the slang intensifier; 완벽 is the standard the intensifier aspires to": 완전 is whole (完全), 완벽 is flawless, and 완성 is merely finished, which is the only one you can schedule.

證明 proof-bright: the proof-證 of M83's 학생증 ("學生證: M4's 학생 + 證 proof — a first by hanja") + the bright-明 of M34's 분명하다 ("分明 divided-bright") — to make a thing bright enough to stand as proof. 신분을 증명하다 (M95's 신분) = to prove who you are, at the counter and at the border; 사실을 증명하다 (M24's 사실). 증명서 = a certificate (riding frozen), the paper the office prints when the proving is done. Sort against M34's 분명하다: 분명하다 is a thing being obvious on its own; 증명하다 is you doing the work to make it so.

en: to be pointed out (as a fault)
notes: M93's 지적하다 run through the 되다-row M70 shelved — "swap the 하다, get the happen-form" — and 指摘 point-pick keeps every bit of its meaning: the finger still points, but nobody has to be named holding it. That note's own example flips cleanly: "문제점을 지적하다 (M63's 문제점) = to point out the problem" becomes 문제점이 지적됐어요, the same fault with the pointer deleted. 여러 차례 지적된 문제 (M29's 여러) = a problem flagged repeatedly — the audit's phrase. Print reaches for 지적되다 precisely because the active form would have to name a person.

PAYS M75's 해석, which ended its list with three words — "해석하다 rides free" — and the ride ends here. 解釋 untie-explain, unchanged: 꿈을 해석하다 (M8's 꿈) = to read a dream, 문장을 해석하다 (M33's 문장) = to parse a sentence, 법을 해석하다 (M39's 법) = to construe the law, which is what courts are for. Sort against 번역하다 exactly as that note did — "you can 번역하다 a line and still fail to 해석하다 it": one carries the words across, the other says what they meant. The 解 is the untie-解 of M56's 해결하다.

PAYS M75's 신고 — "신고하다 rides free" — collected. 申告 state-and-tell: the 申 of M64's 신청 ("申 (state)") + the tell-告 of M32's 광고 ("廣告 wide-tell"). 경찰에 신고하다 (M16's 경찰), and that note printed the number itself: "112에 신고하세요". The same verb files a lost bag, a tax return in May, and the neighbours' noise at midnight. Radar it kept and you keep: 신청 asks for something, 신고 tells on something — one wants a favour, the other wants a record.

PAYS M89's 철저하다, which named this adverb and left it riding: "철저하게 (the -게 adverbializer from M33) or 철저히 (the -히 adverb, riding frozen) = thoroughly" — today the -히 form is yours outright. 徹底 pierce-bottom, both characters still going all the way down: 철저히 조사하다 (M56's 조사하다), 철저히 준비하다 (M8's 준비하다), 철저히 관리하다 (관리하다 — to manage, riding frozen). Sort the twins: they mean the same thing, but -게 is the live machine and -히 is the fossil, and print picks the fossil nearly every time.

連續 link-continue: the link-連 of M72's 연결하다 ("連結 link-tie") + the 續 that M100's 지속적 decoded as "續, to continue — a first". One thing after another with no gap between: 삼 연속 우승 (M2's 삼, M51's 우승) = three championships in a row, written in hangul the way every sentence here is; 연속극 = a serial drama, on M96's 극; 연속으로 이기다 (M17's 이기다). RADAR: this 속 is 續, not M28's 속 (the inside) and not the speed-速 M57's 속도 flagged — "this 속 is speed-速, not M28's inside-속" — three 속s, one syllable, and the compound referees.

PAYS M86's 작용하다, which ran it frozen as half of a pair — "유리하게/불리하게 작용하다 (유리 and 불리 — favourable and unfavourable, riding frozen; -게 from M33)" — and the favourable half lands today. 有利 have-profit: the have-有 of M81's 유명 ("有名 have-name") + the profit-利 of M43's 이익 ("利益 edge-plus-increase") — holding the edge. 유리한 조건 (M39's 조건) = favourable terms, 우리에게 유리해요, 유리한 위치. Its mirror 불리하다 still rides frozen and is one module short of landing. RADAR, mandatory: M36's 유리 is 琉璃, glass — "琉璃: glass" — a homograph sharing no hanja at all, so 유리하다 never means glassy.

M104's 보장하다 dismounted, exactly as that note promised: "The noun 보장 rides frozen: 사회 보장 = social security" — and today the noun stands on its own. 保障 keep-and-wall: the keep-保 of M43's 보험 ("保 is keeping-safe") + 障, the barrier that returns in M104's 천장. 사회 보장 (M32's 사회, "社會 gather-meet"), 품질 보장 (M101's 품질) = a quality guarantee, 보장이 없어요 = there is no guarantee. The verb pair 보장하다 and 보장되다 works off the 되다-row M70 shelved, and print leans on the bare noun because a guarantee belongs to no one.

防止 defend-stop: the defend-防 you met ten entries ago in 예방, now moved to the front, + 止, to stop — a first. 사고 방지 (M36's 사고) = accident prevention, 재발 방지 (재발 — recurrence, riding frozen) = keeping it from happening again, 방지턱 (the speed bump — riding frozen); 방지하다 rides frozen. Sort the pair this module hands you twice over: 예방 keeps a disease or a fire from ever starting, 방지 keeps a known danger from recurring — Korean says 예방 주사 and 사고 방지, and never swaps them.

en: to be limited to, to be confined to
notes: 限定 limit-fix: the limit-限 of M39's 한계 ("限界 limit-boundary") + the fix-定 of M33's 결정하다 ("決定 decide-fix") — a boundary fixed in advance — then the 되다-row from M70. 한정 판매 (M43's 판매, "販賣 sell-sell") = a limited run; 한정판 is a limited edition, on today's 판. Sort against M64's 제한, the word that note called "The word a rule shrunk down to its ceiling": 제한 caps how much, 한정 confines to whom or to what. RADAR: the 한 is 限, not the 韓 of the 한정식 M81's 정식 left frozen — one is a ceiling, the other is Korea.

M64's 제한 with 하다. That note read the halves as "制 (control) + 限 (limit)" and the whole as "The word a rule shrunk down to its ceiling"; the verb just hands a rule the power to set it. 속도를 제한하다 (M57's 속도) = to limit the speed, and 제한 속도 is the number painted on the sign; 인원을 제한하다 (M58's 인원), 시간을 제한하다.
