Its 되다 partner 제한되다 rides frozen off the same M70 row. Sort against today's 한정되다: 제한하다 is a rule acting on an amount, 한정되다 is a scope already closed.

分離 divide-part: the divide-分 of M32's 부분 ("部分 section-portion") + the part-離 of M47's 이혼 ("離婚 part-marriage") — pulling apart what was one. It PAYS two earlier notes at once: M54's 쓰레기통 called the thing by name — "Korea's real civics exam is 분리수거 — separated recycling, frozen here as a concept" — and M80's 플라스틱 put you at the bins, "in the 분리수거 (frozen — sorted collection) bins every apartment block polices on its own night". 분리수거 is today's 분리 + 수거 (collection, riding frozen); 분리하다 and 분리되다 ride the M70 row. Said 불리 — the ㄴ turning ㄹ before ㄹ, as in 신라.

en: a considerable amount; considerable (before a noun)
notes: The bare root under two words you already own — M85's 상당히 and M89's 상당하다, whose note closed the loop with "相當 mutual-fitting, and it lives in the badge". Today 相當 takes no ending at all and stamps the noun from the front: 상당 부분 (M32's 부분) = a considerable part, 상당 기간 (M38's 기간, "期間 term-between") = a good while, 상당 수 = quite a number. Three shapes, one root: 상당히 grades a verb, 상당한 badges a noun, and bare 상당 fuses to the noun — the print-only determiner shape M55's 단 and M99's 현 already taught you to read.

en: the price paid, the cost (of an act)
notes: PAYS M94's 치르다, which carried it frozen in the price job: "대가를 치르다 (대가 — the cost of a thing, riding frozen) = pay for it, in the sense the drama means" — and today the noun lands. 代價 substitute-price: the substitute-代 of M39's 대신 ("代身 substitute-body") + the price-價 of M87's 평가 ("評價 judge-price") — what you hand over in exchange. 대가를 치르다, 노력의 대가 (M39's 노력) = the reward for effort — it swings both ways. RADAR: a second 대가 is 大家, the master of an art (서예의 대가, riding frozen); NIKL lists only the 代價 row, and M55's 대 already gave the rule — "Three hanja under one syllable; context referees."

反撥 turn-back-push: the turn-back-反 that M64's 위반 isolated ("違 (go against) + 反 (turn back)") + 撥, to push away — a first. What a decision runs into on its way out the door: 반발이 크다, 반발을 사다 (M2's 사다, in its invite-it job) = to draw a backlash, 거센 반발 (거세다 — fierce, riding frozen); 반발하다 rides frozen. RADAR: neither syllable is what it looks like — not M5's 반 (half) or M15's 반 (the homeroom), and not M14's 발 (a foot), which that note spent on toes.

辱, a first — and two earlier notes already handed it to you. M75's 비판하다 set it aside in a clause: "비판 (argued) is not 욕 (abuse — riding frozen, glossed)"; and M31's 뉴욕 told you outright, for fun: "욕 alone is the word for a swear word (욕하다 = to curse)". 욕을 하다 = to swear at someone; 욕을 먹다 (M1's 먹다) = to get an earful, the food idiom in the gap deck. RADAR, two sound-alikes: the 욕 of M45's 욕심 is 欲 ("欲心 desire-heart"), a wanting and not an insult — and the 욕 buried in 해수욕장 is 浴, a bath, the beach M23's 바닷가 sorted when it said "해수욕장 is the official swimming beach; 바닷가 is anywhere the land runs out."

NIKL files three 벌s and this module takes all three — the M99 lesson, run again. 罰 is the punishment a parent or a teacher hands out, and M100's 처벌 already sorted it: "Sort against bare 벌 (riding frozen), the plain penalty a teacher or a parent gives — 벌을 서다, standing in the corner; 처벌 needs a court." 벌을 받다 (M9's 받다); 벌금 (a fine — riding frozen) is the money version. The second 벌 is the counter for suits of clothing: 양복 한 벌 (M84's 양복, "洋服 Western-clothes"). The third is the bee — 꿀벌 riding frozen, beside M22's 벌레, the generic bug ("벌레가 있어요! — the apartment emergency"). RADAR: M16's 벌다 is a verb, "돈을 벌다", and shares nothing with any of them.

監獄 oversee-prison: the oversee-監 of M96's 감독, split in that note as "監 (to oversee) + 督 (to supervise)", + 獄, the prison-獄 the M98 gap deck already ran inside 지옥 — "地獄 — hell, riding frozen". A watched enclosure, literally: 감옥에 가다 (M1's 가다), 감옥에서 나오다 (M28's 나오다), 감옥살이. The official word is 교도소, the correction house (riding frozen), which is what the news and the forms use; 감옥 belongs to drama and to history. RADAR: not M80's 감 (the persimmon) — that note said plainly, "The NIKL row here is the fruit".

en: to lean on, to rely on
notes: 依支 lean-support: the lean-依 of M56's 의하다 ("依 lean-on") + the support-支 of M65's 지점 ("支 (support, branch-off)") — to put your weight on something that holds. 부모님께 의지하다 (M4's 부모님, 께 from M27) = to depend on your parents; 지팡이에 의지하다 (지팡이 — a cane, riding frozen). RADAR, mandatory, because lookup --comp flags both traps: this is NOT M39's 의지, the will ("意志 intent-aim") — that noun is willpower and shares no hanja with this verb of leaning — and the 지하 sitting inside the spelling is not M12's 지하 ("The 지하 in 지하철 — now you own both halves"). Sort them: you 의지하다 a person, and M39's 의지 is what you need when there is nobody to lean on.

PAYS M101's 인격, which ran it frozen in its first example — "인격을 존중하다 (존중 — respect, riding frozen) = to respect someone's dignity" — and today the verb lands. 尊重 honour-heavy: the honour-尊 M103's 자존심 decoded ("尊, to honour — a FIRST, the 尊 of 존경 (respect, riding frozen)") + the heavy-重 of M41's 체중 ("體重 body-heavy") — to hold a thing as weighty. 의견을 존중하다 (M24's 의견), 문화를 존중하다 (M26's 문화). Sort against M26's 존경하다: 존경하다 looks UP at a person — "세종대왕을 존경해요" — while 존중하다 stays level with them, which is why it takes opinions and rights as its objects and 존경하다 takes people.

M39's 책임 ("責任 duty-charge") fused to 지다, and that note wrote the receipt in advance: "책임을 지다 = to bear responsibility (지다's third job: lose, set, and now carry — M17's verb keeps volunteering)". The spaced 책임을 지다 and the fused 책임지다 are the same sentence with different spacing rules. The 지다 here is the carrying one, as in 짐을 지다 (M13's 짐) — NOT the losing verb, whose other job M17's 지다 gave as "Also what the sun does at dusk — 해가 지다." 제가 책임지겠습니다 (-겠- from M49) is the press-conference line; 책임자 is the person in charge, on the person-者 M72's 전자 note pointed at.

鬼神 ghost-spirit: 鬼, a ghost — a first — + the 神 of M69's 신 ("神: a god — or God") and M34's 정신 ("精神 essence-spirit"). 귀신 이야기 (M24's 이야기) is the summer-camp genre; 귀신이 나오다 (M28's 나오다) = a ghost appears; 처녀귀신 (riding frozen) is the standing archetype in white. And the idiom that outgrew the ghost: 귀신같이 (같이 from M9) = uncannily — 귀신같이 알아요 = you know it as if by magic, said admiringly about a mother or a striker. RADAR: not M14's 귀 (the ear); the syllable here is 鬼, and it keeps no company with hearing.

遺物 left-behind-thing: 遺, to leave behind — a first — + the thing-物 of M35's 식물 ("植物 planted-thing") and M83's 준비물 (準備物). What the past left in the ground: 삼국 시대 유물 (M26's 시대), 유물이 발견되다 (M56's 발견하다 through the M70 되다-row), 유물 발굴. Its two siblings: M96's 문화재 is the state's category, and that note's radar sorted its tail — "the 재 is 財 wealth, as in 재산 — not the timber-材 of M40's 재료" — while 유산 (heritage, riding frozen) is what gets handed down. 유물 is what gets dug up. RADAR: not M1's 물 (water).

en: a board; a round (of a game); an edition; a scene
notes: NIKL files 판 four times, and the M99 thesis runs again: "a Sino syllable is a row in a table, not a word." Row one, 板 the board, you have owned since M15's 칠판 ("칠 (paint) + 판 (board) — a painted board.") and M23's 간판 ("The 판 of M15's 칠판 — a board again, now advertising."), and M101's 자판 read it as "a board of characters — the keyboard". Row two is the dependent noun for rounds: 한 판 더 = one more round, 마지막 판 (M15's 마지막). Row three is 版, an edition — 초판, 개정판, riding frozen. Row four is the scene: 판이 벌어지다 = a scene breaks out; 판을 벌이다 = to start one up. RADAR: 板 is a flat plank, while the 盤 of today's 나침반 and M46's 초반 is a round dial.
